40After Peter had sent everyone out of the room, he knelt down and prayed. Then he turned to the body of Dorcas and said, “Tabitha, get up!” The woman opened her eyes, and when she saw Peter, she sat up. 41He took her by the hand and helped her to her feet.
Peter called in the widows and the other followers and showed them that Dorcas had been raised from death. 42Everyone in Joppa heard what had happened, and many of them put their faith in the Lord. 43Peter stayed on for a while in Joppa in the house of a man named Simon, who made leather.
translation_text:
Saulo tsuitsakemi
(Bɔfo 22.6-16; 26.12-18)
1Saulo ngɛ nɔ ngɛ he gbeye womi kɛ nɔ gbemi mumi mue kɛ ngɛ Nyɔmtsɛ ɔ kaseli ɔmɛ a nɔ puee kɛ mwɔɔ. E ya osɔfo nɔkɔtɔma a ngɔ, 2nɛ e ya bi lɛ womihi nɛ e kɛ ya Damasko kpe he ɔmɛ, benɛ pee nɛ ke e na ni kome nɛ hɛɛ kikɛmɛ a tsɔɔmi nɛ ɔ mi ɔ, nyumuhi jio, yihi jio, nɛ e fi mɛ nɛ e kpaka mɛ kɛ ba Yerusalem.
3Se bnɛ e nyɛɛ blɔ ɔ nɔ kɛ yaa nɛ e su Damasko ta a, si kake too ɔ, la kpɛ kɛ je hiɔwe kɛ ba bɔle lɛ, 4nɛ e tsɔ fia si, nɛ e nu gbi ko nɛ ngɛ lɛ dee ke: “Saulo, Saulo, mɛ he je o ngɛ mi yi mi wae?” 5Nɛ e ke: “Mo mɛnɔ, Mawetsɛ?” Se Nyɔmtsɛ ɔ ke: “Imi ji Yesu, nɔ nɛ o ngɛ lɛ yi mi wae ɔ nɛ. 6Tee si nɛ o ya ma a mi nɛ a maa tsɔɔ mɔ nɔ nɛ sa kaa o pee.” 7Kɛkɛ nɛ nyumuhi nɛ kɛ lɛ nyɛɛ ɔmɛ a nya ma kɛ daa si, a ngɛ gbi ɔ nue mohu se a nɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko. 8Saulo te si; se benɛ e bli e hɛngmɛ ɔ, e hyɛ we nɔ; nɛ a pɛtɛ e nine nya nɛ a kɛ lɛ ya Damasko. 9E hyɛ we nɔ, jeha nɛ ɔ hu e yi ni nɛ e nui nɔ ko hulɔ ligbi etɛ sɔuu.
10Se kaselɔ ko ngɛ Damasko nɛ a tsɛɛ lɛ Anania; nɛ Nyɔmtsɛ ɔ de lɛ ngɛ ninami mi ke: “Anania!” Nɛ e ke: “Ne mi, Nyɔmtsɛ.” 11Nɛ Nyɔmtsɛ ɔ de lɛ ke: “Tee si nɛ o ya gbɛjegbɛ nɛ a tsɛɛ Tlɔmɔɔ ɔ nɔ, nɛ o ya bi nɔ ko nɛ a tsɛɛ lɛ Saulo nɛ je Tarso ɔ si ngɛ Yuda we ɔ mi; oʼɛ, e ngɛ sɔlee.” 12Nɛ Saulo na ngɛ ninami mi kaa nyumu ko nɛ a tsɛɛ lɛ Anania a ma e ngɔ, nɛ e kɛ eninehi ngɛ e nɔ fɔe, benɛ pee nɛ e hyɛ nɔ ekohu. 13Se Anania he nɔ nɛ e ke: “Nyɔmtsɛ, i nu kikɛmɛ a nyumu nɛ ɔ he sane ngɛ nihi fuu a nya kaa e pee o ni klɔuklɔu ɔmɛ nɛ ngɛ Yerusalem ɔ ni yayami babauu. 14Nɛ hiɛ ɔ hu tete, e na he blɔ kɛ je osɔfo nikɔtɔma amɛ a ngɔ kaa e ba fi nihi tsuo nɛ tɛliɔ ngɛ o biɛ ɔ mi ɔ.” 15Se Nyɔmtsɛ ɔ de lɛ ke: “Yaa, ejakaa nɔ nɛ ɔ ji ye dɛ mi dade nɛ a hla ha mi, konɛ e hɛɛ ye biɛ ɔ kɛ ya majemajeli kɛ matsɛmɛ kɛ Israelbi ɔmɛ hu a hɛ mi. 16Ejakaa ma tsɔɔ lɛ dengmehi abɔ nɛ e maa na ngɛ ye biɛ ɔhe.”
17Kɛkɛ nɛ Anania pue nɔ kɛ ho nɛ e ya sɛ we ɔ mi, nɛ e kɛ e ninehi pue e nɔ nɛ e ke: “Maminyumu Saulo, Mawetsɛ Yesu, nɔ nɛ je e he kpo tsɔɔ mo benɛ o ma ngɛ blɔ ɔ nɔ ɔ tsɔ mi o ngɔ, benɛ pee nɛ o hyɛ nɔ ekohu nɛ o hyi fuu kɛ Mumi Klɔuklɔu ɔ.” 18Nɛ amlɔ ɔ ni komɛ je e hɛngmɛ nɔ pue si kaa lo toto nɛ e hyɛ nɔ́ amlɔ, nɛ e te si nɛ a baptisi lɛ; 19nɛ e ye ni, nɛ e he wa lɛ. Nɛ e kɛ kaseli nɛ ngɛ Damasko ɔ hi si be bɔɔ ko.
Saulo fiɛ ngɛ Damasko
20Nɛ amlɔ ɔ nɔuu, e fiɛ ngɛ kpe he ɔmɛ ke Yesu ji Mawu bi ɔ nɛ. 21Nɛ nihi kulaa nɛ nu ɔ nya kpɛ a he, nɛ a ke: “Anɛ pi nɔ nɛ ɔ nɛ kpataa nihi nɛ tɛliɔ ngɛ kikɛmɛ a biɛ nɛ ɔ mi ɔ a hɛ mi ngɛ Yerusalem ɔ ji nɛ ɔ lo? Nɛ hiɛ ɔ hu tete, lɔ ɔ nɔuu he e ba ngɛ, konɛ e ba fi mɛ nɛ e kpaka mɛ kɛ ya osɔfo nikɔtɔma amɛ a ngɔ?”
22Se Saulo na hewami babauu, nɛ e ha Yudafohi nɛ ngɛ Damasko ɔmɛ a nya mi munyu ta, ejakaa e tsɔɔ mɛ pãa kaa nɔ nɛ ɔ ji Kristo ɔ nɛ.
23Be saii se ɔ, Yudafo ɔmɛ ya sae yi nɔ ke a maa gbe lɛ. 24Se Saulo ba nu a somi ɔ he. Nɛ a buu ma a agbo ɔmɛ a nya daa nyɔ kɛ pia benɛ pee nɛ a gbe lɛ. 25Se kaseli ɔmɛ ngɔ lɛ wo kusii mi nyɔ mi, nɛ a siu lɛ kɛ gu gli ɔ nɔ kɛ ya ma si.
Saulo ngɛ Yerusalem
26Benɛ Saulo ba Yerusalem ɔ, e ka e he kɛ kaseli ɔmɛ a he bɔmi, se mɛ tsuo a ngɛ lɛ gbeye yee, a he we yi kaa kaselɔ ji lɛ. 27Se Barnaba ngɔ lɛ kɛ ya bɔfo ɔmɛ a ngɔ, nɛ e ya sɛɛ ha mɛ bɔ nɛ Paulo na Nyɔmtsɛ ɔ ngɛ blɔ ɔ nɔ nɛ e kɛ lɛ tu munyu, kɛ bɔ nɛ e pee kã ngɛ Yesu biɛ ɔ mi ngɛ Damasko. 28Nɛ e kɛ mɛ yaa baa ngɛ Yerusalem nɛ e pee kã ngɛ Yesu biɛ ɔ mi. 29Nɛ e kɛ Helenebi ɔmɛ tu munyu nɛ e kɛ mɛ hla nihi a nya; se mɛɛ lɛɛ a ngɛ lɛ hlae nɛ a gbe. 30Benɛ nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ nu he ɔ, a ya sɛ lɛ Kaisarea, nɛ a ha e ho Tarso ya.
31Jeha nɛ ɔ asafo ɔ na he jɔmi ngɛ Yudea kɛ Galilea kɛ Samaria tsuo, nɛ a nane nu si, nɛ a nyɛɛ ngɛ Nyɔmtsɛ ɔ gbeye yemi mi, nɛ a he sange mɛ ngɛ Mumi Klɔuklɔu ɔ bua womi mi.
Petro ngɛ Lida kɛ Yopa
32E ba mi kaa benɛ Petro ya kpa he ɔmɛ tsuo ɔ, e ba ni klɔuklɔuhi nɛ ngɛ Lida a hu a ngɔ. 33Nɛ e ba na nyumu ko ngɛ lejɛ ɔ nɛ a tsɛɛ lɛ Ainea nɛ e fɔɔ si ngɛ sa nɔ kɛ kuɔmi hiɔ jeha kpaanyɔ sɔuu. 34Nɛ Petro de lɛ ke: “Ainea, Yesu Kristo ngɛ mo tsae; tee si nɛ mo nitsɛ o dla o sa a!” Nɛ amlɔ ɔ, e te si. 35Nɛ nihi tsuo nɛ ngɛ Lida kɛ Saron ɔ na lɛ, nɛ a tsake kɛ ba Nyɔmtsɛ ɔ ngɔ.
36Se yo kaselɔ ko ngɛ Yopa nɛ a tsɛɛ lɛ Tabita, e sisi ji Dorka (odabɔ). Lɛɛ e hyi tɔ kɛ ni tsumi kpakpahi kɛ ohiafohi a hyemi. 37Se e ba mi kaa jamɛ a be ɔmɛ a mi ɔ, e ba nu hiɔ nɛ e gbo. A du ha lɛ nɛ a kɛ lɛ ya fɔ hiɔwe tsu ko mi. 38Se akɛnɛ Lida kɛ Yopa kɛ we, nɛ kaseli ɔmɛ nu kaa Patro ngɛ lejɛ ɔ he je ɔ, a tsɔ nyumuhi enyɔ kɛ ya e ngɔ ya kpa lɛ pɛɛ ke e ko hlua si, se e ba a ngɔ oya. 39Petro te si nɛ e kɛ mɛ ho. Nɛ benɛ e su lejɛ ɔ, a kɛ lɛ ya hiɔwe tsu ɔ mi, nɛ yaloyi ɔmɛ tsuo ba daa si ngɛ e kasa nya ngɛ ya foe, nɛ a kɛ gugue tadehi kɛ tadehi nɛ Dorka pee benɛ e kɛ mɛ ngɛ ɔ ngɛ lɛ tsɔɔe. 40Nɛ Petro fie mɛ kulaa kɛ je kpo, nɛ e kpla si nɛ e sɔle, nɛ e plɛ e he kɛ ya nɔ gbogboe ɔ ngɔ nɛ e ke: “Tabita, tee si!” Nɛ e bli e hɛngmɛ, nɛ benɛ e na Petro ɔ, e te si hi si. 41Nɛ Petro nu e nine si, nɛ e wo e nɔ; nɛ e tsɛ ni klɔuklɔu ɔmɛ kɛ yalɔyi ɔmɛ kɛ ba, nɛ e kɛ lɛ ba da a hɛ mi hɛkalɔ. 42Nɛ a nu he ngɛ Yopa tsuo, nɛ nihi fuu he Nyɔmtsɛ ɔ nɔ ye. 43Nɛ Petro hi Yopa be saii ngɛ Simon, lohwe he womi tsopa wolɔ ɔ ngɔ.

english_text:
Peter and Cornelius
1In Caesarea there was a man named Cornelius, who was the captain of a group of soldiers called “The Italian Unit.” 2Cornelius was a very religious man. He worshiped God, and so did everyone else who lived in his house. He had given a lot of money to the poor and was always praying to God.
3One afternoon at about three o'clock, Cornelius had a vision. He saw an angel from God coming to him and calling him by name. 4Cornelius was surprised and stared at the angel. Then he asked, “What is this all about?”
The angel answered, “God has heard your prayers and knows about your gifts to the poor. 5Now send some men to Joppa for a man named Simon Peter. 6He is staying with Simon the leather maker, who lives in a house near the sea.” 7After saying this, the angel left.
Cornelius called in two of his servants and one of his soldiers who worshiped God. 8He explained everything to them and sent them off to Joppa.
9 The next day about noon these men were coming near Joppa. Peter went up on the roof of the house to pray 10and became very hungry. While the food was being prepared, he fell sound asleep and had a vision. 11He saw heaven open, and something came down like a huge sheet held up by its four corners. 12In it were all kinds of animals, reptiles, and birds. 13A voice said to him, “Peter, get up! Kill these and eat them.”
14 But Peter said, “Lord, I can't do that! I've never eaten anything that is unclean and not fit to eat.”
15The voice spoke to him again, “When God says that something can be used for food, don't say it isn't fit to eat.”
16This happened three times before the sheet was suddenly taken back to heaven.
17Peter was still wondering what all this meant, when the men sent by Cornelius came and stood at the gate. They had found their way to Simon's house 18and were asking if Simon Peter was staying there.
19While Peter was still thinking about the vision, the Holy Spirit said to him, “Three men are here looking for you. 20Hurry down and go with them. Don't worry, I sent them.”
21Peter went down and said to the men, “I am the one you are looking for. Why have you come?”
22They answered, “Captain Cornelius sent us. He is a good man who worships God and is liked by the Jewish people. One of God's holy angels told Cornelius to send for you, so he could hear what you have to say.” 23Peter invited them to spend the night.
The next morning, Peter and some of the Lord's followers in Joppa left with the men who had come from Cornelius. 24The next day they arrived in Caesarea where Cornelius was waiting for them. He had also invited his relatives and close friends.
25When Peter arrived, Cornelius greeted him. Then he knelt at Peter's feet and started worshiping him. 26But Peter took hold of him and said, “Stand up! I am nothing more than a human.”
27As Peter entered the house, he was still talking with Cornelius. Many people were there, 28and Peter said to them, “You know that we Jews are not allowed to have anything to do with other people. But God has shown me that he doesn't think anyone is unclean or unfit. 29I agreed to come here, but I want to know why you sent for me.”
30Cornelius answered:
Four days ago at about three o'clock in the afternoon I was praying at home. Suddenly a man in bright clothes stood in front of me. 31He said, “Cornelius, God has heard your prayers, and he knows about your gifts to the poor. 32Now send to Joppa for Simon Peter. He is visiting in the home of Simon the leather maker, who lives near the sea.”
33I sent for you at once, and you have been good enough to come. All of us are here in the presence of the Lord God, so that we can hear what he has to say.
34 Peter then said:
Now I am certain that God treats all people alike. 35God is pleased with everyone who worships him and does right, no matter what nation they come from. 36This is the same message that God gave to the people of Israel, when he sent Jesus Christ, the Lord of all, to offer peace to them.
37You surely know what happened everywhere in Judea. It all began in Galilee after John had told everyone to be baptized. 38God gave the Holy Spirit and power to Jesus from Nazareth. He was with Jesus, as he went around doing good and healing everyone who was under the power of the devil. 39We all saw what Jesus did both in Israel and in the city of Jerusalem.
Jesus was put to death on a cross. 40But three days later, God raised him to life and let him be seen. 41Not everyone saw him. He was seen only by us, who ate and drank with him after he was raised from death. We were the ones God chose to tell others about him.
42God told us to announce clearly to the people that Jesus is the one he has chosen to judge the living and the dead. 43Every one of the prophets has said that all who have faith in Jesus will have their sins forgiven in his name.
44While Peter was still speaking, the Holy Spirit took control of everyone who was listening. 45Some Jewish followers of the Lord had come with Peter, and they were surprised that the Holy Spirit had been given to Gentiles. 46Now they were hearing Gentiles speaking unknown languages and praising God.
Peter said, 47“These Gentiles have been given the Holy Spirit, just as we have! I am certain that no one would dare stop us from baptizing them.” 48Peter ordered them to be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ, and they asked him to stay on for a few days.
translation_text:
Petro kɛ Kornelio
1Nyumu ko ngɛ Kaisarea nɛ a tsɛɛ lɛ Kornelio nɛ ji Italia aslaafo ɔmɛ a nɔ Sasafoatsɛ. 2Mawu jalɔ ji lɛ, nɛ e kɛ e we ɔ tsuo yee Mawu gbeye, nɛ e peɔ ma mi bi ɔmɛ kpakpahi fuu, nɛ e kpaa Mawu pɛɛ daa. 3Ligbi ko gbɔkuɛ maa pee ngmlɛ etɛ mi ɔ, e na ngɛ ninami mi paa kaa Mawu bɔfo ko ba e ngɔ ba de lɛ ke: “Kornelio!” 4Nɛ e hyɛ lɛ too, nɛ e ye gbeye nɛ e ke: “Mo mɛnɔ ʼi, Nyɔmtsɛ?” Nɛ Nyɔmtsɛ ɔ de lɛ ke: “O sɔlemihi kɛ ni kpakpahi nɛ o peɔ ɔ ba su hiɔwe nɛ, e pee kaimi nɔ́ ngɛ Mawu hɛ mi. 5Nɛ jeha nɛ ɔ tsɔ nihi kɛ ya Yopa nɛ o ya kpee Simon nɛ a tsɛɛ lɛ Petro hulɔ ɔ kɛ ba. 6E ya to Simon lohwe he womi tsopa wolɔ ɔ nɛ we ngɛ wo ɔ nya a ngɔ.” 7Benɛ bɔfo ɔ nɛ kɛ lɛ ba tu munyu ɔ je ɔ, e tsɛ e webi ɔmɛ a ti ni enyɔ kɛ aslaafono ko nɛ yee Mawu gbeye nɛ ji nihi nɛ sɔmɔɔ lɛ ɔ a ti nɔ kake, 8nɛ e sɛɛ ni nɛ ɔmɛ tsuo ngɔ ha mɛ, nɛ e tsɔ mɛ Yopa.
9Enɔ je na a, benɛ a nyɛɛ blɔ ɔ nɔ nɛ e piɛ bɔɔ nɛ a maa su ma a mi ɔ, Petro ho sɔlemi ya ngɛ tsu ɔ yi mi, maa pee ngmlɛ nyɔngma kɛ enyɔ mi. 10Hwɔ ye lɛ wawɛɛ, nɛ e ngɛ nɔ́ ko hlae nɛ e ye. Se benɛ a ngɛ niyeni ɔ pee ɔ, e pee kaa nɔ́ nɛ nɔ́ nɔ e nɔ, 11nɛ e na kaa hiɔwe nya bli, nɛ nɔ́ ko ngɛ si kplee kaa bo ngua nɛ a hɛɛ e kɔ nya eywiɛ ɔ mi nɛ a ngɛ siue kɛ ma zugba. 12Zugba nɔ lohwe nane eywiɛeywiɛtsɛmɛ kɛ waami lohwehi, kɛ hiɔwe lohwe pɛlitsmɛ slɔɔto ɔmɛ tsuo eko ngɛ mi. 13Nɛ gbi ko de lɛ ke: “Petro, tee si, gbee nɛ o ye!” 14Se Petro ke: “Dɛbi, Nyɔmtsɛ, ejakaa i yi yakayaka nɔ́ ko loo nɔ́ ko nɛ he tsɔ we hyɛ.” 15Nɛ gbi ɔ kpale de lɛ nɔ nɛ ji si enyɔ ke: “Nɔ́ nɛ Mawu tsukɔ he ɔ, koo bu lɛ kaa yakayaka nɔ́ ko.” 16A pee ja si etɛ, nɛ a wo nɔ́ ɔ kɛ ho hiɔwe ya ekohu.
17Jeha nɛ ɔ benɛ Petro dɛ yaa kaa kɛ ji nɔ́ nɛ e na nɛ ɔ sisi kɛɛ ɔ, oʼɛ, nyumu ɔmɛ nɛ Kornelio tsɔ ɔ ngɛ Simon we ɔ si bie, nɛ a ba da agbo ɔ nya. 18A tsɛ nɛ a bi ke: “Anɛ hiɛ ɔ Simon nɛ a tsɛɛ lɛ Petro hulɔ ɔ ba to ɔ lo?” 19Se benɛ Petro ngɛ nɔ́ nɛ e na a he susue ɔ, Mumi ɔ de lɛ ke: “Oʼɛ nyumuhi etɛ komɛ ngɛ mo hlae. 20Lɔ ɔ he ɔ tee si nɛ o kple si nɛ o kɛ mɛ nɛ ho, nɛ koo je nɔ, ejakaa imi lɛ i tsɔ mɛ.” 21Kɛkɛ nɛ Petro kple si, nɛ e ya de nyumu ɔmɛ ke: “Oʼɛ, imi ji nɛ ɔ nɛ nyɛ ngɛ hlae ɔ nɛ; mɛni sane he nyɛ ba ngɛ?” 22Nɛ a ke: “Asafoatsɛ Kornelio, nɛ ji nyumu dalɔ kɛ Mawu gbeye yelɔ nɛ Yudafohi a ma mluku ɔ kulaa tuɔ e he munyu kpakpa a, lɛ hiɔwe bɔfo klɔuklɔu ko de lɛ ke e tsɔ nɛ a ba kpee mo kɛ ba e we ɔ mi, konɛ e bu o nya munyu tue.” 23Kɛkɛ nɛ Petro tsɛ mɛ kɛ ba we ɔ mi nɛ e ba pee mɛ nibwɔ. Nɛ e nɔ je na a, Petro kɛ mɛ pue nɔ kɛ ho, nɛ nyɛmimɛ nɛ ngɛ Yopa a a ti ni komɛ piɛ e he.
24E nɔ je na ekohu ɔ, a ya su Kaisarea. Kornelio ngɛ mɛ blɔ hyɛe, nɛ e tsɛ e wekuli kɛ e huɛmɛ kpakpahi kɛ ba kpe. 25Nɛ e ba mi kaa benɛ Petro ngɛ we ɔ mi sɛe ɔ, Kornelio kɛ lɛ ba kpe, nɛ e ba bu si ngɛ e nane nya nɛ e ja lɛ. 26Se Petro wo e nɔ, nɛ e ke: “Tee si, se imi hu nɔmlɔ ji mi.” 27Nɛ e kɛ lɛ ngɛ ni sɛɛe kɛ ya sɛ we ɔ mi, nɛ eya na nihi babauu nɛ ba bua a he nya a. 28Nɛ Petro de mɛ ke: “Nyɛ nitsɛmɛ nyɛ le bɔ nɛ Yuda no be he blɔ kaa e kɛ nɔ ko nɛ ji ma kpã mi no bɔɔ aloo e baa e ngɔ. Se imi lɛɛ, Mawu tsɔɔ mi ke ma ko tsɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko yaka nɔmlɔ, loo nɔ nɛ he tsɔ we. 29Lɔ ɔ he hulɔ nɛ benɛ a tsɔ ba kpee mi ɔ, i je we nya nɛ i ba nɛ ɔ nɛ. Nɛ jeha nɛ ɔ i ngɛ nyɛ bie ke: Mɛni sane he je nɛ nyɛ tsɔ kɛ ba kpee mi ɔ?”
30Kornelio ha heto ke: “Mwɔnɔ ji ligbi eywiɛ ɔ, i ngɛ sɔlee ngɛ ye we ɔ mi maa pee gbɔkuɛ ngmlɛ etɛ mi; nɛ oʼɛ, nyumu ko nɛ wo tade klaiklai ba da ye hɛ mi, 31nɛ e ke: ‘Kornelio, a bu o sɔlemi ɔ tue, nɛ o ni kpakpahi nɛ o peɔ ɔ hu a kai ngɛ Mawu hɛ mi. 32Lɔ ɔ he ɔ tsɔ nihi kɛ ya Yopa, nɛ a ya kpee Simon nɛ a tsɛɛ lɛ Petro hulɔ ɔ kɛ ba. E ya to Simon lohwe he womi tsopa wolɔ ɔ nɛ we ngɛ wo ɔ nya a ngɔ.’ 33Kɛkɛ nɛ amlɔ ɔ nɔuu nɛ i tsɔ o ngɔ, nɛ o pee saminya kaa o ba. Lɔ ɔ he ɔ jeha nɛ ɔ wɔ tsuo wa ngɛ hiɛ ɔ ngɛ Mawu hɛ mi, konɛ waa bu nihi tsuo kulaa nɛ Mawu de mo ngɔ to ɔ tue.”
Petro munyu nɛ e tu
34Kɛkɛ nɛ Petro pa e nya mi nɛ e ke: “Niinɛ, i kpa si kaa Mawu pi nimli a hɛ mi hyɛlɔ; 35se mohu ma tsuaa ma mi ɔ, nɔ nɛ yee lɛ gbeye nɛ e tsuɔ dami nihi ɔ, lɛ ji nɔ nɛ saa e hɛ mi. 36Mawu tsɔ nɛ a kɛ munyu ɔ ya ha Israelbi, nɛ a gu Yesu Kristo nɔ kɛ jaje he jɔmi sane kpakpa a ngɔ tsɔɔ mɛ, lɛ ji nihi tsuo a Nyɔmtsɛ. 37Nyɛ nitsɛmɛ nyɛ le sane ɔ nɛ ba ngɛ Yudea tsuo, nɛ e je sisi kɛ je Galilea, ngɛ baptisimi nɛ Yohane fiɛ ɔ se ɔ, 38bɔ nɛ Mawu ngɔ Mumi Klɔuklɔu kɛ he wami ngɔ pɔ Yesu nɛ je Nazaret ɔ nu, nɛ e kpaa si peɔ kpakpa, nɛ e tsaa nihi kulaa nɛ abosiami haoɔ mɛ ɔ, ejakaa Mawu kɛ lɛ ngɛ. 39Nɛ wɔ ji nihi tsuo kulaa nɛ e pee ngɛ Yudafo ɔmɛ a zugba a nɔ kɛ Yerusalem ɔ he odase yeli; nɔ nɛ a sɛu ngɛ tso nɔ nɛ a gbe lɛ ɔ. 40Lɛ nɔuu Mawu tle si ligbi nɛ ji ligbi etɛ ɔ, nɛ e ha e je e he kpo ngɔ tsɔɔ paa, 41tsa pi ma mluku ɔ tsuo, se mohu odase yeli nɛ Mawu hla ngɔ to momo ɔ, nɛ ji wɔ nihi nɛ waa kɛ lɛ ye ni nɛ waa kɛ lɛ nu, benɛ e te si kɛ je gbeje ɔ se ɔ. 42Nɛ e wo wɔ kita ke waa fiɛ ngɔ tsɔɔ ma a nɛ waa ye odase kaa lɛ ji nɔ nɛ Mawu je ngɔ to nɛ e kojo hɛ kali kɛ ni gbogboehi ɔ nɛ. 43Lɛ e he odase gbali ɔmɛ kulaa yeɔ, kaa nɔ tsuaa nɔ nɛ heɔ e nɔ yeɔ ɔ ma na e he yayami pami ngɛ e biɛ ɔ he.”
Majemajeli ɔmɛ na Mumi Klɔuklɔu ɔ
44Benɛ Petro ngɛ kikɛmɛ a munyu nɛ ɔmɛ tue nɔuu ɔ, Mumi Klɔuklɔu ɔ ba nihi tsuo nɛ nu munyu ɔ nɔ. 45Nɛ Yudafohi nɛ he ye nɛ a kɛ Petro ba a nya kpɛ a he kaa a nɛ Mumi Klɔuklɔu nɔke nɔ ɔ ngɔ pue majemajeli ɔmɛ hu a nɔ. 46Ejakaa a nu kaa a ngɛ ma se munyuhi slɔɔtohi tue, nɛ a ngɛ Mawu yi jee. Kɛkɛ nɛ Petro he nɔ ke: 47“Anɛ nɔ ko ma nyɛ nyu nya maa tsi, nɛ a ko baptisi ni nɛ ɔmɛ nɛ na Mumi Klɔuklɔu ɔ ka wɔ kɛ̃ ɔ lo?” 48Nɛ e fa ke a baptisi mɛ ngɛ Nyɔmtsɛ ɔ biɛ ɔ mi. Kɛkɛ nɛ a kpa lɛ pɛɛ ke e kɛ mɛ nɛ hi si be bɔɔ ko.

english_text:
Peter Reports to the Church in Jerusalem
1The apostles and the followers in Judea heard that Gentiles had accepted God's message. 2So when Peter came to Jerusalem, some of the Jewish followers started arguing with him. They wanted Gentile followers to be circumcised, and 3they said, “You stayed in the homes of Gentiles, and you even ate with them!”
4Then Peter told them exactly what had happened:
5I was in the town of Joppa and was praying when I fell sound asleep and had a vision. I saw heaven open, and something like a huge sheet held by its four corners came down to me. 6When I looked in it, I saw animals, wild beasts, reptiles, and birds. 7I heard a voice saying to me, “Peter, get up! Kill these and eat them.”
8But I said, “Lord, I can't do that! I've never taken a bite of anything that is unclean and not fit to eat.”
9The voice from heaven spoke to me again, “When God says that something can be used for food, don't say it isn't fit to eat.” 10This happened three times before it was all taken back into heaven.
11Suddenly three men from Caesarea stood in front of the house where I was staying. 12The Holy Spirit told me to go with them and not to worry. Then six of the Lord's followers went with me to the home of a man 13who told us that an angel had appeared to him. The angel had ordered him to send to Joppa for someone named Simon Peter. 14Then Peter would tell him how he and everyone in his house could be saved.
15After I started speaking, the Holy Spirit was given to them, just as the Spirit had been given to us at the beginning. 16 I remembered that the Lord had said, “John baptized with water, but you will be baptized with the Holy Spirit.” 17God gave those Gentiles the same gift that he gave us when we put our faith in the Lord Jesus Christ. So how could I have gone against God?
18When they heard Peter say this, they stopped arguing and started praising God. They said, “God has now let Gentiles turn to him, and he has given life to them!”
The Church in Antioch
19 Some of the Lord's followers had been scattered because of the terrible trouble that started when Stephen was killed. They went as far as Phoenicia, Cyprus, and Antioch, but they told the message only to the Jews.
20Some of the followers from Cyprus and Cyrene went to Antioch and started telling Gentiles the good news about the Lord Jesus. 21The Lord's power was with them, and many people turned to the Lord and put their faith in him. 22News of what was happening reached the church in Jerusalem. Then they sent Barnabas to Antioch.
23When Barnabas got there and saw how God had blessed them with undeserved grace, he was very glad. So he begged them to remain faithful to the Lord with all their hearts. 24Barnabas was a good man of great faith, and he was filled with the Holy Spirit. Many more people turned to the Lord.
25Barnabas went to Tarsus to look for Saul. 26He found Saul and brought him to Antioch, where they met with the church for a whole year and taught many of its people. There in Antioch the Lord's followers were first called Christians.
27During this time some prophets from Jerusalem came to Antioch. 28 One of them was Agabus. Then with the help of the Spirit, he told that there would be a terrible famine everywhere in the world. And it happened when Claudius was Emperor. 29The followers in Antioch decided to send whatever help they could to the followers in Judea. 30So they appointed Barnabas and Saul to take their gifts to the church leaders in Jerusalem.
translation_text:
Petro amaniɛ nɛ e bɔ Yerusalem asafo ɔ
1Bɔfo ɔmɛ kɛ nyɛmimɛ nɛ ngɛ Yudea a tsuo nu kaa majeli a bimɛ ɔmɛ hu pɛtɛ Mawu munyu ɔ he. 2Nɛ benɛ Petro ba Yerusalem ɔ, nihi nɛ je ninɛmɛ nɛ a po mɛ ɔmɛ a kpɛti ɔ kɛ lɛ na, 3a ke: “O ya mɔmlɔtɔtsɛmɛ a ngɔ nɛ o kɛ mɛ ya ye ni.” 4Se Petro je sisi nɛ e bɔ mɛ amaniɛ ɔ tsuo ke:
5“I ngɛ Yopa ma a mi i ngɛ sɔlee, nɛ e pee kaa nɔ́ nɛ nɔ nɔ ye nɔ, nɛ i na ninami ko kaa nɔ́ ko je hiɔwe kaa bo ngua ko nɛ a hɛɛ e kɔ nya eywiɛ ɔ mi, nɛ a ngɛ siue kɛ ma zugba, nɛ e ba ye ngɔ tataata. 6Se benɛ i hyɛ mi too ɔ, i na zugba lohwe nane eywiɛtsɛmɛ kɛ nga mi lohwehi kɛ waami nihi kɛ hiɔwe lohwe pɛlitsɛmɛ ngɛ mi. 7Nɛ i nu gbi ko hu nɛ de mi ke: ‘Petro, tee si, gbee nɛ o ye!’ 8Se i de ke: ‘Dɛbi, Nyɔmtsɛ, ejakaa i yi yakayaka nɔ́ ko loo nɔ́ ko nɛ he tsɔ we hyɛ.’ 9Se gbi nɛ je hiɔwe ɔ he nɔ nɔ́ nɛ ji si enyɔ ke: ‘Nɔ́ nɛ Mawu tsukɔ he ɔ, mo ko bu lɛ yakayaka nɔ́ ko.’ 10A pee jã si etɛ, nɛ a sa kulaa kɛ ho hiɔwe ya ekohu, 11Jamɛ a be ɔ mi nɔuu ɔ nyumuhi etɛ ba da we he nɛ i ngɛ ɔ agbo ɔ nya; a tsɔ mɛ kɛ je Kaisarea kɛ ba ye ngɔ. 12Nɛ mumi ɔ de mi ke i kɛ mɛ nɛ ya nɛ ma ko to tslee. Nyɛmimɛ ekpa nɛ ɔmɛ hu kɛ mi ya; nɛ wa ya sɛ nyumu ɔ we ɔ mi. 13Nɛ e sɛɛ wɔ bɔ nɛ e na bɔfo ɔ ngɛ e we ɔ mi nɛ e daa si nɛ e de lɛ ke: ‘Tsɔ nihi kɛ ya Yopa nɛ o ya kpee Simon nɛ a tsɛɛ lɛ Petro hulɔ ɔ kɛ ba, 14lɛ e ma de mo munyuhi nɛ a maa gu nɔ kɛ he mo kɛ o we ɔ kulaa yi wami.’ 15Se benɛ i bɔni munyu ɔ tumi ɔ, Mumi Klɔuklɔu ɔ ba ma a nɔ, kaa bɔ nɛ e ba ma wɔ hu wa nɔ kekle ɔ. 16Nɛ i kai Nyɔmtsɛ ɔ munyu ɔ nɛ e tu ke: ‘Yohane ɔ, e kɛ nyu baptisi, se nyɛɛ lɛɛ a maa baptisi nyɛ kɛ Mumi Klɔuklɔu’ ɔ. 17Jeha nɛ ɔ ke Mawu ha mɛ jamɛ a nɔke nɔ́ ɔ nɔuu nɛ e ha wɔ nɛ wa heɔ Nyɔmtsɛ Yesu nɔ yeɔ hulɔ ɔ, imi lɛɛ, mɛnɔ ji mi nɛ ma nyɛ Mawu nya ma tsi?” 18Se benɛ a nu munyu nɛ ɔmɛ ɔ, a ma a nya, nɛ a wo Mawu hɛ mi nyami de ke: ‘Lɛɛ majeli ɔmɛ hu Mawu ha mɛ tsui tsakemi nɛ a kɛ he a yi wami!’
Antiokia asafo ɔ
19Jeha nɛ ɔ nihi nɛ gbɛ fia ngɛ Stefano amanenlu ɔ mi ɔ po mi kɛ ya Foinike kɛ Kipro kɛ Antiokia lokoo, se a fiɛ we munyu ɔ ngɔ tsɔɔ we nɔ ko nɔ ko kaa ja Yudafo ɔmɛ kɛkɛ. 20Se a ti ni komɛ ɔ, Kiprobihi kɛ Kireenebihi ji mɛ, nɛ ni nɛ ɔmɛ ba Antiokia ba tu munyu tsɔɔ Helabi ɔmɛ hulɔ, nɛ a fiɛ Nyɔmtsɛ Yesu he sane kpakpa a ngɔ tsɔɔ mɛ. 21Nɛ Nyɔmtsɛ ɔ piɛ a he, nɛ nihi babauu he ye, nɛ a tsake kɛ ba Nyɔmtsɛ ɔ ngɔ.
22Nɛ a he sane nɛ ɔ ba su Yerusalem asafo ɔ tue mi, nɛ a tsɔ Barnaba Antiokia. 23Nɛ benɛ e su lejɛ ɔ nɛ e ba na Mawu dloomi ɔ, e bua jɔ e he, nɛ e tu munyu tsɔɔ mɛ tsuo ke a kɛ tsui nɛ fi si nɛ pɛtɛ Nyɔmtsɛ ɔ he. 24Nɔmlɔ kpakpa ji lɛ nɛ e hyi tɔ kɛ Mumi Klɔuklɔu kɛ hemi kɛ yemi. Nɛ a ngɔ nihi babauu kɛ ba Nyɔmtsɛ ɔ ngɔ.
25Nɛ Barnaba pue nɔ kɛ ho Tarso ya ya hla Saulo, nɛ benɛ e na lɛ ɔ, e kɛ lɛ ba Antiokia ekohu. 26Nɛ e ba mi kaa a kɛ asafo ɔ hi si jeha mluku, nɛ a tsɔɔ nihi babauu ni, nɛ Antiokia ji he nɛ a wo kaseli ɔmɛ biɛ kekleekle ngɛ ke Kristofohi.
27Se kikɛmɛ a be nɛ ɔmɛ a mi ɔ, gbali komɛ je Yerusalem kɛ ba Antiokia. 28Nɛ a kpɛti nɔ ko nɛ a tsɛɛ lɛ Agabo ɔ te si, nɛ e tsɔɔ ngɛ Mumi ɔ nya kaa hwɔ kpetekpleenyɛ maa ba je mi tsuo kulaa, nɛ e ba mi ja ngɛ Kaisare Klaudio yi nɔ. 29Kaseli ɔmɛ kpɛ mi kaa a ma tsu nɔ́ ko ngɔ mane nyɛmimɛ nɛ ngɛ Yudea a nɛ a kɛ ya pɛne mɛ, nɔ tsuaa nɔ bɔ nɛ o ma nyɛ. 30Nɛ a pee ja, nɛ a ngɔ mane nikɔtɔma amɛ kɛ gu Barnaba kɛ Saulo nɔ.

english_text:
Herod Causes Trouble for the Church
1At that time King Herod caused terrible suffering for some members of the church. 2He ordered soldiers to cut off the head of James, the brother of John. 3 When Herod saw that this pleased the Jewish people, he had Peter arrested during the Festival of Thin Bread. 4He put Peter in jail and ordered four squads of soldiers to guard him. Herod planned to put him on trial in public after the festival.
5While Peter was being kept in jail, the church never stopped praying to God for him.
Peter Is Rescued
6The night before Peter was to be put on trial, he was asleep and bound by two chains. A soldier was guarding him on each side, and two other soldiers were guarding the entrance to the jail. 7Suddenly an angel from the Lord appeared, and light flashed around in the cell. The angel poked Peter in the side and woke him up. Then he said, “Quick! Get up!”
The chains fell off his hands, 8and the angel said, “Get dressed and put on your sandals.” Peter did what he was told. Then the angel said, “Now put on your coat and follow me.” 9Peter left with the angel, but he thought everything was only a dream. 10They went past the two groups of soldiers, and when they came to the iron gate to the city, it opened by itself. They went out and were going along the street, when all at once the angel disappeared.
11Peter now realized what had happened, and he said, “I am certain that the Lord sent his angel to rescue me from Herod and from everything the Jewish leaders planned to do to me.” 12Then Peter went to the house of Mary the mother of John whose other name was Mark. Many of the Lord's followers had come together there and were praying.
13Peter knocked on the gate, and a servant named Rhoda came to answer. 14When she heard Peter's voice, she was too excited to open the gate. She ran back into the house and said Peter was standing there.
15“You are crazy!” everyone told her. But she kept saying it was Peter. Then they said, “It must be his angel.” 16But Peter kept on knocking, until finally they opened the gate. They saw him and were completely amazed.
17Peter motioned for them to keep quiet. Then he told how the Lord had led him out of jail. He also said, “Tell James and the others what has happened.” After that, he left and went somewhere else.
18The next morning the soldiers who had been on guard were terribly worried and wondered what had happened to Peter. 19Herod ordered his own soldiers to search for him, but they could not find him. Then he questioned the guards and had them put to death. After this, Herod left Judea to stay in Caesarea for a while.
Herod Dies
20 Herod and the people of Tyre and Sidon were very angry with each other. But their country got its food supply from the region that he ruled. So a group of them went to see Blastus, who was one of Herod's high officials. They convinced Blastus that they wanted to make peace between their cities and Herod, 21and a day was set for them to meet with him.
Herod came dressed in his royal robes. He sat down on his throne and made a speech. 22The people shouted, “You speak more like a god than a man!” 23At once an angel from the Lord struck him down because he took the honor that belonged to God. Later, Herod was eaten by worms and died.
24God's message kept spreading. 25And after Barnabas and Saul had done the work they were sent to do, they went back to Jerusalem with John, whose other name was Mark.
translation_text:
A wa asafo ɔ yi mi babauu
1Jamɛ a be ɔ mi nɔuu ɔ, matsɛ Herode wo e nine nɔ, konɛ e pee asafo ɔ mi bi ɔmɛ a ti ni komɛ yayami. 2E kɛ klaate gbe Yohane nyɛmi Yakobo. 3Nɛ benɛ e na kaa e ngɔ Yudafo ɔmɛ a nya a, e ya nɔ nɛ e nu Petro hulɔ. Se akpiti ligbi ɔmɛ a mi ʼi. 4Nɛ benɛ e nu lɛ ɔ, e wo lɛ tsu mi, nɛ e tu lɛ ngɔ wo aslaafohi eywiɛeywiɛ kuhi eywiɛ dɛ mi nɛ a bu e he. E susu kaa Hetsɔmi ɔ se ɔ e kɛ lɛ maa ba ma a hɛ mi. 5Lɔ ɔ he ɔ a tsi Petro nya ngɛ tsu ɔ mi mohu, se asafo ɔ hɛɛ sɔlemi mi kɛ ha lɛ wawɛɛ ngɛ Mawu hɛ mi.
A je Petro ngɛ tsu mi
6Se benɛ Herode ke e kɛ lɛ maa ba ma a hɛ mi ɔ, jamɛ a nyɔ ɔ mi ɔ, Petro hwɔɔ si ngɛ aslaafohi enyɔ a kpɛti, nɛ a wo lɛ kɔsɔkɔsɔhi enyɔ, nɛ buli hu daa si ngɛ sinya a nya ngɛ tsu ɔ he bue. 7Nɛ oʼɛ, Nyɔmtsɛ ɔ bɔfo ko ba da e kasa nya, nɛ la kpɛ ngɛ tsu ɔ mi. Bɔfo ɔ gba Petro kasa ma nɛ e tsɛ̃ɛ lɛ ke: “Tee si esɔesɔ!” Nɛ e kɔsɔkɔsɔ ɔmɛ kplɔ ngɛ e nine. 8Kɛkɛ nɛ bɔfo ɔ de lɛ ke: “Mia nɛ o fi o tokota amɛ!” Nɛ Petro pee ja. Nɛ e de lɛ ke: “Haa o bo ɔ nɛ o nyɛɛ ye se!” 9Nɛ Petro nyɛɛ e se kɛ je kpo, se e li kaa nɔ́ nɛ bɔfo ɔ ngɛ pee ɔ ngɛ mi, se e pee lɛ kaa e ngɛ ni nae. 10Se benɛ a be kekle buli ɔmɛ kɛ nihi nɛ ji enyɔ ɔmɛ a he ɔ, a su dade agbo nɛ ngɛ kɛ yaa ma a mi ɔ he nɛ lɛ nitse e bli ha mɛ, nɛ a je kpo kɛ po gbɛjegbɛ kake mi, kɛkɛ nɛ bɔfo ɔ si lɛ.
11Benɛ Petro hɛ mi tsɔ lɛ ɔ, e ke: “Kpaako i na le tutuutu kaa Nyɔmtsɛ ɔ tsɔ e bɔfo kɛ ba nɛ e ba je mi ngɛ Herode dɛ mi kɛ nɔ́ nɛ Yudafo ɔmɛ a ma a ngɛ blɔ hyɛe ɔ kulaa mi.”
12Nɛ benɛ e yo enɛ ɔ ɔ, e ba Yohane nɛ a tsɛɛ lɛ Marko hulɔ ɔ nyɛ Maria we ɔ mi, he nɛ nihi fuu ba bua a he nya ngɛ nɛ a ngɛ sɔlee ɔ. 13Se benɛ Petro si agbo ɔ, yiheyo ko nɛ a tsɛɛ lɛ Rode ɔ ba tue bumi. 14Benɛ e yo Petro gbi ɔ, bua jɔmi sɔuu nya a, e bli we agbo ɔ, se mohu e tu fo kɛ ho ya de ke Petro daa si ngɛ agbo ɔ se. 15Se a de lɛ ke: “O nu godo.” Se e ma nɔ mi ke e ngɛ mi ja. Kɛkɛ nɛ a ke: “Lɛɛ e dbɔfo ʼi.” 16Se Petro ngɛ nɔ ngɛ sie, nɛ benɛ a bli ɔ, a na lɛ, nɛ a nya kpɛ a he. 17Se e wo mɛ nine ke a pee kɔ, nɛ e bɔ mɛ bɔ nɛ pee nɛ Nyɔmtsɛ ɔ je lɛ ngɛ tsu ɔ mi ɔ; nɛ e ke: “Nyɛɛ ya nɛ nyɛ ya sɛɛ kikɛmɛ a ni nɛ ɔmɛ ngɔ ha Yakobo kɛ nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ.” Nɛ e je lejɛ ɔ kɛ ho he kpa ya.
18Benɛ je na a, pi haomi bi nɛ ba aslaafo ɔmɛ a kpɛti akɛnɛ a li nɔ́ nɛ ba Petro nɔ ɔ. 19Se benɛ Herode hla lɛ nɛ e nɛ́ lɛ ɔ, e kojo buli ɔmɛ nɛ e fa ke a gbe mɛ. Nɛ Herode si Yudea kɛ ho Kaisarea ya nɛ e ya hi lejɛ ɔ.
Herode gbenɔ
20Jeha nɛ ɔ Herode muklii mi fu Tirobi ɔmɛ kɛ Zidonbi ɔmɛ wawɛɛ; nɛ a kɛ juɛmi kake ba e ngɔ. A ba hla matsɛ ɔ sɔmɔlɔ Blasto ɔ he blɔ nɛ a ba kpa pɛɛ, ejakaa matsɛ ɔ zugba nɔ ni a yeɔ.
21Se ligbi nɛ a to ko nɔ ɔ, Herode wo e matsɛ tade ɔ, nɛ e ya hi kojomi sɛ ɔ nɔ, nɛ e kɛ mɛ tu munyu. 22Nɛ ni ɔmɛ kpa ngmlaa ke: “Mawu gbi ji nɛ ɔ nɛ, se tsa pi nɔmlɔ gbi ʼi.” 23Nɛ amlɔ ɔ nɔuu ɔ, Nyɔmtsɛ ɔ bɔfo fia lɛ nɔ, ejakaa e kɛ nyami ɔ ha we Mawu, nɛ e wo gɔgɔ, nɛ e gbo.
24Se Mawu munyu ɔ keke nɛ e gbɛ fia.
25Benɛ Barnaba kɛ Saulo gbe a sɔmɔmi ɔ nya a, a kpale a se kɛ je Yerusalem, nɛ a ngɔ Yohane, nɔ nɛ a tsɛɛ lɛ Marko hulɔ ɔ ngɔ piɛ a he.

english_text:
Barnabas and Saul Are Chosen and Sent
1The church at Antioch had several prophets and teachers. They were Barnabas, Simeon, also called Niger, Lucius from Cyrene, Manaen, who was Herod's close friend, and Saul. 2While they were worshiping the Lord and going without eating, the Holy Spirit told them, “Appoint Barnabas and Saul to do the work for which I have chosen them.” 3Everyone prayed and went without eating for a while longer. Next, they placed their hands on Barnabas and Saul to show that they had been appointed to do this work. Then everyone sent them on their way.
Barnabas and Saul in Cyprus
4After Barnabas and Saul had been sent by the Holy Spirit, they went to Seleucia. From there they sailed to the island of Cyprus. 5They arrived at Salamis and began to preach God's message in the synagogues. They also had John as a helper.
6Barnabas and Saul went all the way to the city of Paphos on the other end of the island, where they met a Jewish man named Bar-Jesus. He practiced witchcraft and was a false prophet. 7He also worked for Sergius Paulus, who was very smart and was the governor of the island. Sergius Paulus wanted to hear God's message, and he sent for Barnabas and Saul. 8But Bar-Jesus, whose other name was Elymas, was against them. He even tried to keep the governor from having faith in the Lord.
9Then Saul, better known as Paul, was filled with the Holy Spirit. He looked straight at Elymas 10and said, “You son of the devil! You are a liar, a crook, and an enemy of everything that is right. When will you stop speaking against the true ways of the Lord? 11The Lord is going to punish you by making you completely blind for a while.”
Suddenly the man's eyes were covered by a dark mist, and he went around trying to get someone to lead him by the hand. 12When the governor saw what had happened, he was amazed at this teaching about the Lord. So he put his faith in the Lord.
Paul and Barnabas in Antioch of Pisidia
13Paul and the others left Paphos and sailed to Perga in Pamphylia. But John left them and went back to Jerusalem. 14The rest of them went on from Perga to Antioch in Pisidia. Then on the Sabbath they went to the synagogue and sat down.
15After the reading of the Law and the Prophets, the leaders sent someone over to tell Paul and Barnabas, “Friends, if you have anything to say that will help the people, please say it.”
16Paul got up. He motioned with his hand and said:
People of Israel, and everyone else who worships God, listen! 17 The God of Israel chose our ancestors, and he let our people prosper while they were living in Egypt. Then with his mighty power he led them out, 18 and for about 40 years he took care of them in the desert. 19 He destroyed seven nations in the land of Canaan and gave their land to our people. 20 All this happened in about 450 years.
Then God gave our people judges until the time of the prophet Samuel, 21 but the people demanded a king. So for 40 years God gave them King Saul, the son of Kish from the tribe of Benjamin. 22 Later, God removed Saul and let David rule in his place. God said about him, “David the son of Jesse is the kind of person who pleases me most! He does everything I want him to do.”
23God promised that someone from David's family would come to save the people of Israel, and this one is Jesus. 24 But before Jesus came, John was telling everyone in Israel to turn back to God and be baptized. 25 Then, when John's work was almost done, he said, “Who do you people think I am? Do you think I am the Promised One? He will come later, and I am not good enough to untie his sandals.”
26Now listen, you descendants of Abraham! Pay attention, all of you Gentiles who are here to worship God! Listen to this message about how to be saved, because it is for everyone. 27The people of Jerusalem and their leaders didn't realize who Jesus was. And they didn't understand the words of the prophets they read each Sabbath. So they condemned Jesus just as the prophets had said.
28-29 They did exactly what the Scriptures said they would. Even though they couldn't find any reason to put Jesus to death, they still asked Pilate to have him killed.
After Jesus had been put to death, he was taken down from the cross and placed in a tomb. 30But God raised him from death! 31 Then for many days Jesus appeared to his followers who had gone with him from Galilee to Jerusalem. Now they are telling our people about him.
32God made a promise to our ancestors. And we are here to tell you the good news 33 that he has kept this promise to us. It is just as the second Psalm says about Jesus,
“You are my son because today
I have become your Father.”
34 God raised Jesus from death and will never let his body decay. It is just as God said,
“I will make to you
the same holy promises
that I made to David.”
35 And in another psalm it says, “God will never let the body of his Holy One decay.”
36When David was alive, he obeyed God. Then after he died, he was buried in the family grave, and his body decayed. 37But God raised Jesus from death, and his body did not decay.
38My friends, the message is that Jesus can forgive your sins! The Law of Moses could not set you free from all your sins. 39But everyone who has faith in Jesus is set free. 40Make sure what the prophets have said doesn't happen to you. They said,
41 “Look, you people
who make fun of God!
Be amazed
and disappear.
I will do something today
that you won't believe,
even if someone
tells you about it!”
42As Paul and Barnabas were leaving the synagogue, the people begged them to say more about these same things on the next Sabbath. 43After the service, many Jews and a lot of Gentiles who worshiped God went with them. Paul and Barnabas begged them all to remain faithful to God, who had treated them with undeserved grace.
44The next Sabbath almost everyone in town came to hear the message about the Lord. 45When the Jewish people saw the crowds, they were very jealous. They insulted Paul and spoke against everything he said.
46But Paul and Barnabas bravely said:
We had to tell God's message to you before we told it to anyone else. But you rejected the message! This proves that you don't deserve eternal life. Now we are going to the Gentiles. 47 The Lord has given us this command,
“I have placed you here
as a light
for the Gentiles.
You are to take
the saving power of God
to people everywhere on earth.”
48This message made the Gentiles glad, and they praised what they had heard about the Lord. Everyone who had been chosen for eternal life then put their faith in the Lord.
49The message about the Lord spread all over this region. 50But the Jewish leaders went to some of the important men in the town and to some respected women who were religious. They turned them against Paul and Barnabas and started making trouble for them. They even chased them out of this part of the country.
51 Paul and Barnabas shook the dust from that place off their feet and went on to the city of Iconium.
52But the Lord's followers in Antioch were very happy and were filled with the Holy Spirit.
translation_text:
A hla Saulo kɛ Barnaba nɛ a tsɔ mɛ
1Gbali kɛ tsɔɔli komɛ ngɛ Antiokia asafo ɔ mi, mɛ ji Barnaba kɛ Simeon, nɔ nɛ a tsɛɛ lɛ Niger ɔ, kɛ Lukio Kireene no ɔ, kɛ Manahen, nɔ nɛ a lɛ lɛ kɛ amlalo Herode ɔ, kɛ Saulo. 2Benɛ a ngɛ Nyɔmtsɛ ɔ jae nɛ a ngɛ hwɔ hae ɔ. Mumi Klɔuklɔu ɔ ke: “Nyɛ je Barnaba kɛ Saulo ngɔ ha mi kɛ ha ni tsumi nɛ i tsɛ mɛ ngɛ he ɔ.” 3Kɛkɛ nɛ a ha hwɔ nɛ a sɔle, nɛ a kɛ a ninehi pue a nɔ nɛ a wo mɛ blɔ.
Saulo kɛ Barnaba ngɛ Kipro
4Jeha nɛ ɔ ni nɛ ɔmɛ ɔ, akɛnɛ Mumi Klɔuklɔu ɔ tsɔ mɛ ke a ya he je ɔ, a pue nɔ kɛ ho Seleukia ya, nɛ a sɛ lɛ mi ngɛ lejɛ ɔ, nɛ a hia kɛ ho Kipro ya. 5Benɛ a su Salami ɔ, a fiɛ Mawu munyu ɔ ngɛ Yudafo ɔmɛ a kpe he ɔmɛ. Nɛ a kɛ Yohane hu nyɛɛ kaa a sɔmɔlɔ.
6Nɛ benɛ a po mi ngɛ zugba kpɔ nɛ nyu bɔle lɛ ɔ nɔ kɛ ba su Pafo ɔ, a na Yuda no kunya yelɔ kɛ lakpa gbalɔ ko nɛ a tsɛɛ lɛ Bar-yesu ɔ, 7nɔ nɛ ngɛ amlaalo Sergio Paulo ngɔ lɛ be ɔ mi ɔ. Sergio Paulo ji nyumu hɛ si kalɔ ko; lɛ nɛ e tsɛ Barnaba kɛ Saulo kɛ ba e ngɔ, nɛ e ngɛ hlae nɛ e bu Mawu munyu ɔ tue. 8Se Elima, kunya yelɔ ɔ (ja ji e biɛ ɔ sisi ngɛ Hela gbi mi) ka nɛ e tsi a nya, nɛ e ngɛ hlae nɛ e kpale amlaalo ɔ kɛ je hemi kɛ yemi ɔ he. 9Nɛ Saulo, nɔ nɛ a tsɛɛ lɛ Paulo hulɔ, nɛ Mumi Klɔuklɔu hyi lɛ tɔtɔɔtɔ ɔ, hyɛ lɛ too, 10nɛ e ke: “Oo, abosiami bi nɛ sisimi kɛ kutupɔ tsuo hyi mo tɔtɔɔtɔ, mo dami kulaa henyɛlɔ; anɛ o be Nyɔmtsɛ ɔ blɔ tlɔmɔɔ ɔmɛ a kpemi jɔɔe? 11nɛ jeha nɛ ɔ oʼɛ, Nyɔmtsɛ ɔ nine fɔɔ si ngɛ o nɔ, nɛ o hɛ ma yu, nɛ o be pu hyɛe kɛ yaa su be ko.” Nɛ amlɔ ɔ nɔuu ɔ afua kɛ diblii wo lɛ, nɛ e lilaa si ngɛ nihi hlae nɛ a ta e dɛ mi nɛ a ya je lɛ blɔ. 12Kɛkɛ nɛ amlaalo ɔ, benɛ e na nɔ́ nɛ a pee ɔ, e he ye, nɛ e he nya si lɛ ngɛ Nyɔmtsɛ ɔ tsɔɔmi ɔ he.
Paulo ba Antiokia nɛ ngɛ Pisidia a
13Benɛ Paulo kɛ e nimli ɔmɛ hia kɛ je Pafo ɔ, a ba Perge ngɛ Pamfilia; nɛ Yohane kpale ngɛ a se, snɛ e kpale e se kɛ ho Yerusalem ya ekohu. 14Se mɛɛ lɛɛ a je Perge nɛ a po mi kɛ ba Antiokia ngɛ Pisidia. A ya kpe he ɔ ngɛ Hejɔɔmi Ligbi ɔ nɔ nɛ a ya hi si. 15Nɛ benɛ a kane a Mlaa a kɛ gbali ɔmɛ a womi ɔ se ɔ, kpe he ɔ nikɔtɔma amɛ tsɔ ba de mɛ ke: “Tsaatsɛmɛ kɛ mamimɛ, ke nyɛ ngɛ munyu kɛ tsɔɔmi ko nɛ nyɛ maa tu ngɔ tsɔɔ ni ɔmɛ ɔ, nyɛɛ tu.” 16Kɛkɛ nɛ Paulo te si da si, nɛ e fɔ e nine nɛ e ke:
“Tsaatsɛmɛ Israel nyumuhi kɛ nyɛ nihi nɛ nyɛ yee Mawu gbeye, nyɛɛ bu tue! 17Kikɛmɛ a Israel ma nɛ ɔ Mawu lɛ hla wa tsɛmɛ ɔmɛ, nɛ benɛ a ya to nibwɔ ngɛ Mizraim zugba a nɔ ɔ, e wo ma a nɔ, nɛ e kɛ e nine nɛ e wo nɔ ɔ je mɛ kɛ je lejɛ ɔ. 18E hɛɛ mɛ nɛ e lɛ mɛ ngɛ nga a nɔ maa pee jeha nyingmi eywiɛ, 19nɛ e kpata majemaje ma kpaago hɛ mi ngɛ Kanaan zugba a nɔ, nɛ ye dla a zugba a mi ngɔ ha mɛ, konɛ e plɛ a nɔ. 20Nɛ lɔ ɔ se maa pee jeha lafa eywiɛ kɛ nyingmi enuɔ ɔ, e ha mɛ kojoli kɛ ba su gbalɔ Samuel nɔ. 21Nɛ kɔlɔ ɔ se ɔ a bi matsɛ, nɛ Mawu ngɔ Kish bi Saul, nyumu ko nɛ je Benyamin wetso ɔ mi ɔ ha mɛ jeha nyingmi eywiɛ. 22Nɛ benɛ e kpa lɛ ɔ, e wo David nɔ, nɛ e wo lɛ a nɔ matsɛ, nɔ nɛ he odase nɛ e ye ke: ‘I na David, Ishai bi ɔ, nyumu nɛ i ngɛ e he tsui, nɔ nɛ maa pee ye suɔmi nya ni ɔmɛ kulaa.’ 23Nɔ nɛ ɔ nina mi Mawu je Yesu kɛ je, dngɛ si womi ɔ nya, nɛ e kɛ lɛ pee Israel yi wami helɔ. 24Yohane sɛ hlami ba fiɛ baptisimi nɛ a kɛ naa tsui tsakemi ngɔ tsɔɔ Israel ma mluku ɔ tsuo kulaa. 25Nɛ loko Yohane maa gbe e nitsumi ɔ nya a, e ke: ‘Mɛnɔ nyɛ susuu kaa i ji? Tsa pi imi ji nɔ nɛ blɔ nɛ nyɛ ngɛ hyɛe ɔ. Se oʼɛ, nɔ ko ma ngɛ ye se, nɛ i sɛ́ nɔ nɛ pɛneɔ e tokota ngɛ e nane.’
26“Tsaatsɛmɛ kɛ mamimɛ, Abraham nina kɛ nyɛ kpɛti nihi nɛ yee Mawu gbeye, nyɛ a kɛ kikɛmɛ a yi wami hemi muyu nɛ ɔ ba ha. 27Ejakaa nihi nɛ ngɛ Yerusalem ɔ kɛ a ma a mi nikɔtɔma amɛ ɔ, akɛnɛ a li Yesu, nɛ jeha nɛ ɔ hu anui gbali ɔmɛ a munyu nɛ a kaneɔ daa Hejɔɔmi Ligbi ɔ nɛ ɔ he je ɔ, a bu lɛ fɔ nɛ lɔ ɔ ha gbali ɔmɛ a gbami ɔmɛ ba mi. 28Nɛ pohu a nɛ́ gbenɔ sane ko ngɛ e he mohu, se kɛ ɔ a kpa Pilato pɛɛ ke e gbe lɛ. 29Nɛ benɛ a ha nihi kulaa nɛ a ngma ngɛ e he ɔ ba mi ɔ, a je lɛ ngɛ tso ɔ nɔ, nɛ a ya to lɛ ngɛ yɔkɔ ko mi. 30Se Mawu tle lɛ si kɛ je gbeje; 31nɛ e je e he kpo ligbihi fuu kɛ tsɔɔ nihi nɛ kɛ lɛ je Galilea kɛ ba Yerusalem ɔ, nihi nɛ ji e odase yeli ha ma a. 32Nɛ wɔɔ lɛɛ, si nɛ e wo wa tsɛmɛ ɔmɛ ɔ he sane kpakpa a wa ngɛ fiɛe kɛ ngɛ tsɔɔe nɛ ɔ nɛ, 33kaa kɔlɔ ɔ nɔuu Mawu ha e ba mi ha wɔ nɛ wa ji a bimɛ ɔ, kaa nɛ e tle Yesu si kaa bɔ nɛ a ngma ngɛ La nɛ ji enyɔ ɔ mi hu ke: ‘Ye bi ji mo, mwɔnɛ i fɔ mo’ ɔ.
34“Se akɛnɛ e tle lɛ si kɛ je gbeje nɛ e be e se kpalee kɛ ya puɛmi mi hu he je ɔ, e de kikɛ:
‘Ma ngɔ David dloomi nihi nɛ maa si kpɛii ɔ ngɔ ha nyɛ.’ 35Lɔ ɔ he hu nɛ e de ngɛ he kpa ke:
‘O be hae nɛ o nɔ klɔuklɔu ɔ nɛ na puɛmi’ ɔ nɛ.
36Ejakaa David ɔ, benɛ e tsu Mawu yi mi tomi nya ni ngɛ e yi nɔ ɔ, e gbo nɛ a ngɔ lɛ ngɔ piɛ e tsɛmɛ ɔmɛ a he nɛ e puɛ. 37Se nɔ nɛ Mawu tle lɛ si ɔ puɛ we. 38Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, tsaatsɛmɛ kɛ mamimɛ, nyɛ na nɛ nyɛɛ le kaa nɔ nɛ ɔ nɔuu nɔ a guu kɛ jajeɔ yayamipami ngɔ tsɔɔ nyɛ ɔ nɛ; ejakaa nihi kulaa nɛ a be nyɛ nguɔ nyɛe maa wo ngɛ he ngɛ Mose Mlaa a nya a, 39nɔ nɛ ɔ mi ɔ, nɔ tsuaa nɔ nɛ heɔ yeɔ ɔ, a woɔ lɛ nguɔ. 40Lɔ ɔ he ɔ nyɛɛ hyɛ nɛ hi, konɛ bɔ nɛ gbali ɔmɛ de ɔ ko ba nyɛ nɔ ke:
41‘Nyɛ he guɛ gbeli, nyɛɛ hyɛ nɛ nyɛ hɛ mi nɛ pee nyɛ
yaa, nɛ nyɛɛ laa;
Ejakaa ma tsu ni tsumi ko ngɛ nyɛ yi nɔ,
Ni tsumi ko nɛ ke nɔ ko sɛɛ ha nyɛ tete po ɔ,
Nyɛ be hee maa ye kɔkɔɔkɔ.’ ”
42Se benɛ Paulomɛ je Yudafo ɔmɛ a kpe he ɔ, majeli ɔmɛ kpa mɛ pɛɛ ke a ba jaje kikɛmɛ a munyu nɛ ɔmɛ ngɔ tsɔɔ mɛ ekohu ngɛ Hejɔɔmi Ligbi nɛ ma a nɔ. 43Se benɛ nihi nɛ ngɛ kpe he ɔ kpa a, Yudafohi kɛ nihi nɛ a tsake mɛ ngɔ pee Yudafohi nɛ a yee Mawu gbeye ɔmɛ a ti nihi fuu nyɛɛ Paulo kɛ Barnaba se, nɛ a tu munyu tsɔɔ mɛ nɛ a wo mɛ ga ke a pɛtɛ Mawu dloomi ɔ he.
44Nɛ Hejɔɔmi Ligbi nɛ nyɛɛ se ɔ nɔ ɔ, e piɛ bɔɔ nɛ ma mluku ɔ kulaa ba bua a he nya nɛ a ba bu Mawu munyu ɔ tue. 45Se benɛ Yudafo ɔmɛ na asafo ɔmɛ ɔ, hunga jemi babauu te si ngɛ a mi, nɛ a kɛ munyu tumi-kɛ-simi kɛ musu bɔmi munyu ku nihi nɛ Paulo ngɛ dee ɔ nya. 46Nɛ Paulo kɛ Barnaba tu munyu kɛ kã ke: “Nyɛ kekle e sa kaa a jajeɔ Mawu munyu ɔ ngɔ tsɔɔ, se akɛnɛ nyɛ kua munyu ɔ nɛ nyɛ bui nyɛ he kaa nyɛ sa neneene wami ɔ he je ɔ, oʼɛ, wa dɔ wa yi kɛ yaa majeli ɔmɛ a ngɔ. 47Ejakaa jã Nyɔmtsɛ ɔ wo wɔ kita ke:
‘I ngɔ mo ngɔ to kaa majeli ɔmɛ a la,
Konɛ o plɛ yi wami hemi kɛ ya su zugba a nyagbe he ɔmɛ.”
48Benɛ majeli ɔmɛ nu e nɛ ɔ ɔ, a na bua jɔmi, nɛ a wo Nyɔmtsɛ ɔ hɛ mi nyami, nɛ nihi abɔ nɛ a je ngɔ to neneene wami ɔ he ye.
49Nɛ Nyɔmtsɛ ɔ munyu ɔ gbɛ fia ngɛ lejɛ ɔ ni ɔmɛ a mi tsuo. 50Se Yudafo ɔmɛ wo yihi Mawu gbeye yeli nɛ a buu mɛ ɔ kɛ ma a mi nihi nɛ hɛ mi ka si ɔmɛ a yi mi, nɛ a ha yi mi wami te si ngɔ wo Paulo kɛ Barnaba, nɛ a fie mɛ kɛ je a kpo ɔmɛ a mi. 51Se mɛɛ lɛɛ a blɛ a nane he bunyuku ngɔ pue a nɔ, nɛ a pue nɔ kɛ ho Ikoniom ya. 52Nɛ kaseli ɔmɛ hyi tɔtɔɔtɔ kɛ bua jɔmi kɛ Mumi Klɔuklɔu.

english_text:
Paul and Barnabas in Iconium
1Paul and Barnabas spoke in the synagogue in Iconium, just as they had done at Antioch, and many Jews and Gentiles put their faith in the Lord. 2But the Jews who did not have faith in him made the other Gentiles angry and turned them against the Lord's followers.
3Paul and Barnabas stayed there for a while, having faith in the Lord and bravely speaking his message. The Lord gave them the power to work miracles and wonders, and he showed that their message about his gift of undeserved grace was true.
4The people of Iconium did not know what to think. Some of them believed the Jewish group, and others believed the apostles. 5Finally, some Gentiles and Jews, together with their leaders, decided to make trouble for Paul and Barnabas and to stone them to death.
6-7But when the two apostles found out what was happening, they escaped to the region of Lycaonia. They preached the good news there in the towns of Lystra and Derbe and in the nearby countryside.
Paul and Barnabas in Lystra
8In Lystra there was a man who had been born with paralyzed feet and had never been able to walk. 9The man was listening to Paul speak, when Paul saw that he had faith in Jesus and could be healed. So he looked straight at the man 10and shouted, “Stand up!” The man jumped up and started walking around.
11When the crowd saw what Paul had done, they yelled out in the language of Lycaonia, “The gods have turned into humans and have come down to us!” 12The people then gave Barnabas the name Zeus, and they gave Paul the name Hermes, because he did the talking.
13The temple of Zeus was near the entrance to the city. Its priest and the crowds wanted to offer a sacrifice to Barnabas and Paul. So the priest brought some bulls and flowers to the city gates. 14When the two apostles found out about this, they tore their clothes in horror and ran to the crowd, shouting:
15 Why are you doing this? We are humans just like you. Please give up all this foolishness. Turn to the living God, who made the sky, the earth, the sea, and everything in them. 16In times past, God let each nation go its own way. 17But he showed he was there by the good things he did. God sends rain from heaven and makes your crops grow. He gives food to you and makes your hearts glad.
18Even after Paul and Barnabas had said all this, they could hardly keep the people from offering a sacrifice to them.
19Some Jewish leaders from Antioch and Iconium came and turned the crowds against Paul. They hit him with stones and dragged him out of the city, thinking he was dead. 20But when the Lord's followers gathered around Paul, he stood up and went back into the city. The next day he and Barnabas went to Derbe.
Paul and Barnabas Return to Antioch in Syria
21Paul and Barnabas preached the good news in Derbe and won some people to the Lord. Then they went back to Lystra, Iconium, and Antioch in Pisidia. 22They encouraged the followers and begged them to remain faithful. They told them, “We have to suffer a lot before we can get into God's kingdom.” 23Paul and Barnabas chose some leaders for each of the churches. Then they went without eating and prayed that the Lord would take good care of these leaders who had trusted in the Lord.
24Paul and Barnabas went on through Pisidia to Pamphylia, 25where they preached in the town of Perga. Then they went down to Attalia 26and sailed to Antioch in Syria. It was there that they had been placed in God's care for the work they had now completed.
27After arriving in Antioch, they called the church together. They told the people what God had helped them do and how he had made it possible for the Gentiles to believe. 28Then they stayed there with the followers for a long time.
translation_text:
Paulo kɛ Barnaba ngɛ Ikoniom
1E ba mi kaa benɛ a ngɛ Ikoniom ɔ, Paulo kɛ Barnaba ya Yudafo ɔmɛ a kpe he ɔ nɛ a ya tu munyu tsɔɔ mɛ saminya, nɛ Yudafo ɔmɛ kɛ Helabi ɔmɛ a ti nihi babauu he ye. 2Se Yudafohi tue gboli ɔmɛ puɛ majeli ɔmɛ a tue, nɛ a ha a plɛ a hɛ mi ngɔ wo nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ. 3Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, a se kɛ ngɛ lejɛ ɔ nɛ a kɛ kã tu Nyɔmtsɛ ɔ he munyu, nɛ lɛ hu e ye e dloomi munyu ɔ he odase nɛ e ha a gu a nine nɔ pee okadihi kɛ nyakpɛ nihi fuu. 4Se ma a mi bi ɔmɛ a mi gba enyɔ: Fã piɛ Yudafo ɔmɛ a he, nɛ fã hu piɛ bɔfo ɔmɛ a he.
5Se benɛ majeli ɔmɛ kɛ Yudafo ɔmɛ kɛ a nikɔtɔma amɛ bu kɛ ba nɛ a ba pee mɛ hãihãi nɛ a fia mɛ tɛ ɔ; 6a na le, nɛ a tu fo kɛ ho Likaonia mahi nɛ ji Listra kɛ Derbe kɛ lejɛ ɔ ni ɔmɛ a mi ya, 7nɛ a ya fiɛ Sane Kpakpa a tsɔɔ mɛ ngɛ lejɛ ɔ hulɔ.
Paulo kɛ Barnaba ngɛ Listra
8Nyumu ko ngɛ Listra nɛ e nyɛ we si nɛ e da, se si e hii nɛ e ji nɔ nɛ hule kɛ je e nyɛ muklii mi lokoo nɛ e nyɛɛ we gblee. 9Nɛ benɛ Paulo ngɛ munyu tue ɔ, e bu lɛ tue. Nɛ benɛ Paulo hyɛ lɛ too nɛ e na kaa e ngɛ hemi kɛ yemi kaa a ma tsa lɛ ɔ, 10e kɛ gbi wawɛɛ de lɛ ke: “Tee si nɛ o da o nane nɔ tlɔmɔɔ!” Nɛ e hlu ma si nɛ e nyɛɛ. 11Nɛ benɛ ni ɔmɛ na nɔ́ nɛ Paulo pee ɔ, a de ngɛ Likaonia gbi mi ke: “Mawu ɔmɛ plɛ a he kaa nimli kɛ kple si kɛ ba wa ngɔ.” 12Nɛ a tsɛ Barnaba ke Dio, kɛ Paulo hu ke Herme, ejakaa lɛ titli lɛ e ngɛ munyu ɔ tue ɔ nɛ. 13Se Dio osɔfo nɛ ngɛ a ma a agbo ɔ nya a hɛɛ nakuhi kɛ nyinyla kɛ ba agbo ɔ nya, konɛ lɛ kɛ asafo ɔ kɛ sa bɔ. 14Se benɛ bɔfo ɔmɛ nɛ ji Barnaba kɛ Paulo nu he ɔ, a gba a tadehi nɛ a sa fo kɛ ya sɛ asafo ɔ kpɛti kɛ ngmlaa 15ke: “Tsaatsɛmɛ, mɛni nyɛ ngɛ pee nɛ ɔ? wɔ hu nimli adesahi ji wɔ kaa nyɛ nɔuu, nɛ wa ngɛ sane kpakpa a fiee kɛ ngɛ nyɛ tsɔɔe, konɛ nyɛɛ kpale nyɛ se kɛ je kikɛmɛ a yakayaka ni nɛ ɔmɛ a he kɛ ba Mawu hɛkalɔ ɔ ngɔ, nɔ nɛ pee hiɔwe kɛ zugba kɛ wo kɛ nihi kulaa nɛ ngɛ a mi ɔ; 16nɔ nɛ blemabi ɔmɛ a yinɔhi nɛ be ɔ mi ɔ, e ha majemajeɔ tsuo nyɛɛ mɛ nitsɛmɛ a blɔ ɔmɛ a nɔ. 17Se kɛ̃ ɔ, e jɔɔ we lɛ nitsɛ e he odase yemi, se mohu e peɔ kpakpa nɛ e haa hiɔmi jee hiɔwe nɛɛ haa nyɛ, kɛ jehahi nɛ baa ni fuu hulɔ, e kɛ ngma kɛ bua jɔmi woɔ nyɛ tsuihi a mi tɔ.” 18Nɛ a gbo dengme loko a kɛ kikɛmɛ a munyu nɛ ɔmɛ tsi bɔ nɛ jinɛ ni ɔmɛ maa sã ha mɛ ɔ nya.
19Se Yudafohi komɛ je Antiokia kɛ Ikoniom ba lejɛ ɔ ba wo asafo ɔmɛ a yi mi; a fia Paulo tɛ, nɛ a sã lɛ si kɛ je ma a mi, a susu kaa e gbo. 20Se benɛ kaseli ɔmɛ ba bɔle lɛ kɛ kpe ɔ, e te si nɛ e ho ma a mi ya. Nɛ e nɔ je na a, e kɛ Barnaba pue nɔ kɛ ho Derbe ya.
Paulo kɛ Barnaba ba Antiokia ekohu
21Benɛ a fiɛ sane kpakpa a tsɔɔ ma a, nɛ a ha nihi fuu tsake pee kaseli ɔ, a kpale a se kɛ ho Listra kɛ Ikoniom kɛ Antiokia ya. 22A kpale wo kaseli ɔmɛ a mumi mi wami ɔ he wami, nɛ a tu munyu tsɔɔ mɛ ke a hɛɛ hemi kɛ yemi ɔ mi, nɛ jeha nɛ ɔ hu e sa kaa wa guu dengme fuu mi kɛ sɛɛ Mawu matsɛ yemi ɔ mi. 23Nɛ a hia nikɔtɔmahi ngɔ to asafo tsuaa asafo nya, nɛ a kɛ sɔlemi kɛ hwɔ hami tu mɛ ngɔ wo Nyɔmtsɛ nɔ nɛ a he ye ɔ dɛ mi. 24Nɛ a po mi ngɛ Pisidia nɛ a ba Pamfilia. 25Nɛ benɛ a fiɛ munyu ɔ ngɔ tsɔɔ ngɛ Perge ɔ, a ngɔ pue nɔ kɛ ba Atalia. 26Nɛ a sɛ lɛ mi ngɛ lejɛ ɔ, nɛ a hia kɛ ba Antiokia, ngɛ he nɛ a tu mɛ ngɔ wo Mawu dloomi ɔ dɛ mi kɛ ha ni tsumi nɛ a tsu gbe nya a ngɛ ɔ.
27Benɛ a ba lejɛ ɔ nɛ a ba bua asafo ɔ nya a, a sɛɛ mɛ nihi nɛ Mawu kɛ mɛ ya tsu ɔ kulaa, kɛ bɔ nɛ e bli blɔ ngɔ ha majeli ɔmɛ. 28Nɛ a kɛ kaseli ɔmɛ hi si be saii.

english_text:
1 Some people came from Judea and started teaching the Lord's followers that they could not be saved, unless they were circumcised as Moses had taught. 2This caused trouble, and Paul and Barnabas argued with them about this teaching. So it was decided to send Paul and Barnabas and a few others to Jerusalem to discuss this problem with the apostles and the church leaders.
The Church Leaders Meet in Jerusalem
3The men who were sent by the church went through Phoenicia and Samaria, telling how the Gentiles had turned to God. This news made the Lord's followers very happy. 4When the men arrived in Jerusalem, they were welcomed by the church, including the apostles and the leaders. They told them everything God had helped them do. 5But some Pharisees had become followers of the Lord. They stood up and said, “Gentiles who have faith in the Lord must be circumcised and told to obey the Law of Moses.”
6The apostles and church leaders met to discuss this problem about Gentiles. 7 They had talked it over for a long time, when Peter got up and said:
My friends, you know that God decided long ago to let me be the one from your group to preach the good news to the Gentiles. God did this so they would hear and obey him. 8 He knows what is in everyone's heart. And he showed he had chosen the Gentiles, when he gave them the Holy Spirit, just as he had given his Spirit to us. 9God treated them in the same way that he treated us. They put their faith in him, and he made their hearts pure.
10Now why are you trying to make God angry by placing a heavy burden on these followers? This burden was too heavy for us or our ancestors. 11But we believe that we will be saved by the gift of undeserved grace from our Lord Jesus Christ, just as the Gentiles are.
12Everyone kept quiet and listened as Barnabas and Paul told how God had given them the power to work a lot of miracles and wonders for the Gentiles.
13After they had finished speaking, James said:
My friends, listen to me! 14Simon Peter has told how God first came to the Gentiles and made some of them his own people. 15This agrees with what the prophets wrote,
16 “I, the Lord, will return
and rebuild
David's fallen house.
I will build it from its ruins
and set it up again.
17Then other nations
will turn to me
and be my chosen ones.
I, the Lord, say this.
18I promised it long ago.”
19And so, my friends, I don't think we should place burdens on the Gentiles who are turning to God. 20 We should simply write and tell them not to eat anything that has been offered to idols. They should be told not to eat the meat of any animal that has been strangled or that still has blood in it. They must also not commit any terrible sexual sins.
21We must remember that the Law of Moses has been preached in city after city for many years, and every Sabbath it is read in our synagogues.
A Letter to Gentiles Who Had Faith in the Lord
22The apostles, the leaders, and all the church members decided to send some men to Antioch along with Paul and Barnabas. They chose Silas and Judas Barsabbas, who were two leaders of the Lord's followers. 23They wrote a letter that said:
We apostles and leaders send friendly greetings to all of you Gentiles who are followers of the Lord in Antioch, Syria, and Cilicia.
24We have heard that some people from here have terribly upset you by what they said. But we did not send them! 25So we met together and decided to choose some men and to send them to you along with our good friends Barnabas and Paul. 26These men have risked their lives for our Lord Jesus Christ. 27We are also sending Judas and Silas, who will tell you in person the same things that we are writing.
28The Holy Spirit has shown us that we should not place any extra burden on you. 29 But you should not eat anything offered to idols. You should not eat any meat that still has the blood in it or any meat of any animal that has been strangled. You must also not commit any terrible sexual sins. If you follow these instructions, you will do well.
We send our best wishes.
30The four men left Jerusalem and went to Antioch. Then they called the church members together and gave them the letter. 31When the letter was read, everyone was pleased and greatly encouraged. 32Judas and Silas were prophets, and they spoke a long time, encouraging and helping the Lord's followers.
33The men from Jerusalem stayed on in Antioch for a while. And when they left to return to the ones who had sent them, the followers wished them well. 34-35But Paul and Barnabas stayed on in Antioch, where they and many others taught and preached about the Lord.
Paul and Barnabas Go Their Separate Ways
36Sometime later Paul said to Barnabas, “Let's go back and visit the Lord's followers in the cities where we preached his message. Then we will know how they are doing.” 37Barnabas wanted to take along John, whose other name was Mark. 38 But Paul did not want to, because Mark had left them in Pamphylia and had stopped working with them.
39Paul and Barnabas argued, then each of them went his own way. Barnabas took Mark and sailed to Cyprus, 40but Paul took Silas and left after the followers had placed them in God's care. 41They traveled through Syria and Cilicia, encouraging the churches.
translation_text:
A kpe ngɛ Yerusalem
1Ni komɛ je Yudea kɛ ba nɛ a ba tsɔɔ nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ ke: “Ke a pui nyɛ ngɛ Mose Mlaa a nya a, a be nyɛ yiwami nyɛe ma he.” 2Nɛ benɛ Paulo kɛ Barnaba kɛ mɛ sa nya nɛ a kɛ mɛ je nɔ hluu ɔ, a to kaa Paulo kɛ Barnaba kɛ a ti ni komɛ hu nɛ ya bɔfo ɔmɛ kɛ nikɔtɔmahi nɛ ngɛ Yerusalem ɔmɛ a ngɔ ngɛ kikɛmɛ a munyu nɛ ɔ he.
3Lɔ ɔ he ɔ benɛ asafo ɔ ba je mɛ blɔ ɔ, a gu Foinike kɛ Samaria nɛ a sɛɛ majeli ɔmɛ a tsakemi ɔ he sane ha mɛ, nɛ a kɛ ha nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ tsuo na bua jɔmi wawɛɛ. 4Nɛ benɛ a su Yerusalem ɔ, asafo ɔ kɛ bɔfo ɔmɛ kɛ nikɔtɔma amɛ he mɛ hɛmuɔ, nɛ a sɛɛ nihi kulaa nɛ Mawu kɛ mɛ tsu ɔ ha mɛ. 5Se ni komɛ nɛ je Farisifo ɔmɛ a ku ɔ mi nɛ he ye ɔ te si nɛ a de ke: “Ja a po mɛ nɛ a wo mɛ kita ke a ye Mose Mlaa a nɔ.”
6Nɛ bɔfo ɔmɛ kɛ nikɔtɔma amɛ ba bua a he nya konɛ a hla kikɛmɛ a sane nɛ ɔ mi. 7Se benɛ a sa nya hluu ɔ, Petro te si da si, nɛ e de mɛ ke: “Tsaatsɛmɛ kɛ mamimɛ, nyɛ nitsɛmɛ nyɛ le kaa kɛ je lokoo nɛ Mawu hla mi kaa majeli ɔmɛ a nu sane kpakpa a kɛ je ye nya, nɛ a he ye. 8Nɛ Mawu nɛ le tsui mi nihi ɔ ye mɛ odase nɛ e ha mɛ Mumi Klɔuklɔu ɔ kaa bɔ nɛ e ha wɔ ɔ nɔuu, 9nɛ e hlɛ́ nimli a mi ngɛ waa kɛ mɛ kpɛti, nɛ e kɛ hemi kɛ yemi tsukɔ a tsuihi a he. 10Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, jeha nɛ ɔ, mɛni he je nyɛ ngɛ Mawu kae nɛ nyɛɛ kɛ pã tso nɛ waa kɛ wa tsɛmɛ ɔmɛ kulaa nyɛ we tloomi fɔ́ɔ kaseli ɔmɛ a ko nɔ? 11Se wa heɔ yeɔ kaa Nyɔmtsɛ Yesu Kristo dloomi ɔ mohu nɔ a maa gu kɛ he waa kɛ mɛ tsuo yiwami.”
12Kɛkɛ nɛ mɛ tsuo a ma a nya nɛ a bu Barnaba kɛ Paulo nɛ sɛɛ mɛ okadihi kɛ nyakpɛ nihi abɔ nɛ Mawu gu a nine nɔ kɛ pee ngɛ majemajeli ɔmɛ a kpɛti ɔ tue. 13Benɛ a tu munyu ɔta a, Yakobo he nɔ nɛ e ke: “Tsaatsɛmɛ kɛ mamimɛ, nyɛɛ bu mi tue. 14Simeon sɛɛ bɔ nɛ Mawu ba slaa majemajeli ɔmɛ kekle, nɛ e hla a kpɛti ma ko ngɔ ha e biɛ ɔ. 15Nɛ gbali ɔmɛ a munyu ɔmɛ hu kɛ enɛ ɔ sɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ, bɔ nɛ a ngma ke:
16‘Ni nɛ ɔmɛ a se ɔ, ma kpale ye se kɛ ba,
Nɛ ma dla David bo tsu nɛ ku ɔ ma ma;
Nɛ o tsu kokue ɔmɛ hu ma fia ekohu,
Nɛ ma tle lɛ si ngɔ ma si;
17Benɛ pee nɛ nimli nɛ piɛ ɔ kɛ majemajeli ɔmɛ kulaa hu
Nɛ a kɛ ye biɛ wo mɛ ɔ
A hla Nyɔmtsɛ ɔ se blɔ.’
18Nyɔmtsɛ ɔ nɛ ha a le enɛ ɔmɛ kulaa kɛ je lokoo ɔ lɛ de.
19“Lɔ ɔ he ɔ nɔ́ nɛ i ngɛ dee ji kaa a ko doo nihi nɛ kpale a se kɛ je majeli ɔmɛ a kpɛti kɛ ba Mawu ngɔ ɔ nya tsɔ. 20Se mohu a ngma mɛ ke a nyɛ wɔ nihi kɛ a ajuama bɔmi kɛ lohwehi nɛ a kika mɛ kɛ gbe kɛ dmuɔ. 21Ejakaa kɛ je blema lokoo ɔ Mose ngɛ nihi nɛ fiɛɔ lɛ ngɛ ma tsuaa ma nɔ, nɛ daa Hejɔɔmi Ligbi ɔ a kaneɔ e womi ɔmɛ ngɛ kpe he ɔmɛ.”
Womi nɛ a ngma mane mejeli nɛ he ye ɔ
22Kɛkɛ nɛ bɔfo ɔmɛ kɛ nikɔtɔma amɛ kɛ asafo mluku ɔ kulaa ma nya si kaa a hia nyumuhi komɛ kɛ je mɛ nitsɛmɛ a kpɛti, nɛ a tsɔ mɛ kɛ Paulo kɛ Barnaba kɛ ya Antiokia. Mɛ ji Yuda, nɔ nɛ a tsɛɛ lɛ Barsaba hulɔ ɔ, kɛ Sila, nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ a kpɛti nikɔtɔma amɛ. 23Nɛ a ngma womi ngɔ ha mɛ ke:
“Bɔfo ɔmɛ kɛ nikɔtɔma amɛ kɛ nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ biɔ nyɛmimɛ nɛ je majeli ɔmɛ a kpɛti ngɛ Antiokia kɛ Siria kɛ Kilikia a saminya. 24Akɛnɛ wa nu kaa wa ti nikomɛ pue nɔ kɛ ba ba doo nyɛ nya kɛ munyuhi komɛ nɛ a kɛ puɛ nyɛ juɛmi de ke a po nyɛ nɛ nyɛɛ ye Mose Mlaa a nɔ, pohu wa wui mɛ jamɛ a kita ko he je ɔ, 25e sa wa hɛ mi kaa, nɛ wa nya pee kake nɛ ɔ ɔ, waa hia nihi ngɔ piɛ Barnaba kɛ Paulo nɛ wa suɔ ɔ he 26nihi nɛ ji nimli nɛ ngɔ a wami ngɔ ha ngɛ wa Nyɔmtsɛ Yesu biɛ ɔ he ɔ, konɛ waa tsɔ mɛ nyɛ ngɔ. 27Lɔ ɔ he ɔ wa tsɛ Yuda kɛ Sila, konɛ mɛ hu a kɛ a nya mi munyu ba jaje kikɛmɛ a ni nɛ ɔmɛ nɔuu ngɔ tsɔɔ nyɛ. 28Ejakaa e sa Mumi Klɔuklɔu ɔ hɛ mi, nɛ e sa wɔ hu wa hɛ mi kaa, waa kɛ tlomi ko nɛ ko fɔ nyɛ nɔ hu, kaa ja nihi nɛ he hia nɛ ɔmɛ nɔuu. 29Kaa nyɛɛ nyɛ lo nɛ a gbe ha wɔhi kɛ muɔ kɛ lohwehi nɛ a kika a kuɛ kɛ ajuama bɔmi. Ke nyɛ nyɛ enɛ ɔmɛ ɔ, nyɛ pee saminya. Nyɛɛ hi si saminya!”
30Jeha nɛ ɔ, benɛ a wo bɔfo ɔmɛ blɔ ɔ, a ba Antiokia, nɛ a ba bua asafo ɔ nya nɛ a je womi ɔ ngɔ ha mɛ. 31Nɛ benɛ a kane ɔ, a bua jɔ a he ngɛ a bua womi munyu ɔ he. 32Se Yuda kɛ Sila a, akɛnɛ mɛ nitsɛmɛ hu gbali ji mɛ he je ɔ, a kɛ munyuhi babauu jɔɔ nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ a bua nɛ a wo mɛ he wami. 33Nɛ benɛ a se kɛ bɔɔ ngɛ lejɛ ɔ, nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ wo mɛ blɔ ngɛ he jɔmi mi kɛ ho nihi nɛ tsɔ mɛ ɔmɛ a ngɔ ya. [ 34Se Sila lɛɛ, e suɔ kaa e maa hi lejɛ ɔ.]
35Paulo kɛ Barnaba hi Antiokia nɛ a tsɔɔ ni nɛ a fiɛ Nyɔmtsɛ ɔ he sane kpakpa a, nɛ ni kpa komɛ fuu hu pee ja.
Paulo kɛ Barnaba gba a mi
36Be ko se ɔ Paulo de Barnaba ke: “Ha waa kpale wa se ya slaa wa nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ ngɛ ma tsuaa ma nɛ wa fiɛ Nyɔmtsɛ ɔ munyu ɔ ngɛ mi ɔ, nɛ waa hyɛ bɔ nɛ a ngɛ.” 37Barnaba hɛ ngɛ nɔ kaa a maa ngɔ Yohane nɛ a tsɛɛ lɛ Marko ɔ ngɔ piɛ a he. 38Se Paulo lɛɛ, e susu kaa e sɛ́ kaa a ngɔ nɔ nɛ kpale ngɛ a se ngɛ Pamfilia nɛ e kɛ mɛ yɛ́ ni tsumi ɔ ngɔ piɛ a he. 39Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, enɛ ɔ pee mɛ nya sami babauu nɛ e ha a gba a mi, nɛ Barnaba ngɔ Marko ngɔ piɛ e he, nɛ a gu lɛ mi kɛ ho Kipro ya. 40Se Paulo lɛɛ, e hia Sila ngɔ piɛ e he, nɛ benɛ nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ tu lɛ ngɔ wo Mawu dloomi ɔ dɛ mi ɔ, e pue nɔ kɛ ho. 41Nɛ e gu Siria kɛ Kilikia ya wo asafo ɔmɛ he wami.

english_text:
Timothy Works with Paul and Silas
1Paul and Silas went back to Derbe and Lystra, where there was a follower named Timothy. His mother was also a follower. She was Jewish, and his father was Greek. 2The Lord's followers in Lystra and Iconium said good things about Timothy, 3and Paul wanted him to go with them. But Paul first had him circumcised, because all the Jewish people around there knew that Timothy's father was Greek.
4As Paul and the others went from city to city, they told the followers what the apostles and leaders in Jerusalem had decided, and they urged them to follow these instructions. 5The churches became stronger in their faith, and each day more people put their faith in the Lord.
Paul's Vision in Troas
6Paul and his friends went through Phrygia and Galatia, but the Holy Spirit would not let them preach in Asia. 7After they arrived in Mysia, they tried to go into Bithynia, but the Spirit of Jesus would not let them. 8So they went on through Mysia until they came to Troas.
9During the night, Paul had a vision of someone from Macedonia who was standing there and begging him, “Come over to Macedonia and help us!” 10After Paul had seen the vision, we began looking for a way to go to Macedonia. We were sure that God had called us to preach the good news there.
Lydia Becomes a Follower of the Lord
11We sailed straight from Troas to Samothrace, and the next day we arrived in Neapolis. 12From there we went to Philippi, which is a Roman colony in the first district of Macedonia.
We spent several days in Philippi. 13Then on the Sabbath we went outside the city gate to a place by the river, where we thought there would be a Jewish meeting place for prayer. We sat down and talked with the women who came. 14One of them was Lydia, who was from the city of Thyatira and sold expensive purple cloth. She was a worshiper of the Lord God, and he made her willing to accept what Paul was saying. 15Then after she and her family were baptized, she kept on begging us, “If you think I really do have faith in the Lord, come stay in my home.” Finally, we accepted her invitation.
Paul and Silas Are Put in Jail
16One day on our way to the place of prayer, we were met by a slave girl. She had a spirit in her that gave her the power to tell the future. By doing this she made a lot of money for her owners. 17The girl followed Paul and the rest of us, and she kept yelling, “These men are servants of the Most High God! They are telling you how to be saved.”
18This went on for several days. Finally, Paul got so upset that he turned and said to the spirit, “In the name of Jesus Christ, I order you to leave this girl alone!” At once the evil spirit left her.
19When the girl's owners realized they had lost all chances for making more money, they grabbed Paul and Silas and dragged them into court. 20They told the officials, “These Jews are upsetting our city! 21They are telling us to do things we Romans are not allowed to do.”
22The crowd joined in the attack on Paul and Silas. Then the officials tore the clothes off the two men and ordered them to be beaten with a whip. 23After they had been badly beaten, they were put in jail, and the jailer was told to guard them carefully. 24The jailer did as he was told. He put them deep inside the jail and chained their feet to heavy blocks of wood.
25About midnight Paul and Silas were praying and singing praises to God, while the other prisoners listened. 26Suddenly a strong earthquake shook the jail to its foundations. The doors opened, and the chains fell from all the prisoners.
27When the jailer woke up and saw that the doors were open, he thought that the prisoners had escaped. He pulled out his sword and was about to kill himself. 28But Paul shouted, “Don't harm yourself! No one has escaped.”
29The jailer asked for a torch and went into the jail. He was shaking all over as he knelt down in front of Paul and Silas. 30After he had led them out of the jail, he asked, “What must I do to be saved?”
31They replied, “Have faith in the Lord Jesus and you will be saved! This is also true for everyone who lives in your home.”
32Then Paul and Silas told him and everyone else in his house about the Lord. 33While it was still night, the jailer took them to a place where he could wash their cuts and bruises. Then he and everyone in his home were baptized. 34They were very glad they had put their faith in God. After this, the jailer took Paul and Silas to his home and gave them something to eat.
35The next morning the officials sent some police with orders for the jailer to let Paul and Silas go. 36The jailer told Paul, “The officials have ordered me to set you free. Now you can leave in peace.”
37But Paul told the police, “We are Roman citizens, and the Roman officials had us beaten in public without giving us a trial. They threw us into jail. Now do they think they can secretly send us away? No, they cannot! They will have to come here themselves and let us out.”
38When the police told the officials that Paul and Silas were Roman citizens, the officials were afraid. 39So they came and apologized. They led them out of the jail and asked them to please leave town. 40But Paul and Silas went straight to the home of Lydia, where they saw the Lord's followers and encouraged them. Then they left.
translation_text:
Paulo kɛ Sila ngɔ Timoteo
1Kɛkɛ nɛ Paulo ba Derbe kɛ Listra. Nɛ oʼɛ, kaselɔ ko ngɛ lejɛ ɔ nɛ a tsɛɛ lɛ Timoteo, Yudayo ko nɛ he ye ɔ bi, se e tsɛ ɔ Helano ʼi. 2Nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ nɛ ngɛ Listra kɛ Ikoniom ɔ yeɔ e he odase kpakpa. 3Paulo hla kaa e kɛ Timoteo nɛ ya, lɔ ɔ he ɔ e ngɔ lɛ nɛ e po lɛ ngɛ Yudafohi nɛ ngɛ lejɛ ɔ ni ɔmɛ a mi ɔ he; ejakaa mɛ kulaa a le kaa e tsɛ ɔ Helano ʼi. 4Se benɛ a ngɛ ma amɛ a nɔ kpae ɔ, a kɛ mlaahi nɛ bɔfo ɔmɛ kɛ nikɔtɔma amɛ nɛ ngɛ Yerusalem ɔ wo ɔ ha mɛ, konɛ a ye nɔ. 5Lɔ ɔ he ɔ asafo ɔ na he wami ngɛ hemi kɛ yemi mi, nɛ a he hiɛɛ daa ligbi.
Paulo ninami ngɛ Troia
6Akɛnɛ Mumi Klɔuklɔu ɔ tsi mɛ blɔ ke a ko fiɛ munyu ɔ ngɔ tsɔɔ ngɛ Asia he je ɔ, a po mi ngɛ Frigia kɛ Galatia zugba a nɔ. 7A ba Misia ni ɔmɛ a mi, nɛ a ka kaa a maa ya Bitinia, se Yesu Mumi ɔ ngmɛ́ mɛ blɔ. 8Kɛkɛ nɛ a gu Misia nɛ a ba Troia. 9Nɛ nyɔ ɔ mi ɔ Paulo na ni, kaa nyumu Makedonia no ko daa si ngɛ lɛ pɛɛ kpae ke: “Ba Makedonia nɛ o ba ye bua wɔ!” 10Se benɛ e na ni ɔ pɛ ɔ, amlɔ ɔ wa hla kaa waa ya Makedonia, ejakaa wa na le tutuutu kaa Nyɔmtsɛ ɔ tsɛ wɔ kɛ yaa lejɛ ɔ, konɛ wa ya fiɛ sane kpakpa a ngɔ tsɔɔ mɛ.
Lidia tsakemi ngɛ Filipi
11Lɔ ɔ he ɔ wa hia kɛ lɛ kɛ je Troia nɛ wa nyɛɛ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ ya Samotrake, nɛ e nɔ je na a wa ba Neapoli. 12Nɛ wa je lejɛ ɔ, wa ya Filipi nɛ ji Makedonia zugba a nɔ ma ngua kɛ Romabi a nɔ yemi he. Wa hi ma nɛ ɔ mi be saii. 13Nɛ Hejɔɔmi Ligbi ɔ nɔ ɔ, wa je ma a mi kɛ ya pa nya he nɛ wa juɛmi de wɔ ke a pɔɔ sɔlemi ngɛ ɔ, nɛ wa hi si nɛ waa kɛ yihi nɛ ba bua a he nyɛ ngɛ lejɛ ɔ tu munyu. 14Nɛ yo ko nɛ a tsɛɛ lɛ Lidia nɛ ji kɔjai jualɔ ko nɛ je Tiatira ma a mi nɛ yee Mawu gbeye ɔ hu nu. Nɛ Nyɔmtsɛ ɔ bli e tsui nya, kaa e bu nihi nɛ Paulo ngɛ dee ɔ tue. 15Nɛ benɛ a baptisi lɛ kɛ e we ɔ, e kpa wɔ pɛɛ ke: “Ke nyɛ bu mi kaa i he Nyɔmtsɛ ɔ ye anɔkuale mi ɔ, lɛɛ nyɛɛ ba ye we ɔ nɛ nyɛ ba hi lejɛ ɔ.” Nɛ e hɛɛ wɔ hluu nɛ wa kplɛɛ nɔ.
A wo Paulo kɛ Sila tsu mi
16E ba mi kaa ligbi ko benɛ wa yaa he nɛ a sɔlee ngɛ ɔ, tsɔlɔyo ko nɛ klaami mumi ngɛ e mi kɛ wɔ ba kpe; e kɛ e klaami ɔ haa e nyɔmtsɛmɛ naa ni fuu. 17E nyɛɛ waa kɛ Paulo se, nɛ e kpa ngmlaa ke: “Kikɛmɛ a nimli nɛ ɔmɛ ɔ, Mawu nɛ ngɛ hiɔwe lokoo ɔ tsɔli ji mɛ, nɛ a ngɛ yi wami hemi blɔ ɔ jajee kɛ ngɛ nyɛ tsɔɔe.” 18Nɛ e pee ja ligbihi fuu. Se e dɔ Paulo wawɛɛ, nɛ e plɛ e he nɛ e de mumi ɔ ke: “I ngɛ mo fae ngɛ Yesu Kristo biɛ mi kaa o je e mi.” Nɛ e je kpo ngɛ jamɛ a ngmlɛfia a nɔ nɔuu. 19Se benɛ e nyɔmtsɛmɛ ɔmɛ na kaa a ni nami hɛ kɛ nɔ fɔmi ɔ be hu ɔ, a nu Paulo kɛ Sila nɛ a sã mɛ kɛ ya ganɔ ɔmɛ a hɛ mi ngɛ jua a nɔ. 20Benɛ a kpaka mɛ kɛ ya asafoatsɛmɛ ɔmɛ a hɛ mi ɔ, a ke: “Kikɛmɛ a nimli nɛ ɔmɛ nɛ ji Yudafohi ɔ ngɛ wa ma a mi hliihlii woe. 21Nɛ a ngɛ kusumihi komɛ tsɔɔe nɛ wa be he blɔ ka wa pɛtɛɛ he loo wa yeɔ nɔ, ejakaa Romabi ji wɔ.” 22Nɛ ma mi bi ɔmɛ hu te si wo mɛ nɛ a po klaangma wo a he, nɛ asafoatsɛmɛ ɔmɛ ha a je a tade ɔmɛ ngɛ a he, nɛ a fa ke a fia mɛ kpa. 23Nɛ benɛ a fia mɛ kpa saminya a, a wo mɛ tsu mi, nɛ a wo pa mi tsɛmɛ a nɔ hyɛlɔ ɔ kita ke e ngɔ mɛ ngɔ to sɔkee. 24Nɛ akɛnɛ a wo lɛ kikɛmɛ a kita he je ɔ, e kɛ mɛ ya wo tsu nɛ ngɛ se je ɔ mi, nɛ e bɔ a nanehi pa.
25Se nyɔ mi kpɛti ɔ Paulo kɛ Sila ngɛ sɔlee nɛ a ngɛ lae kɛ ngɛ Mawu yi jee; nɛ pa mi tsɛmɛ ɔmɛ ngɛ mɛ tue bue. 26Nɛ tlukaa a, zugba mimiɛ wawɛɛ; nɛ tsu ɔ fanesi ɔmɛ mimiɛ, nɛ amlɔ ɔ sinya amɛ kulaa bli, nɛ mɛ tsuo a kɔsɔkɔsɔ ɔmɛ kplɔ ngɛ a he. 27Se benɛ pa mi tsɛmɛ a nɔ hyɛlɔ ɔ hɛli si kɛ je mahɛ mi nɛ e na kaa tsu ɔ sinya amɛ kulaa a nya fɔɔ si ɔ, e hia klaate nɛ jinɛ e maa gbe e he, ejakaa e susu kaa pa mi tsɛmɛ ɔmɛ tu fo. 28Se Paulo nga ke: “Koo pee o he yayami ko, se wɔ tsuo wa ngɛ hiɛ ɔ.” 29Kɛkɛ nɛ pã mi tsɛmɛ a nɔ hyɛlɔ ɔ tsɛ nɛ a ba ha lɛ la, nɛ e sa fo kɛ sɛ tsu ɔ mi, nɛ e kɛ hedomi be nɔ Paulo kɛ Sila hɛ mi; 30nɛ e kɛ mɛ je kpo nɛ e ke: “Nyɔmtsɛmɛ, kɛ ma pee kɛɛ nɛ ma na yi wami hemi?”
31Nɛ a ke: “He Nyɔmtsɛ Yesu Kristo nɔ ngɔ ye, nɛ a ma he o kɛ o we ɔ kulaa yi wami.” 32Nɛ a jaje Nyɔmtsɛ ɔ munyu ɔ tsɔɔ lɛ kɛ nihi kulaa nɛ ngɛ e we ɔ mi ɔ. 33Nɛ e ngɔ mɛ jamɛ a nyɔ ɔ mi ngmlɛfia a nɔuu, nɛ e fɔ a kpa amɛ a nya ha mɛ, nɛ a baptisi lɛ kɛ e we ɔ mi bimɛ kulaa amlɔ ɔ nɔuu. 34Nɛ e kɛ mɛ ya e we ɔ mi, nɛ e ya ngmɛ mɛ okplɔɔ, nɛ e kɛ e we ɔ kulaa nya kaa e he Mawu ye.
35Se benɛ je na a, asafoatsɛmɛ ɔmɛ tsɔ aslaafohi ba de ke: “Ngmɛɛ nimli ɔmɛ a he nɛ a ho”. 36Se pa mi tsɛmɛ a nɔ hyɛlɔ ɔ jaje kikɛmɛ a munyu nɛ ɔ ngɔ tsɔɔ Paulo ke: “Asafoatsɛmɛ ɔmɛ tsɔ kɛ ba ke a ngmɛɛ nyɛ he, lɔ ɔ he ɔ jeha nɛ ɔ nyɛɛ je kpo, nɛ nyɛɛ kɛ nyɛɛmi saminya.” 37Se Paulo de mɛ ke: “Wɔ nɛ Romabi ji wɔ nɛ a bui wɔ fɔ ɔ, a fia wɔ kpa, nɛ a wo wɔ tsu mi hulɔ, nɛ kpaako a ngɛ wɔ fiee zaa lo? Dɛbi, se mohu ha mɛ nitsɛmɛ a ba nɛ a ba je wɔ.” 38Nɛ aslaafo ɔmɛ ya jaje kikɛmɛ a munyu nɛ ɔ ngɔ tsɔɔ asafoatsɛmɛ ɔmɛ. Nɛ benɛ a nu kaa Romabi ji mɛ ɔ, a ye gbeye. 39Nɛ a ba ba kpa mɛ pɛɛ, nɛ benɛ a je mɛ ɔ, a kpa mɛ pɛɛ ke a je ma a mi. 40Se benɛ a je tsu ɔ mi ɔ, a ho Lidia we ɔ mi ya. Nɛ benɛ a na nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ nɛ a jɔɔ a bua a, a pue nɔ kɛ ho.

english_text:
Trouble in Thessalonica
1After Paul and his friends had traveled through Amphipolis and Apollonia, they went on to Thessalonica. A synagogue was in that city. 2So as usual, Paul went there to worship, and on three Sabbaths he spoke to the people. He used the Scriptures 3to show them that the Messiah had to suffer, but that he would rise from death. Paul also told them that Jesus is the Messiah he was preaching about. 4Some of them believed what Paul had said, and they became followers with Paul and Silas. Some Gentiles and many important women also believed the message.
5The Jewish leaders were jealous and got some troublemakers who hung around the marketplace to start a riot in the city. They wanted to drag Paul and Silas out to the mob, and so they went straight to Jason's home. 6But when they did not find them there, they dragged out Jason and some of the Lord's followers. They took them to the city authorities and shouted, “Paul and Silas have been upsetting things everywhere. Now they have come here, 7and Jason has welcomed them into his home. All of them break the laws of the Roman Emperor by claiming that someone named Jesus is king.”
8The officials and the people were upset when they heard this. 9So they made Jason and the other followers pay bail before letting them go.
People in Berea Welcome the Message
10That same night the Lord's followers sent Paul and Silas on to Berea, and after they arrived, they went to the synagogue. 11The people in Berea were much nicer than those in Thessalonica, and they gladly accepted the message. Day after day they studied the Scriptures to see if these things were true. 12Many of them put their faith in the Lord, including some important Greek women and several men.
13When the Jewish leaders in Thessalonica heard that Paul had been preaching God's message in Berea, they went there and caused trouble by turning the crowds against Paul.
14At once the followers sent Paul down to the coast, but Silas and Timothy stayed in Berea. 15Some men went with Paul as far as Athens, and then returned with instructions for Silas and Timothy to join him as soon as possible.
Paul in Athens
16While Paul was waiting in Athens, he was upset to see all the idols in the city. 17He went to the synagogue to speak to the Jews and to anyone who worshiped with them. Day after day he also spoke to everyone he met in the market. 18Some of them were Epicureans and some were Stoics, and they started arguing with him.
People were asking, “What is this know-it-all trying to say?”
Some even said, “Paul must be preaching about foreign gods! That's what he means when he talks about Jesus and about people rising from death.”
19They brought Paul before a council called the Areopagus, and said, “Tell us what your new teaching is all about. 20We have heard you say some strange things, and we want to know what you mean.”
21More than anything else the people of Athens and the foreigners living there loved to hear and to talk about anything new. 22So Paul stood up in front of the council and said:
People of Athens, I see that you are very religious. 23 As I was going through your city and looking at the things you worship, I found an altar with the words, “To an Unknown God.” You worship this God, but you don't really know him. So I want to tell you about him. 24 This God made the world and everything in it. He is Lord of heaven and earth, and he doesn't live in temples built by human hands. 25 He doesn't need help from anyone. He gives life, breath, and everything else to all people. 26 From one person God made all nations who live on earth, and he decided when and where every nation would be.
27 God has done all this, so that we will look for him and reach out and find him. He isn't far from any of us, 28and he gives us the power to live, to move, and to be who we are. “We are his children,” just as some of your poets have said.
29Since we are God's children, we must not think that he is like an idol made out of gold or silver or stone. He isn't like anything that humans have thought up and made. 30In the past, God forgave all this because people did not know what they were doing. But now he says that everyone everywhere must turn to him. 31He has set a day when he will judge the world's people with fairness. And he has chosen the man Jesus to do the judging for him. God has given proof of this to all of us by raising Jesus from death.
32As soon as the people heard Paul say a man had been raised from death, some of them started laughing. Others said, “We will hear you talk about this some other time.” 33When Paul left the council meeting, 34some of the men put their faith in the Lord and went with Paul. One of them was a council member named Dionysius. A woman named Damaris and several others also put their faith in the Lord.
translation_text:
Paulo kɛ Sila ngɛ Tesalonika
1Jeha nɛ ɔ a gu Amfipoli kɛ Apolonia, nɛ a ba Tesalonika, he nɛ Yudafohi a kpe he ko ngɛ ɔ. 2Nɛ Paulo ya a ngɔ kaa bɔ nɛ e pɔɔ peemi ɔ, nɛ e kɛ mɛ ya sa nya Hejɔɔmi Ligbi etɛ sɔuu ngɛ ngmami ɔmɛ a he. 3E blɛke munyu ɔ mi tsɔɔ mɛ faii kaa ja Kristo ɔ na amanehlu nɛ e te si kɛ je gbeje, nɛ kaa “kikɛmɛ a Yesu, nɛ i ngɛ e he sane jajee kɛ ngɛ nyɛ tsɔɔe nɛ ɔ, ji Kristo ɔ nɛ.” 4Nɛ a ti ni komɛ kplɛɛ nɛ a kɛ a he bɔ Paulo kɛ Sila he, kɛ Helabi Mawu gbeye yeli ɔmɛ a kpɛti nihi babauu, kɛ yihi nɛ a buu mɛ hu fuu.
5Se e pee Yudafo ɔmɛ tai, nɛ a ya kpaka yakayaka nimli ɔmɛ a kpɛti dikali komɛ ngɔ piɛ a he, nɛ benɛ a nya ba kpane fuu ɔ, a wo ma a mi hliihlii. A ya tua Yason we ɔ, nɛ a ngɛ hlae nɛ a kpaka Paulo kɛ Sila ya ha ma a. 6Se benɛ a nɛ́ mɛ ɔ, a kpaka Yason kɛ nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ a ti ni komɛ kɛ ya ma a mi nikɔtɔma amɛ a hɛ mi nɛ a kpa ngmlaa ke: “Ni nɛ ɔmɛ nɛ plɛ je mi hɛ mi ngɔ bu si nɛ ɔ ba hiɛ ɔ hulɔ, 7nɛ Yason he mɛ to. Ni nɛ ɔmɛ tsuo kuɔ Kaisare mlaa a nya deɔ ke matsɛ kpa ko ngɛ nɛ ji Yesu ko.” 8Nɛ a ha ma a mi bi ɔmɛ kɛ nikɔtɔma amɛ tsuo nu sawale kɛ kikɛmɛ a munyu nɛ ɔmɛ. 9Nɛ benɛ a he se dami ni ngɛ Yason kɛ ni kpa amɛ a dɛ ɔ, a ngmɛɛ a he.
Paulo kɛ Sila ngɛ Beroia
10Nɛ amlɔ ɔ nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ je Paulo kɛ Sila blɔ nyɔ mi kɛ ho Beroia ya. Nɛ benɛ a su lejɛ ɔ a ya sɛ Yudafo ɔmɛ a kpe he ɔ. 11Ni nɛ ɔmɛ a su hi pe ninɛmɛ nɛ ngɛ Tesalonika a, mɛɛ lɛɛ a je a yi mi pɛtɛ munyu ɔ he, nɛ daa a kpaa ngmami ɔmɛ a mi hyɛɛ kaa ni nɛ ɔmɛ ngɛ mi ja lo? 12Lɔ ɔ he ɔ a ti nihi fuu he ye, kɛ Helayi nɛ ngɛ biɛ kɛ nyumuhi hu fuu. 13Se benɛ Yudafohi nɛ ngɛ Tesalonika a nu he kaa Paulo ya jaje Mawu munyu ɔ ngɛ Beroia hulɔ ɔ, a ba lejɛ ɔ hu nɛ a ba wo ni ɔmɛ yi, nɛ a pee basabasa. 14Kɛkɛ nɛ amlɔ ɔ nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ ya je Paulo blɔ nɛ e ya gu wo hɛ mi; se Sila kɛ Timoteo hi lejɛ ɔ. 15Se nihi nɛ ya sɛ Paulo ɔ kɛ lɛ ya su Atene tɔɔ. Akɛnɛ Paulo sɛ mɛ ke a ha Sila kɛ Timoteo nɛ a ba e ngɔ oya he je ɔ, a pue nɔ kɛ ho.
Paulo ngɛ Atene
16Jeha nɛ ɔ benɛ Paulo ngɛ mɛ mlɛe ngɛ Atene ɔ, e mumi mi wo la ngɛ e mi, benɛ e na ma a nɛ mi hyi tɔ kɛ amagahi sɔuu ɔ. 17Lɔ ɔ he ɔ e kɛ Yudafohi nɛ ngɛ kpe he ɔ kɛ Mawu gbeye yeli ɔmɛ kɛ nihi nɛ kɛ lɛ kpee daa nɛ ɔ ngɛ jua a nɔ ɔ saa nya. 18Se ni leli nɛ je Epikurotsɛmɛ kɛ Stoatsɛmɛ ɔmɛ a ti ni komɛ kɛ lɛ sa nya; nɛ ni komɛ ke: “Mɛni nyapuutsɛ nɛ ɔ ma de po?” Ni komɛ hu ke: “E ngɛ kaa nɔ ko nɛ jajeɔ ma se wɔhi a he sane tsɔɔ;” ejakaa e jaje Yesu kɛ e si temi he sane kpakpa a tsɔɔ mɛ. 19Nɛ a ngɔ lɛ kɛ ya Areopago (kojomi he) ɔ, nɛ a ke: “Anɛ o ma ha waa le tsɔɔmi he nɛ o ngɛ he munyu tue nɛ ɔ lo? 20Ejakaa o ha wa tue nu ma se sanehi; lɔ ɔ he ɔ wa ngɛ sisi hlae nɛ waa le.” 21Se Atenebihi tsuo kɛ nibwɔhi nɛ ngɛ lejɛ ɔ, nɔ́ nɛ piɛ mɛ pɛ ji sane he ko sɛɛmi kɛ tue bumi.
22Paulo ya da Areopago ɔ kpɛti nɛ e ke: “Tsaatsɛmɛ Atenebihi, i naa ngɛ nihi kulaa mi kaa nyɛ jaa wɔhi pɛpɛɛpɛ. 23Ejakaa benɛ i bee nɛ i hyɛ nihi nɛ nyɛ ngɛ jae ɔ, i na bɔ sami latɛ ko hu nɛ a ngma ngɛ nɔ ke: ‘Mawu nɛ a li ɔ nɔ ʼi.’ Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, nɔ nɛ nyɛ li lɛ se kɛ̃ ɔ nyɛ jaa lɛ ɔ, lɛ nɔuu e he sane i ngɛ jajee kɛ ngɛ nyɛ tsɔɔe ɔ nɛ. 24Mawu nɛ pee je ɔ kɛ e mi nihi kulaa, nɛ ji hiɔwe kɛ zugba nyɔmtsɛ ɔ, e hi sɔlemi tsuhi nɛ a kɛ nine pee mi, 25nɛ jeha nɛ ɔ hu a kɛ nimli a ninehi ja we lɛ, kaa nɔ ko nɛ nɔ́ ko fiɔ lɛ; lɛ mohu e dɛ mi wami kɛ mumi kɛ nihi tsuo jee kɛ baa haa nimli kulaa. 26Muɔ kake e kɛ pee nimli adesahi kulaa nɛ a hi zugba a tsuo hɛ mi, nɛ yinɔhi nɛ e to ɔ kɛ a sihi he ɔmɛ a huzu ɔmɛ ɔ, e kpɛ mi ngɔ to momo, 27konɛ a hla Mawu se blɔ, kaa eko ɔ ke a lilaa si ɔ, a maa na lɛ lo; pohu e kɛ wa ti nɔ tsuaa nɔ kpɛti kɛ we. 28Ejakaa
‘E mi nɔuu wa hɛ ngɛ ngɛ, nɛ wa tsɛ̃ɛ wa he,
nɛ wa ngɛ ngɛ.’
