6I ngɛ enɛ ɔ dee ngɛ ga womi nya se pi ngɛ kita nya. 7Ke ka ye he ɔ jinɛ nimli kulaa nɛ hi si kaa bɔ nɛ i ngɛ nɛ ɔ; se nɔ tsuaa nɔ ngɛ lɛ nitsɛ e dloomi nike ni kɛ je Mawu dɛ mi, nɔ ko nɔ́ kikɛ, nɛ nɔ ko hu ekpa.
8Nyumukuyo ɔmɛ kɛ yalɔyi ɔmɛ ɔ, i ngɛ mɛ dee ke: E hi ha mɛ ke a hi si kaa bɔ nɛ imi hu i ngɛ nɔ. 9Se ke a nyɛ we a he nɔ nɛ a ye ɔ, a sɛ gba si himi mi; ejakaa gba si himi hi pe nɔ́ nɛ akɔnɔ maa hao mo.
10Ninɛmɛ nɛ sɛ gba si himi mi ɔ, imi, nɛ tsa pi imi tete, se Nyɔmtsɛ ɔ mohu lɛ ngɛ mɛ kita woe ke, yo ko je gba. 11Nɛ ke e je gba tete po ɔ, e hi si ja, nɛ e ko gba, aloo e kɛ e huno ɔ ya dla; nɛ yotsɛ ɔ hu e ko ngmɛɛ e yo he.
12Se ninɛmɛ nɛ piɛ ɔ, pi Nyɔmtsɛ ɔ, se imi i ngɛ mɛ dee ke: ke nyɛmi ko ngɛ yo ko nɛ he we yi, nɛ kɛ̃ ɔ yo ɔ kplɛɛ kaa e kɛ lɛ maa hi si ɔ, e ko ngmɛɛ e he. 13Nɛ ke yo ko hu ngɛ huno ko nɛ he we yi, nɛ kɛ̃ ɔ nyumu ɔ kplɛɛ kaa e kɛ lɛ maa hi si ɔ, e ko kua lɛ gbami. 14Ejakaa a tsukɔɔ nyumu nɛ he we yi ɔ hu he ngɛ yo ɔ mi, nɛ a tsukɔɔ yo nɛ he we yi ɔ hu he ngɛ huno ɔ mi. Ejakaa ke pi ja jinɛ nyɛ bimɛ ɔmɛ hu a he sɛ mu; se jehanɛ ɔ, a he tsɔ. 15Se ke nɔ nɛ he we yi ɔ ngɛ e he si sae kɛ yaa a, e ya; a yi nyɛmi nyumu lo nyɛmi yo nyɔguɛ ngɛ kikɛmɛ a sane nɛ ɔmɛ a mi. He jɔmi mi Mawu tsɛ wɔ ngɛ. 16Yo, mo o ma he o huno ɔ yi wami jio, o le? Aloo nyumu, mo hu lɛ o ma he o yo ɔ yi wami jio, o le?
Hii si bɔ nɛ Mawu tsɛ mo ɔ
17Bɔ nɛ Mawu dla ngɔ ha nɔ tsuaa nɔ kɛ bɔ nɛ Nyɔmtsɛ ɔ tsɛ nɔ tsuaa nɔ ha a, e hi si ja. Ja i to hulɔ ngɛ asafo ɔmɛ kulaa mi. 18Kɛ a po nɔ ko nɛ a tsɛ lɛ ɔ, e ko pee e he mɔmlɔtɔtsɛ; mɔmlɔtɔ mi a tsɛ nɔ ko ngɛ hu, e ko po e he. 19Nɔpomi pi nɔ́ ko, nɛ mɔmlɔtɔ hu pi nɔ́ ko, se Mawu kita amɛ a nɔ yemi mohu ji nɔ́ nɛ he hia. 20Nɔ tsuaa nɔ tsɛmi nɛ a tsɛ lɛ ɔ, kɔlɔ ɔ mi nɔuu e hi. 21Ke nyɔguɛ ji mo nɛ a tsɛ mo jio, ko ha lɔ ɔ nɛ dɔ mo; se ke o ma nyɛ o he kpɔ ɔ, bɔɔ he mɔde. 22Nɔ nɛ a tsɛ lɛ ngɛ Nyɔmtsɛ ɔ mi nɛ e ji nyɔguɛ ɔ, Nyɔmtsɛ ɔ odehe ʼi. Ja nɔuu kɛ̃ nɔ nɛ a tsɛ lɛ nɛ e ji odehe ɔ, Kristo nyɔguɛ ʼi. 23A he nyɛ kɛ jua wawɛ; nyɛ ko pee nyɛ he nimli a nyɔguɛhi. 24Mamimɛ, nɔ tsuaa nɔ ɔ, nɔ́ mi nɛ a tsɛ lɛ ngɛ ɔ, kɔlɔ ɔ mi nɔuu e hi ngɛ Mawu mi.
Yihewi nɛ gba we kɛ yalɔyi a he sane
25Jehanɛ yihewi nɛ gba we ɔ, i be Nyɔmtsɛ ɔ kita ko ha mɛ, se nɔ́ nɛ wi susuu ɔ i ngɛ dee, kaa nɔ ko nɛ Nyɔmtsɛ ɔ na lɛ mɔbɔ konɛ e ye anɔkuale.
26Jehanɛ, nɔ́ nɛ i susuu kaa e hi ji: Amlɔ nɛ ɔ he hiami nɛ ɔ he ɔ, e hi ha nɔmlɔ kaa e hi si bɔ nɛ e ngɛ ɔ. 27Ke a fi mo mɛtɛ yo he jio, ko hia pɛnemi; a pɛne mo kɛ je yo he jio, ko hia yo. 28Se ke o ngɔ yo hu ɔ, o pee we yayami; nɛ ke yiheyo hu gba a, e pee we yayami; se he lo blɔfami dengme ni nɛ ɔmɛ ma na, se imi lɛɛ, nyɛ he ya i ngɛ foe.
29Mamimɛ, nɔ́ nɛ i ngɛ dee ji kaa, be ɔ pi hu; nɔ́ nɛ piɛ ji kaa, yitsɛmɛ tete a pee kaa ninɛmɛ nɛ be eko; 30nɛ ninɛmɛ nɛ ngɛ ya foe ɔ hu a pee kaa ninɛmɛ nɛ fo we ya; nɛ ninɛmɛ nɛ ngɛ nyae ɔ hu a pee kaa ninɛmɛ nɛ nya we; nɛ ninɛmɛ nɛ heɔ hu a pee kaa ninɛmɛ nɛ be nɔ́ ko; 31nɛ ninɛmɛ nɛ tsuɔ je nɛ ɔ he ni ɔ, a pee kaa ninɛmɛ nɛ tsu we he ni; ejakaa je nɛ ɔ, bɔ nɛ wa naa a bee kɛ yaa.
32Se i suɔ kaa nyɛ ko na haomi. Nɔ nɛ ngɔɛ yo ɔ, e kɛ e he tsuo haa Nyɔmtsɛ ɔ ni tsumi ɔ, bɔ nɛ e maa pee nɛ e sane nɛ sa Nyɔmtsɛ ɔ hɛ mi. 33Se nɔ nɛ ngɛ yo ɔ, haoɔ e he ngɛ je nɛ ɔ mi nihi a he, bɔ nɛ e maa pee nɛ e sane nɛ sa e yo ɔ hɛ mi. 34Eslo yogbayo, nɛ jehanɛ hu eslo zangmayo. Nɔ nɛ gba we ɔ kɛ e he tsuo haa Nyɔmtsɛ ɔ ni tsumi ɔ, konɛ e pee klɔuklɔu ngɛ nɔmlɔ tso kɛ mumi tsuo blɔfami. Se nɔ nɛ gba a haoɔ e he ngɛ je nɛ ɔ mi nihi a he, benɛ pee nɛ e sane nɛ sa e huno hɛ mi.
35Enɛ ɔ lɛɛ nyɛ kpakpa he i ngɛ dee ngɛ, pi nyɛ kuɛ kpa nɛ i ngɛ woe, se mohu benɛ pee nɛ e pee fɛu, konɛ nyɛ sɔmɔ Nyɔmtsɛ ɔ, nɛ nɔ́ ko nɔ́ ko nɛ ko doo nyɛ nya.
36Ke nɔ ko susu kaa e bi yo nɛ nɔ zangma a, e ko wa tsɔ loko e gba, nɛ lɔ ɔ he ɔ e sa nɛ a pee he nɔ́ ko ɔ, e pee bɔ nɛ e suɔ; e pee we yayami ko ke e ya gba. 37Se nɔ nɛ daa si kpɛii ngɛ e tsui mi, nɛ nɔ́ ko nɔ́ ko fi we lɛ, se e ngɛ he wami ngɛ lɛ nitsɛ e suɔmi nɔ ɔ, nɛ e ma nya si ngɛ lɛ nitsɛ e tsui mi kaa e maa baa e bi zangmayo ɔ yi ɔ, e pee saminya. 38Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, nɔ nɛ ngɔ lɛ ha gba a e pee saminya, se nɔ nɛ kɛ lɛ ha we gba a pee saminya pe nɔ kaketsɛ ɔ.
39Yo ɔ, be abɔ nɛ e huno hɛ ngɛ nɛ ɔ ɔ, a kɛ mlaa fi lɛ; se ke e huno ɔ gbo ɔ, e ngɛ he blɔ kaa e gbaa nɔ nɛ e suɔ, se ja a pee ngɛ Nyɔmtsɛ ɔ mi. 40Se ke e hi si bɔ nɛ e ngɛ ɔ, ye juɛmi nya a, e ngɛ bua jɔmi babauu; nɛ e peɔ mi kaa imi hu i ngɛ Mawu mumi.

english_text:
Food Offered to Idols
1In your letter you asked me about food offered to idols. All of us know something about this subject. But knowledge makes us proud of ourselves, while love makes us helpful to others. 2In fact, people who think they know so much don't know anything at all. 3But God has no doubts about who loves him.
4Even though food is offered to idols, we know that none of the idols in this world are alive. After all, there is only one God. 5Many things in heaven and on earth are called gods and lords, but none of them really are gods or lords. 6We have only one God, and he is the Father. He created everything, and we live for him. Jesus Christ is our only Lord. Everything was made by him, and by him life was given to us.
7Not everyone knows these things. In fact, many people have grown up with the belief that idols have life in them. So when they eat meat offered to idols, they are bothered by a weak conscience. 8But food doesn't bring us any closer to God. We are no worse off if we don't eat, and we are no better off if we do.
9Don't cause problems for someone with a weak conscience, just because you have the right to eat anything. 10You know all this, and so it doesn't bother you to eat in the temple of an idol. But suppose a person with a weak conscience sees you and decides to eat food that has been offered to idols. 11Then what you know has destroyed someone Christ died for. 12When you sin by hurting a follower with a weak conscience, you sin against Christ. 13So if I hurt one of the Lord's followers by what I eat, I will never eat meat as long as I live.
translation_text:
Wɔhi a nya bɔsami niyeni
1Jehanɛ ngɛ wɔhi a nya bɔ sami niyeni ɔmɛ a he ɔ, wa le kaa “wɔ kulaa wa le ni.” Ni lemi haa nɔ woɔ e he nɔ, se suɔmi haa nɔ nane nuu si. 2Ke nɔ ko susu kaa e le nɔ́ ko ɔ, e li nɔ́ ko bɔ nɛ sa kaa e le. 3Se ke nɔ ko suɔ Mawu ɔ, lɛ Mawu le.
4Jehanɛ ngɛ wɔhi a nya bɔ sami niyeni a yemi he ɔ, wa le kaa wɔ ko wɔ ko pi nɔ́ ko ngɛ je nɛ ɔ mi, nɛ jehanɛ mawu ko mawu ko be ja Mawu kake kɛkɛ. 5Ejakaa ke ni komɛ ngɛ nɛ a tsɛɛ mɛ “mawuhi” ɔ, hiɔwe a ngɛ jio, zugba a nɔ a ngɛ jio, kaa bɔ nɛ “mawuhi” pɔ he nɛ “nyɔmtsɛmɛ” hu pɔ he ɔ, 6kɛ̃ ɔ wɔɔ lɛɛ, Mawu kaketoo wa ngɛ, Tsɛ ɔ, nɔ mi nɛ nihi kulaa je nɛ wa ngɛ ha lɛ ɔ, kɛ Nyɔmtsɛ kake hu nɛ ji Yesu Kristo ɔ, nɔ nɔ nɛ nihi kulaa gu kɛ ba nɛ wɔ hu wa gu e nɔ ɔ.
7Se kɛ ɔ pi nihi tsuo a mi nɛ kikɛmɛ a ni lemi nɛ ɔ ngɛ. Ni komɛ ngɛ kɛ ba su mwɔnɛ nɛ a kɛ wɔhi a nɔ hemi kɛ yemi yeɔ wɔhi a nya bɔ sami niyeni, nɛ akɛnɛ a he ni lemi gbɔjɔ he je ɔ, a bleɔ lɛ. 8Ngma kɛ wɔ yɛ Mawu hɛ mi; ke wa yeɔ ɔ, e ha we nɛ waa hi pe nine, nɛ jehanɛ ke wa yi hu, wa laa we nɔ ko.
9Nyɛɛ hyɛ nɛ hi konɛ nyɛ he blɔ nɛ ɔ ko ba plɛ kpangmi ha nihi nɛ gbɔjɔ ɔmɛ. 10Ejakaa ke nɔ ko na mo nɛ ji “ni lelɔ” ɔ kaa o hii si ngɛ wɔ piɛ mi ngɛ ni yee ɔ, anɛ pi he wami nɛ o ngɛ nɔ nɛ gbɔjɔ ɔ he ni lemi woe konɛ e ya ye wɔhi a nya bɔ sami niyeni ɔmɛ lo? 11Lɔ ɔ lɛɛ, o “ni lemi” ɔ ma nyɛ ma ha nyɛmi nɛ gbɔjɔ nɛ Kristo ba gbo ngɛ lɛ hu e he ɔ hɛ mi ma kpata. 12Se ke nyɛ peɔ nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ yayami kikɛ, nɛ nyɛɛ kɛ plaa a he ni lemi nɛ he wɛ ɔ, lɔ ɔ lɛɛ Kristo nyɛ ngɛ yayami ɔ pee kɛ ngɛ sie ɔ nɛ. 13Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, ke ngma ma ha ye nyɛmi nane ma kpata a, lɔɔ lɛɛ i be lo yee gblegbleegblee hu, konɛ ma ko ha ye nyɛmi ɔ nane nɛ kpata.

english_text:
The Rights of an Apostle
1I am free. I am an apostle. I have seen the Lord Jesus and have led you to have faith in him. 2Others may think that I am not an apostle, but you are proof that I am an apostle to you.
3When people question me, I tell them 4that Barnabas and I have the right to our food and drink. 5We each have the right to marry one of the Lord's followers and to take her along with us, just as the other apostles and the Lord's brothers and Peter do. 6Are we the only ones who have to support ourselves by working at another job? 7Do soldiers pay their own salaries? Don't people who raise grapes eat some of what they grow? Don't shepherds get milk from their own goats?
8-9 I am not saying this on my own authority. The Law of Moses tells us not to muzzle an ox when it is grinding grain. But was God concerned only about an ox? 10No, he wasn't! He was talking about us. This was written in the Scriptures so that all who plow and all who grind the grain will look forward to sharing in the harvest.
11 When we told the message to you, it was like planting spiritual seed. So we have the right to accept material things as our harvest from you. 12If others have the right to do this, we have an even greater right. But we haven't used this right of ours. We are willing to put up with anything to keep from causing trouble for the message about Christ.
13 Don't you know that people who work in the temple make their living from what is brought to the temple? Don't you know that a person who serves at the altar is given part of what is offered? 14 In the same way, the Lord wants everyone who preaches the good news to make a living from preaching this message.
15But I have never used these privileges of mine, and I am not writing this because I want to start now. I would rather die than have someone rob me of the right to take pride in this. 16I don't have any reason to brag about preaching the good news. Preaching is something God told me to do, and if I don't do it, I am doomed. 17If I preach because I want to, I will be paid. But even if I don't want to, it is still something God has sent me to do. 18What pay am I given? It is the chance to preach the good news free of charge and not to use the privileges that are mine because I am a preacher.
19I am not anyone's slave. But I have become a slave to everyone, so I can win as many people as possible. 20When I am with the Jews, I live like a Jew to win Jews. They are ruled by the Law of Moses, and I am not. But I live by the Law to win them. 21And when I am with people who are not ruled by the Law, I forget about the Law to win them. Of course, I never really forget about the law of God. In fact, I am ruled by the law of Christ. 22When I am with people whose faith is weak, I live as they do to win them. I do everything I can to win everyone I possibly can. 23I do all this for the good news, because I want to share in its blessings.
A Race and a Fight
24 You know that many runners enter a race, and only one of them wins the prize. So run to win! 25 Athletes work hard to win a crown that cannot last, but we do it for a crown that will last forever. 26I don't run without a goal. And I don't box by beating my fists in the air. 27I keep my body under control and make it my slave, so I won't lose out after telling the good news to others.
translation_text:
Bɔfo blɔ nya kɛ e nitsumi
1Anɛ i hɛɛ we ye he lo? Anɛ pi bɔfo ji mi lo? Anɛ i nɛ Yesu Kristo, wa Nyɔmtsɛ ɔ lo? Pi ye nine nya ni tsumi ji nyɛ ngɛ Nyɔmtsɛ ɔ mi lo? 2Ke pi bɔfo ji mi kɛ ha ni kpahi ɔ, nyɛɛ lɛɛ i ji kɛ ha nyɛ; ejakaa ye bɔfo ni tsumi ɔ nya sɔumi nɔ ji nyɛ ngɛ Nyɔmtsɛ ɔ mi.
3Enɛ ɔ ji nɔ́ nɛ i kɛ faa ye he ngɛ nihi nɛ biɔ ye he sane ɔmɛ a hɛ mi. 4Anɛ wa be he blɔ kaa wa yeɔ ni nɛ wa nuu lo? 5Anɛ wa be he blɔ kaa waa kɛ nyɛmi yo nɛ ji wa yo nvɛɛ kaa bɔfo kpa amɛ hu kɛ Nyɔmtsɛ ɔ nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ kɛ Kefa? 6Aloo i kɛ Barnaba kɛkɛ lɛ be he blɔ kaa wa jɔɔ ni tsumi lo? 7Aslaafono te nɛɛ nɛ bɔ lɛ nitsɛ e he apaa kɛ ya ta hyɛ? Mɛnɔ lɛ peɔ wai ngmɔ nɛ e yi e mi yiblii ɔ eko? Aloo mɛnɔ lɛ lɛɛ lohwehi a kuu nɛ e nui a nyɔ nyu ɔ eko?
8Nɔ nɛ i ngɛ dee nɛ ɔ, anɛ nimli kɛkɛ lɛ peɔ ja? Anɛ mlaa hu de we ja nɔuu lo? 9Ejakaa a ngma ngɛ Mose Mlaa a mi ke: “Koo wo na nɛ gblɛɛ blɛfo ɔ nya kotoku.” Anɛ nahi a he nɛ dɔɔ Mawu he je 10nɛ pi wa he munyu nɛ e ngɛ tue nɛ ɔ lo? Ejakaa wa he nɔuu nɛ a ngma ke, nɔ nɛ huɔ ɔ, e kɛ hɛ kɛ nɔ fɔmi nɛ hu, nɛ nɔ nɛ hluɛɛ blɛfo hu e hɛ nɛ hi nɔ kaa e maa ye eko. 11Ke wɔɔ lɛɛ wa duɔ mumi mi nihi haa nyɛ ɔ, anɛ e ji nɔ ko tsɔ kaa wa ma kpa he lo mi nihi lo? 12Jehanɛ hu ke ni kpahi ngɛ kikɛmɛ a he blɔ ngɛ nyɛ nɔ ɔ, anɛ pi wɔ mohu nɛ wa ngɛ pe mɛ po lo? Se kɛ ɔ, wa pee we kikɛmɛ a he blɔ nɛ ɔ he nɔ ko, se mohu wa to wa tsui si ngɛ nɔ tsuaa nɔ mi, konɛ wa ko tsi Kristo Sane Kpakpa a blɔ? 13Anɛ nyɛ li kaa nihi nɛ tsuɔ ni ngɛ sɔlemi we ɔ, sɔlemi we ni ɔmɛ eko nɔuu a yeɔ lo? Nɛ ninɛmɛ nɛ sɔmɔɔ ngɛ bɔ sami latɛ ɔ he ɔ, bɔ sami latɛ ɔ nɔ ni ɔmɛ eko nɔuu a naa lo? 14Jã nɔuu kɛ Nyɔmtsɛ ɔ to kaa ninɛmɛ nɛ jajeɔ Sane Kpakpa a, a ye sane kpakpa a he ni.
15Se imi lɛɛ, i pee we kikɛmɛ a ni nɛ ɔmɛ kake po he nɔ ko. Nɛ i ngmɛ́ enɛ ɔ konɛ a pee ja ngɔ ha mi, ejakaa ke ka nɔ́ nɛ nɔ ko ma ha ye fiami ɔ nɛ pee yaka a, afani nɛ i gbo mohu. 16Ejakaa ke i jaje sane kpakpa a po hu ɔ, e pee we mi fiami; ejakaa a ngɔ fi ye nɔ kaa ma jaje, ejakaa ke i jaje we sane kpakpa a, kusiɛ ha mi! 17Ejakaa ke imi nitsɛ ye suɔmi nya nɛ i tsu enɛ ɔ ɔ, i ngɛ hiɔwo, se ke pi suɔmi nya tete ɔ, a tu sɔmɔlɔ nɔkɔtɔma yemi ni tsumi ngɔ wo ye dɛ kɛ̃. 18Jehanɛ mɛni ji ye hiɔwo mɔ? Lɔ ɔ ji kaa ke i ngɛ sane kpakpa a jajee ɔ, ma jaje lɛ yaka, nɛ i he we nɔ ko ngɛ Kristo Sane Kpakpa a he, benɛ pee nɛ ma ko pee ye he blɔ nɛ i ngɛ ngɛ Sane Kpakpa a fiɛmi mi ɔ he nɔ ko tsɔ ko.
19Pohu i hɛɛ ye he nɛ i pi nɔ ko nɔ ko nyɔguɛ, kɛ̃ ɔ, i kɛ ye he pee nihi tsuo a sɔmɔlɔ, benɛ pee nɛ ye nine nɛ su nihi babauu a nɔ. 20I plɛ Yudafono ha Yudafo ɔmɛ benɛ pee nɛ ye nine nɛ su Yudafohi a nɔ. Ninɛmɛ nɛ ngɛ mlaa sisi hulɔ ɔ, i pee kaa nɔ ko nɛ ngɛ mlaa sisi ngɔ ha mɛ, pohu imi nitsɛ ɔ, i be mlaa sisi, benɛ pee nɛ ye nine nɛ su ninɛmɛ nɛ ngɛ mlaa sisi ɔmɛ a nɔ. 21I plɛ kaa nɔ ko nɛ be mlaa ngɔ ha ninɛmɛ nɛ be mlaa a, pohu i pi nɔ ko nɛ be Mawu mlaa; se mohu i ngɛ Kristo mlaa sisi, benɛ pee nɛ ye nine nɛ su ninɛmɛ nɛ be mlaa amɛ a nɔ. 22I plɛ kaa nɔ nɛ gbɔjɔ ha gbɔjɔli ɔmɛ benɛ pee nɛ ye nine nɛ su gbɔjɔli ɔmɛ a nɔ. I plɛ ye he nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ ngɔ ha nihi kulaa konɛ bɔ tsuaa bɔ nɛ pee ɔ ma kɛ he ni komɛ a yi wami.
23Sane Kpakpa a he nɛ i peɔ enɛ ɔmɛ kulaa ngɛ, benɛ pee nɛ imi hu ma na e mi ni ɔmɛ eko. 24Anɛ nyɛ li kaa ninɛmɛ nɛ tuu fo ɔ, mɛ kulaa a tuu mohu se nɔ kake kɛkɛ nɛ naa ayekoo ni ɔ lo? Nyɛɛ tu fo ɔ ja konɛ nyɛ nine nɛ su nɔ. 25Nɔ tsuaa nɔ hu nɛ kaa e he mi kɛ kunɔ ɔ, e hɛ kaa si ngɛ nihi kulaa mi. Jehanɛ mɛɛ lɛɛ a peɔ ja konɛ a na jlasi nɛ puɛɔ, se wɔɔ lɛɛ konɛ wa na nɔ nɛ puɛ we. 26Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, fo nɛ i ngɛ tue nɛ ɔ, i tui lɛ putuputu; kunɔ nɛ i ngɛ nɔe nɛ ɔ, pi kɔɔhiɔ nɛ i kɛ ngɛ nɔe; 27se mohu i gbaa imi nitsɛ ye nɔmlɔ tso ɔ mahi nɛ i yeɔ lɛ nyɔguɛ, konɛ imi nɛ i fiɛɛ ngɔ tsɔɔ ni kpahi ɔ, imi nitsɛ lɛɛ a ko sake mi ngɔ fɔ he.

english_text:
Don't Worship Idols
1 Friends, I want to remind you that all our ancestors walked under the cloud and went through the sea. 2This was like being baptized and becoming followers of Moses. 3 All of them also ate the same spiritual food 4 and drank the same spiritual drink, which flowed from the spiritual rock that followed them. That rock was Christ. 5 But most of them did not please God. So they died, and their bodies were scattered all over the desert.
6What happened to them is a warning to keep us from wanting to do the same evil things. 7 They worshiped idols, just as the Scriptures say, “The people sat down to eat and drink. Then they got up to dance around.” So don't worship idols. 8 Some of those people did shameful things, and in a single day about 23,000 died. Don't do shameful things as they did. 9 And don't try to test Christ, as some of them did and were later bitten by poisonous snakes. 10 Don't even grumble, as some of them did and were killed by the destroying angel. 11These things happened to them as a warning to us. All this was written in the Scriptures to teach us who live in these last days.
12Even if you think you can stand up to temptation, be careful not to fall. 13 You are tempted in the same way that everyone else is tempted. But God can be trusted not to let you be tempted too much, and he will show you how to escape from your temptations.
14My friends, you must keep away from idols. 15I am speaking to you as people who have enough sense to know what I am talking about. 16 When we drink from the cup we ask God to bless, isn't that sharing in the blood of Christ? When we eat the bread we break, isn't that sharing in the body of Christ? 17By sharing in the same loaf of bread, we become one body, even though there are many of us.
18 Aren't the people of Israel sharing in the worship when they gather around the altar and eat the sacrifices offered there? 19Am I saying that either the idols or the food sacrificed to them is anything at all? 20 No, I am not! This food is really sacrificed to demons and not to God. I don't want you to have anything to do with demons. 21You cannot drink from the cup of demons and still drink from the Lord's cup. You cannot eat at the table of demons and still eat at the Lord's table. 22 We would make the Lord jealous if we did this. And we are not stronger than the Lord.
Always Honor God
23 Some of you say, “We can do whatever we want to!” But I tell you not everything may be good or helpful. 24We should think about others and not about ourselves. 25However, when you buy meat in the market, go ahead and eat it. Keep your conscience clear by not asking where the meat came from. 26 The Scriptures say, “The earth and everything in it belong to the Lord.”
27If an unbeliever invites you to dinner, and you want to go, then go. Eat whatever you are served. Don't cause a problem for someone's conscience by asking where the food came from. 28-29But if you are told it has been sacrificed to idols, don't cause a problem by eating it. I don't mean a problem for yourself, but for the one who told you. Why should my freedom be limited by someone else's conscience? 30If I give thanks for what I eat, why should anyone accuse me of doing wrong?
31When you eat or drink or do anything else, always do it to honor God. 32Don't cause problems for Jews or Greeks or anyone else who belongs to God's church. 33I always try to please others instead of myself, in the hope that many of them will be saved.
translation_text:
Amagahi a he kɔkɔbɔmi
1Se, mamimɛ, i suɔ kaa nyɛ kai kaa wa tsɛmɛ ɔmɛ tsuo hi bɔ ku ɔ sisi, nɛ mɛ tsuo a po wo ɔ, 2nɛ a baptisi mɛ kulaa ngɔ wo Mose mi ngɛ bɔ ku ɔ kɛ wo ɔ mi, 3nɛ mɛ kulaa a, mumi mi niyeni kake ɔ nɔuu a ye, 4nɛ mɛ kulaa a nu mumi mi tɛ sa nɛ kɛ mɛ nyɛɛ ɔ mi nyu, nɛ tɛ sa a ji Kristo? 5Se kɛ̃ ɔ Mawu na we a ti nihi fuu a he tsui, ejakaa a kpata a hɛ mi ngɛ nga a nɔ.
6Se a kɛ enɛ ɔmɛ to wɔ okadi konɛ wa ko ha ni yayahi nɛ pee wɔ akɔnɔ kaa bɔ nɛ e pee mɛ ɔ. 7Jehanɛ hu nyɛ ko plɛ amaga jali kaa a ti ni komɛ pee ɔ, kaa bɔ nɛ a ngma a ke: “Ma a be hi si, nɛ a ye ni, nɛ a nu da, kɛkɛ nɛ a te si nɛ a bɔni fiɛmi.” 8Nɛ jehanɛ hu wa ko bɔ ajuama kaa bɔ nɛ a ti ni komɛ bɔ nɛ ligbi kake nɔ ɔ nihi akpe nyingmi enyɔ kɛ etɛ yi tã a. 9Nɛ jehanɛ hu wa ko ka Nyɔmtsɛ ɔ kaa bɔ nɛ a ti ni komɛ ka lɛ nɛ sinɔhi ba kpata a hɛ mi ɔ. 10Nɛ jehanɛ hu nyɛ ko tu munyu huitihuiti kaa bɔ nɛ a ti ni komɛ tu munyu huitihuiti nɛ nɔ́ puɛlɔ ɔ ba kpata a hɛ mi ɔ.
11A pee mɛ enɛ ɔmɛ kulaa nɛ a kɛ to okadi ha ni kpahi; nɛ a ngma kaa kɔkɔ bɔmi nɔ́ kɛ ha wɔ, wɔ nihi nɛ je ɔ nyagbe ligbi ɔmɛ na wɔ ɔ; 12benɛ pee nɛ nɔ nɛ susuu kaa e daa si ɔ, e hyɛ e he nɛ hi konɛ e ko nɔ si. 13Ka ko bɛ nyɛ nɔ nɛ pi nɔmlɔ he nɔ́; se anɔkualetsɛ ji Mawu, nɔ nɛ be hae nɛ a ka nyɛ pe bɔ nɛ nyɛ ma nyɛ, se mohu e kɛ ka a nɔuu maa je blɔ ha nyɛ nɛ nyɛɛ je mi hulɔ, konɛ nyɛ nyɛ nya nɛ nyɛɛ da.
14Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, mamimɛ, nyɛɛ tu wɔ jami nya fo! 15I kɛ nyɛ ngɛ munyu tue kaa a kɛ ni leli tuɔ munyu; nyɛ nitsɛmɛ nyɛ kɔ nɔ nɛ i ngɛ dee ɔ se. 16Gbaami kplu ɔ nɛ wa gbaa a, anɛ pi waa kɛ Kristo kake peemi ngɛ e muɔ ɔ mi lo? Abolo nɛ wa kuɔ ɔ, anɛ pi waa kɛ Kristo kake peemi ngɛ e nɔmlɔ tso ɔ mi lo? 17Ejakaa abolo kake ʼi, nɛ wɔ fuu ɔ, nɔmlɔ tso kake ji wɔ, ejakaa wɔ kulaa wa yeɔ abolo kake ɔ eko.
18Nyɛɛ hyɛ he lo blɔfami Israel ɔ; anɛ nihi nɛ yeɔ bɔ sami ni ɔmɛ ɔ pi huɛ nɛ a kɛ bɔ sami latɛ ɔ ngɛ bɔe ɔ lo? 19Lɛɛ kɛ i ngɛ tsɔɔe kɛɛ ɔ? Kaa amaga ji nɔ ko, aloo kaa amaga bɔ ji nɔ ko? 20Dɛbi, se mohu i ngɛ dee ke bɔ nɛ wɔ jali ɔmɛ saa a, mumi yayamihi a saa ngɔ haa se pi Mawu; se i sume kaa nyɛɛ kɛ mumi yayamihi bɔɔ huɛ. 21Nyɛ be Nyɔmtsɛ ɔ kplu ɔ kɛ mumi yayamihi a kplu ɔ nyɛe maa nu si kake. Nyɛ be Nyɔmtsɛ ɔ okplɔɔ ɔ nɔ ni kɛ mumi yayamihi a nɔ ɔ nɔ ni nyɛe maa ye si kake. 22Aloo Nyɔmtsɛ ɔ mi mi la wa ngɛ woe? Anɛ wa he wa pe lɛ lo?
23“Wa ngɛ nihi tsuo he blɔ,” se pi nihi tsuo nɛ hi. “Wa ngɛ nihi tsuo he blɔ,” se pi nihi tsuo nɛ haa nɔ nane nuu si. 24Nɔ ko nɔ ko nɛ ko plee ngɔ ha lɛ nitsɛ e he, se mohu nɔ tsuaa nɔ nɛ plee ngɔ ha e nyɛmi.
25Nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ a ngɛ juae ngɛ lo jua nɔ ɔ, nyɛɛ ye; se he ni lemi he ɔ, nyɛ ko bi mi; 26ejakaa “zugba a kɛ e mi ni ɔmɛ kulaa a, Nyɔmtsɛ ɔ nɔ ʼi.”
27Ke nihi nɛ he we yi ɔmɛ a ti nɔ ko kpee nyɛ ni yemi nɛ nyɛ suɔ kaa nyɛ maa ya a, nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ a kɛ maa ma nyɛ hɛ mi ɔ, nyɛɛ ye nɛ nyɛ ko bi mi, ngɛ he ni lemi he. 28Se ke nɔ ko de nyɛ ke: “Enɛ ɔ lɛɛ amaga bɔ sami nihi ʼi” ɔ, nyɛ ko ye ngɛ nɔ nɛ wo nyɛ tue nɔ ɔ kɛ he ni lemi he je. 29Se he ni lemi nɛ i ngɛ dee nɛ ɔ ɔ, pi mo nitsɛ o nɔ ɔ, se mohu nɔ kpa nɔ ɔ. Se mɛ he je nɔ kpa he ni lemi maa kojo ye he yemi ɔ? 30Ke sina i kɛ ye ɔ, mɛ he je a tuɔ ye he munyu yaya ngɛ nihi nɛ i na si ngɛ he ɔmɛ a he?
31Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, ke ni nyɛ ngɛ yee jio, ni nyɛ ngɛ nue jio, aloo nɔ kpa ko nɛ nyɛ ngɛ pee jio, nyɛɛ pee kulaa kɛ wo Mawu hɛ mi nyami. 32Nyɛ ko pee kpangmi ngɔ ha Yudafohi kɛ Helabihi kɛ Mawu asafo ɔ kulaa; 33kaa bɔ nɛ imi hu i suɔ kaa nihi kulaa mi ɔ ma sa nihi kulaa a hɛ mi, nɛ i hla we nɔ́ nɛ hi ha imi nitsɛ ye he, se mohu nɔ́ nɛ hi ha nihi fuu, konɛ a he a yiwami.

english_text:
1 You must follow my example, as I follow the example of Christ.
Rules for Worship
2I am proud of you, because you always remember me and obey the teachings I gave you. 3Now I want you to know that Christ is the head of all men, and a man is the head of a woman. But God is the head of Christ. 4This means that any man who prays or prophesies with something on his head brings shame to his head.
5But any woman who prays or prophesies without something on her head brings shame to her head. In fact, she may as well shave her head. 6A woman should wear something on her head. It is a disgrace for a woman to shave her head or cut her hair. But if she refuses to wear something on her head, let her cut off her hair.
7 Men were created to be like God and to bring honor to God. This means a man should not wear anything on his head. Women were created to bring honor to men. 8 It was the woman who was made from a man, and not the man who was made from a woman. 9He wasn't created for her. She was created for him. 10And so, because of this, and also because of the angels, a woman ought to wear something on her head, as a sign of her authority.
11As far as the Lord is concerned, men and women need each other. 12It is true that the first woman came from a man, but all other men have been given birth by women. Yet God is the one who created everything. 13Ask yourselves if it is proper for a woman to pray without something on her head. 14Isn't it unnatural and disgraceful for men to have long hair? 15But long hair is a beautiful way for a woman to cover her head. 16This is how things are done in all of God's churches, and this is why none of you should argue about what I have said.
Rules for the Lord's Supper
17Your worship services do you more harm than good. I am certainly not going to praise you for this. 18I am told you can't get along with each other when you worship, and I am sure that some of what I have heard is true. 19You are bound to argue with each other, but it is easy to see which of you have God's approval.
20When you meet together, you don't really celebrate the Lord's Supper. 21You even start eating before everyone gets to the meeting, and some of you go hungry, while others get drunk. 22Don't you have homes where you can eat and drink? Do you hate God's church? Do you want to embarrass people who don't have anything? What can I say to you? I certainly cannot praise you.
The Lord's Supper
(Matthew 26.26-29; Mark 14.22-25; Luke 22.14-20)
23I have already told you what the Lord Jesus did on the night he was betrayed. And it came from the Lord himself.
He took some bread in his hands. 24Then after he had given thanks, he broke it and said, “This is my body, which is given for you. Eat this and remember me.”
25 After the meal, Jesus took a cup of wine in his hands and said, “This is my blood, and with it God makes his new agreement with you. Drink this and remember me.”
26The Lord meant that when you eat this bread and drink from this cup, you tell about his death until he comes.
27But if you eat the bread and drink the wine in a way that isn't worthy of the Lord, you sin against his body and blood. 28This is why you must examine the way you eat and drink. 29If you fail to understand that you are the body of the Lord, you will condemn yourselves by the way you eat and drink. 30This is why many of you are sick and weak and why a lot of others have died. 31If we carefully judge ourselves, we won't be punished. 32But when the Lord judges and punishes us, he does it to keep us from being condemned with the rest of the world.
33My dear friends, you should wait until everyone gets there before you start eating. 34If you really are hungry, you can eat at home. Then you won't condemn yourselves when you meet together.
After I arrive, I will instruct you about the other matters.
translation_text:
Yinɔhami ngɛ sɔlemi
1Nyɛɛ kase mi kaa bɔ nɛ imi hu i kaseɔ Kristo ɔ. 2Se, mamimɛ, i ngɛ nyɛ yi jee kaa nyɛ kaii mi ngɛ nihi tsuo mi, nɛ tsɔɔmihi nɛ i kɛ ha nyɛ ɔ, nyɛ hɛɛ mi bɔ pɛ nɛ i kɛ ha nyɛ ɔ. 3Se i suo kaa nyɛɛ le kaa nyumu tsuaa nyumu yi ji Kristo, nɛ yo tsuaa yo hu yi ji nyumu, nɛ Kristo yi ji Mawu. 4Nyumu nɛ sɔlee aloo e gbaa nɛ e kɛ nɔ́ ko haa e yi ɔ nɔ ɔ, e ngɛ e yi ɔ he guɛ gbee. 5Se yo tsuaa yo nɛ sɔlee aloo e gbaa nɛ e hɛ̃ɛ e yi ɔ nɔ gu ɔ, lɛ hu e ngɛ e yi ɔ he guɛ gbee; ejakaa e ngɛ kaa nɔ́ nɛ e sɛ e yi nɔuu kɛ. 6Ejakaa ke yo hɛ́ e yi ɔ nɔ ɔ, lɛɛ e sã e yi ɔ nɔ mɔ. Se ke e ngɛ lɛ zo pee kaa e ma sã eyi ɔ nɔ loo e maa sɛ e yi ɔ, lɛɛ e ha e yi ɔ nɔ mɔ. 7Se nyumu lɛɛ, e sɛ kaa e haa e yi ɔ nɔ, ejakaa Mawu subai kɛ e hɛ mi nyami ji lɛ; se yo lɛɛ, nyumu hɛ mi nyami ji lɛ. 8Ejakaa nyumu ji yo mi, se yo mohu lɛɛ je nyumu mi. 9Nɛ jehanɛ hu, a bɔɛ nyumu ngɛ yo he se yo mohu a bɔ ngɛ nyumu he. 10Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, ngɛ hiɔwe bɔfo ɔmɛ a he ɔ, e sa nɛ yo nɛ na he wami he okadi ko ngɛ e vi ɔ nɔ. 11Ngɛ Nyɔmtsɛ ɔ mi ɔ, nyumu ko si yo se, nɛ ɔ hu ko si nyumu se. 12Ejakaa kaa bɔ nɛ yo je nyumu mi ɔ, ja nɔuu kɛ nyumu hu gu yo mi kɛ ba; se nihi kulaa je Mawu mi.
13Nyɛ nitsɛmɛ nyɛ hla mi ngɛ nyɛ kpɛti. Anɛ e ngɛ fɛu kaa yo maa sɔle ngɛ Mawu hɛ mi nɛ e hɛ́ e yi nɔ lo? 14Anɛ fɔmi su nitsɛ tsɔɔ we nyɛ kaa, ke nyumu fia e yi kusuu ɔ, e ngɛ zo ha lɛ, 15se yo lɛɛ ke e fia e yi kusuu ɔ, e ji hɛ mi nyami ha lɛ lo? Ejakaa a kɛ yi bwɔmi ɔ ha lɛ kaa he hami nɔ. 16Se ke nɔ ko suɔ kaa e pee e he nya sãlɔ ngɛ enɛ ɔ he ɔ, wɔɔ lɛɛ wa pee we ja, nɛ Mawu asafo ɔmɛ hu pee we ja.
Nyɔmtsɛ Niyeni ɔ
17Kita nɛ i ngɛ nyɛ woe nɛ ɔ, pi nyɛ yi nɛ i kɛ ngɛ jee, ejakaa ke nyɛ kpe ɔ, nɔ́ kpakpa ko ji mi, se mohu nɔ́ yaya lɛ jee mi. 18Se kekleekle ɔ, i nuɔ kaa ke nyɛ ya bua nyɛ he nyɛ ngɛ asafo ɔ mi ɔ, mi gbamihi ngɛ nyɛ kpɛti, nɛ i heɔ yeɔ fã kɛ fã; 19ejakaa e sa kaa migbami nɛ te si ngɛ nyɛ kpɛti konɛ ni kpakpa amɛ a je a he si paa ngɛ nyɛ kpɛti. 20Jehanɛ ke nyɛ nya ba bua ngɛ he kake ɔ, pi Nyɔmtsɛ Niyeni ɔ yemi nɛ nyɛ ba; 21ejakaa kikɛmɛ a nyɛ ni yemi nɛ ɔ mi ɔ, nɔ tsuaa nɔ ngɔɔ lɛ nitsɛ e ni ye ni nɛ e yeɔ, nɛ benɛ hwɔ ngɛ nɔ ko yee ɔ, blɔɔ nɔ ko de da. 22Anɛ nyɛ be wehi nɛ nyɛ maa ye ni nɛ nyɛ maa nu ngɛ lejɛ ɔmɛ lo? Aloo Mawu asafo ɔ he guɛ nyɛ ngɛ gbee, nɛ nyɛ ngɛ nihi nɛ be nɔ́ ko ɔmɛ a hɛ mi si puee ɔ? Kɛ ma de nyɛ kɛɛ? Ma je nyɛ yi lo? Enɛ ɔ lɛɛ i be nyɛ yi jee ngɛ he.
23Ejakaa imi nitsɛ nɔ́ nɛ i na kɛ je Nyɔmtsɛ dɛ mi nɛ i kɛ ha nyɛ ɔ ji nɛ ɔ nɛ, kaa: Nyɔmtsɛ Yesu ɔ, jamɛ a nyɔ ɔ mi nɔuu nɛ a tsɔɔ e se blɔ ɔ, e kɛ̃ abolo, 24nɛ e na si, nɛ e kuɔ mi, nɛ e ke: “Enɛ ɔ ji ye nɔmlɔ tso nɛ a kuɔ ngɛ nyɛ ke. Nyɛɛ pee e nɛ ɔ nɛ nyɛ kɛ kai mi.” 25Ja nɔuu e wo kplu ɔ hu ngɛ niyeni ɔ se, nɛ e ke: “Kikɛmɛ a kplu nɛ ɔ ji somi he ɔ ngɛ ye muɔ ɔ mi. Nyɛɛ pee enɛ ɔ; si abɔ nɛ nyɛ maa nu ɔ nɛ nyɛ kɛ kai mi.” 26Ejakaa si abɔ nɛ nyɛ yeɔ kikɛmɛ a bolo nɛ ɔ, nɛ nyɛ nuu kikɛmɛ a kplu nɛ ɔ hulɔ ɔ, nyɛ ngɛ Nyɔmtsɛ ɔ gbenɔ ɔ jajee kɛ ngɛ tsɔɔe kɛ maa su be nɛ e maa ba.
27Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, nɔ tsuaa nɔ nɛ yeɔ kikɛmɛ a abolo nɛ ɔ nɛ e nuu Nyɔmtsɛ ɔ kplu ɔ bɔ nɛ sɛ́ ɔ, e ngɛ Nyɔmtsɛ ɔ nɔmlɔ tso ɔ kɛ e muɔ ɔ nɔ tɔe. 28Nɔmlɔ nɛ ka lɛ nitsɛ e he loko e ye abolo nɛ ɔ eko nɛ e nu kplu nɛ ɔ eko; 29ejakaa nɔ nɛ yeɔ nɛ e nuu bɔ nɛ sɛ́ ɔ, kojomi mohu e yeɔ nɛ e nuu haa e he ejakaa e bui Nyɔmtsɛ e nɔmlɔ tso ɔ. 30Kɔlɔ ɔ he hu nɛ nyɛ ti nihi fuu ngɛ gboe nɛ a he wɛ mɛ, nɛ nihi babauu hu gbo nɛ ɔ nɛ. 31Se e ji wa kaa wɔ nitsɛmɛ wa he hyɛɛ jinɛ a be wɔ kojoe. 32Se ke a kojo wɔ ɔ, Nyɔmtsɛ ɔ tsɔsemi ʼi, benɛ pee nɛ a ko bu wɔ kɛ je ɔ kulaa fɔ.
33Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, mamimɛ, ke nyɛ nya ba bua nɛ nyɛ maa ye ni ɔ, nyɛɛ mlɛ nyɛ sibi. 34Se ke hwɔ ngɛ nɔ ko yee ɔ, e ye ni ngɛ we mi lolo, benɛ pee nɛ nyɛ he nya buami ɔ ko tsɛ kojomi ha nyɛ. Nihi nɛ piɛ ɔmɛ ɔ, ke i ba a, ma to mɛ blɔ nɔ.

english_text:
Spiritual Gifts
1My friends, you asked me about spiritual gifts. 2I want you to remember that before you became followers of the Lord, you were led in all the wrong ways by idols that cannot even talk. 3Now I want you to know that if you are led by God's Spirit, you will say that Jesus is Lord, and you will never curse Jesus.
4 There are different kinds of spiritual gifts, but they all come from the same Spirit. 5There are different ways to serve the same Lord, 6and we can each do different things. Yet the same God works in all of us and helps us in everything we do.
7The Spirit has given each of us a special way of serving others. 8Some of us can speak with wisdom, while others can speak with knowledge, but these gifts come from the same Spirit. 9To others the Spirit has given great faith or the power to heal the sick 10or the power to work mighty miracles. Some of us are prophets, and some of us recognize when God's Spirit is present. Others can speak different kinds of languages, and still others can tell what these languages mean. 11But it is the Spirit who does all this and decides which gifts to give to each of us.
One Body with Many Parts
12 The body of Christ has many different parts, just as any other body does. 13Some of us are Jews, and others are Gentiles. Some of us are slaves, and others are free. But God's Spirit baptized each of us and made us part of the body of Christ. Now we each drink from that same Spirit.
14Our bodies don't have just one part. They have many parts. 15Suppose a foot says, “I'm not a hand, and so I'm not part of the body.” Wouldn't the foot still belong to the body? 16Or suppose an ear says, “I'm not an eye, and so I'm not part of the body.” Wouldn't the ear still belong to the body? 17If our bodies were only an eye, we couldn't hear a thing. And if they were only an ear, we couldn't smell a thing. 18But God has put all parts of our body together in the way that he decided is best.
19A body isn't really a body, unless there is more than one part. 20It takes many parts to make a single body. 21That's why the eyes cannot say they don't need the hands. That's also why the head cannot say it doesn't need the feet. 22In fact, we cannot get along without the parts of the body that seem to be the weakest. 23We take special care to dress up some parts of our bodies. We are modest about our personal parts, 24but we don't have to be modest about other parts.
God put our bodies together in such a way that even the parts that seem the least important are valuable. 25He did this to make all parts of the body work together smoothly, with each part caring about the others. 26If one part of our body hurts, we hurt all over. If one part of our body is honored, the whole body will be happy.
27Together you are the body of Christ. Each one of you is part of his body. 28 First, God chose some people to be apostles and prophets and teachers for the church. But he also chose some to work miracles or heal the sick or help others or be leaders or speak different kinds of languages. 29Not everyone is an apostle. Not everyone is a prophet. Not everyone is a teacher. Not everyone can work miracles. 30Not everyone can heal the sick. Not everyone can speak different kinds of languages. Not everyone can tell what these languages mean. 31I want you to desire the best gifts. So I will show you a much better way.
translation_text:
Mumi mi dloomi nike nihi
1Jehanɛ, mamimɛ, i suɔ kaa ma ha nyɛɛ le nɔ́ ko ngɛ mumi mi nihi a he. 2Nyɛ le kaa benɛ nyɛ ji wɔ jali ɔ, amaga mumuihi a ngɔ a kpaka nyɛ kɛ ya, bɔ tsuaa bɔ nɛ a kpaka nyɛ ha a. 3Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, i ngɛ hae nɛ nyɛɛ le kaa, nɔ nɛ tuɔ munyu ngɛ Mawu mumi mi ɔ, de we ke Yesu ɔ musutsɛ ji lɛ, nɛ nɔ ko be nyɛe ma de ke Yesu ji Nyɔmtsɛ hulɔ, kaa ja Mumi Klɔuklɔu ɔ kpaka lɛ.
4Dloomi nike nihi slɔɔtohi ngɛ, se mumi kake ɔ nɔuu lɛ haa. 5Sɔmɔmi ni tsumihi slɔɔtohi hu ngɛ, se Nyɔmtsɛ kake ɔ nɔuu a kɛ sɔmɔɔ; 6nɛ ni tsumihi slɔɔtohi hu ngɛ, se Mawu kake ɔ nɔuu ji nɔ nɛ tsuo kulaa ngɛ nihi kulaa mi. 7Se nɔ tsuaa nɔ ɔ, a haa Mumi ɔ jeɔ e he kpo ngɛ e mi konɛ e hi ha nihi. 8Mumi ɔ haa nɔ ko ni lemi munyu; nɛ nɔ ko hu jamɛ a Mumi ɔ nɔuu haa lɛ nihi a sisi nami he ni lemi. 9Lɛ Mumi ɔ nɔuu haa nɔ ko hemi kɛ yemi; nɛ nɔ kpa hu tsami dloomi nike nihi, 10Nɔ ko ɔ, he wami nihi a tsumi; nɔ ko ɔ gbami; nɔ ko hu mumihi a si kpami; nɔ ko hu gbi slɔɔtohi a tumi; nɛ nɔ kpa hu munyuhi a sisi tsɔɔmi. 11Se kikɛmɛ a ni nɛ ɔmɛ kulaa a, Mumi kake ɔ nɔuu lɛ tsuo, nɛ e dlaa ngɔ haa nɔ tsuaa nɔ kakaaka, bɔ nɛ e suɔ.
Nɔmlɔ tso kake kɛ e he nihi slɔɔtohi
12Ejakaa kaa bɔ nɛ nɔmlɔ tso ɔ kake ʼi, se e hɛɛ he nihi fuu, nɛ nɔmlɔ tso ɔ he nihi fuu ɔ kulaa ji nɔmlɔ tso kake ɔ, ja nɔuu hu ji Kristo. 13Ejakaa Yudafohi ji wɔ jio, Helabihi ji wɔ jio, nyɔguɛhi jio, he yeli jio, wɔ tsuo ɔ Mumi kake mi a gu a baptisi wɔ ngɔ wo nɔmlɔ tso kake mi; nɛ wɔ tsuo Mumi kake akɛ ha wɔ nɛ waa nu.
14Ejakaa nɔmlɔ tso ɔ hu pi he nɔ kake ʼi, se fuu ʼi. 15Ke nane ma de ke: “Akɛnɛ i pi nine he je ɔ, i pi nɔmlɔ tso ɔ he ni ɔmɛ eko” ɔ, anɛ enɛ ɔ he je ɔ, e pi nɔmlɔ tso ɔ he ni ɔmɛ eko lo? 16Nɛ ke tue hu ma de ke: “Akɛnɛ i pi hɛngmɛ he je ɔ, i pi nɔmlɔ tso ɔ he ni ɔmɛ eko” ɔ, anɛ enɛ ɔ he je ɔ, e pi nɔmlɔ tso ɔ he ni ɔmɛ eko lo? 17Ke nɔmlɔ tso mluku ɔ kulaa ji hɛngmɛ ɔ, jije nɔ numi ngɛ? Ke nɔ numi sɔuu ʼi ɔ, jije nɔ he fu numi ɔ ngɛ? 18Se jehanɛ Mawu kɛ he nɔ́ tsuaa he nɔ́ ma nɔmlɔ tso ɔ he bɔ nɛ e suɔ. 19Se ke mɛ kulaa ji he nɔ́ kake ɔ, jije nɔmlɔ tso ɔ ngɛ? 20Se jehanɛ he nihi fuu ʼi mohu, se nɔmlɔ tso kake ʼi.
21Hɛngmɛ be nyɛe ma de nine ke: “I be o he ni tsumi;” nɛ jehanɛ hu yi be nyɛe ma de nanehi ke: “I be nyɛ he ni tsumi.” 22Nɔmlɔ tso ɔ he nihi nɛ peɔ wɔ kaa a he wɛ́ kulaa a, mɛ mohu a he hiaa wɔ titli, 23nɛ nihi nɛ e peɔ wɔ kaa a ji nɔmlɔ tso he nihi nɛ hɛ mi be nyami kulaa a, kɔlɔ ɔmɛ titli a hɛ mi nyami wa woɔ, nɛ wa he nihi nɛ be fɛu ɔ mohu naa he fɛu; 24se wa he nihi nɛ ngɛ fɛu momo ɔ, a hia we hɛ mi nyami womi. Se Mawu tsla nɔmlɔ tso ɔ ngɛ blɔ nɔ nɛ nɔ́ nɛ piɛ lɛ nɔ́ ko ɔ, kɔlɔ ɔ titli e kɛ bu haa; 25konɛ mi gbami nɛ ko ba nɔmlɔ tso ɔ mi, se mohu he ni ɔmɛ nɛ baa a sibi a yi pɛpɛɛpɛ. 26Nɛ ke he nɔ kake ngɛ nɔ nae ɔ, he ni ɔmɛ kulaa kɛ lɛ naa nɔ. Nɛ ke he nɔ kake hɛ mi ba nyami hu, he ni ɔmɛ kulaa kɛ lɛ naa bua jɔmi.
27Jehanɛ nyɛ tsuo ɔ, Kristo nɔmlɔ tso ji nyɛ, nɛ kakaaka a, e he nihi. 28Nɛ kekleekle ɔ, Mawu wo ni komɛ bɔfohi ngɛ asafo ɔ mi, nɔ́ nɛ ji enyɔ ɔ, gbali, nɔ́ nɛ ji etɛ ɔ, tsɔɔli; kɔlɔ ɔ se ɔ he wami ni tsuli, kɔlɔ ɔ se ɔ, hiɔhi a tsami dloomi nike nihi, yemi kɛ buami, nɔyemihi, gbi slɔɔtohi a tumi. 29Anɛ nihi tsuo ji bɔfohi lo? Anɛ nihi tsuo ji gbali lo? Anɛ nihi tsuo ji tsɔɔli lo? Anɛ nihi tsuo ji he wami ni tsuli lo? 30Anɛ nihi tsuo lɛ ngɛ hiɔhi a tsami dloomi nike nihi lo? Anɛ nihi tsuo lɛ tuɔ munyu slɔɔtohi lo? Anɛ nihi tsuo lɛ tsɔɔ munyuhi a sisi lo? 31Nyɛ hɛ nɛ dɔ ngɛ dloomi nike nihi nɛ hi saminya amɛ a he. Nɛ ma kpale tsɔɔ nyɛ blɔ nɛ hi pe kulaa.

english_text:
Love
1What if I could speak
all languages of humans
and even of angels?
If I did not love others,
I would be nothing more
than a noisy gong
or a clanging cymbal.
2 What if I could prophesy
and understand all mysteries
and all knowledge?
And what if I had faith
that moved mountains?
I would be nothing,
unless I loved others.
3What if I gave away all
that I owned
and let myself
be burned alive?
I would gain nothing,
unless I loved others.
4Love is patient and kind,
never jealous, boastful,
proud, or 5rude.
Love isn't selfish
or quick tempered.
It doesn't keep a record
of wrongs that others do.
6Love rejoices in the truth,
but not in evil.
7Love is always supportive,
loyal, hopeful,
and trusting.
8Love never fails!
Everyone who prophesies
will stop,
and unknown languages
will no longer
be spoken.
All that we know
will be forgotten.
9We don't know everything,
and our prophecies
are not complete.
10But what is perfect
will someday appear,
and what isn't perfect
will then disappear.
11When we were children,
we thought and reasoned
as children do.
But when we grew up,
we quit our childish ways.
12Now all we can see of God
is like a cloudy picture
in a mirror.
Later we will see him
face to face.
We don't know everything,
but then we will,
just as God completely
understands us.
13For now there are faith,
hope, and love.
But of these three,
the greatest is love.
translation_text:
Suɔmi
1Ke i kɛ nimli kɛ hiɔwe bɔfohi a lilɛ tuɔ munyu se be suɔmi ɔ, lɛɛ i ngɛ kaa ayawa nɛ jijeɔ loo ngmlɛ nɛ pɛɛ. 2Nɛ ke i ngɛ gbami, nɛ i naa laami mi nihi kulaa nya, nɛ i le nihi kulaa, nɛ ke i ngɛ hemi kɛ yemi kulaa hulɔ, bɔ nɛ ma nyɛ yokuhi ma hia, se i be suɔmi ɔ, lɛɛ i pi nɔ́ ko? 3Nɛ ke i ngɔ ye nihi kulaa ngɔ ke nihi, nɛ ke i ngɔ ye nɔmlɔ tso ngɔ ha nɛ a sa mi, se i be suɔmi ɔ, i na we se ko.
4Suɔmi toɔ e tsui si, e mi mi hi; suɔmi ji hunga; suɔmi fiɛ̃, e pee we pupuupu, 5e pee we nihi nɛ sɛ, e plee we lɛ nitsɛ e nɔ he, e mi mi wui la, e kɛ nɔ tɔmi wui e mi. 6E nya we nɔ yayami he, se mohu e nyaa anɔkuale he? 7Suɔmi maa e nya ngɛ nihi kulaa mi, e heɔ nihi kulaa yeɔ, e ngɛ hɛ kɛ nɔ fɔmi, e miaa e hɛ mi ngɛ nihi kulaa mi.
8Suɔmi se pui gblegbleegblee. Se ke gbamihi ʼi ɔ, a se maa po; ke munyuhi slɔɔtohi a tumi ʼi ɔ, a maa jɔɔ; ke ni lemi ʼi ɔ, e se maa po. 9Ejakaa wa ni nɛ wa le ɔ, fã kɛ fã ʼi, nɛ wa gbami hu fa kɛ fa ʼi. 10Se ke nɔ́ nɛ hi kɛ pi si ɔ ba a, lɔ ɔ lɛɛ nɔ́ nɛ ji fa kɛ fa a se maa po.
11Benɛ i ji bimwɔyo ɔ, i tuɔ munyu kaa bimwɔyo, i juɛɛ ni a he kaa bimwɔyo, i susuu kaa bimwɔyo; se benɛ i ba plɛ nyumu nɔkɔtɔma a, i sake bimwɔwi a ni ɔmɛ ngɔ pue se. 12Ejakaa mwɔnɛ mwɔnɛ ɔ, ahuhuɛ mi wa guu kɛ hyɛɛ nɔ tsuu, se jamɛ a be ɔ mi ɔ, hɛ mi kɛ hɛ mi. Mwɔnɛ mwɔnɛ ɔ, i le ni fã kɛ fã, sɛ jamɛ a bɛ ɔ ɔ mi ɔ, ma lɛ ni kɛ pi si kaa bɔ nɛ a le mi kɛ pi si ɔ.
13Se jehanɛ hemi kɛ yemi, hɛ kɛ nɔ tɔmi, suɔmi, kikɛmɛ a nihi etɛ nɛ ɔmɛ hii si; se suɔmi ji a kpɛti nɔ nɛ pe kulaa.

english_text:
Speaking Unknown Languages and Prophesying
1Love should be your guide. Be eager to have the gifts that come from the Holy Spirit, especially the gift of prophecy. 2If you speak languages that others don't know, God will understand what you are saying, though no one else will know what you mean. You will be talking about mysteries that only the Spirit understands. 3But when you prophesy, you will be understood, and others will be helped. They will be encouraged and made to feel better.
4By speaking languages that others don't know, you help only yourself. But by prophesying you help everyone in the church. 5I am glad for you to speak unknown languages, although I prefer that you would prophesy. In fact, prophesying does much more good than speaking unknown languages, unless someone can help the church by explaining what you mean.
6My friends, what good would it do, if I came and spoke unknown languages to you and didn't explain what I meant? How would I help you, unless I told you what God had shown me or gave you some knowledge or prophecy or teaching? 7If all musical instruments sounded alike, how would you know the difference between a flute and a harp? 8If a bugle call isn't clear, how would you know to get ready for battle?
9This is how it is when you speak unknown languages. If no one can understand what you are talking about, you will only be talking to the wind. 10There are many different languages in this world, and all of them make sense. 11But if I don't understand the language that someone is using, we will be like foreigners to each other. 12If you really want spiritual gifts, choose the ones that will be most helpful to the church.
13When we speak languages that others don't know, we should pray for the power to explain what we mean. 14For example, if I use an unknown language in my prayers, my spirit prays but my mind is useless. 15Then what should I do? There are times when I should pray with my spirit, and times when I should pray with my mind. Sometimes I should sing with my spirit, and at other times I should sing with my mind.
16Suppose some strangers are in your worship service, when you are praising God with your spirit. If they don't understand you, how will they know to say, “Amen”? 17You may be worshiping God in a wonderful way, but no one else will be helped. 18I thank God that I speak unknown languages more than any of you. 19But words that make sense can help the church. This is why in church I would rather speak five words that make sense than to speak 10,000 words in a language that others don't know.
20My friends, stop thinking like children. Think like mature people and be as innocent as tiny babies. 21 In the Scriptures the Lord says,
“I will use strangers
who speak unknown languages
to talk to my people.
They will speak to them
in foreign languages,
but still my people
won't listen to me.”
22Languages others don't know may mean something to unbelievers, but not to the Lord's followers. Prophecy, on the other hand, is for followers, not for unbelievers. 23Suppose everyone in your worship service started speaking unknown languages, and some outsiders or some unbelievers come in. Won't they think you are crazy? 24But suppose all of you are prophesying when those unbelievers and outsiders come in. They will realize that they are sinners, and they will want to change their ways because of what you are saying. 25They will tell what is hidden in their hearts. Then they will kneel down and say to God, “We are certain that you are with these people.”
Worship Must Be Orderly
26My friends, when you meet to worship, you must do everything for the good of everyone there. That's how it should be when someone sings or teaches or tells what God has said or speaks an unknown language or explains what the language means. 27No more than two or three of you should speak unknown languages during the meeting. You must take turns, and someone should always be there to explain what you mean. 28If no one can explain, you must keep silent in church and speak only to yourself and to God.
29Two or three persons may prophesy, and everyone else must listen carefully. 30If someone sitting there receives a message from God, the speaker must stop and let the other person speak. 31Let only one person speak at a time, then all of you will learn something and be encouraged. 32A prophet should be willing to stop and let someone else speak. 33God wants everything to be done peacefully and in order.
When God's people meet in church, 34the women must not be allowed to speak. They must keep quiet and listen, as the Law of Moses teaches. 35If there is something they want to know, they can ask their husbands when they get home. It is disgraceful for women to speak in church.
36God's message did not start with you people, and you are not the only ones it has reached.
37If you think of yourself as a prophet or a spiritual person, you will know I am writing only what the Lord has commanded. 38So don't pay attention to anyone who ignores what I am writing. 39My friends, be eager to prophesy and don't stop anyone from speaking languages that others don't know. 40But do everything properly and in order.
translation_text:
Mumi mi dloomi nike nihi
1Nyɛɛ di suɔmi se. Nyɛ hɛ nɛ dɔ ngɛ mumi mi nihi a he, se titli ɔ, gbami. 2Ejakaa nɔ nɛ tuɔ munyu kɛ lilɛ slɔɔto ko ɔ, pi nimli nɛ e kɛ ngɛ tue, se Mawu mohu, ejakaa nɔ ko nɔ ko nui, se mumi mi e ngɛ laami munyu ɔmɛ tue ngɛ. 3Nɔ nɛ gbaa a, nimli e gbaa ngɔ tsɔɔ konɛ e kɛ ha a nane nɛ nu si nɛ e bɔ mɛ kɔkɔ nɛ e jɔɔ a bua. 4Nɔ nɛ tuɔ munyu kɛ lilɛ slɔɔto ko ɔ, yeɔ buaa lɛ nitsɛ e he, se nɔ nɛ gbaa a, e yeɔ buaa asafo ɔ.
5Se i ko suɔ nɛ nyɛ tsuo nyɛ ko tu munyu kɛ lilɛ slɔɔtohi Se nɔ́ nɛ i ko suɔ titli ji kaa nyɛɛ gba, ejakaa nɔ nɛ gbaa a, e pe nɔ nɛ tuɔ munyu kɛ lilɛ slɔɔtohi, ja e tsɔɔ sisi hulɔ konɛ e ye bua asafo ɔ kulaa. 6Jehanɛ, mamimɛ, ke i ba nyɛ ngɔ ba tu munyu kɛ lilɛ slɔɔtohi nɛ pi kpo jemi loo ni lemi loo gbami loo ni tsɔɔmi ko ɔ, mɛni se i haa nyɛ naa?
7Kaa bɔ nɛ nihi nɛ wami be mi ɔ pɛɛ ɔ, bɛ jio, saku jio, ke e pɛmi ɔ mi tsɔ we ɔ, kɛ maa pee kɛɛ nɛ a maa le nɔ nɛ a ngɛ kpae aloo nɔ nɛ a ngɛ fiae ɔ nɛɛ? 8Ejakaa ke titimati pɛ́ pɛmi nɛ ngɛ faii ɔ, mɛnɔ ma dla e he ngɔ to ta? 9Ja nɔuu kɛ nyɛ hu, ngɛ munyu tumi blɔfami ɔ, ke nyɛ tu we munyu nɛ sisi ngɛ faii ɔ, kɛ maa pee kɛɛ nɛ a maa le nɔ nɛ nyɛ ngɛ dee ɔ? Ejakaa kɔlɔ ɔ lɛɛ nyɛ ngɛ kaa nihi nɛ ngɛ munyu tue woɔ kɔhiɔ mi. 10Gbi slɔɔtohi fuu ngɛ je ɔ mi mohu, se eko eko be nɛ be sisi. 11Se jehanɛ ke i nui munyu ɔ sisi ɔ, lɛɛ ma plɛ maje no ngɛ nɔ nɛ ngɛ munyu ɔ tue ɔ hɛ mi, nɛ nɔ nɛ ngɛ munyu ɔ tue ɔ hu ma plɛ maje no ngɛ ye hɛ mi. 12Be abɔ nɛ nyɛ hɛ dɔɔ ngɛ mumi mi nihi a he ɔ, ja nɔuu hu nyɛɛ bɔ mɔde konɛ nyɛɛ be nɔ ngɛ nihi nɛ ma ha asafo ɔ maa wa a mi.
13Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, nɔ nɛ tuɔ munyu kɛ lilɛ slɔɔto ko ɔ, e sɔle konɛ e nyɛ sisi hu nɛ e tsɔɔ. 14Ejakaa ke i sɔlee kɛ lilɛ slɔɔto ɔ, ye mumi ɔ sɔlee lɛɛ, se ye juɛmi ɔ piɛ we he. 15Jeha nɛ kɛ ma pee kɛɛ? I kɛ mumi maa sɔle, nɛ i kɛ juɛmi hu maa sɔle. Ma fia kɛ mumi, nɛ ma la kɛ juɛmi hulɔ. 16Ejakaa ke o kɛ mumi ngɛ Mawu yi jee ɔ, kɛ maa pee kɛɛ nɛ nɔ nɛ hii si ngɛ ninɛmɛ nɛ li mi eko ɔmɛ a blɔ he ɔ ma de Amen ngɔ si o sina a nɔ, akɛnɛ e li nɔ nɛ o ngɛ dee ɔ? 17Moo lɛɛ, o ngɛ si nae saminya mohu, se kɛ ɔ, o yi bua we nɔ kpa a kulaa.
18I naa ye Mawu ɔ si kaa i pe nyɛ tsuo ngɛ gbi slɔɔtohi a tumi mi. 19Se ke ɔ, ngɛ asafo ɔ mi ɔ, i suɔ kaa i kɛ ye juɛmi nɛ tu munyu kakaaka enuɔ, konɛ ma kɛ tsɔɔ ni kpahi a ni mohu, pe nɔ nɛ ma tu munyu kakaaka akpe nyɔngma ngɛ gbi slɔɔtohi a mi.
20Mamimɛ, nyɛ ko pee nyɛ he jokuɛwi ngɛ juɛmi blɔfami, se yayami blɔfami ɔ, nyɛɛ pee nyɛ he bimwɔwi, se juɛmi blɔfami ɔ, nyɛɛ pee nyɛ he nihi nɛ a wa. 21A ngma ngɛ Mlaa a mi ke: “Nyɔmtsɛ ɔ ke:
Gbi slɔɔtohi a mi kɛ nya slɔɔtohi a nɔ
Ma gu nɛ i kɛ kikɛmɛ a ma nɛ ɔ maa tu munyu,
Se lɔ ɔ hu tete a be mi tue bue.”
22Lɔ ɔ he ɔ gbi slɔɔtohi ɔmɛ ɔ a pi okadi ha ninɛmɛ nɛ heɔ yeɔ, se mohu a ji okadi ha ninɛmɛ nɛ he we yi. Gbami ɔ, e pi ninɛmɛ nɛ he we yi ɔmɛ a nɔ, se mohu ninɛmɛ nɛ heɔ ye ɔmɛ a nɔ.
23Lɔ ɔ he ɔ jehanɛ, ke asafo mluku ɔ tsuo nya ba bua ngɛ he kake, nɛ ni ɔmɛ tsuo kɛ gbi slɔɔtohi ngɛ munyu tue, nɛ ninɛmɛ nɛ li mi eko aloo ninɛmɛ nɛ he we yi ɔmɛ a ti ni komɛ hu ba lejɛ ɔ, anɛ a be dee ke nyɛ ngɛ godo nue lo? 24Se ke ni ɔmɛ kulaa ngɛ gbae, nɛ nɔ ko nɛ he we yi aloo e li mi eko ba lejɛ ɔ, ni ɔmɛ tsuo ma kã lɛ, ni ɔmɛ tsuo maa kojo lɛ, 25a ma je e tsui mi laami nihi a kpo paa nɛ lɔ ɔ ma ha e kɛ e hɛ mi ma bu si nɛ e ja Mawu, nɛ e maa jaje ke Mawu ngɛ nyɛ kpɛti niinɛ.
Blɔnyatomi ngɛ asafo ɔ mi
26Lɛɛ mɛni mɔ, mamimɛ? Ke nyɛ nya ba bua, nɛ nyɛ ti nɔ ko ngɛ la ko, nɔ ko hu ngɛ tsɔɔmi ko, nɔ ko ngɛ gbi slɔɔto ko, nɔ ko ngɛ kpo jemi ko, nɔ ko ngɛ sisi tsɔɔmi ko ɔ, a pee kulaa bɔ nɛ e maa ye bua nihi. 27Ke a ngɛ gbi slɔɔto tue ɔ, nyɛ ha ni enyɔ loo ke e hiɛ hluu ɔ, ni etɛ pɛ nɛ tu, kakaaka, nɛ nɔ kake hu nɛ tsɔɔ sisi. 28Ke sisi tsɔɔlɔ ko be ɔ, e ma e nya ngɛ asafo ɔ mi, se e tu munyu ha lɛ nitsɛ e he kɛ Mawu. 29Se gbali ɔmɛ ɔ, ni enyɔ loo ni etɛ nɛ tu munyu, nɛ nihi nɛ piɛ ɔ a susu he. 30Se ke a je nɔ ko kpo tsɔɔ nɔ ko nɛ hii si ɔ, nɔ nɛ ngɛ munyu ɔ tue ɔ e jɔɔ tumi. 31Ejakaa nyɛ tsuo nyɛ maa gba, kakaaka, konɛ nɔ tsuaa nɔ nɛ kase nɔ ko nɛ a tu munyu ngɔ tsɔɔ nihi kulaa kɛ wo mɛ he wami. 32Gbali a mumi baa a he si haa gbali ɔmɛ, 33ejakaa Mawu ɔ, e pi basabasa peemi Mawu, se mohu he jɔmi Mawu, kaa bɔ nɛ e ngɛ ngɛ he tsɔli asafo ɔmɛ kulaa mi ɔ.
34Nyɛ ha yi ɔmɛ nɛ pee kɔ ngɛ asafo kpehi a mi, ejakaa a ngmɛ mɛ blɔ nɛ a tu munyu, se mohu a ba a he si kaa bɔ nɛ Mlaa a hu deɔ ɔ. 35Ke a suɔ kaa a kase nɔ ko ɔ, a bi mɛ nitsɛmɛ a hunomɛ ngɛ we mi. Ejakaa e ngɛ zo ha yihi kaa a maa tu munyu ngɛ asafo kpehi a mi.
36Anɛ nyɛ ngɔ Mawu munyu ɔ je? Aloo nyɛ kɛkɛ nyɛ ngɔ e ba? 37Ke e peɔ nɔ ko kaa gbalɔ loo mumi mi nɔmlɔ ji lɛ ɔ, e sa nɛ e le kaa nɔ nɛ i ngma nyɛ nɛ ɔ, Nyɔmtsɛ ɔ kita ʼi; 38se ke nɔ ko li enɛ ɔ ɔ, nyɛ ko le lɛ. 39Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, mamimɛ, nyɛ hɛ nɛ dɔ ngɛ gbami he, nɛ gbi slɔɔtohi a tumi hu nyɛ ko tsi nya. 40A pee nɔ tsuaa nɔ bɔ nɛ ngɛ fɛu ngɛ blɔ nya blɔ nya.

english_text:
Christ Was Raised to Life
1My friends, I want you to remember the message I preached and that you believed and trusted. 2You will be saved by this message, if you hold firmly to it. But if you don't, your faith was all for nothing.
3 I told you the most important part of the message exactly as it was told to me. This part is:
Christ died for our sins,
as the Scriptures say.
4 He was buried,
and three days later
he was raised to life,
as the Scriptures say.
5 Christ appeared to Peter,
then to the twelve.
6After this, he appeared
to more than five hundred
other followers.
Most of them are still alive,
but some have died.
7He also appeared to James,
then to all of the apostles.
8 Finally, he appeared to me, even though I am like someone who was born at the wrong time.
9 I am the least important of all the apostles. In fact, I caused so much trouble for God's church that I don't even deserve to be called an apostle. 10But God treated me with undeserved grace! He made me what I am, and his grace wasn't wasted. I worked much harder than any of the other apostles, although it was really God's grace at work and not me. 11But it doesn't matter if I preached or if they preached. All of you believed the message just the same.
God's People Will Be Raised to Life
12If we preach that Christ was raised from death, how can some of you say the dead will not be raised to life? 13If they won't be raised to life, Christ himself wasn't raised to life. 14And if Christ wasn't raised to life, our message is worthless, and so is your faith. 15If the dead won't be raised to life, we have told lies about God by saying he raised Christ to life, when he really did not.
16So if the dead won't be raised to life, Christ wasn't raised to life. 17Unless Christ was raised to life, your faith is useless, and you are still living in your sins. 18And those people who died after putting their faith in him are completely lost. 19If our hope in Christ is good only for this life, we are worse off than anyone else.
20But Christ has been raised to life! And he makes us certain that others will also be raised to life. 21Just as we will die because of Adam, we will be raised to life because of Christ. 22Adam brought death to all of us, and Christ will bring life to all of us. 23But we must each wait our turn. Christ was the first to be raised to life, and his people will be raised to life when he returns. 24Then after Christ has destroyed all powers and forces, the end will come, and he will give the kingdom to God the Father.
25 Christ will rule until he puts all his enemies under his power, 26and the last enemy he destroys will be death. 27 When the Scriptures say he will put everything under his power, they don't include God. It was God who put everything under the power of Christ. 28After everything is under the power of God's Son, he will put himself under the power of God, who put everything under his Son's power. Then God will mean everything to everyone.
29 If the dead are not going to be raised to life, what will people do who are being baptized for them? Why are they being baptized for those dead people? 30And why do we always risk our lives 31and face death every day? The pride that I have in you because of Christ Jesus our Lord is what makes me say this. 32 What do you think I gained by fighting wild animals in Ephesus? If the dead are not raised to life,
“Let's eat and drink.
Tomorrow we die.”
33Don't fool yourselves. Bad friends will destroy you. 34Be sensible and stop sinning. You should be embarrassed that some people still don't know about God.
What Our Bodies Will Be Like
35Some of you have asked, “How will the dead be raised to life? What kind of bodies will they have?” 36Don't be foolish. A seed must die before it can sprout from the ground. 37Wheat seeds and all other seeds look different from the sprouts that come up. 38This is because God gives everything the kind of body he wants it to have. 39People, animals, birds, and fish are each made of flesh, but none of them are alike. 40Everything in the heavens has a body, and so does everything on earth. But each one is very different from all the others. 41The sun isn't like the moon, the moon isn't like the stars, and each star is different.
42That's how it will be when our bodies are raised to life. These bodies will die, but the bodies that are raised will live forever. 43These ugly and weak bodies will become beautiful and strong. 44As surely as there are physical bodies, there are spiritual bodies. And our physical bodies will be changed into spiritual bodies.
45 The first man was named Adam, and the Scriptures tell us that he was a living person. But Jesus, who may be called the last Adam, is a life-giving spirit. 46We see that the one with a spiritual body did not come first. He came after the one who had a physical body. 47The first man was made from the dust of the earth, but the second man came from heaven. 48Everyone on earth has a body like the body of the one who was made from the dust of the earth. And everyone in heaven has a body like the body of the one who came from heaven. 49Just as we are like the one who was made out of earth, we will be like the one who came from heaven.
50My friends, I want you to know that our bodies of flesh and blood will decay. This means they cannot share in God's kingdom, which lasts forever. 51 I will explain a mystery to you. Not every one of us will die, but we will all be changed. 52It will happen suddenly, quicker than the blink of an eye. At the sound of the last trumpet the dead will be raised. We will all be changed, so we will never die again. 53Our dead and decaying bodies will be changed into bodies that won't die or decay. 54 The bodies we now have are weak and can die. But they will be changed into bodies that are eternal. Then the Scriptures will come true,
“Death has lost the battle!
55 Where is its victory?
Where is its sting?”
56Sin is what gives death its sting, and the Law is the power behind sin. 57But thank God for letting our Lord Jesus Christ give us the victory!
58My dear friends, stand firm and don't be shaken. Always keep busy working for the Lord. You know that everything you do for him is worthwhile.
translation_text:
Kristo sitemi
1Jehanɛ, mamimɛ, i ngɛ nyɛ kaie kaa Sane Kpakpa a nɛ i jaje tsɔɔ nyɛ nɛ nyɛ pɛtɛ he hulɔ nɛ nyɛ hɛɛ mi ɔ, 2kɔlɔ ɔ a kɛ heɔ nyɛ yi wami hulɔ, ke nyɛ pɛtɛ he bɔ nɛ i jaje tsɔɔ nyɛ ɔ, ke pi ja a lɛɛ nyɛ he ye yaka gu.
3Ejakaa sanehi nɛ he hia pe kulaa nɛ a kɛ ha mi nɛ imi hu i kɛ ha nyɛ ɔ ji kaa, Kristo gbo ngɛ wa he yayami ɔmɛ a he ngɛ ngmami ɔmɛ a nya, 4kaa a pu lɛ, nɛ a tle lɛ si ekohu ngɛ ligbi nɛ ji ligbi etɛ ɔ nɔ ngɛ ngmami ɔmɛ a nya; 5nɛ kaa e je e he kpo ngɔ tsɔɔ Kefa, lɔ ɔ se ɔ, ni nyɔngma kɛ enyɔ ɔ. 6Lɔ ɔ se ɔ, e je e he kpo ngɔ tsɔɔ nyɛmimɛ pe lafa enuɔ si kake, nihi nɛ a ti nihi fuu ngɛ kɛ ba su mwɔnɛ, se ni komɛ hu gbo. 7Lɔ ɔ se ɔ, e je e he kpo ngɔ tsɔɔ Yakobo, lɔ ɔ se ɔ bɔfo ɔmɛ tsuo kulaa.
8Se mɛ kulaa a se ɔ, e je e he kpo ngɔ tsɔɔ imi hulɔ nɛ i ngɛ kaa nɔ ko nɛ a kpatu fɔ lɛ ɔ. 9Ejakaa imi lɛɛ, i ji enɔ wayo kulaa ngɛ bɔfo ɔmɛ a kpɛti, nɛ i sɛ́ tete kaa a tsɛɛ mi bɔfo po, ejakaa i wa Mawu asafo ɔ yi mi. 10Se Mawu dloomi nya i kɛ ji nɔ nɛ i ji nɛ ɔ nɛ, nɛ e dloomi nɛ e kɛ dloomi ɔ pee we yaka; se mohu, i tsu ni wawɛɛ pe mɛ tsuo pɛpɛɛpɛ, se pi imi tete, se mohu Mawu dloomi nɛ kɛ mi ngɛ ɔ. 11Lɔ ɔ he ɔ jehanɛ, imi jio, mɛ jio, enɛ ɔ ji wa fiɛmi, nɛ enɛ ɔ hu ji nɔ́ nɛ nyɛ he ye.
Wa sitemi
12Jehanɛ ke a fiɛ ngɛ Kristo he kaa a tle lɛ si kɛ je gbeje ɔ, mɛni he je nɛ nyɛ ti ni komɛ deɔ ke ni gbogboehi a si temi ko be ɔ? 13Se ke ni gbogboehi a si temi ko be ɔ, lɛɛ Kristo hu a tle we lɛ si. 14Nɛ ke a tle we Kristo si ɔ, lɛɛ wa fiɛmi ɔ pee yaka, nɛ nyɛ hemi kɛ yemi ɔ hu pee yaka gu. 15Jeha nɛ a kpa wɔ si kaa Mawu he lakpa odase yeli ji wɔ, ejakaa wa ye Mawu he odase kaa e tle Kristo si, nɔ nɛ, ke e ngɛ mi kaa ni gbogboehi ti si ɔ, lɛɛ e tle we lɛ si? 16Ejakaa ke a tle we ni gbogboehi a si ɔ, lɛɛ Kristo hu a tle we lɛ si. 17Nɛ jehanɛ ke a tle we Kristo si ɔ, lɔ ɔ lɛɛ nyɛ hemi kɛ yemi ɔ pee yaka nɛ nyɛ fɔɔ si ngɛ nyɛ he yayami ɔmɛ a mi kɛ mwɔɔ; 18lɔ ɔ lɛɛ nihi nɛ gbo ngɛ Kristo mi ɔ hu laa. 19Ke wami nɛ ɔ mi kɛkɛ wa hɛ ngɛ Kristo nɔ ngɛ ɔ, wa ni ngɛ mɔbɔ pe nimli kulaa.
20Se anɔkuale ɔ ji kaa, a tle Kristo si kɛ je gbeje, e pee kekleekle nɔ ngɛ nihi nɛ gbo ɔmɛ a kpɛti. 21Ejakaa bɔ nɛ gbenɔ gu nɔmlɔ nɔ kɛ ba a, ja nɔuu si temi ɔ hu gu nɔmlɔ nɔ kɛ ba. 22Ejakaa, kaa bɔ nɛ Adam mi nɛ nihi kulaa gboɔ ngɛ ɔ, ja nɔuu kɛ̃ Kristo mi nɛ mɛ kulaa a yi ma na wa ngɛ. 23Nɔ tsuaa nɔ ngɛ lɛ nitsɛ e blɔ he: Kekleekle nɔ ji Kristo, lɔ ɔ se ɔ nihi nɛ ji Kristo ni ɔmɛ ngɛ e bami ɔ mi. 24Lɔ ɔ se loko nyagbe ɔ maa ba, benɛ e maa ngɔ matsɛ yemi ɔ ngɔ ha Mawu nɛ ji Tsɛ ɔ; nɛ e maa po nɔ yemi kulaa kɛ he blɔ kulaa kɛ he wami kulaa se ɔ. 25Ejakaa ja Kristo ye matsɛ kɛ maa su be nɛ Mawu maa ngɔ henyɛli kulaa ngɔ wo e nane si. 26Nyagbe henyɛlɔ nɛ a ma kpata e hɛ mi ji gbenɔ. 27Ejakaa ngmami ɔ ke: “Mawu ngɔ nihi tsuo kulaa ngɔ wo e nane si.” Se ke e de ke a ngɔ nihi kulaa ngɔ wo e sisi ɔ, blɔɔ e ngɛ paa kaa nɔ nɛ ngɔ nihi kulaa ngɔ wo e sisi ɔ be mi. 28Se e benɛ a ngɔ nihi kulaa ngɔ wo Bi ɔ sisi ɔ, lɔ ɔ lɛɛ Bi ɔ nitsɛ hu maa ngɔ e he ngɔ wo nɔ nɛ ngɔ nihi kulaa ngɔ wo e sisi ɔ sisi, konɛ Mawu nɛ pee nihi kulaa yi.
29Ejakaa, kɛ nihi nɛ haa a baptisii mɛ ngɛ ni gbogboehi a nane mi ɔ maa pee kɛɛ? Ke ni gbogboehi be si tee kulaa a, mɛ he je mɔ nɛ a haa a baptisii mɛ ngɛ ni gbogboehi a nane mi ɔ? 30Mɛ he je wɔ hu wa naa amane ngmlɛfia tsuaa ngmlɛfia a? 31I na nyɛ he fiami nɛ i ngɛ ngɛ wa Nyɔmtsɛ Kristo Yesu mi ɔ, kaa i gboɔ daa nɛ ɔ. 32Ke nimli a blɔfami nɛ i kɛ “lohwe dikali” hwu ta ngɛ Efeso ɔ, jinɛ mɛni se i naa? Ke ni gbogboehi ti si ɔ, “Nyɛ ha waa ye ni nɛ waa nu ni, ejakaa hwɔɔ ɔ wa ma gbo!”
33Nyɛ ko ha nɛ a sisi nyɛ. “Huɛ yaya bɔmi puɛɔ je mi bami kpakpa.” 34Nyɛ ha nyɛ hɛ mi nɛ tsɔ nyɛ saminya, nɛ nyɛ ko pee yayami; ejakaa nyɛ ti ni komɛ li nɔ́ ko nɔ́ ko ngɛ Mawu he. I ngɛ enɛ ɔ dee nɛ ma kɛ gbe nyɛ zo.
Nɔmlɔ tso nɛ a kɛ maa te si
35Se eko ɔ nɔ ko ma bi ke: “Kɛ ni gbogboehi maa pee kɛ te si kɛɛ? Nɛ jehanɛ mɛni nɔmlɔ tso a ma kɛ ba?” 36Lohwe! Nɔ́ nɛ mo nitsɛ o du ɔ, ja e gbo lolo loko e yi ma na wa. 37Nɛ jehanɛ hu, nɔ́ nɛ o duɔ ɔ, pi tso nɛ maa puɛ ʼi, se mohu dumi wu ngmelu kɛkɛ, ke ngma jio, nihi nɛ piɛ ɔmɛ eko ʼi jio. 38Mawu haa wu ɔ tso bɔ nɛ e suɔ, nɛ wu tsuaa wu ɔ, e haa lɛ lɛ nitsɛ e tso.
39Pi he lo tsuo ji he lo kake, se mohu eslo nimli a he lo, nɛ e slo lohwehi a he lo, eslo nyu mi lohi a nɔ, nɛ eslo lohwe pɛlitsɛmɛ a nɔ hulɔ.
40Hiɔwe nɔmlɔ tsohi ngɛ, nɛ zugba nɔ nɔmlɔ tsohi hu ngɛ; se kɛ ɔ eslo hiɔwe nihi a hɛ mi nyami, nɛ eslo zugba nɔ ni ɔmɛ hu a nɔ. 41Eslo pu hɛ mi nyami, nɛ eslo hlami hu hɛ mi nyami, nɛ eslo dodoehi a hɛ mi nyami; ejakaa eslo dodoe kake hɛ mi nyami ngɛ dodoe kpa hɛ mi nyami he.
42Jã nɔuu ji ni gbogboehi a sitemi ɔ hulɔ. A duɔ lɛ ngɛ puemi mi, a tleɔ lɛ si ngɛ nɔ́ nɛ puɛ we mi; 43a duɔ lɛ ngɛ nɔ́ nɛ be nyami mi, a tleɔ lɛ si ngɛ nyami mi; a duɔ lɛ ngɛ gbɔlemi mi, a tleɔ lɛ si ngɛ he wami mi. 44A duɔ klaa nɔmlɔ tso, a tleɔ mumi nɔmlɔ tso si. Ke klaa nɔmlɔ tso ngɛ ɔ, mumi nɔmlɔ tso hu ngɛ. 45Jã a ngma hulɔ ke: “Adam nɛ ji kekle nɔmlɔ ɔ plɛ klaa nɛ hɛ ngɛ; nyagbe Adam ɔ plɛ mumi nɛ haa nɔ yi naa wa.” 46Se tsa pi mumi nɔ ɔ ji kekle nɔ, se mohu klaa nɔ ɔ, kɔlɔ ɔ se ɔ mumi nɔ ɔ. 47Kekle nɔmlɔ nɛ je zugba a mi ɔ, zu ʼi, nɔmlɔ nɛ ji enyɔ ɔ je hiɔwe. 48Bɔ nɛ zugba nɛ ɔ nɔ no ɔ ngɛ ɔ, jã zugba nɛ ɔ nɔ bi ɔmɛ hu ngɛ; nɛ bɔ nɛ hiɔwe no ɔ ngɛ ɔ, ja hiɔwe bi ɔmɛ hu ngɛ. 49Nɛ kaa bɔ nɛ wa hɛɛ zugba nɛ ɔ nɔ no ɔ subai ɔ, jã nɔuu wa maa hɛɛ hiɔwe no ɔ hu subai.
50Mamimɛ, nɔ́ nɛ i ngɛ tsɔɔe ji kaa, he lo kɛ muɔ nine be Mawu matsɛ yemi ɔ nɔ sue, nɛ jehanɛ puemi hu nine be nɔ́ nɛ puɛ we ɔ nɔ sue.
51Oʼɛ, laami sane i ngɛ nyɛ dee nɛ ɔ nɛ: Tsa pi wɔ tsuo kulaa nɛ wa ma gbo ɔ, se a ma tsake wɔ tsuo, 52tlukaa ngɛ hɛngmɛfia mi, benɛ a ma kpa nyagbe titimati ɔ; ejakaa a ma kpa titimati, nɛ a ma tle ni gbogboehi a si nɛ a be puɛe hu, nɛ wɔɔ lɛɛ, a ma tsake wɔ. 53Ejakaa ja puɛmi nɔ́ nɛ ɔ wo nɔ́ nɛ puɛ we ɔ, nɛ kikɛmɛ a gbomi nɔ́ nɛ ɔ wo nɔ́ nɛ gbo we ɔ. 54Se benɛ kikɛmɛ a puemi nɔ́ nɛ ɔ wo nɔ́ nɛ puɛ we ɔ, nɛ kikɛmɛ a gbomi nɔ́ nɛ ɔ wo nɔ́ nɛ gbo we ɔ, lɔ ɔ lɛɛ munyu nɛ a ngma a maa ba mi ke:
“A mi gbenɔ ngɛ kunimi yemi mi.
55Mo gbenɔ, jije o kɛ̃ɛ ɔ ngɛ?
Mo gbeje, jije o kunimi yemi ɔ ngɛ?”
56Se gbenɔ kɛ̃ɛ ji yayami, nɛ yayami he wami ji Mlaa a. 57Se sina ha Mawu, nɔ nɛ guu wa Nyɔmtsɛ Yesu Kristo nɔ haa wa yeɔ kunimi ɔ. 58Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, mamimɛ nɛ i suɔ, nyɛ fi si nɛ nyɛ ko gbɔle, nɛ nyɛɛ ya nɔ ngɛ Nyɔmtsɛ ɔ ni tsumi ɔ mi daa nɛ ɔ, ejakaa nyɛ le kaa nyɛ dengme gbomi ɔ be yaka pee ngɛ Nyɔmtsɛ ɔ mi.

english_text:
A Collection for God's People
1 When you collect money for God's people, I want you to do exactly what I told the churches in Galatia to do. 2That is, each Sunday each of you must put aside part of what you have earned. If you do this, you won't have to take up a collection when I come. 3Choose some followers to take the money to Jerusalem. I will send them on with the money and with letters which show that you approve of them. 4If you think I should go along, they can go with me.
Paul's Travel Plans
5 After I have gone through Macedonia, I hope to see you 6and visit with you for a while. I may even stay all winter, so that you can help me on my way to wherever I will be going next. 7If the Lord lets me, I would rather come later for a longer visit than to stop off now for only a short visit. 8 I will stay in Ephesus until Pentecost, 9because there is a wonderful opportunity for me to do some work here. But there are also many people who are against me.
10 When Timothy arrives, give him a friendly welcome. He is doing the Lord's work, just as I am. 11Don't let anyone mistreat him. I am looking for him to return to me together with the other followers. So when he leaves, send him off with your blessings.
12I have tried hard to get our friend Apollos to visit you with the other followers. He doesn't want to come just now, but he will come when he can.
Personal Concerns and Greetings
13Keep alert. Be firm in your faith. Stay brave and strong. 14Show love in everything you do.
15 You know that Stephanas and his family were the first in Achaia to have faith in the Lord. They have done all they can for God's people. My friends, I ask you 16to obey leaders like them and to do the same for all others who work hard with you.
17I was glad to see Stephanas and Fortunatus and Achaicus. Having them here was like having you. 18They made me feel much better, just as they made you feel better. You should appreciate people like them.
19 Greetings from the churches in Asia.
Aquila and Priscilla, together with the church that meets in their house, send greetings in the name of the Lord.
20All the Lord's followers send their greetings.
Give each other a warm greeting.
21I am signing this letter myself: PAUL.
22I pray that God will put a curse on everyone who doesn't love the Lord. And may the Lord come soon.
23I pray the Lord Jesus will be kind to you.
24I love everyone who belongs to Christ Jesus.
translation_text:
Oniatsumi kɛ ha Yerusalem asafo ɔ
1Jehanɛ ngɛ onia nɛ a tsuɔ kɛ haa Mawu webi ɔmɛ a he ɔ, kaa bɔ nɛ i to ha Galatia asafo ɔmɛ ɔ, nyɛ hu nyɛɛ pee ja. 2Daa otsi kekleekle ligbi ɔ nɔ ɔ, nyɛ ti nɔ tsuaa nɔ nɛ je nɔ́ ko ngɔ to, ngɛ bɔ nɛ e naa a nya, konɛ ma ko ba loko a tsu onia a. 3Nɛ ke i ba a, ma tsɔ nihi nɛ nyɛ buu kaa a sa kɛ womi nɛ a hɛɛ nyɛ nike ni ɔmɛ kɛ ya Yerusalem. 4Se ke e sa kaa imi hu ma ya a, i kɛ mɛ maa ya.
Paulo yimitomi
5Se ma ya gu Makedonia loko ma ba nyɛ ngɔ, ejakaa Makedonia ma ya gu. 6Eko ɔ ma hi nyɛ gɔ bɔɔ, nɛ eko ɔ ma ye fiɛ̃ be ɔ hu ngɛ lejɛ ɔ, konɛ he tsuaa he nɛ i yaa a nɛ nyɛ ya je mi blɔ. 7Ejakaa i sume kaa ma na nyɛ ngɛ blɔ kpɛ kɛkɛ, se ye hɛ ngɛ nɔ kaa ke Nyɔmtsɛ ɔ maa ngmɛ mi blɔ ɔ, ma kɛ bɔɔ ngɛ nyɛ ngɔ.
8Se ma hi Efeso kɛ maa su Pentekoste ligbi ɔ nɔ. 9Ejakaa a bli sinya kpetekpleenyɛ nya ha mi, kɛ ha ni tsumi fuu nɛ maa wo yiblii, se ninɛmɛ nɛ kuɔ nya a hu hiɛ.
10Ke Timoteo ba nyɛ ngɔ ɔ, nyɛɛ hyɛ nɛ nyɛ he lɛ hɛmuɔ, ejakaa Nyɔmtsɛ ɔ ni tsumi nɔuu e ngɛ tsue kaa imi. 11Kɔlɔ ɔ he ɔ nɔ ko ko bu lɛ kaa pi nɔ ko ji lɛ; se nyɛ je lɛ blɔ ngɛ he jɔmi mi konɛ e ba ye ngɔ. Ye hɛ ngɛ nɔ kaa e kɛ nyamimɛ ɔmɛ maa ba.
12Wa nyɛmi Apolo ɔ, i kpa lɛ pɛɛ hluu nɛ e kɛ nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ nɛ ba nyɛ ngɔ, se e kplɛɛ we kulaa kaa e maa ba amlɔ nɛ ɔ, se ke e na e he deka hu e maa ba.
Nyagbe munyuhi
13Nyɛɛ huɔ, nyɛɛ da si kpɛii ngɛ hemi kɛ yemi ɔ mi, nyɛɛ pee nyumu, nɛ nyɛ he nɛ wa! 14Nyɛɛ pee nyɛ nihi kulaa ngɛ suɔmi mi.
15Mamimɛ, nyɛ le Stefana we mi bi ɔmɛ kaa mɛ ji Akaia kekleekle yiblii, nɛ a ngɔ Mawu webi ɔmɛ a sɔmɔmi ɔ ngɔ fɔ a nɔ. 16I kpa nyɛ pɛɛ konɛ nyɛ hu nyɛɛ ba nyɛ he si ha ni nɛ ɔmɛ, kɛ nɔ tsuaa nɔ nɛ kɛ mɛ tsuɔ ni nɛ e bɔɔ mɔde ɔ.
17I na buajɔmi ngɛ Stefana kɛ Fortunato kɛ Akaiko bami ɔ he, ejakaa nɛ nyɛ be ye ngɔ nɛ ɔ, mɛ lɛ a ba ye nyɛ nɛne mi. 18Ejakaa a ba wo ye bua kaa bɔ nɛ a wo nyɛ hu nyɛ bua a. Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, nimli nɛ ngɛ kaa ni nɛ ɔmɛ ɔ nyɛɛ le mɛ saminya.
19Asia asafo ɔmɛ biɔ nyɛ. Akwila kɛ Priskila kɛ asafo nɛ ngɛ a we ɔ mi ɔ biɔ nyɛ saminya ngɛ Nyɔmtsɛ ɔ mi. 20Nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ kulaa biɔ nyɛ. Nyɛ nga nyɛ he kɛ nya he fiɔmi klɔuklɔu.
21Ami Paulo nitsɛ ye nine nya biɔmi ji nɛ ɔ nɛ.
22Ke nɔ ko sume Nyɔmtsɛ Yesu Kristo sane ɔ, jamɛ a nɔ ɔ e plɛ musutsɛ! Wa Nyɔmtsɛ, ba! (Maran ata.)
23Nyɔmtsɛ Yesu Kristo dloomi ɔ kɛ nyɛ nɛ hi si!
24Ye suɔmi ɔ kɛ nyɛ tsuo nɛ hi si ngɛ Kristo Yesu mi! Amen.

english_text:
1 From Paul, chosen by God to be an apostle of Jesus Christ, and from Timothy, who is also a follower.
To God's church in Corinth and to all of God's people in Achaia.
2I pray that God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ will be kind to you and will bless you with peace!
Paul Gives Thanks
3Praise God, the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ! The Father is a merciful God, who always gives us comfort. 4He comforts us when we are in trouble, so that we can share this same comfort with others in trouble. 5We share in the terrible sufferings of Christ, but also in the wonderful comfort he gives. 6We suffer in the hope that you will be comforted and saved. And because we are comforted, you will also be comforted, as you patiently endure suffering like ours. 7You never disappoint us. You suffered as much as we did, and we know that you will be comforted as we were.
8 My friends, I want you to know what a hard time we had in Asia. Our sufferings were so horrible and so unbearable that death seemed certain. 9In fact, we felt sure we were going to die. But this made us stop trusting in ourselves and start trusting God, who raises the dead to life. 10God saved us from the threat of death, and we are sure that he will do it again and again. 11Please help us by praying for us. Then many people will give thanks for the blessings we receive in answer to all these prayers.
Paul's Change of Plans
12We can be proud of our clear conscience. We have always lived honestly and sincerely, especially when we were with you. And we were guided by God's gift of undeserved grace instead of by the wisdom of this world. 13I am not writing anything you cannot read and understand. I hope you will understand it completely, 14just as you already partly understand us. Then when our Lord Jesus returns, you can be as proud of us as we are of you.
15I was so sure of your pride in us that I had planned to visit you first of all. In this way you would have the blessing of two visits from me— 16 once on my way to Macedonia and again on my return from there. Then you could send me on to Judea. 17Do you think I couldn't make up my mind about what to do? Or do I seem like someone who says “Yes” or “No” simply to please others? 18God can be trusted, and so can I, when I say our answer to you has always been “Yes” and never “No.” 19 This is because Jesus Christ the Son of God is always “Yes” and never “No.” And he is the one Silas, Timothy, and I told you about.
20Christ says “Yes” to all God's promises. This is why we have Christ to say “Amen” for us to the glory of God. 21And so God makes it possible for you and us to stand firmly together with Christ. God is also the one who chose us 22and put his Spirit in our hearts to show that we belong only to him.
23God is my witness that I stayed away from Corinth, just to keep from being hard on you. 24We are not bosses who tell you what to believe. We are working with you to make you glad, because your faith is strong.
translation_text:
1Imi Paulo, nɛ ji Yesu Kristo bɔfo ngɛ Mawu suɔmi nya a, kɛ wa nyɛmi Timoteo ɔ ngma ya ha Mawu asafo nɛ ngɛ Korinto kɛ he tsɔli kulaa nɛ ngɛ Akaia tsuo ɔ:
2Dloomi kɛ he jɔmi nɛ je wa tsɛ Mawu kɛ Nyɔmtsɛ Yesu Kristo dɛ mi ɔ ha nyɛ.
Paulo naa Mawu si
3A gbaa Mawu kɛ wa Nyɔmtsɛ Yesu Kristo Tsɛ ɔ, nɔ nɛ ji mi mi sali a tsɛ, kɛ ɛbua womi kulaa Mawu ɔ, 4nɔ nɛ jɔɔ wa bua ngɛ wa nɔ nami ɔmɛ kulaa mi, konɛ wɔ hu wa nyɛ nɛ waa kɛ bua womi nɛ Mawu kɛ woɔ wa bua a nɛ wo nihi nɛ naa amanehlu tsuaa amanehlu ɔmɛ a bua. 5Nɛ bɔ nɛ Kristo amanehlu ɔmɛ baa wa nɔ kɛ bee nɔ ɔ, ja nɔuu kɛ Kristo he ɔ, wa bua womi ɔ hu hiɛɛ kɛ bee nɔ. 6Se ke amanehlu wa naa a, nyɛ bua womi kɛ yi wami hemi he ʼi; nɛ ke wa bua a woɔ hu, e ji nyɛ bua womi nɛ haa nyɛ toɔ nyɛ tsui si kpoo kɛ naa amanehlu nɛ wa naa a nɔuu eko. 7Nɛ wa hɛ nɛ ngɛ nyɛ nɔ ɔ gbɔle we, ejakaa wa le kaa bɔ nɛ nyɛ naa amanehlu ɔ eko ɔ, ja nɔuu kɛ nyɛ naa bua womi ɔ hu eko.
8Mamimɛ, wa sume kaa waa ngɔ wa nɔ́ nɛ wa na ngɛ Asia a kɛ laa nyɛ. Wa na nɔ tsɔ, pe bɔ nɛ wa ma nyɛ po, nɛ wa hɛ be je mi himi nɔ tete. 9Wɔ nitsɛmɛ wa na ngɛ wa mi paa kaa wa ma gbo, konɛ wa ko ngɔ wa hɛ ngɔ fɔ wɔ nitsɛmɛ wa he nɔ, se mohu wa ngɔ fɔ Mawu nɛ tleɔ ni gbogboehi a si ɔ nɔ, 10Mawu nɛ je wɔ kɛ je gbenɔ nɛ ngɛ gbeye nɛ ɔ mi, nɛ e ngɛ wɔ jee kɛ mwɔɔ, nɛ wa hɛ ngɛ e nɔ kaa e maa kpale je wɔ kulaa. 11Nyɛ hu nyɛɛ piɛ wa he kɛ kpa pɛɛ konɛ nihi fuu nɛ na si ha wɔ ngɛ dloomi nike nihi nɛ a kɛ ha wɔ ngɛ nihi fuu a pɛɛ kpami ɔ he.
Paulo tsake e yimitomi ɔmɛ
12Se wa fiami ji nɛ ɔ nɛ: wa he ni lemi odase nɛ e yeɔ wɔ, kaa Mawu klɔuklɔu peemi kɛ he tsɔmi mi wa ba wa je mi ngɛ ngɛ je nɛ ɔ mi, titli ɔ, ngɛ nyɛ kpɛti, nɛ pi he lo mi ni lemi nya, se mohu Mawu dloomi nya. 13Ejakaa wa ngmɛ́ ni kpahi ha we nyɛ, pe nihi nɛ nyɛ kaneɔ nɛ jehanɛ hu nyɛ le, nɛ ye hɛ ngɛ nɔ kaa nyɛ maa le kɛ maa ya nyagbe hulɔ ɔ. 14Kaa bɔ nɛ nyɛ na le wɔ hulɔ fa kɛ fa, kaa nyɛ fiami nɔ́ ji wɔ, kaa bɔ nɛ nyɛ hu nyɛ ji wa nɔ́ ngɛ Nyɔmtsɛ Yesu ligbi ɔ nɔ ɔ.
15Kikɛmɛ a hɛ kɛ nɔ fɔmi nɛ ɔ he je nɛ i to ye yi mi kaa ma ba nyɛ ngɔ kekle ɔ nɛ, konɛ nyɛ na dloomi si enyɔ. 16Ma ba gu nyɛ ngɔ kɛ ya Makedonia, nɛ jehanɛ hu ma kpale ye se kɛ je Makedonia kɛ ba nyɛ ngɔ ekohu, konɛ nyɛ ya je mi blɔ kɛ ya Yudea. 17Blɔɔ nɛ i to ye yi mi kikɛ ɔ, yi flɛflɛ i kɛ pee lo? Aloo ye yi mi nɛ i to ɔ, he lo nya i to ngɛ konɛ ma de “Ee,” kɛ “Dɛbi,” ngɛ be kake mi lo? 18Mawu ji wa odase, kaa wa munyu nɛ waa kɛ nyɛ tu ɔ, e pi “Ee” kɛ “Dɛbi” ngɛ be kake mi. 19Ejakaa Mawu bi Yesu Kristo, nɔ nɛ i kɛ Silvano kɛ Timoteo fiɛ e he sane ngɛ nyɛ kpɛti ɔ, e pi “Ee” kɛ “Dɛbi” se mohu e ji “Ee”. 20Ejakaa Mawu si womihi abɔ nɛ ngɛ ɔ, e mi “Ee” ɔ ngɛ, nɛ e mi nɔuu “Amen” ɔ ngɛ, konɛ a gu e nɔ kɛ wo Mawu hɛ mi nyami. 21Se Mawu ji nɔ nɛ haa waa kɛ nyɛ tsuo nane pii si ngɛ Kristo mi, nɛ e pɔ wɔ nu, 22nɛ e sɔu wa nya, nɛ e kɛ Mumi ɔ yi ba pomi nɔ́ ha wɔ ngɛ wa tsui mi hulɔ.
23Se imi lɛɛ i ngɛ Mawu tsɛe nɛ ba ye ye klaa he odase kaa yɛ yi baami he je nɛ i na we ma ba Korinto ɔ nɛ. 24Wa yi nyɛ hemi kɛ yemi nyɔguɛ, ejakaa nyɛ daa si tutuutu ngɛ hemi kɛ yemi ɔ mi, se mohu wa piɛ nyɛ he kɛ ngɛ nyɛ bua jɔmi he ni tsue.

english_text:
1I have decided not to make my next visit with you so painful. 2If I make you feel bad, who would be left to cheer me up, except the people I had made to feel bad? 3The reason I want to be happy is to make you happy. I wrote as I did because I didn't want to visit you and be made to feel bad, when you should make me feel happy. 4At the time I wrote, I was suffering terribly. My eyes were full of tears, and my heart was broken. But I didn't want to make you feel bad. I only wanted to let you know how much I cared for you.
Forgiveness
5I don't want to be hard on you. But if one of you has made someone feel bad, I am not really the one who has been made to feel bad. Some of you are the ones. 6Most of you have already pointed out the wrong that person did, and this is punishment enough for what was done.
7When people sin, you should forgive and comfort them, so they won't give up in despair. 8You should make them sure of your love for them.
9I also wrote because I wanted to test you and find out if you would follow my instructions. 10I will forgive anyone you forgive. Yes, for your sake and with Christ as my witness, I have forgiven whatever needed to be forgiven. 11I have done this to keep Satan from getting the better of us. We all know what goes on in his mind.
12 When I went to Troas to preach the good news about Christ, I found that the Lord had already prepared the way. 13But I was worried when I didn't find my friend Titus there. So I left the other followers and went on to Macedonia.
14I am grateful that God always makes it possible for Christ to lead us to victory. God also helps us spread the knowledge about Christ everywhere, and this knowledge is like the smell of perfume. 15-16In fact, God thinks of us as a perfume that brings Christ to everyone. For people who are being saved, this perfume has a sweet smell and leads them to a better life. But for people who are lost, it has a bad smell and leads them to a horrible death.
No one really has what it takes to do this work. 17A lot of people try to get rich from preaching God's message. But we are God's sincere messengers, and by the power of Christ we speak our message with God as our witness.
translation_text:
1Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, i pee ye juɛmi kaa i kɛ kɔmɔ yemi be nyɛ ngɔ bae hu. 2Ejakaa ke i ha nyɛ ye kɔmɔ ɔ, mɛnɔ ji nɔ nɛ haa ye bua jɔɔ mɔ, kaa ja nɔ nɛ i ha e ye kɔmɔ ɔ nɔuu? 3Enɛ ɔ he je nɛ i ngma nyɛ enɛ ɔ, konɛ, ke i ba a, ma ko ba ye kɔmɔ ngɛ nihi nɛ jinɛ sa kaa i naa a he bua jɔmi ɔmɛ a he, ejakaa ye hɛ ngɛ nyɛ tsuo nyɛ nɔ kaa ye bua jɔmi ji nyɛ tsuo nyɛ bua jɔmi. 4Se tsui yemi kɛ fimi babauu mi i je kɛ ngma nyɛ, kɛ gu vo nyu babauu hu mi, tsa pi nɛ nyɛɛ ye kɔmɔ he je, se mohu nɛ nyɛɛ na suɔmi babauu nɛ i suɔ nyɛ.
Nɔtɔlɔ he yayamipami
5Se ke nɔ ko ha a ye kɔmɔ ɔ, pi imi nɛ e ha i ye kɔmɔ se (kone ye nya nɛ ko wa tsɔ ɔ) e ha nyɛ kulaa nyɛ ye kɔmɔ ko kɛ. 6Jamɛ a tsɛ ɔ, e hɛ mi nɛ nihi fuu kã a hiɛ ha lɛ, 7lɔ ɔ he ɔ, jehanɛ nyɛ kɛ pa lɛ, nɛ nyɛɛ jɔɔ e bua mohu, konɛ kɔmɔ yemi fuu tsɔ ɔ ko ba ha e nine mi nɛ wo nyu. 8Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, i kpaa nyɛ pɛɛ nɛ nyɛ ha e le kaa nyɛ suɔ lɛ, 9ejakaa enɛ ɔ he hulɔ nɛ i ngma nyɛ womi ɔ nɛ, konɛ ma kɛ ka nyɛ kaa nyɛ buɔ tue ngɛ nihi kulaa mi lo? 10Nɔ nɛ nyɛɛ kɛ nɔ́ ko paa lɛ ɔ, imi hu i kɛ paa lɛ, ejakaa imi hu, ke i kɛ nɔ́ ko pa a, nɔ́ nɛ i kɛ pa a, i kɛ pa ngɛ nyɛ he ngɛ Kristo hɛ mi, 11konɛ Satan nine nɛ ko su wa nɔ, ejakaa e juɛmi ɔmɛ ɔ a kɛ laa wɔ.
Paulo tsuiyemi ngɛ Troa
12Bene i ba Troa ngɛ Kristo sane kpakpa a he nɛ ya bli sinya ha mi ngɛ Nyɔmtsɛ ɔ mi ɔ, 13i hao ngɛ mumi mi, ejakaa i nɛ́ ye nyɛmi Tito; lɔ ɔ he ɔ, i sɛ mɛ nɛ i pue nɔ kɛ ba Makedonia.
Kunimiyemi kɛ gu Kristo nɔ
14Se sina ha Mawu, ejakaa ngɛ waa kɛ Kristo kake peemi mi ɔ, e haa wa yeɔ kunimi daa, nɛ e haa e he nilemi he via a guu wa nɔ jee kpo ngɛ he tsuaa he. 15Ejakaa Kristo he viami kpakpa ji wɔ ha Mawu ngɛ nihi nɛ a heɔ a yi wami kɛ nihi nɛ a hɛ mi kpataa a kulaa mi: 16ni nɛ ɔmɛ ɔ, wa ji gbenɔ via ha mɛ kɛ yaa gbenɔ mi, se ni kpa amɛ ɔ, wa ji wami via ha mɛ kɛ yaa wami mi. Nɛ mɛnɔ lɛ sa ha enɛ ɔmɛ? 17Ejakaa wa be kaa ni komɛ nɛ juaa Mawu munyu ɔ, se mohu wa tuɔ lɛ ngmingmiingmi bɔ nɛ e je Mawu mi ɔ ngɛ Mawu hɛ mi, ngɛ Kristo mi.

english_text:
God's New Agreement
1Are we once again bragging about ourselves? Do we need letters to you or from you to tell others about us? Some people do need letters telling about them. 2But you are our letter, and you are in our hearts for everyone to read and understand. 3 You are like a letter written by Christ and delivered by us. But you are not written with pen and ink or on tablets made of stone. You are written in our hearts by the Spirit of the living God.
4We are sure about all this. Christ makes us sure in the very presence of God. 5We don't have the right to claim that we have done anything on our own. God gives us what it takes to do all we do. 6 He makes us worthy to be the servants of his new agreement that comes from the Holy Spirit and not from a written Law. After all, the Law brings death, but the Spirit brings life.
7 The Law of Moses brought only the promise of death, even though it was carved on stones and given in a wonderful way. Still the Law made Moses' face shine so brightly the people of Israel could not look at it, even though it was a fading glory. 8So won't the agreement the Spirit brings to us be even more wonderful? 9If something that brings the death sentence is glorious, won't something that makes us acceptable to God be even more glorious? 10In fact, the new agreement is so wonderful that the Law is no longer glorious at all. 11The Law was given with a glory that faded away. But the glory of the new agreement is much greater, because it will never fade away.
12This wonderful hope makes us feel like speaking freely. 13 We are not like Moses. His face was shining, but he covered it to keep the people of Israel from seeing the brightness fade away. 14The people were stubborn, and something still keeps them from seeing the truth when the Law is read. Only Christ can take away the covering that keeps them from seeing.
15When the Law of Moses is read, they have their minds covered over 16 with a covering that is removed only for those who turn to the Lord. 17The Lord and the Spirit are one and the same, and the Lord's Spirit sets us free. 18 So our faces are not covered. They show the bright glory of the Lord, as the Lord's Spirit makes us more and more like our glorious Lord.
translation_text:
Somi He ɔ he sɔmɔli
1Anɛ pe wa kpale ngɛ wa he yi jee? Aloo e hia kaa wa hɛɛ yi jemi womi, kaa bɔ nɛ ni komɛ hɛɛ kɛ ba haa nyɛ loo kɛ jee nyɛ ngɔ ɔ lo? 2Nyɛ nitsɛmɛ ji wa womi nɛ a ngma ngɔ wo wa tsui mi nɛ nihi tsuo le nɛ a kaneɔ. 3A je nyɛ ngɔ tsɔɔ paa kaa nyɛ ji Kristo womi nɛ wa ngma, pi kɛ ni ngmami nyu, se mohu Mawu hɛ kalɔ ɔ mumi ɔ a kɛ ngma, pi ngɛ tɛ sleetihi a nɔ, se mohu tsui nɛ ji he lo sleeti nɔ.
