1Jehanɛ moo lɛɛ, ye bi, o he nɛ wa ngɛ dloomi nɛ ngɛ Kristo Yesu mi ɔ mi. 2Nihi nɛ o nu ngɛ ye nya ngɛ odasefohi fuu a nya a, kɔlɔ ɔ nɔuu o tu ngɔ wo nimli anɔkualetsɛmɛ a dɛ, nihi nɛ ngɛ he wami nɛ a ma kɛ tsɔɔ ni kpahi hulɔ.
3Mia o hɛ mi ngɛ nɔ nami mi, kaa Yesu Kristo ta bulɔ kpakpa ko. 4Nɔ ko nyɛɛ we ta blɔ nɛ e kɛ e he wo we mi munyuhi a mi, ejakaa e suɔ kaa e sa e tatsɛ ɔ hɛ mi. 5Nɛ ke nɔ ko ngɛ nɔ́ ko ngɛ nɔ ko he plee hu ɔ, a be lɛ manye jlasi fie, kaa ja e plee he ngɛ mlaa nya. 6Ngmɔ hulɔ nɛ tsuɔ ni ɔ, lɛ kekle sa kaa e ye ngmɔ ni ɔ eko. Susuu nɔ nɛ i ngɛ mo dee nɛ ɔ he. 7Nyɔmtsɛ ɔ ma ha o na nihi kulaa sisi.
8O hɛ nɛ hi Yesu Kristo nɔ nɛ te si kɛ je gbeje nɛ je David nina mi ɔ nɔ, bɔ nɛ i fiɛ ngɛ ye sane kpakpa a mi ɔ, 9nɔ́ nɛ he amane nɛ i ngɛ nae, kɛ yaa su kpa mi tete, kaa yayami peelɔ ko; se kɛ ɔ, Mawu munyu ɔ, a wui lɛ kpa 10Enɛ ɔ he je ɔ i miaa ye hɛ mi ngɛ sanehi kulaa mi ngɛ nihi nɛ ahla mɛ ɔ a he, konɛ mɛ hu a nine nɛ su yi wami hemi nɛ ngɛ Kristo Yesu mi ɔ kɛ neneene hɛ mi nyami ɔ nɔ. 11Anɔkuale munyu ji nɛ ɔ nɛ:
“Ke waa kɛ lɛ gbo ɔ, waa kɛ lɛ ma na wami hulɔ.
12Ke wa mia wa hɛ mi ngɛ nɔ nami mi ɔ, waa kɛ lɛ maa ye matsɛ hulɔ;
Ke wa kpa ngɛ e se ɔ, lɛ hu e ma kpa ngɛ wa se.
13Ke wa pee we wa he anɔkualetsɛmɛ ɔ, lɛɛ e maa hi si
anɔkualetsɛ, ejakaa e be nyɛe ma je lɛ nitsɛ e he se.”
Nitsulɔ kpakpa
14Kaii mɛ kikɛmɛ a ni nɛ ɔmɛ, nɛ o ma nɔ mi ha mɛ ngɛ Nyɔmtsɛ ɔ hɛ mi, ykonɛ a ko hwu lilɛ ta nɛ se nami ko be he, se e butuu nihi nɛ nuɔ ɔ mohu ɔ. 15Bɔɔ mɔde nɛ o da si ngɛ Mawu hɛ mi kaa znɔ ko nɛ sa, ni tsulɔ nɛ gbo we zo nɛ tsɔɔ anɔkuale munyu ɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ. 16Se yakayaka ni sɛɛmi nɛ bleɔ nɔ ɔ, sã o he kɛ je he; ejakaa e fieɔ nihi kɛ jee Mawu he kɛ yaa lokoo, 17nɛ a munyu ɔ ma sã nɔ kaa hiɔ yaya sãa nɔ ɔ: a ti ni komɛ ji Himeneo kɛ Fileto, 18nihi nɛ tla blɔ kɛ je anɔkuale ɔ he, nɛ a deɔ ke si temi ɔ be momo, nɛ a butuu ni komɛ a hemi kɛ yemi ɔ. 19Se Mawu sisi tomi tɛ na he wa a maa si kpɛii, nɛ e hɛɛ kikɛmɛ a nyasɔomi nɔ nɛ ɔ: “Nyɔmtsɛ ɔ le lɛ nitsɛ e ni ɔmɛ,” kɛ: “Ha nɛ nɔ tsuaa nɔ nɛ woɔ Kristo biɛ ɔ ta a nɛ sã e he kɛ je nihi nɛ dɛ blɔ ɔmɛ a he.”
20We ngua ko mi ɔ pi sika tsu nihi kɛ sika hiɔ nihi kɛkɛ nɛ ngɛ lejɛ ɔ, se mohu tso nihi kɛ zu nihi hu ngɛ mi, ekomɛ ɔ a buo, se ekomɛ hu a bui. 21Jehanɛ ke nɔ ko tsukɔ e he kɛ je kikɛmɛ a ni nɛ ɔmɛ a he ɔ, e ma plɛ nɔ́ ko nɛ a buu nɛ a tsukɔ he klɔuu nɛ hi ha wetsɛ ɔ saminya nɛ a dla lɛ kɛ ha ni tsumi kpakpa tsuaa ni tsumi kpakpa. 22Se nihewi a kɔnɔ ɔmɛ ɔ, tuu nya fo, nɛ o kɛ nihi nɛ tsɛɔ Nyɔmtsɛ ɔ kɛ jee tsui nɛ mi tsɔ mi ɔ nɛ nyɛɛ dami, hemi kɛ yemi, suɔmi kɛ he jɔmi se. 23Se kuasiahi a nɔ jemi nɛ a kɛ kase we nɔ ko ɔ guu, ejakaa o le kaa e kɛ pɛ baa. 24Nyɔmtsɛ ɔ sɔmɔlɔ ɔ, e sɛ kaa e pɛɛ, se mohu e mi nɛ jɔ ha nihi kulaa, nɔ nɛ le ni tsɔɔmi, nɔ nɛ toɔ e tsui si haa yayami, 25nɔ nɛ kɛ mi mi jɔmi tuɔ munyu tsɔɔ nihi nɛ tee si siɔ lɛ ɔ, kaa alinɔ Mawu ma ha mɛ tsui tsakemi nɛ a le anɔkuale ɔ lo? 26nɛ a hɛ mi nɛ tsɔ mɛ kɛ je abosiami klama a mi, ejakaa e kɛ du mɛ nɛ a pee e suɔmi nya ni.

english_text:
What People Will Be Like in the Last Days
1You can be certain that in the last days there will be some very hard times. 2People will love only themselves and money. They will be proud, stuck-up, rude, and disobedient to their parents. They will also be ungrateful, godless, 3heartless, and hateful. Their words will be cruel, and they will have no self-control or pity. These people will hate everything good. 4They will be sneaky, reckless, and puffed up with pride. Instead of loving God, they will love pleasure. 5Even though they will make a show of being religious, their religion won't be real. Don't have anything to do with such people.
6Some men fool whole families, just to get power over those women who are slaves of sin and are controlled by all sorts of desires. 7These women always want to learn something new, but they never can discover the truth. 8 Just as Jannes and Jambres opposed Moses, these people are enemies of the truth. Their minds are sick, and their faith isn't real. 9But they won't get very far with their foolishness. Soon everyone will know the truth about them, just as Jannes and Jambres were found out.
Paul's Last Instructions to Timothy
10Timothy, you know what I teach and how I live. You know what I want to do and what I believe. You have seen how patient and loving I am, and how in the past I put up with 11 trouble and suffering in the cities of Antioch, Iconium, and Lystra. Yet the Lord rescued me from all those terrible troubles. 12In fact, anyone who belongs to Christ Jesus and wants to live right will have trouble from others. 13But evil people who pretend to be what they are not will become worse than ever, as they fool others and are fooled themselves.
14Keep on being faithful to what you were taught and to what you believed. After all, you know who taught you these things. 15Since childhood, you have known the Holy Scriptures that are able to make you wise enough to have faith in Christ Jesus and be saved. 16Everything in the Scriptures is God's Word. All of it is useful for teaching and helping people and for correcting them and showing them how to live. 17The Scriptures train God's servants to do all kinds of good deeds.
translation_text:
Nyagbe ligbi ɔmɛ
1Se na nɛ o le kaa nyagbe ligbi ɔmɛ a mi ɔ, he hiami be maa ba. 2Ejakaa nimli ma plɛ a he hesuɔli, sikasuɔli, fiali, he woli, musu bɔli, fɔli a nɔ tue gboli, otlumuhi, nihi nɛ a he tsɔ we, 3nihi nɛ plee we nɔ he, somi mi kuli, sieku yeli, nihi nɛ nyɛ we a kɔnɔ nɔ nɛ a ye, nihi nɛ a hɛ jɔɛ, nihi nɛ sume nɔ́ kpakpa, 4nɔ se blɔ tsɔɔli, yi mi wali, he nɔ woli, nihi nɛ suɔ fiɛmi nɛ ngɔɔ pe Mawu, 5nihi nɛ hɛɛ Mawu jami su, se a kua e mi he wami ɔ. Sã o he kɛ je kikɛmɛ a nimli a he? 6Ejakaa ni nɛ ɔmɛ a kpɛti ni komɛ ji nihi nɛ juɔ si sɛɛ wehi a mi nɛ a ya ngɔɔ yihi nɛ be yi mi nɛ yayami ye a nɔ nɛ akɔnɔ slɔɔtohi kpakaa mɛ 7nɛ a hlaa ni kasemi, se kɛ ɔ, a nyɛ we nɛ a le anɔkuale ɔ. 8Se kaa bɔ nɛ Yane kɛ Yambre te si si Mose ɔ, ja nɔuu kikɛmɛ a nimli nɛ ɔmɛ kuɔ anɔkuale ɔ nya, nihi nɛ a yi mi puɛ, nihi nɛ pi ni komɛ ngɛ hemi kɛ yemi ɔ blɔfami. 9A be a hɛ mi yae tsɔ ko, ejakaa a kuasia peemi ɔ maa je kpo paa ngɛ nihi tsuo a hɛ mi, kaa bɔ nɛ Yane kɛ Yambremɛ a nɔ ɔ hu je kpo ɔ.
Nyagbe ni tsɔɔmi
10Se moo lɛɛ, o le ye tsɔɔmi, ye je mi bami, ye yi mi tomi, ye hemi kɛ yemi, ye tsui si tomi, ye suɔmi, ye hɛ mi miami, 11ye nɔ namihi, ye omane hluhi nɛ i na ngɛ Antiokia kɛ Ikonium kɛ Listra a; yi mi wamihi abɔ nɛ i na nɛ Nyɔmtsɛ ɔ je mi kɛ je kulaa mi ɔ. 12Lɔ ɔ he ɔ nihi kulaa hu nɛ hlaa kaa a hi si ngɛ Mawu jami nya ngɛ Kristo Yesu mi ɔ, a maa wa mɛ yi mi. 13Se nimli yayamihi kɛ sisili maa ya hɛ mi ngɛ yayami peemi mi; a sisiɔ nihi, nɛ mɛ hu a sisiɔ mɛ. 14Se moo lɛɛ hii si ngɛ nihi nɛ o kase nɛ o ngɛ he wami ngɛ nɔ ɔmɛ a mi, ejakaa o le nɔ nɛ nya nɛ o kase kɛ je, 15nɛ o jokuɛwi a si o je nɛ o le ngmami klɔuklɔu ɔ, nɛ ma nyɛ ma ha o le nihi nɛ maa gu Kristo Yesu nɔ hemi kɛ yemi nɔ kɛ ya yi wami hemi mi ɔ. 16Ngmami tsuaa ngmami nɛ je Mawu mumi mi ɔ, e hi ha ni tsɔɔmi kɛ hɛ mi kami kɛ nɔ dlami kɛ tsɔsemi nɛ ngɛ dami mi ɔ, 17konɛ Mawu nɔmlɔ ɔ nɛ hi kɛ pi si, nɛ a dla lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ ha ni tsumi kpakpa tsuaa ni tsumi kpakpa.

english_text:
1When Christ Jesus comes as king, he will be the judge of everyone, whether they are living or dead. So with God and Christ as witnesses, I command you 2to preach God's message. Do it willingly, even if it isn't the popular thing to do. You must correct people and point out their sins. But also cheer them up, and when you instruct them, always be patient. 3The time is coming when people won't listen to good teaching. Instead, they will look for teachers who will please them by telling them only what they are itching to hear. 4They will turn from the truth and eagerly listen to senseless stories. 5But you must stay calm and be willing to suffer. You must work hard, telling the good news and to do your job well.
6Now the time has come for me to die. My life is like a drink offering being poured out on the altar. 7I have fought well. I have finished the race, and I have been faithful. 8So a crown will be given to me for pleasing the Lord. He judges fairly, and on the day of judgment he will give a crown to me and to everyone else who wants him to appear with power.
Personal Instructions
9Come to see me as soon as you can. 10 Demas loves the things of this world so much that he left me and went to Thessalonica. Crescens has gone to Galatia, and Titus has gone to Dalmatia. 11 Only Luke has stayed with me.
Mark can be very helpful to me, so please find him and bring him with you. 12 I sent Tychicus to Ephesus.
13 When you come, bring the coat I left at Troas with Carpus. Don't forget to bring the scrolls, especially the ones made of leather.
14 Alexander, the metalworker, has hurt me in many ways. But the Lord will pay him back for what he has done. 15Alexander opposes what we preach, so you had better watch out for him.
16When I was first put on trial, no one helped me. In fact, everyone deserted me. I hope it won't be held against them. 17But the Lord stood beside me. He gave me the strength to tell his full message, so that all Gentiles would hear it. And I was kept safe from hungry lions. 18 The Lord will always keep me from being harmed by evil, and he will bring me safely into his heavenly kingdom. Praise him forever and ever! Amen.
Final Greetings
19 Give my greetings to Priscilla and Aquila and to the family of Onesiphorus.
20 Erastus stayed at Corinth.
Trophimus was sick when I left him at Miletus.
21Do your best to come before winter.
Eubulus, Pudens, Linus, and Claudia send you their greetings, and so do the rest of the Lord's followers.
22I pray that the Lord will bless your life and will be kind to you.
translation_text:
1I ngɛ mo dee faii ngɛ Mawu kɛ Mawetsɛ Yesu Kristo nɛ maa ba ba kojo hɛ kali kɛ ni gbogboehi ngɛ e bami kɛ e matsɛ yemi ɔ mi ɔ hɛ mi ke: 2Fiɛ munyu ɔ, koo jɔɔ, deka ngɛ jio, deka be jio, ka hɛ mi, wo ga, bɔɔ kɔkɔ ngɛ tsui si tomi kɛ ni tsɔɔmi kulaa mi. 3Ejakaa be ko maa ba nɛ a be anɔkuale tsɔɔmi ɔ tue bue hu, ngɛ mɛ nitsɛmɛ a kɔnɔ ɔmɛ a nya, se mohu a ma bua tsɔɔli a nya ngɔ wo a he, ninɛmɛ nɛ ma de mɛ nihi nɛ a suɔ kaa a nu. 4A ma blɛ anɔkuale ɔ ngɔ pue a tue se, nɛ a maa kpale ya bu nyaziahi mohu tue. 5Se moo lɛɛ, o hɛ nɛ ka si ngɛ nihi kulaa mi, mia o hɛ mi ngɛ dengme gbomihi a mi, tsu sane kpakpa jajelɔ ni tsumi ɔ, nɛ gbee o sɔmɔmi ni tsumi ɔ nya kulaa!
6Ejakaa ami lɛɛ, a ngɛ ye muɔ plee kɛ ngɛ si puee mo kaa bɔ, nɛ ye jemi be ɔ su. 7Ta kpakpa a, i hwu; fo ɔ, i tu gbe nya; hemi kɛ yemi ɔ i hɛɛ mi; 8nɔ nɛ piɛ nɛ fɔɔ si ha mi ji dami jlasi ɔ, nɛ Nyɔmtsɛ nɛ ji dami kojolɔ ɔ ma ha mi ngɛ jamɛ a Ligbi ɔ nɔ ɔ, nɛ pi ye nɔ kake nɛ e ma ha, se mohu nihi kulaa nɛ suɔ e bami ɔ hulɔ ɔ.
Slɔmi ha Timoteo nitsɛ
9Bɔɔ mɔde nɛ o ba ye ngɔ mla. 10Ejakaa nɛ Dema suɔ amlɔ amlɔ je nɛ ɔ mi he je ɔ, e je ye he kɛ ho Tesalonika ya; Kreske ho Galata ya, Tito ho Dalmatia ya; 11Luka pɛ lɛ e kɛ mi ngɛ. Ngɔɔ Marko nɛ o kɛ lɛ nɛ ba, ejakaa e hi ha mi ngɛ sɔmɔmi ɔ he. 12Tihiko ɔ lɛɛ i tsɔ lɛ Efeso. 13Kotoku ɔ nɛ i je he ngɛ Troia ngɛ Karpo ngɔ ɔ, o kɛ ba, kɛ womi ɔmɛ hulɔ, se titli ɔ lohwehi a he womi nɛ a ngmaa ni ngɛ nɔ ɔ. 14Aleksandro, sɔlɔ ɔ, peemi yayami wawɛɛ nitsɛ. Nyɔmtsɛ ɔ nɛ to lɛ nane mi ngɛ e ni tsumi ɔmɛ a nya. 15Mo hu hyɛ o he nɔ nɛ hi ngɛ e he, ejakaa e te si ngɔ si wa munyu ɔmɛ wawɛɛ. 16Ngɛ ye kekle nya jemi ɔ mi ɔ, a ti nɔ ko nɔ ko ya sɛ mi, se mohu mɛ kulaa a si mi, a ko bu enɛ ɔ ngɔ fɔ a nɔ. 17Se Nyɔmtsɛ ɔ fi ye se nɛ e wo mi he wami, konɛ a gu ye nɔ kɛ ma fiɛmi ɔ nɔ mi, nɛ maje li ɔmɛ kulaa a nu, nɛ a je mi kɛ je jata a nya mi. 18Nɛ Nyɔmtsɛ ɔ ma je mi kokooko kɛ maa je ni yayahi kulaa mi, nɛ e ma he ye yi wami kɛ maa ya e hiɔwe matsɛ yemi ɔ mi: Lɛ a ngɔ anuminyami ngɔ ha kɛ ya neneene kɛ neneene! Amen.
Nyagbe sɛyemi
19I biɔ Priska kɛ Akwila kɛ Onesiforo we ɔ. 20Erasto ngɛ Korinto; se Trofimo ɔ, i si lɛ ngɛ Mileto nɛ e ngɛ gboe. 21Bɔɔ mɔde nɛ o ba loko fiɛ be ɔ nɛ su. Eubulo kɛ Pude kɛ Lino kɛ Klaudia kɛ nyamimɛ ɔmɛ kulaa ke a biɔ mo.
22Mawetsɛ Yesu Kristo kɛ o mumi ɔ nɛ hi si! Mawu dloomi ɔ kɛ nyɛ nɛ hi si! Amen.

english_text:
1From Paul, a servant of God and an apostle of Jesus Christ.
I encourage God's own people to have more faith and to understand the truth about religion. 2Then they will have the hope of eternal life God promised long ago. And God never tells a lie! 3So, at the proper time, God our Savior gave this message and told me to announce what he had said.
4 Titus, because of our faith, you are like a son to me. I pray that God our Father and Christ Jesus our Savior will be kind to you and will bless you with peace!
What Titus Was To Do in Crete
5I left you in Crete to do what had been left undone and to appoint leaders for the churches in each town. As I told you, 6 they must have a good reputation and be faithful in marriage. Their children must be followers of the Lord and not have a reputation for being wild and disobedient.
7Church officials are in charge of God's work, and so they must also have a good reputation. They must not be bossy, quick-tempered, heavy drinkers, bullies, or dishonest in business. 8Instead, they must be friendly to strangers and enjoy doing good things. They must also be sensible, fair, pure, and self-controlled. 9They must stick to the true message they were taught, so their good teaching can help others and correct everyone who opposes it.
10There are many who don't respect authority, and they fool others by talking nonsense. This is especially true of some Jewish followers. 11But you must make them be quiet. They are after money, and they upset whole families by teaching what they should not. 12It is like one of their own prophets once said,
“The people of Crete
always tell lies.
They are greedy and lazy
like wild animals.”
13This surely is a true saying. And you should be hard on such people, so you can help them grow stronger in their faith. 14Don't pay any attention to any of those senseless Jewish stories and human commands. These are made up by people who won't obey the truth.
15Everything is pure for someone whose heart is pure. But nothing is pure for an unbeliever with a dirty mind. That person's mind and conscience are destroyed. 16Such people claim to know God, but their actions prove they really don't. They are disgusting. They won't obey God, and they are too worthless to do anything good.
translation_text:
1Paulo, Mawu sɔmɔlɔ, kɛ Yesu Kristo bɔfo. Ahla mi nɛ a tsɔ mi nɛ ma ya ye bua ninɛmɛ nɛ Mawu hla amɛ a hemi kɛ yemi, nɛ ma kɛ mɛ nɛ ba anɔkuale nɛ wa jami ɔ tsɔɔ, 2nɛ maa si ngɛ neneene wami ɔ he hɛ kɛ nɔ fɔmi ɔ mi. Mawu nɛ yi lakpa a wo wɔ kikɛmɛ a wami nɛ ɔ he si loko a bɔ je mi be ɔmɛ, 3nɛ ngɛ be nɛ sa mi ɔ, e je lɛ si ngɛ e munyu ɔ mi. Fiɛmi sane nɛ ɔ a tu ngɔ wo ye dɛ ngɛ Mawu nɛ ji wa yi wami helɔ ɔ fami nya.
4I ngma ya ha Tito nɛ ji ye bi nitsɛ ngɛ hemi kɛ yemi kake ɔ nɔuu blɔfami ɔ:
Dloomi, mɔbɔ nami kɛ he jɔmi nɛ je Tsɛ Mawu ɔ kɛ Mawetsɛ Yesu Kristo, wa yiwami helɔ ɔ, dɛ mi ɔ ha mo!
Tito nitsumi ngɛ Kreta
5Nɔ́ nɛ he je nɛ i si mo ngɛ Kreta a ji konɛ o to nihi nɛ piɛ ɔ blɔ nɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ, nɛ o wo nikɔtɔmahi ngɛ ma tsuaa ma mi, kaa bɔ nɛ i de mo momo ɔ: 6lɔ ɔ ji, a ti nɔ tsuaa nɔ nɛ pee nɔ ko nɛ piami ko be e he, nɛ e ji nɔ nɛ ngɛ yo kake, nɛ e ngɛ bimɛ nɛ heɔ yeɔ nɛ a tui a he munyu yaya kaa yaholi loo tuegboli ji mɛ. 7Ejakaa nɔ hyɛlɔ ɔ, e sɛ kaa piami ko hii e he, akɛnɛ Mawu we mi sɔmɔlɔ nɔkɔtɔma ji lɛ he je ɔ; pi nɔ nɛ peɔ lɛ nitsɛ e tsui nya ni, pi mi mi latsɛ, pi da nulɔ, pi nine kpokpookpotsɛ, pi kpɛletsɛ, 8se mohu nibwɔ peelɔ, nɔ nɛ suɔ nɔ́ nɛ hi, nɔ nɛ juɛmi ka si, dalɔ, nɔ nɛ he tsɔ, nɔ nɛ hɛ mi ka si, 9nɔ nɛ hɛɛ anɔkuale tsɔɔmi ɔ mi, konɛ e nyɛ nɛ e tu munyu ngɔ tsɔɔ nihi ngɛ ni tsɔɔmi nɛ tsaa nɔ ɔ mi, nɛ ninɛmɛ nɛ tee si siɔ munyu ɔ hu, e ka a hɛ mi.
10Ejakaa nihi fuu ngɛ nɛ ji atua tsɔli kɛ yakayaka munyu tuli nɛ sisiɔ nɔ, titli ɔ, ninɛmɛ nɛ je nihi nɛ a po mɛ ɔmɛ a kpɛti ɔ; 11nihi nɛ sa kaa a ku a nya, ejakaa a butuu we mlukuhi kulaa, nɛ zo nihi a se nami he ɔ a tsɔɔ tsɔɔmihi nɛ dɛ. 12A ti nɔ ko nɛ ji mɛ nitsɛmɛ a gbalɔ ɔ de ke: “Kretabi yeɔ lakpa daa; lohwe yayamihi kɛ jiklɔɔtsɛmɛ kɛ hejɔli.” 13Odase nɛ ɔ ɔ anɔkuale ʼi. Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, kã a hɛ mi veveeve, konɛ a he nɛ wa ngɛ hemi kɛ yemi ɔ mi, 14nɛ a ko bu Yudafohi a nyazia amɛ kɛ nimli nɛ kpaleɔ kɛ jee anɔkuale ɔ mi ɔ a kita amɛ tue. 15Nihi nɛ a he tsɔ ɔ, nihi kulaa he tsɔ ha mɛ; se nihi nɛ a he tsɔ we kɛ nihi nɛ he we yi ɔ, nɔ́ ko nɔ́ ko be nɛ he tsɔ ha mɛ, se mohu a yi mi kɛ a he nile kulaa mi sɛ mu. 16A deɔ ke a le Mawu, se a kɛ a ni tsumihi kuaa lɛ, nɛ a ji musutsɛmɛ, kɛ tue gboli, nihi nɛ hi ha ni tsumi kpakpa ko kulaa.

english_text:
Instructions for Different Groups of People
1Titus, you must teach only what is correct. 2Tell the older men to have self-control and to be serious and sensible. Their faith, love, and patience must never fail.
3Tell the older women to behave as those who love the Lord should. They must not gossip about others or be slaves of wine. They must teach what is proper, 4so the younger women will be loving wives and mothers. 5Each of the younger women must be sensible and kind, as well as a good homemaker, who puts her own husband first. Then no one can say insulting things about God's message.
6Tell the young men to have self-control in everything.
7Always set a good example for others. Be sincere and serious when you teach. 8Use clean language that no one can criticize. Do this, and your enemies will be too ashamed to say anything against you.
9Tell slaves always to please their owners by obeying them in everything. Slaves must not talk back to their owners 10or steal from them. They must be completely honest and trustworthy. Then everyone will show great respect for what is taught about God our Savior.
God's Kindness and the New Life
11God has shown us undeserved grace by coming to save all people. 12He taught us to give up our wicked ways and our worldly desires and to live decent and honest lives in this world. 13We are filled with hope, as we wait for the glorious return of our great God and Savior Jesus Christ. 14 He gave himself to rescue us from everything evil and to make our hearts pure. He wanted us to be his own people and to be eager to do right.
15Teach these things, as you use your full authority to encourage and correct people. Make sure you earn everyone's respect.
translation_text:
Tsɔɔmi kpakpa
1Se moo lɛɛ tsɔɔ tsɔɔmi kpakpa a. 2Nimowi ɔmɛ ɔ, kãa a hɛ nɛ ka si, a pee nihi nɛ a hɛ mi jiɔ, a juɛmi nɛ ka si, a he nɛ wa ngɛ hemi kɛ yemi kɛ suɔmi kɛ tsui si tomi mi. 3Yimowi hu ja nɔuu kãa a ba a je mi bɔ nɛ sa ni klɔuklɔu ɔmɛ. A ko tu nihi a he munyu a ko pee dadeli, a pee nihi nɛ tsɔɔ ni kpakpahi, 4konɛ a tsɔɔ yihewi ɔmɛ nɛ a suɔ a hunomɛ, a suɔ a bimɛ, 5a hɛ nɛ ka si, a he nɛ tsɔ, a baa a we yi saminya, a mi mi nɛ jɔ, a ba a he si ha a hunomɛ, konɛ a ko tu Mawu munyu ɔ he musu bɔmi munyu.
6Nihewi hu ja nɔuu, tu munyu tsɔɔ mɛ konɛ a juɛmi nɛ ka si. 7Nɛ nihi kulaa blɔfami ɔ, ngɔɔ mo nitsɛ o he ngɔ to mɛ okadi ngɛ ni tsumi kpakpahi a he, nɛ ni tsɔɔmi mi ɔ, o tsɔɔ tsɔɔmi klɔuu, nihi nɛ haa nɔ hɛ mi jiɔ, 8munyu kpakpa nɛ a be he nɔ yaya ko nae nɛ a ma de, benɛ pee nɛ zo nɛ gbe nɔ nɛ kɛ wɔ yi ɔ, ejakaa e be wa he nɔ́ yaya ko nɛ e ma de.
9Sɔmɔli ɔmɛ ɔ, de mɛ ke a ba a he si ngɔ ha a nyɔmtsɛmɛ ɔmɛ, a sa a hɛ mi ngɛ nihi tsuo mi, a ko je munyu nya, 10a ko ju, se mohu a kɛ anɔkuale yemi nitsɛ nɛ tsɔɔ mɛ, konɛ a kɛ wo Mawu nɛ ji wa yi wami helɔ ɔ tsɔɔmi ɔ hɛ mi nyami ngɛ nihi kulaa mi.
11Ejakaa Mawu dloomi nɛ a kɛ heɔ nimli kulaa a yi wami ɔ je kpo, 12nɛ e tsɔseɔ wɔ konɛ wa kua nɔ yaya peemi kɛ je nɛ ɔ mi akɔnɔ ɔmɛ, nɛ waa kɛ juɛmi kpakpa kɛ dami kɛ Mawu gbeye yemi nɛ hi si ngɛ je nɛ ɔ mi, 13nɛ waa hyɛ Mawu Ope ɔ kɛ wa yiwami helɔ Yesu Kristo gbaami nɛ wa hɛ ngɛ nɔ ɔ kɛ e hɛ mi nyami ɔ he kpo jemi ɔ blɔ; 14nɔ nɛ ngɔ nitsɛ e he ngɔ ha ngɛ wa nane mi, konɛ e kpɔ wɔ kɛ je nɔ tɔmi kulaa mi, nɛ e tsukɔ wa he ngɔ pee lɛ nitsɛ e ma klɔuu nɛ hɛ dɔɔ ngɛ ni tsumi kpakpahi a he.
15De mɛ ni nɛ ɔmɛ, nɛ o wo mɛ ga ngɛ he, nɛ o kã a hɛ mi ngɛ he kɛ he wami tsuo. Ko ha nɔ ko nɛ ngɔ mo kaa nɔ nɛ sɛ bumi.

english_text:
Doing Helpful Things
1Remind your people to obey the rulers and authorities and not to be rebellious. They must always be ready to do something helpful 2and not say cruel things or argue. They should be gentle and kind to everyone. 3We used to be stupid, disobedient, and foolish, as well as slaves of all sorts of desires and pleasures. We were evil and jealous. Everyone hated us, and we hated everyone.
4God our Savior showed us
how good and kind he is.
5He saved us because
of his mercy,
and not because
of any good things
we have done.
God washed us by the power
of the Holy Spirit.
He gave us new birth
and a fresh beginning.
6God sent Jesus Christ
our Savior
to give us his Spirit.
7Jesus treated us much better
than we deserve.
He made us acceptable to God
and gave us the hope
of eternal life.
8This message is certainly true.
These teachings are useful and helpful for everyone. I want you to insist that the people follow them, so that all who have faith in God will be sure to do good deeds. 9But don't have anything to do with stupid arguments about ancestors. And stay away from disagreements and quarrels about the Law of Moses. Such arguments are useless and senseless.
10Warn troublemakers once or twice. Then don't have anything else to do with them. 11You know their minds are twisted, and their own sins show how guilty they are.
Personal Instructions and Greetings
12 I plan to send Artemas or Tychicus to you. After he arrives, please try your best to meet me at Nicopolis. I have decided to spend the winter there.
13 When Zenas the lawyer and Apollos get ready to leave, help them as much as you can, so they won't have need of anything.
14Our people should learn to spend their time doing something useful and worthwhile.
15Greetings to you from everyone here. Greet all of our friends who share in our faith.
I pray that the Lord will be kind to all of you!
translation_text:
Kristofohi a jemibami
1Kaii mɛ nɛ a ba a he si ngɔ ha nikɔtɔmahi kɛ nɔ yeli ɔmɛ, a bu mɛ tue, a dla a he kɛ ha ni tsumi kpakpa tsuaa ni tsumi kpakpa, 2a ko tu nɔ ko he munyu yaya, a ko hla pɛ; se mohu a pee kpoo, nɛ a kɛ a he nɛ tsɔɔ nɔ fɛɛ nɔ kaa a he jɔ. 3Ejakaa sa a wɔ hu wa li nɔ́ ko, tue gboli, blɔ dali, nihi nɛ sɔmɔɔ akɔnɔ ni kɛ helo se di ni slɔɔtohi fuu, nɛ wa baa wa je mi ngɛ ni yayahi kɛ he tsɛmi mi, wa he ngɛ tai, nɛ wa nyɛɛ wa he. 4Se benɛ Mawu nɛ ji yi wami helɔ ɔ mi mi jɔmi kɛ e nimli a he dɔmi ɔ je kpo ɔ, 5lɔ ɔ lɛɛ pi dami ni tsumihi nɛ wa tsu nya, se mohu lɛ nitsɛ e mɔbɔ nami nya, kɛ gu ehe fɔmi, he dumi kɛ Mumi Klɔuklɔu ɔ ehe peemi ɔ nɔ he wa yiwami, 6nɔ nɛ gu Yesu Kristo wa yi wami helɔ ɔ nɔ plɛ pue wa nɔ babauu ɔ, 7konɛ bɔ nɛ a wo wɔ nguɔ ngɛ lɛ nɔuu e dloomi nya a, a ha waa pee neneene wami ɔ yeli ngɛ hɛ kɛ nɔ fɔmi ɔ nya. 8Anɔkuale munyu ji nɛ ɔ nɛ.
Kikɛmɛ a ni nɛ ɔmɛ a nɔ mi i ngɛ hlae kaa o ma, konɛ ninɛmɛ nɛ a he Mawu nɔ ye ɔ, a bɔ nitsumi kpakpahi a he mɔde. Enɛ ɔmɛ ji nihi nɛ ngɛ fɛu nɛ hi ha nimli. 9Se kuasiahi a nɔ jemi kɛ weku sisi tsɔɔmi kɛ pɛ kɛ mlaa he kunɔ nɔmi ɔ, sã o he kɛ je he, ejakaa a he be senami nɛ a pi nɔ́ ko. 10Nɔ ko nɛ kɛ mi gbami baa a, ke o bɔ lɛ kɔkɔ si kake kɛ si enyɔ ɔ, kua lɛ; 11ejakaa o le kaa nɔ ko nɛ ngɛ ja a e je e glɔ nɔ, nɛ e he yayami ɔ buu lɛ fɔ.
Nyagbe nitsɔɔmi
12Ke i tsɔ Artema loo Tihiko kɛ ba o ngɔ ɔ, bɔɔ mɔde nɛ o ba ye ngɔ ngɛ Nikopoli, ejakaa lejɛ ɔ i to kaa ma ya ye fiɛ be ɔ ngɛ. 13Bɔɔ mɔɔde nɛ o wo Zena, mlaa tsɔɔlɔ ɔ kɛ Apolo blɔ saminya nɛ nɔ́ ko nɔ́ ko he ko hia mɛ. 14Se ha nɛ wɔ nitsɛmɛ wa ni ɔmɛ hu nɛ kase ni tsumi kpakpahi a he mɔde bɔmi, ke e fi loo e hia nɔ ko ɔ, konɛ a ko pee nihi nɛ wui yiblii.
15Ninɛmɛ nɛ kɛ mi ngɛ ɔ kulaa ke a biɔ mo. Wa biɔ ninɛmɛ nɛ suɔ wɔ ngɛ hemi kɛ yemi mi ɔ.
Mawu dloomi ɔ kɛ nyɛ tsuo nɛ hi si! Amen.

english_text:
1From Paul, who is in jail for serving Christ Jesus, and from Timothy, who is like a brother because of our faith.
Philemon, you work with us and are very dear to us. This letter is to you 2 and to the church that meets in your home. It is also to our dear friend Apphia and to Archippus, who serves the Lord as we do.
3I pray that God our Father and our Lord Jesus Christ will be kind to you and will bless you with peace!
Philemon's Love and Faith
4Philemon, each time I mention you in my prayers, I thank God. 5I hear about your faith in our Lord Jesus and about your love for all God's people. 6As you share your faith with others, I pray they may come to know all the blessings Christ has given us. 7My friend, your love has made me happy and has greatly encouraged me. It has also cheered the hearts of God's people.
Paul Speaks to Philemon about Onesimus
8Christ gives me the courage to tell you what to do. 9But I would rather ask you to do it simply because of love. Yes, as someone in jail for Christ, 10 I beg you to help Onesimus! He is like a son to me because I led him to Christ here in jail. 11Before this, he was useless to you, but now he is useful both to you and to me.
12Sending Onesimus back to you makes me very sad. 13I would like to keep him here with me, where he could take your place in helping me while I am here in prison for preaching the good news. 14But I won't do anything unless you agree to it first. I want your act of kindness to come from your heart, and not be something you feel forced to do.
15Perhaps Onesimus was taken from you for a little while so you could have him back for good, 16but not as a slave. Onesimus is much more than a slave. To me he is a dear friend, but to you he is even more, both as a person and as a follower of the Lord.
17If you consider me a friend because of Christ, then welcome Onesimus as you would welcome me. 18If he has cheated you or owes you anything, charge it to my account. 19With my own hand I write: I, PAUL, WILL PAY YOU BACK. But don't forget you owe me your life. 20My dear friend and follower of Christ our Lord, please cheer me up by doing this for me.
21I am sure you will do all I have asked, and even more. 22Please get a room ready for me. I hope your prayers will be answered, and I can visit you.
23 Epaphras is also here in jail for being a follower of Christ Jesus. He sends his greetings, 24 and so do Mark, Aristarchus, Demas, and Luke, who work together with me.
25I pray that the Lord Jesus Christ will be kind to you!
translation_text:
1Paulo nɛ ji Kristo Yesu opa mi no ɔ, kɛ wa nyɛmi Timoteo ngma ya ha Filemon, wa suɔlɔ kɛ wa huɛ ni tsulɔ ɔ, kɛ asafo nɛ kpee ngɛ o we ɔ tsuo 2kɛ wa nyɛmi yo Apia, kɛ Arkipo nɛ ji wa huɛ ta bu lɔ ɔ.
3Dloomi kɛ hejɔmi nɛ je wa Tsɛ Mawu ɔ kɛ Mawetsɛ Yesu Kristo ɔ dɛ mi ɔ ha nyɛ!
Filemon suɔmi kɛ hemi kɛ yemi
4I naa ye Mawu ɔ si daa, nɛ i woɔ o ta ngɛ ye pɛɛ kpamihi a mi, 5akɛnɛ i nuɔ o suɔmi kɛ hemi kɛ yemi nɛ o hɛɛ ngɛ Mawetsɛ Yesu kɛ ni klɔuklɔu ɔmɛ tsuo a he ɔ; 6nɛ i kpaa pɛɛ kaa kikɛmɛ a huɛ bɔmi nɛ je hemi kɛ yemi mi ɔ nɛ ha mo sisi numi ngɛ ni tsumi kpakpa tsuaa ni tsumi kpakpa nɛ wa nyɛɔ tsuɔ ha Kristo Yesu ɔ mi. 7Ejakaa i na bua jɔmi babauu kɛ tsui ngɛ o suɔmi ɔ he, mami, akɛnɛ o ha ni klɔuklɔu ɔmɛ a tsui nɔ a mi ɔ.
Pɛɛkpami ha Onesimo
8Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, e ngɛ mi kaa i ngɛ kã babauu ngɛ Kristo mi nɛ ma kɛ wo mo kita ngɛ nɔ́ nɛ sa he, 9kɛ̃ ɔ, suɔmi he ɔ, pɛɛ mohu i ngɛ mo kpae. Hyɛ imi nɔmoyo Paulo bɔ nɛ i ngɛ nɛ ɔ, nɛ jehanɛ hu i ji Yesu Kristo pa mi no nɛ ɔ; 10i kpa mo pɛɛ ngɛ yebi Onesimo nɛ i fɔ ngɛ ye tsu mi womi ɔ mi ɔ he, 11nɔ nɛ sa a e he be se nami ko ha mo, se jeha nɛ ɔ e he ngɛ se nami saminya ha i kɛ mo tsuo ɔ.
12I ha e ngɛ kpalee kɛ ma o ngɔ. He lɛ kaa bɔ nɛ o ma he imi nitsɛ. 13I ko suɔ kaa e kɛ mi nɛ hi si konɛ e sɔmɔ mi ngɛ o nane mi ngɛ sane kpakpa a fiɛmi mi. 14Se i sume kaa ma je o se kɛ pee nɔ́ ko, benɛ pee nɛ nɔ́ kpakpa nɛ o maa pee ɔ e ko ba pee nɔ nyɛmi nya ni, se mohu tsui mi jɔmi nya ni.
15Ejakaa eko ɔ enɛ ɔ he nɛ nyɛ kpɛti gba bɔɔ ɔ nɛ, konɛ jehanɛ e hi o ngɔ kulaa, 16pi kaa sɔmɔlɔ hu, se mohu nɔ nɛ pe sɔmɔlɔ tete, nɔ nɛ ji suɔmi nyɛmi, nɛ i fiɛ we e he, nɛ mo mohu e ji o nɔ kulaa ngɛ he lo kɛ Nyɔmtsɛ ɔ blɔfami ɔ.
17Lɔ ɔ he ɔ jehanɛ ke o buu mi kaa o nyɛmi ɔ, he lɛ kaa o ma he imi nitsɛ. 18Ke e ye mo sane yaya ko aloo ke e hɛɛ mo hiɔ ko ɔ, buu jamɛ a akɔtaa a ba ha mi. 19Imi Paulo nitsɛ, i ngɛ enɛ ɔ ngmae kɛ ye nine kaa, ma wo mo hiɔ (e hia we kaa ma kai mo ke o hɛɛ mi mo nitsɛ o yi hiɔ tete.) 20Ee, mami, ha ma na o he se ngɛ Nyɔmtsɛ ɔ mi; ha ye tsui nɛ nɔ ye mi ngɛ Kristo mi.
21Akɛnɛ ye hɛ ngɛ o nɔ kaa o maa bu mi tue he je nɛ i ngma mo nɛ ɔ nɛ, ejakaa i le kaa o maa pee pe bɔ nɛ i de mo nɛ ɔ tete. 22Jehanɛ dla he ko ngɔ to mi, ejakaa ye hɛ ngɛ nɔ kaa nyɛ pɛɛ kpami ɔmɛ a he ɔ, a maa ngmɛɛ ye he ha nyɛ ekohu.
Nyagbe sɛyemi
23Epafra, nɛ ji ye huɛ pa mi no ngɛ Kristo Yesu mi ɔ ke e biɔ mo, 24kɛ Marko hulɔ kɛ Aristarko kɛ Dema kɛ Luka, nihi nɛ ji ye huɛmɛ ni tsuli.
25Wa Nyɔmtsɛ Yesu Kristo dloomi ɔ kɛ nyɛ mumi ɔ nɛ hi si! Amen.

english_text:
1Long ago in many ways and at many times God's prophets spoke his message to our ancestors. 2 But now at last, God sent his Son to bring his message to us. God created the universe by his Son, and everything will someday belong to the Son. 3 God's Son has all the brightness of God's own glory and is like him in every way. By his own mighty word, he holds the universe together.
After the Son had washed away our sins, he sat down at the right side of the glorious God in heaven. 4He had become much greater than the angels, and the name he was given is far greater than any of theirs.
God's Son Is Greater than Angels
5 God has never said
to any of the angels,
“You are my Son, because today
I have become your Father!”
Neither has God said
to any of them,
“I will be his Father,
and he will be my Son!”
6 When God brings his first-born Son into the world, he commands all of his angels to worship him.
7 And when God speaks about the angels, he says,
“I change my angels into wind
and my servants
into flaming fire.”
8 But God says about his Son,
“You are God,
and you will rule
as King forever!
Your royal power
brings about justice.
9You loved justice
and hated evil,
and so I, your God,
have chosen you.
I appointed you
and made you happier
than any of your friends.”
10 The Scriptures also say,
“In the beginning, Lord,
you were the one
who laid the foundation
of the earth
and created the heavens.
11They will all disappear
and wear out like clothes,
but you will last forever.
12You will roll them up
like a robe
and change them
like a garment.
But you are always the same,
and you will live forever.”
13 God never said to any
of the angels,
“Sit at my right side
until I make your enemies
into a footstool for you!”
14 Angels are merely spirits sent to serve people who are going to be saved.
translation_text:
Mawu munyu nɛ e kɛ gu e Bi ɔ nɔ
1Blema be ɔmɛ a mi ɔ, Mawu kɛ wa tsɛmɛ ɔmɛ tu munyu kɛ gu gbali ɔmɛ a nɔ, ngɛ blɔ slɔɔtohi a nɔ, 2se ngɛ nyagbe ligbi nɛ ɔmɛ a mi ɔ, e Bi ɔ nya e kɛ wɔ tu munyu ngɛ, nɔ nɛ e ngɔ lɛ ngɔ pee nihi kulaa yelɔ ɔ, nɔ nɛ nɔ hu nɛ e gu kɛ bɔ je ɔ kɛ e mi ni ɔmɛ; 3nɔ hu nɛ ji e hɛ mi nyami ɔ kpɛmi ɔ su ɔ henɔ, nɛ e kɛ lɛ nitsɛ e he wami munyu ɔ hɛɔ nihi kulaa a, benɛ e tsukɔ wa he kɛ je wa he yayami ɔmɛ a mi ɔ, e ho ya hi si ngɛ hɛ mi nyamitsɛ agbo ɔ hiɛ ɔ nɔ ngɛ hiɔwe.
Bi ɔ kle pe hiɔwe bɔfo ɔmɛ
4Enɛ ɔ he ɔ Bi ɔ kle pe hiɔwe bɔfo ɔmɛ akɛnɛ biɛ nɛ Mawu ha lɛ ɔ kle pe a nɔ ɔ. 5Ejakaa te bɔfo nɛ Mawu de lɛ hyɛ ke:
“Ye bi ji mo,
Mwɔnɛ i fɔ mo?”
Loo,
“Ma pee e tsɛ,
Nɛ lɛ hu e maa pe ye bi?” ɔ nɛɛ?
6Nɛ benɛ e kɛ e bi Tete ɔ ma je ɔ mi ɔ, e kpale de ke:
“Ha Mawu bɔfo ɔmɛ kulaa nɛ a ja lɛ.”
7Nɛ hiɔwe bɔfo ɔmɛ ɔ, e de ngɛ a he ke:
“Nɔ nɛ plɛɛ e bɔfo ɔmɛ ngɔ peɔ kɔɔhiɔhi,
Nɛ e sɔmɔli ɔmɛ hu e peɔ mɛ la lilɛhi” ɔ.
8Se Bi ɔ lɛɛ e de ngɛ e he ke:
“Oo Mawu, o matsɛ sɛ ɔ maa si kɛ yaa neneene kɛ neneene
Nɛ o matsɛ yemi tso ɔ, dami matsɛ yemi tso ʼi,
9O suɔ nɔ́ nɛ da, o nyɛɛ nɔ́ yaya peemi
Lɔ ɔ he ɔ Mawu nɛ ji o Mawu ɔ
Kɛ bua jɔmi nu ɔ pɔ mo pe o nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ.”
10Kɛ jehanɛ:
“Nyɔmtsɛ, sisije ɔ, Mo lɛ o to zugba a sisi,
Nɛ hiɔwe ɔ, o nine nya ni tsumi ʼi.
11Mɛɛ lɛɛ a hɛ mi ma kpata, se moo lɛɛ, o ngɛ daa, nɛ mɛ tsuo a maa bwɔ kaa tade;
12Nɛ o ma koklo mɛ kaa bo, nɛ a ma tsake;
Se moo lɛɛ o ngɛ bɔ nɛ o ngɛ ɔ nɔuu, nɛ o jeha amɛ tɛ̃.”
13Se hiɔwe bɔfo ɔmɛ a ti mɛnɔ po nɛ e de ngɛ e he hyɛ ke:
“Hii ye hiɛ ɔ nɔ
Kɛ yaa su be nɛ ma ngɔ
O he nyɛli ɔmɛ ngɔ pee o nane si sɛ?” ɔ nɛɛ?
14Anɛ mɛ kulaa a, pi mumihi nɛ sɔmɔɔ ji mɛ, nɛ nihi nɛ ma na yi wami hemi ɔ a sɔmɔmi he je nɛ a tsɔ mɛ?

english_text:
This Great Way of Being Saved
1We must give our full attention to what we were told, so we won't drift away. 2The message spoken by angels proved to be true, and all who disobeyed or rejected it were punished as they deserved. 3So if we refuse this great way of being saved, how can we hope to escape? The Lord himself was the first to tell about it, and people who heard the message proved to us that it was true. 4God himself showed that his message was true by working all kinds of powerful miracles and wonders. He also gave his Holy Spirit to anyone he chose to.
The One Who Leads Us To Be Saved
5We know that God did not put the future world under the power of angels. 6 Somewhere in the Scriptures someone says to God,
“What makes you care
about us humans?
Why are you concerned
for weaklings such as we?
7You made us lower
than the angels
for a while.
Yet you have crowned us
with glory and honor.
8And you have put everything
under our power!”
God has put everything under our power and has not left anything out of our power. But we still don't see it all under our control. 9What we do see is Jesus, who for a little while was made lower than the angels. Because of God's gift of undeserved grace, Jesus died for everyone. And now that Jesus has suffered and died, he is crowned with glory and honor!
10Everything belongs to God, and all things were created by his power. So God did the right thing when he made Jesus perfect by suffering, as Jesus led many of God's children to be saved and to share in his glory. 11Jesus and the people he makes holy all belong to the same family. This is why he isn't ashamed to call them his brothers and sisters. 12 He even said to God,
“I will tell them your name
and sing your praises
when they come together
to worship.”
13 He also said,
“I will trust God.”
Then he said,
“Here I am with the children
God has given me.”
14We are people of flesh and blood. This is why Jesus became one of us. He died to destroy the devil, who had power over death. 15But he also died to rescue all of us who live each day in fear of dying. 16 Jesus clearly did not come to help angels, but he did come to help Abraham's descendants. 17He had to be one of us, so he could serve God as our merciful and faithful high priest and sacrifice himself for the forgiveness of our sins. 18And now that Jesus has suffered and was tempted, he can help anyone else who is tempted.
translation_text:
Yi wami hemi ngua a
1Lɔ ɔ he ɔ e sa kaa waa pɛtɛ nihi nɛ wa nu ɔmɛ a he wawɛɛ konɛ wa ko tsɔ kɛ je he. 2Ejakaa ke munyu nɛ a tu ngɛ hiɔwe bɔfohi a nya a maa si kpɛii, nɛ a wo nɔ tɔmi tsuaa nɔ tɔmi kɛ tuegbenɔ tsuaa tuegbenɔ he hiɔ bɔ nɛ sa a, 3kɛ wa maa pee kɛ tu nya fo kɛɛ, ke wa bui kikɛmɛ a yi wami hemi kpetekpleenyɛ nɛ ɔ? Nyɔmtsɛ ɔ nitsɛ ji nɔ nɛ tu he munyu kekle, nɛ ninɛmɛ nɛ nu ɔ hu ma nɔ mi ha wɔ, 4nɛ Mawu nitsɛ hu kɛ okadihi kɛ nyakpɛ nihi kɛ hewami nihi slɔɔtohi kɛ Mumi Klɔuklɔu hami ɔ ngɛ he odase yee kɛ ngɛ nɔ sie, ngɛ lɛ nitsɛ e suɔmi nya.
Yi wami hemi mi hɛminyɛɛlɔ
5Ejakaa pi hiɔwe bɔfohi a sisi nɛ e kɛ je nɛ maa ba nɛ wa ngɛ he munyu tue ɔ wo. 6Nɔ ko ye he odase faii ngɛ he ko ke:
“Mɛnɔ ji nɔmlɔ adesa nɛ o kaii lɛ?
Loo nɔmlɔ bi hu nɛ o hɛ ngɛ e he nɔ?
7Piɛ bɔɔ kɛkɛ nɛ o ha e kɛ hiɔwe bɔfohi nɛ sɔ;
O kɛ hɛ mi nyami kɛ bu fi lɛ jlasi.”
8O ngɔ nihi kulaa ngɔ woʼe nane si. Ejakaa ke e kɛ nihi kulaa wo e nane si ɔ, e piɛ́ nɔ́ ko nɔ́ ko nɛ a kɛ wui e sisi. Jehanɛ wa na we nɛ waa na kaa a kɛ nihi tsuo wo e sisi. 9Se nɔ nɛ a ha nɛ piɛ bɔɔ nɛ e kɛ hiɔwe bɔfo ɔmɛ nɛ sɔ ɔ, wa na kaa Yesu ʼi, nɔ nɛ gbenɔ mi amanehlu ɔ he nɛ a kɛ hɛ mi nyami kɛ bu fi lɛ jlasi ɔ, benɛ pee nɛ Mawu dloomi nya a e sa e nya gbenɔ ha nɔ tsuaa nɔ. 10Ejakaa e sa lɛ, nɔ nɛ he nɛ nihi kulaa ngɛ kɛ nɔ nɛ nɔ nɛ a gu nɛ nihi kulaa ngɛ ɔ, nɔ nɛ ngɔɔ bimɛ babauu kɛ baa hɛ mi nyami mi ɔ, kaa e ha a yi wami hemi tatsɛ nɔkɔtɔma a nɛ gu amanehluhi a mi nɛ e hi kɛ pi si.
11Ejakaa nɔ nɛ tsukɔɔ nihi a he kɛ ninɛmɛ nɛ a tsukɔɔ a he ɔ kulaa je nɔ kake mi, lɔɔ he je nɛ zo pee we lɛ kaa e ma tsɛ mɛ nyɛmimɛ ɔ nɛ. 12Nɛ eke:
“Ma wo o biɛ ɔ tã ngɔ tsɔɔ ye nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ;
Asafo kpɛti hu ma la kɛ je o yi ngɛ.”
13Kɛ jehanɛ hu:
“Ma ngɔ ye hɛ ngɔ fɔ e nɔ.”
Kɛ jehanɛ: “Oʼɛ mi kɛ bimɛ nɛ Mawu ngɔ ha mi ɔ.”
14Lɔ ɔ he ɔ akɛnɛ bimɛ ɔmɛ hɛɛ he lo kɛ muɔ he je ɔ, lɛ hu e ngɔ kɔlɔ ɔ nɔuu eko kaa mɛ, konɛ e gu gbenɔ nɔ kɛ kpata nɔ nɛ ngɛ gbenɔ nɔ he wami nɛ ji abosiami ɔ hɛ mi, 15nɛ e kpɔ nihi nɛ gbenɔ gbeye yemi he ɔ a plɛ pee nyɔguɛhi ngɛ a wami be kulaa mi ɔ. 16Ejakaa e fɔɔ si faii kaa, tsa pi hiɔwe bɔfohi nɛ e yeɔ buaa, se mohu Abraham nina e yeɔ buaa. 17Lɔ ɔ he ɔ nihi kulaa blɔfami ɔ, e sa kaa e hi kaa e nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ, konɛ e plɛ mɔbɔ nalɔ kɛ anɔkuale osɔfo nɔkɔtɔma ngɛ Mawu hɛ mi, konɛ e kpa ma a yi musu. 18Ejakaa akɛnɛ lɛ nitsɛ ɔ e na amanehlu nɛ a ka lɛ he je ɔ, e nyɛɔ e yeɔ buaa ninɛmɛ nɛ a kaa mɛ ɔ.

english_text:
Jesus Is Greater than Moses
1My friends, God has chosen you to be his holy people. So think about Jesus, the one we call our apostle and high priest! 2 Jesus was faithful to God, who appointed him, just as Moses was faithful in serving all God's people. 3But Jesus deserves more honor than Moses, just as the builder of a house deserves more honor than the house. 4Of course, every house is built by someone, and God is really the one who built everything.
5Moses was a faithful servant and told God's people what would be said in the future. 6But Christ is the Son in charge of God's people. And we are those people, if we keep on being brave and don't lose hope.
A Rest for God's People
7 It is just as the Holy Spirit says,
“If you hear God's voice today,
8don't be stubborn!
Don't rebel like those people
who were tested
in the desert.
* 9 For forty years your ancestors
tested God and saw
the things he did.
10“Then God got tired of them
and said,
‘You people never
show good sense,
and you don't understand
what I want you to do.’
11God became angry
and told the people,
‘You will never enter
my place of rest!’ ”
12My friends, watch out! Don't let evil thoughts or doubts make any of you turn from the living God. 13You must encourage one another each day. And you must keep on while there is still a time that can be called “today.” If you don't, then sin may fool some of you and make you stubborn. 14We were sure about Christ when we first became his people. So let's hold tightly to our faith until the end. 15 The Scriptures say,
“If you hear his voice today,
don't be stubborn
like those who rebelled.”
16 Who were those people that heard God's voice and rebelled? Weren't they the same ones that came out of Egypt with Moses? 17Who were the people that made God angry for 40 years? Weren't they the ones that sinned and died in the desert? 18And who did God say would never enter his place of rest? Weren't they the ones that disobeyed him? 19We see that those people did not enter the place of rest because they did not have faith.
translation_text:
Yesu kle pe Mose
1Enɛ ɔ he ɔ, mamimɛ, nyɛɛ tɛ̃tɛ̃ nyɛ hɛ mi, nyɛ ni klɔuklɔuhi nɛ na hiɔwe tsemi ɔ eko, nɛ nyɛɛ hyɛ Yesu wa hemi kɛ yemi jajemi ɔ he bɔfo kɛ osɔfo nɔkɔtɔma a; 2nɔ nɛ yeɔ nɔ nɛ hla lɛ ɔ anɔkuale, kaa bɔ nɛ Mose hu ye Mawu we ɔ kulaa nɔ anɔkuale ɔ. 3Kaa bɔ nɛ nɔ nɛ bɔɔ we ko ɔ bu hiɛ pe we ɔ nɔ́ ɔ, ja nɔuu Yesu hu hɛ mi ngɛ nyami pe Mose. 4We tsuaa we ɔ nɔ ko kɛ̃ lɛ bɔɔ, se nɔ nɛ bɔɔ nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ ji Mawu. 5Mose ye anɔkuale ngɛ Mawu we mluku ɔ kulaa nɔ kaa sɔmɔlɔ, konɛ e ye nihi nɛ a ma de ɔmɛ a he odase; 6se Kristo ɔ e ye anɔkuale kaa bi ngɛ Mawu we ɔ nɔ; lɛ e we ji wɔ, ke wa hɛɛ hɛ kɛ nɔ fɔmi kã kɛ fiami ɔ mi kpɛii kɛ ya su nyagbe ɔ.
Hejɔɔmi ha Mawu webi
7Lɔ ɔ he ɔ kaa bɔ nɛ Mumi Klɔuklɔu ɔ de ɔ:
“Mwɔnɛ, ke nyɛ nu e gbi ɔ,
8Nyɛ ko wlua nyɛ tsui,
Kaa bɔ nɛ a pee ngɛ mi mi la womi ɔ mi,
Ngɛ nyatsɔmi ligbi ɔ nɔ ngɛ nga a nɔ ɔ,
9He nɛ nyɛ tsɛmɛ ɔmɛ tsɔ ye nya nɛ a ka mi,
Nɛ a na ye ni tsumi ɔmɛ ngɛ, jeha nyingmi eywiɛ sɔuu ɔ.
10Lɔ ɔ he ɔ ye mi mi fu jamɛ a yi nɔ bi ɔmɛ
Nɛ i ke: ‘Daa nɛ ɔ a tlaa blɔ ngɛ a juɛmi mi,
Nɛ a li ye blɔ ɔmɛ.’
11Lɔ ɔ ha ye mi mi fu nɛ i ka kita
Ke: ‘Ke a sɛ ye he jɔɔmi ɔ mi fii!’ ”
12Nyɛɛ hyɛ nɛ hi, mamimɛ, konɛ nyɛ ti nɔ ko ko hi tsui nɛ he we yi nɛ e kpale kɛ je Mawu hɛ kalɔ ɔ he; 13se mohu nyɛɛ tu munyu ngɔ tsɔɔ nyɛ he ligbi tsuaa ligbi nɛ a tsɛɛ lɛ “mwɔnɛ” ɔ, konɛ yayami ko sisi nyɛ nɛ nyɛ wlua nyɛ tsui. 14Ejakaa Kristo he piɛli ji wɔ ke wa hɛɛ wa he nɛ waa kɛ fɔɔ e nɔ kɛ je sisije ɔ mi kpɛii kɛ ya su nyagbe ɔ. 15Ngmami ɔ de ke:
“Mwɔnɛ ke nyɛ nu e gbi ɔ,
Nyɛ ko wlua nyɛ tsui
Kaa bɔ nɛ nyɛ pee
Benɛ nyɛ tsɔ ye hɛ mi atua a.”
16Nihi nɛ nu ɔ a ti mɛnɔmɛ lɛ a wo e mi mi la a? Anɛ pi ninɛmɛ nɛ kɛ Mose je Mizraim ɔ tsuo ʼi? 17Nɛ mɛnɔmɛ e mi mi fu jeha nyingmi eywiɛ sɔuu ɔ? Anɛ pi ninɛmɛ nɛ pee yayami nɛ a fia si gbo ngɛ nga a nɔ ɔ lo? 18Nɛ mɛnɔmɛ a nɔ e kã kita ngɔ fɔ kaa a be e he jɔɔmi ɔ mi sɛe ɔ? Anɛ pi tuegboli ɔmɛ lo? 19Nɛ wa naa kaa hemi nɛ a he we yi ɔ he nɛ a nyɛ we mi nɛ a sɛ ɔ nɛ.

english_text:
1The promise to enter the place of rest is still good, and we must take care that none of you miss out. 2We have heard the message, just as they did. But they failed to believe what they heard, and the message did not do them any good. 3 Only people who have faith will enter the place of rest. It is just as the Scriptures say,
“God became angry
and told the people,
‘You will never enter
my place of rest!’ ”
God said this, even though everything has been ready from the time of creation. 4 In fact, somewhere the Scriptures say that by the seventh day, God had finished his work, and so he rested. 5 We also read that he later said, “You people will never enter my place of rest!” 6This means that the promise to enter is still good, because those who first heard about it disobeyed and did not enter. 7 Much later God told David to make the promise again, just as I have already said,
“If you hear his voice today,
don't be stubborn!”
8 If Joshua had really given the people rest, there would not be any need for God to talk about another day of rest. 9But God has promised us a Sabbath when we will rest, even though it has not yet come. 10 On that day God's people will rest from their work, just as God rested from his work.
11We should do our best to enter the place of rest, so none of us will disobey and miss going there, as they did. 12God's word is alive and powerful! It is sharper than any double-edged sword. His word can cut through our spirits and souls and through our joints and marrow, until it discovers the desires and thoughts of our hearts. 13 Nothing is hidden from God! He sees through everything, and we will have to tell him the truth.
Jesus Is the Great High Priest
14We have a great high priest, who has gone into heaven, and he is Jesus the Son of God. This is why we must hold on to what we have said about him. 15Jesus understands every weakness of ours, because he was tempted in every way that we are. But he did not sin! 16So whenever we are in need, we should come bravely before the throne of our merciful God. There we will be treated with undeserved grace, and we will find help.
translation_text:
1Nɛ Mawu si e he jɔɔmi ɔ mi sɛmi he si womi ngɔ ha wɔ nɛ ɔ, nyɛ ha waa hyɛ nɛ hi konɛ alinɔ e ko ba mi kaa e fɔ wa ti nɔ ko. 2Ejakaa wɔ hu a fiɛ Sane kpakpa a ngɔ ha wɔ, kaa bɔ nɛ a fiɛ tsɔɔ mɛ ɔ nɔuu; se kɛ̃ ɔ munyu nɛ a nu ɔ he ya bɛ́ se nami ha mɛ, ejakaa ninɛmɛ nɛ nu ɔ kɛ hemi kɛ yemi pɛtɛ we he. 3Ejakaa wɔ ninɛmɛ nɛ wa he ye ɔ wa ngɛ jamɛ a he jɔɔmi ɔ mi sɛe, kaa bɔ nɛ e de ɔ ke:
“Lɔ ɔ ha i kɛ mi mi fumi ka kita ke:
‘Ke a sɛ ye he jɔɔmi ɔ mi fii!’ ”
pohu a gbe Mawu ni tsumi ɔmɛ a nya kɛ je je mi sisije lokoo. 4Ejakaa bɔ nɛ e de ngɛ he ko ngɛ ligbi nɛ ji ligbi kpaago ɔ he ji nɛ ɔ nɛ: “Nɛ Mawu jɔɔ e he ngɛ ligbi nɛ ji ligbi kpaago ɔ nɔ ngɛ e ni tsumi ɔmɛ kulaa mi;” 5nɛ hiɛ ɔ nɛ ɔ e kpale de ke: “Ke a sɛ ye he jɔɔmi ɔ mi fii!” 6Lɔ ɔ he ɔ akɛnɛ e fɔɔ si kaa ni komɛ maa sɛ mi, nɛ ninɛmɛ nɛ a fiɛ Sane kpakpa a ngɔ tsɔɔ kekle ɔ sɛ we mi ngɛ hemi nɛ a he we yi ɔ he je ɔ, 7Mawu kpale to ligbi kpa ko ekohu, nɛ e de ngɛ David nya, ngɛ be babauu nɛ ɔ se ke, Mwɔnɛ, kaa bɔ nɛ la de sa a,
“Mwɔnɛ ke nyɛ nu e gbi ɔ,
Nyɛ ko wlua nyɛ tsui.’ ”
8Ejakaa kaa Yosua na ha mɛ he jɔɔmi jinɛ, pee se ɔ Mawu ko tu we ligbi kpa ko he munyu hu. 9Lɔ ɔ he ɔ he jɔɔmi ligbi yemi ko fɔɔ si kɛ ha Mawu ma a. 10Ejakaa nɔ nɛ sɛ e he jɔɔmi ɔ mi ɔ, lɛ nitsɛ hu e jɔɔ e he ngɛ e ni tsumi ɔmɛ a mi, kaa bɔ nɛ Mawu jɔɔ e he ngɛ e nɔ ɔ mi ɔ. 11Lɔɔ he ɔ nyɛ ha waa bɔ mɔde, konɛ waa sɛ jamɛ a he jɔɔmi ɔ mi, nɛ nɔ ko ko nyɛɛ jamɛ a tue gbomi blɔ ɔ nɔ nɛ e laa.
12Ejakaa Mawu munyu hɛ ngɛ nɛ e ngɛ he wami nɛ e nya ba pe klaate nya enyɔtsɛ, nɛ e gbuu kɛ sɛɛ mi kɛ ya suu be nɛ e gbaa klaa kɛ mumi ɔ kɛ kpɔji nya amɛ kɛ wu mi zɔ ɔmɛ a mi, nɛ e ji tsui mi susumihi kɛ juɛmi ɔmɛ a kojolɔ. 13A laa we bɔ nɔ́ ko ngɛ e hɛ mi, se nihi kulaa ngɛ paa nɛ a bli nɔ ngɛ lɛ nɔ nɛ waa kɛ ngɛ sane ɔ hɛngmɛ mi.
Yesu osɔfo nɔkɔtɔma ngua a
14Jehanɛ, akɛnɛ wa ngɛ osɔfo nɔkɔtɔma ngua nɛ po mi kɛ gu hiɔwe nihi a mi, nɛ ji Yesu, Mawu bi ɔ nɛ ɔ ɔ, nyɛ ha waa pɛtɛ hemi kɛ yemi ɔ he wawɛɛ. 15Ejakaa wa osɔfo nɔkɔtɔma nɛ wa ngɛ ɔ, e pi nɔ nɛ be nyɛe maa nu wa gbɔjɔmi ɔmɛ a he ha wɔ, se e ji nɔ ko nɛ a ka lɛ ngɛ nihi kulaa blɔfami kaa wɔ, nɛ kɛ̃ ɔ yayami ko yayami ko be e he. 16Lɔ ɔ he ɔ nyɛ ha waa kɛ kã nɛ hɛ wɔ kɛ su dloomi sɛ ɔ he, konɛ wa nine nɛ su mɔbɔ nami nɔ nɛ wa na dloomi nɛ maa ye bua wɔ ngɛ be nɛ sa mi.

english_text:
1Every high priest is appointed to help others by offering gifts and sacrifices to God because of their sins. 2A high priest has weaknesses of his own, and he feels sorry for foolish and sinful people. 3 This is why he must offer sacrifices for his own sins and for the sins of others. 4 But no one can have the honor of being a high priest simply by wanting to be one. Only God can choose a priest, and God is the one who chose Aaron.
5 This is how it was with Christ. He became a high priest, but not just because he wanted the honor of being one. It was God who told him,
“You are my Son, because today
I have become your Father!”
6 In another place, God says,
“You are a priest forever
just like Melchizedek.”
7 God had the power to save Jesus from death. And while Jesus was on earth, he begged God with loud crying and tears to save him. He truly worshiped God, and God listened to his prayers. 8Jesus is God's own Son, but still he had to suffer before he could learn what it really means to obey God. 9Suffering made Jesus perfect, and now he can save forever all who obey him. 10This is because God chose him to be a high priest like Melchizedek.
Warning against Turning Away
11Much more could be said about this subject. But it is hard to explain, and all of you are slow to understand. 12 By now you should have been teachers, but once again you need to be taught the simplest things about what God has said. You need milk instead of solid food. 13People who live on milk are like babies who don't really know what is right. 14Solid food is for mature people who have been trained to know right from wrong.
translation_text:
1Ejakaa osɔfo nɔkɔtɔma tsuaa osɔfo nɔkɔtɔma nɛ a hia ngɛ nimli a kpɛti ɔ, a wo lɛ osɔfo konɛ e da nimli a nane mi ngɛ Mawu nihi a blɔfami, konɛ e kɛ nike nihi kɛ bɔhi ba ha ngɛ yayamihi a he, 2kaa nɔ ko nɛ nyɛɔ e nuɔ nɔ́ he haa nihi nɛ li ni kɛ nihi nɛ tla blɔ ɔ, akɛ nɛ lɛ nitsɛ hu ɔ gbedemi bɔle e he kɛ kpe ɔ. 3Nɛ enɛ ɔ he ɔ, e hia kaa, kaa bɔ nɛ e peɔ haa ma a, e pee ja nɔuu ngɔ ha lɛ nitsɛ e he, nɛ e sa yayamihi a he bɔ. 4Nɛ nɔ ko ngɔɛ hɛ mi nyami nɔ ha we lɛ nitsɛ e he, kaa ja Mawu tsɛ lɛ, kaa bɔ nɛ e tsɛ Aaron hu ɔ.
5Ja nɔuu Kristo hu, pi lɛ nitsɛ nɛ e wo e hɛ mi nyami ngɛ osɔfo nɔkɔtɔma yemi mi, se mohu Mawu nɛ de lɛ ke:
“Ye bi ji mo, mwɔnɛ i fɔ mo”
ɔ, lɛ wo e hɛ mi nyami. 6Kaa bɔ nɛ e de ngɛ he kpa hu ke:
“Osɔfo ji mo kɛ yaa neneene
Ngɛ Melkizedek blɔ ɔ nɔ.”
7Ngɛ Yesu he lo be ɔmɛ a mi ɔ, e ngɔ sɔlemi kɛ pɛɛ kpami nɛ ngmlaa kpami nɛ nya wa kɛ vo nyu piɛ he sa bɔ ha nɔ nɛ ngɛ he wami nɛ e kɛ ma he lɛ kɛ je gbenɔ mi ɔ, nɛ a bu lɛ tue hulɔ, ejakaa e buu Mawu. 8Nɛ pohu Mawu bi ji lɛ, se kɛ̃ ɔ e kase tue bumi ngɛ amanehluhi nɛ e na amɛ a mi, 9nɛ benɛ a ha e hi kɛ pi si ɔ, e plɛ nɔ nɛ mi nɛ neneene yi wami hemi jee kɛ haa nihi tsuo nɛ buɔ lɛ tue ɔ, 10ejakaa Mawu wo lɛ osɔfo kaa Melkizedek.
Sigbeemi he kɔkɔbɔmi
11Wa ngɛ munyuhi fuu nɛ wa maa tu ngɛ enɛ ɔ he, se a sisi tsɔɔmi hu wa, ejakaa nyɛ tue mi ti; 12ejakaa nyɛ nɛ jinɛ e sa kaa nyɛ plɛ tsɔɔli mohu ngɛ be ɔ nya a, e hia kaa a tsɔɔ nyɛ Mawu munyu ɔ mi sisije ni ɔmɛ ekohu, nɛ nyɛ plɛ nihi nɛ nyɔ nyu hia mɛ, se pi niyeni nitsɛ. 13Ejakaa nɔ tsuaa nɔ nɛ pupɔɔ nyɔ ɔ li nɔ́ nɛ da kɛ nɔ́ nɛ dɛ, ejakaa bimwɔyo ji lɛ. 14Se ninɛmɛ nɛ wa a, a nɔ ji niyeni nitsɛ, nihi nɛ tsɔse a he numi ni ɔmɛ le slɔɔto nɛ ngɛ kpakpa kɛ yayami kpɛti.

english_text:
1We must try to become mature and start thinking about more than just the basic things we were taught about Christ. We shouldn't need to keep talking about why we ought to turn from deeds that bring death and why we ought to have faith in God. 2And we shouldn't need to keep teaching about baptisms or about the laying on of hands or about people being raised from death and the future judgment. 3Let's grow up, if God is willing.
4-6But what about people who turn away after they have already seen the light and have received the gift from heaven and have shared in the Holy Spirit? What about those who turn away after they have received the good message of God and the powers of the future world? There is no way to bring them back. What they are doing is the same as nailing the Son of God to a cross and insulting him in public!
7A field is useful to farmers, if there is enough rain to make good crops grow. In fact, God will bless such a field. 8 But land that produces only thornbushes is worthless. It is likely to fall under God's curse, and in the end it will be set on fire.
9My friends, we are talking this way. But we are sure that you are doing those really good things people do when they are being saved. 10God is always fair. He will remember how you helped his people in the past and how you are still helping them. You belong to God, and he won't forget the love you have shown his people. 11We wish each of you would always be eager to show how strong and lasting your hope really is. 12Then you would never be lazy. You would be following the example of those who had faith and were patient until God kept his promise to them.
God's Promise Is Sure
13No one is greater than God. So he made a promise in his own name when he said to Abraham, 14 “I, the Lord, will bless you with many descendants!” 15Then after Abraham had been very patient, he was given what God had promised. 16When anyone wants to settle an argument, they make a vow by using the name of someone or something greater than themselves. 17So when God wanted to prove for certain his promise to his people could not be broken, he made a vow. 18God cannot tell lies! And so his promises and vows are two things that can never be changed.
We have run to God for safety. Now his promises should greatly encourage us to take hold of the hope that is right in front of us. 19 This hope is like a firm and steady anchor for our souls. In fact, hope reaches behind the curtain and into the most holy place. 20 Jesus has gone there ahead of us, and he is our high priest forever, just like Melchizedek.
translation_text:
1Lɔ ɔ he ɔ nyɛ ha wa si Kristo he sisije ni tsɔɔmi ɔmɛ, nɛ waa po mi kɛ ya tsɔɔmihi nɛ sa kɛ ha nikɔtɔmahi a he; nɛ wa ko kpale to nitsumihi nɛ gbo a he tsui tsakemi kɛ Mawu nɔ hemi kɛ yemi, 2kɛ baptisimihi a he ni tsɔɔmi kɛ ninehi kɛ nɔ nɔ puemi, kɛ gbogboehi a si temi kɛ neneene kojomi he sane ɔmɛ a sisi ekohu. 3Enɛ ɔ wa maa pee ke Mawu ngmɛ blɔ.
4Ejakaa nihi nɛ la tso ngɛ a nɔ hyɛ nɛ a sa a nya hiɔwe nɔ́ke nɔ́ ɔ nɛ a na Mumi Klɔuklɔu ɔ eko 5nɛ a sa a nya Mawu munyu kpakpa a kɛ je nɛ maa ba a mi hewami ɔmɛ, 6nɛ lɔ ɔ se nɛ a gbee si ɔ, a be nyɛe ma tsake mɛ ngɔ pee ni hehi ekohu ha tsui tsakemi, akɛnɛ a ngɛ Mawu bi ɔ sɛue ekohu kɛ ngɛ a he hae nɛ a ngɛ lɛ ahlua bɔe he ɔ.
7Zugba nɛ mii nyu nɛ nɛɛ pueɔ e nɔ kpitikpiti nɛ baa ni nɛ hi ha ninɛmɛ nɛ huɔ nɔ ɔ naa Mawu gbaami ɔ eko; 8se ke mio kɛ hu e puɛɛ ɔ, a kuaa lɛ, nɛ Mawu gbiɛmi baa e nɔ, nɛ e nyagbe ji a kɛ la maa sa.
9Se mamimɛ, wa ngɛ kikɛ dee mohu, se kɛ̃ ɔ wa hɛ ngɛ nyɛ nɔ kaa nyɛ sane hi pe ja, nɛ yi wami hemi maa nyɛɛ nyɛ se. 10Ejakaa Mawu pi nɔ nɛ yeɔ sane nɛ dɛ́ nɛ e hɛ maa je nyɛ ni tsumi ɔ nɔ kɛ suɔmi he dengme nɛ nyɛ gbo ngɛ e biɛ ɔ he, nɛ nyɛɛ kɛ sɔmɔ ni klɔuklɔu ɔmɛ, nɛ nyɛ pa kɛ ngɛ mɛ sɔmɔe kɛ mwɔ ɔ. 11Wa ngɛ hlae kaa nyɛ ti nɔ tsuaa nɔ nɛ tsɔɔ kikɛmɛ a mɔde bɔmi nɛ ɔ nɔuu, konɛ a ma hɛ kɛ nɔ fɔmi ɔ nɔ mi kɛ ya su nyagbe, 12konɛ nyɛ ko pee hejɔ se mohu nyɛɛ kase ninɛmɛ nɛ guu hemi kɛ yemi kɛ tsui si tomi nɔ naa si womi ɔ.
Mawu siwomi nɛ tsakee we
13Benɛ Mawu wo Abraham si ɔ, akɛnɛ e be nɔ ko nɛ pe lɛ nitsɛ nɛ e ma kã lɛ kita he je ɔ, e ka lɛ nitsɛ e he kita, 14nɛ e ke: Niinɛ, ma gbaa mo, nɛ ma ha o nina maa hiɛ. 15Nɛ akɛnɛ Abraham to e tsui si he je ɔ, e nine su si womi ɔ nɔ. 16Ejakaa nimli ngɛ nɛ ɔ, nɔ nɛ pe mɛ ɔ kita a kaa, nɛ a nya sami nyagbe tsuo ji kita kami nɛ a kɛ maa sane tsuaa sane nɔ mi. 17Lɔ ɔ he hulɔ nɛ benɛ Mawu hia kaa e tsɔɔ si womi ɔ yeli ɔmɛ kaa e yi mi tomi ɔ tsakee we kulaa a, e kɛ kita ma nɔ mi, 18konɛ waa gu sanehi enyɔ nɛ tsakee we nɛ Mawu be nyɛe maa ngɔ nya ngɛ mi ɔ nɔ kɛ na bua womi nɛ wa, konɛ wɔ nihi nɛ wa ya sawe ɔ, wa kɛ hɛɛ hɛ kɛ nɔ fɔmi nɛ ngɛ wa hɛ mi ɔ mi; 19wa hɛɛ hɛ kɛ nɔ fɔmi nɔ kaa wa klaa sɛkɛ nɛ tsɔ we nɛ pi si kpɛii kɛ sɛ mi kɛ ho tsu mi pomi bo ɔ se ya tɔɔ, 20he nɛ hɛ mi nyɛɛlɔ ɔ ji Yesu, nɔ nɛ plɛ neneene osɔfo nɔkɔtɔma kaa Melkizedek ɔ sɛ ha wɔ ɔ.

english_text:
The Priestly Family of Melchizedek
1 Melchizedek was both king of Salem and priest of God Most High. He was the one who went out and gave Abraham his blessing, when Abraham returned from killing the kings. 2Then Abraham gave him a tenth of everything he had.
The meaning of the name Melchizedek is “King of Justice.” But since Salem means “peace,” he is also “King of Peace.” 3We are not told he had a father or mother or ancestors or beginning or end. He is like the Son of God and will be a priest forever.
4Notice how great Melchizedek was! Our famous ancestor Abraham gave him a tenth of what he had taken from his enemies. 5 The Law teaches that even Abraham's descendants must give a tenth of what they possess. And they are to give this to their own relatives, who are the descendants of Levi and are priests. 6Although Melchizedek wasn't a descendant of Levi, Abraham gave him a tenth of what he had. Then Melchizedek blessed Abraham, who had been given God's promise. 7Everyone agrees a person who gives a blessing is greater than the one who receives the blessing.
8Priests are given a tenth of what people earn. But all priests die, except Melchizedek, and the Scriptures teach that he is alive. 9Levi's descendants are now the ones who receive a tenth from people. We could even say that when Abraham gave Melchizedek a tenth, Levi also gave him a tenth. 10This is because Levi was born later into the family of Abraham, who gave a tenth to Melchizedek.
11Even though the Law of Moses says the priests must be descendants of Levi, those priests cannot make anyone perfect. So there needs to be a priest like Melchizedek, rather than one from the priestly family of Aaron. 12And when the rules for selecting a priest are changed, the Law must also be changed.
13The person we are talking about is our Lord, who came from a tribe that had never had anyone to serve as a priest at the altar. 14Everyone knows he came from the tribe of Judah, and Moses never said priests would come from that tribe.
15All of this becomes clearer, when someone who is like Melchizedek is appointed to be a priest. 16That person wasn't appointed because of his ancestors, but because his life can never end. 17 The Scriptures say about him,
“You are a priest forever,
just like Melchizedek.”
18In this way a weak and useless command was put aside, 19because the Law cannot make anything perfect. At the same time, we are given a much better hope, and it can bring us close to God.
20-21 God himself made a promise when this priest was appointed. But he did not make a promise like this when the other priests were appointed. The promise he made is,
“I, the Lord, promise that you
will be a priest forever!
And I will never
change my mind!”
22This means that Jesus guarantees us a better agreement with God. 23There have been a lot of other priests, and all of them have died. 24But Jesus will never die, and so he will be a priest forever! 25He is forever able to save the people he leads to God, because he always lives to speak to God for them.
26Jesus is the high priest we need. He is holy and innocent and faultless, and not at all like us sinners. Jesus is honored above all beings in heaven, 27 and he is better than any other high priest. Jesus doesn't need to offer sacrifices each day for his own sins and then for the sins of the people. He offered a sacrifice once for all, when he gave himself. 28The Law appoints priests who have weaknesses. But God's promise, which came later than the Law, appoints his Son. And he is the perfect high priest forever.
translation_text:
Osɔfo Melkizedek
1Se Melkizedek nɛ ɔ ɔ, lɛ ji Salem matsɛ, Mawu ope ɔ, osɔfo nɛ kɛ Abraham ya kpe benɛ e kpale e se kɛ je matsɛmɛ ɔmɛ a gbemi mi ngɛ ta mi nɛ e gbaa lɛ, 2nɛ Abraham ha lɛ ni ɔmɛ kulaa mi dlami nyɔngma mi kake ɔ nɛ. Melkizedek biɛ ɔ, e kekle sisi tsɔɔmi ji “Dami Matsɛ” nɛ jehanɛ hu e ji “Salem Matsɛ,” nɛ kɔlɔ ɔ sisi hu ji “Hejɔmi Matsɛ.” 3E be tsɛ, e be nyɛ, e be weku kpa, nɛ e be ligbihi a sisije loo wami nyagbe tete, e ngɛ kaa Mawu Bi ɔ; e hii si kaa osɔfo kɛ yaa neneene.
4Jehanɛ nyɛ susu he, bɔ nɛ nɔ nɛ ɔ agbo jemi ngɛ ha: Blemano Abraham ɔ tete ngɔ ta yi bu ni kpakpa amɛ a mi dlami nyɔngma mi kake ngɔ ha lɛ! 5Wa le kaa Levibi ɔmɛ a kpɛti nihi nɛ tsuɔ osɔfo ni tsumi ɔ hu ngɛ kita ko ngɛ Mlaa a nya, kaa a he mi dlami nyɔngma mi kake ngɛ ma a dɛ, lɔ ɔ ji ngɛ a nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ a dɛ, pohu mɛ hu a je Abraham mi. 6Se Melkizedek nɛ be weku sisi tsɔɔmi ko ngɛ Levibi ɔmɛ a kpɛti nɛ ɔ ɔ, e he midlami mi nyɔngma a mi kake ngɛ Abraham po dɛ, nɛ e gbaa nɔ nɛ ngɛ si womi ɔmɛ tete. 7Nguane jemi ko be he kulaa kaa nɔ nɛ kle pe e nyɛmi ɔ lɛ e gbaa nɔ nɛ klee we ɔ. 8Jehanɛ ɔ hiɛ ɔ, nimli nɛ gboɔ ɔmɛ ji nihi nɛ heɔ mi dlami nyɔngma mi kake ɔ, se lejɛ ɔ, nɔ ko nɛ ngmami ɔ ye e he odase kaa e hɛ ngɛ ngmengmle ɔ lɛ he. 9Nɛ, ke ma de jã a, kɛ gu Abraham nɔ ɔ, a he mi dlami nyɔngma mi kake ɔ ngɛ Levi nɛ heɔ lɔ ɔ hu dɛ; 10ejakaa e ngɛ e tsɛ Abraham ɔ mi mi momo bene Melkizedek kɛ lɛ ba kpe ɔ.
11Jehanɛ ke himi kɛ si pimi gu Levi osɔfo yemi ɔ nɔ kɛ ba a (ejakaa e yi nɔ a wo ma a mlaa ngɛ), lɛɛ mɛni he je e hia kɛ̃ kaa osɔfo kpa ko nɛ te si nɛ ngɛ kaa Melkizedek, nɛ pi kaa Aaron ɔ mɔ? 12Ejakaa ke a tsake osɔfo yemi ɔ, lɛɛ e hia kaa a tsake Mlaa a hulɔ. 13Ejakaa nɔ nɛ he nɛ a de ni nɛ ɔmɛ ngɛ ɔ, je wɛtso kpa ko mi, nɔ mi nɛ nɔ ko ji kɛ ba tsu we bɔ sami latɛ ɔ he ni hyɛ. 14Nɔ tsuaa nɔ le kaa Yuda mi nɛ wa Nyɔmtsɛ ɔ je, jamɛ a wetso ɔ Mose de we he nɔ́ ko ngɛ osɔfo yemi he.
Osɔfo kpã ko kaa Melkizedek
15Nɔ́ nɛ haa sane ɔ jee kpo paa a ji kaa osɔfo kpã ko te si nɛ ngɛ kaa Melkizedek, 16nɔ nɛ pi he lo kita mlaa nya nɛ a wo lɛ osɔfo ngɛ, se mohu wami nɛ puɛ we ɔ he wami nya. 17Ejakaa ngmami ɔ yeɔ odase ke: Osɔfo ji mo kɛ yaa neneene kaa Melkizedek. 18Ejakaa kita nɛ sɛ hlami ɔ, akɛnɛ e be he wami nɛ e he be se nami ko he ɔ a gu, 19ejakaa Mlaa ha we nɔ́ ko nɔ́ ko nɛ hi kɛ pi si, se jehanɛ a kɛ hɛ kɛ nɔ fɔmi nɛ hi pe lɔ ɔ nɛ waa kɛ suu Mawu he ɔ ba je mi.
20Enɛ ɔ peemi mi ɔ a si we Mawu kita a se. Ni kpa amɛ ɔ, a wo mɛ osɔfohi mohu se a ka we kita ko. 21Se Yesu lɛɛ, kita kami a kɛ wo lɛ, benɛ Mawu de lɛ ke:
“Nyɔmtsɛ ɔ ka kita
Nɛ e be e he piae:
Osɔfo ji mo kɛ yaa neneene” ɔ.
22Jehanɛ somi nɛ Yesu daa si ngɛ mi ɔ hi pe kulaa. 23Slɔɔto kpa ko hu ji, mɛɛ lɛɛ, akɛnɛ gbenɔ ha we nɛ a se nɛ kɛ he je ɔ, mɛ fuu a ye osɔfo; 24se Yesu lɛɛ, akɛnɛ e hii si kɛ yaa neneene he je ɔ, e sɔfo yemi ɔ se pui. 25Lɔ ɔ he hu ɔ e nyɛɔ nihi nɛ guu e nɔ kɛ baa Mawu ngɔ ɔmɛ a yi wami heɔ, ejakaa e ngɛ daa konɛ e da mi ha mɛ.
26Yesu ji Osɔfo nɔkɔtɔma nɛ sa wɔ pɛ: nɔ nɛ he tsɔ, nɛ yayami ko be e he, nɛ e he be piami ko, nɛ e tsɔ e he kɛ je yayami peeli a he, nɛ a wo e nɔ kɛ be hiɔwe, he; 27nɔ nɛ e hia we lɛ, kaa osɔfo nikɔtɔma kpa amɛ, kaa daa ligbi ɔ e sã lɛ nitsɛ e he yayami ɔmɛ a he bɔ kekle loko e sã ma a hu nɔ; ejakaa e pee enɛ ɔ si kake nyɔngloo, benɛ e ngɔ lɛ nitsɛ e he ngɔ sã bɔ ɔ. 28Ejakaa Mose Mlaa a, nimli gbɔjɔli e ngɔ woɔ osɔfo nikɔtɔmahi ɔ nɛ, se Mawu kita nɛ ba ngɛ Mlaa a se ɔ he munyu ɔ wo Bi nɛ hi kɛ pi si kɛ yaa neneene ɔ osɔfo nɔkɔtɔma.

english_text:
A Better Promise
1 What I mean is we have a high priest who sits at the right side of God's great throne in heaven. 2He also serves as the priest in the most holy place inside the real tent there in heaven. This tent of worship was set up by the Lord, not by humans.
3Since all priests must offer gifts and sacrifices, Christ also needed to have something to offer. 4If he were here on earth, he would not be a priest at all, because here the Law appoints other priests to offer sacrifices. 5 But the tent where they serve is just a copy and a shadow of the real one in heaven. Before Moses made the tent, he was told, “Be sure to make it exactly like the pattern you were shown on the mountain!” 6Now Christ has been appointed to serve as a priest in a much better way, and he has given us much assurance of a better agreement.
7If the first agreement with God had been all right, there would not have been any need for another one. 8 But the Lord found fault with it and said,
“I tell you the time will come,
when I will make
a new agreement
with the people of Israel
and the people of Judah.
9It won't be like the agreement
that I made
with their ancestors,
when I took them by the hand
and led them out of Egypt.
They broke their agreement
with me,
and I stopped caring
about them!
10“But now I tell the people
of Israel
this is my new agreement:
‘The time will come
when I, the Lord,
will write my laws
on their minds and hearts.
I will be their God,
and they will be
my people.
11Not one of them
will have to teach another
to know me, their Lord.’
“All of them will know me,
no matter who they are.
12I will treat them with kindness,
even though they are wicked.
I will forget their sins.”
13When the Lord talks about a new agreement, he means that the first one is out of date. And anything that is old and useless will soon disappear.
translation_text:
Yesu wa sɔfo nɔkɔtɔma
1Se nihi nɛ wa ngɛ dee ɔ kulaa yi ji nɛ ɔ nɛ: Wa ngɛ kikɛmɛ a osɔfo nɔkɔtɔma, nɔ nɛ hii si ngɛ he walɔ ngua a matsɛ sɛ ɔ hiɛ ɔ nɔ ngɛ hiɔwe, 2kaa he klɔuklɔu ɔ kɛ anɔkuale bo tsu nɛ Nyɔmtsɛ ɔ nitsɛ lɛ ma nɛ pi nɔmlɔ ko nɛ ma a mi sɔmɔlɔ.
3Ejakaa osɔfo nɔkɔtɔma tsuaa osɔfo nɔkɔtɔma a, a wo lɛ konɛ e ngɔ nike nihi kɛ bɔ sami nihi kɛ ba ha, lɔ ɔ he je ɔ e hia kaa nɔ nɛ ɔ hu e na nɔ́ ko nɛ e kɛ ba ha. 4Se kaa zugba a nɔ e ngɛ jinɛ, e be osɔfo tete pee, ejakaa osɔfohi nɛ kɛ nike nihi ya haa ngɛ Mlaa nya a ngɛ; 5nihi nɛ hiɔwe ni ɔmɛ a henɔ kɛ a nini kɛkɛ a sɔmɔɔ, kaa bɔ nɛ a tu munyu tsɔɔ Mose, benɛ e maa ma bo tsu ɔ ke: “Hyɛ nɛ hi, konɛ o pee ni ɔmɛ kulaa ngɛ henɔ nɛ a tsɔɔ mo ngɛ yoku ɔ nɔ ɔ nya.” 6Se jehanɛ ɔ, Yesu na osɔfo yemi nɛ hi pe kekle nɔ ɔ, ejakaa somi nɛ hi pe kekle nɔ ɔ nɛ a da si womihi nɛ hi pe kekle ni ɔmɛ a nɔ kɛ kã kita a mi dalɔ ji lɛ.
7Ejakaa kaa kekle somi ɔ hi kɛ pi si jinɛ a be blɔ hlae ngɔ ha nɔ́ nɛ ji enyɔ ɔ. 8Ejakaa Mawu piaa mɛ: E ke:
“Oʼɛ, ligbihi ma,
Nɛ i kɛ Israel we ɔ kɛ Yuda we ɔ
Maa so somi he ko,
9Pi kaa somi nɛ i kɛ a tsɛmɛ ɔmɛ so
Benɛ i pɛtɛ a nine mi nɛ i kɛ mɛ je
Mizraim zugba a nɔ ɔ;
Ejakaa a yi ye somi ɔ nɔ
Nɛ imi hu i bui a he akɔtaa, Nyɔmtsɛ ɔ lɛ de.
10Ejakaa enɛ ɔ ji somi nɛ i kɛ Israel we ɔ maa so
Ngɛ jamɛ a ligbi ɔmɛ a se ɔ nɛ,
Nyɔmtsɛ ɔ de ke:
I kɛ ye mlaahi maa wo a juɛmi mi,
Nɛ ma ngma ngɔ wo a tsui mi,
Nɛ ma pee a Mawu
Nɛ mɛ hu a maa pee ye ma.
11Nɛ a ti nɔ ko be e huɛ loo e nyɛmi tsɔɔe ke:
‘Le Nyɔmtsɛ ɔ.’
Ejakaa mɛ kulaa a maa le mi,
Kɛ maa je a kpɛti nɔ nyafii nɔ
Kɛ yaa su nɔ ngua nɔ.
12Ejakaa ma na mɛ mɔbɔ ngɛ a nɔ tɔmi ɔmɛ a he,
Nɛ a he yayami ɔmɛ hu i be kaie ligbi ko ligbi ko.”
13Somi he nɛ ɔ he munyu ɔ, ha kekle nɔ ɔ pee momo. Se nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ pee momo kɛ nɔ́ nɛ bwɔ ɔ, e be kɛe nɛ e maa laa.

english_text:
The Tent in Heaven
1The first promise included rules for worship and a tent for worship here on earth. 2 The first part of the tent was called the holy place, and a lampstand, a table, and the sacred loaves of bread were kept there.
3 Behind the curtain was the most holy place. 4 The gold altar for burning incense was in this holy place. The gold-covered sacred chest was also there, and inside it were three things. First, there was a gold jar filled with manna. Then there was Aaron's walking stick that sprouted. Finally, there were the flat stones with the Ten Commandments written on them. 5 On top of the chest were the glorious creatures with wings opened out above the place of mercy.
Now isn't the time to go into detail about these things. 6 But this is how everything was when the priests went each day into the first part of the tent to do their duties. 7 However, only the high priest could go into the second part of the tent, and he went in only once a year. Each time he carried blood to offer for his sins and for any sins that the people had committed without meaning to.
8All of this is the Holy Spirit's way of saying no one could enter the most holy place while the tent was still the place of worship. 9This also has a meaning for today. It shows we cannot make our consciences clear by offering gifts and sacrifices. 10These rules are merely about such things as eating and drinking and ceremonies for washing ourselves. And rules about physical things will last only until the time comes to change them for something better.
11 Christ came as the high priest of the good things that are now here. He also went into a much better tent that wasn't made by humans and that doesn't belong to this world. 12Then Christ went once for all into the most holy place and freed us from sin forever. He did this by offering his own blood instead of the blood of goats and bulls.
13 According to the Law of Moses, those people who become unclean are not fit to worship God. Yet they will be considered clean, if they are sprinkled with the blood of goats and bulls and with the ashes of a sacrificed calf. 14But Christ was sinless, and he offered himself as an eternal and spiritual sacrifice to God. This is why his blood is much more powerful and makes our consciences clear. Now we can serve the living God and no longer do things that lead to death.
15Christ died to rescue those who had sinned and broken the old agreement. Now he brings his chosen ones a new agreement with its guarantee of God's eternal blessings! 16In fact, making an agreement of this kind is like writing a will. This is because the one who makes the will must die before it is of any use. 17In other words, a will doesn't go into effect as long as the one who made it is still alive.
18Blood was also used to put the first agreement into effect. 19 Moses told the people all the Law said they must do. Then he used red wool and a hyssop plant to sprinkle the people and the book of the Law with the blood of bulls and goats and with water. 20He told the people, “With this blood God makes his agreement with you.” 21 Moses also sprinkled blood on the tent and on everything else used in worship. 22 The Law says that almost everything must be sprinkled with blood, and no sins can be forgiven unless blood is offered.
Christ's Great Sacrifice
23These things are only copies of what is in heaven, and so they had to be made holy by these ceremonies. But the real things in heaven must be made holy by something better. 24This is why Christ did not go into a tent made by humans and was only a copy of the real one. Instead, he went into heaven and is now there with God to help us.
25Christ did not have to offer himself many times. He wasn't like a high priest who goes into the most holy place each year to offer the blood of an animal. 26If he had offered himself every year, he would have suffered many times since the creation of the world. But instead, near the end of time he offered himself once and for all, so he could be a sacrifice that does away with sin.
27We die only once, and then we are judged. 28 So Christ died only once to take away the sins of many people. But when he comes again, it will not be to take away sin. He will come to save everyone who is waiting for him.
translation_text:
Hiɔwe kɛ Zugba nɔ nɔ jami
1Jehanɛ kekle somi ɔ hu ngɛ Mawu jami blɔ nya nihi kɛ He klɔuklɔu nɛ ji je nɛ ɔ mi nɔ́ ɔ. 2A ma bo tsu ko ngɔ ma si, nɛ e kpo nɔ je ɔ, kane tso kɛ okplɔɔ kɛ hɛ mi mami abolohi ngɛ lejɛ ɔ; a tsɛɛ lejɛ ɔ ke He klɔuklɔu. 3Nɛ tsu mi pomi bo nɛ ji enyɔ ɔ se bo tsu ɔ a tsɛɛ lɛ He klɔuklɔu pe kulaa. 4Lejɛ ɔ tsopa kɛ e he via sami nɔ́ kɛ somi daka nɛ a kɛ sika ha he kulaa a ngɛ, lɔ ɔ mi sika kplu kɛ mana a kɛ Aaron tso nɛ su ba a kɛ somi tɛ tɛtlɛɛ ɔmɛ a nɔ ɔ ngɛ; 5nɛ lɔ ɔ nɔ nyami kerubim nɛ ha kpatami sɛ ɔ nɔ ɔ ngɛ, nihi nɛ amlɔ nɛ ɔ wa be nyɛe a he munyu tumi kakaaka a.
6Bɔ nɛ a dlaa kikɛmɛ a ni nɛ ɔmɛ haa ji nɛ ɔ nɛ: osɔfo ɔmɛ yaa kekle bo tsu ɔ mi daa ligbi ya tsuɔ Mawu jami he ni; 7se bo tsu nɛ ji enyɔ ɔ, osɔfo nɔkɔtɔma a kɛkɛ lɛ yaa mi si kake daa jeha, nɛ e si we muɔ nɛ e ya, nɔ́ nɛ e kɛ ya haa ngɛ lɛ nitsɛ kɛ ma a tɔmihi nɛ a li ɔmɛ a he ɔ. 8Enɛ ɔ Mumi Klɔuklɔu ɔ kɛ tsɔɔ pãa kaa be abɔ nɛ kekle bo tsu ɔ maa si kɛ mwɔ nɛ ɔ ɔ, lɛɛ blɔ nɛ a kɛ yaa he klɔuklɔu ɔ a na we nɛ a bli. 9Enɛ ɔ ji mwɔnɛ mwɔnɛ be nɛ ɔ he abɛ nɛ a bu. Lɔ ɔ tsɔɔ kaa a kɛ nike nihi kɛ bɔ sami nihi be nyɛe ma ha nɔ́ nɛ dɛ́ ɔ nɛ hi kɛ pi si ngɛ he nile blɔfami 10nihi nɛ kɔɔ niye ni kɛ numi nihi kɛ he dumi slɔɔtohi nɛ ji he lo blɔ nya nihi a he nɛ a to ke a pee kɛ ya su ehe peemi be ɔ.
11Se Kristo nɛ ba ba ye ni kpakpahi nɛ maa ba amɛ a he osɔfo nɔkɔtɔma a, gu bo tsu nɛ kle nɛ hi kɛ pi si nɛ pi nine nɛ a kɛ pee, lɔ ɔ ji kaa pi je nɛ ɔ mi bɔ nihi a mi nɛ e je ɔ mi, 12nɛ pohu, pi tokuhi loo na bimɛ a muɔ, se mohu lɛ nitsɛ e muɔ ɔ e kɛ sɛ he klɔuklɔu ɔ mi si kake nyɔngloo, nɛ e kɛ na neneene kpɔmi ɔ. 13Ejakaa ke nahi kɛ tokui a muɔ kɛ na bimɛ a lazu nɛ a kɛ fiãa nihi nɛ bleɔ a he ɔ nɔ ɔ fɔɔ a he nɛ a he tsɔɔ ngɛ he lo blɔfami ɔ, 14si nyɛmɛ nɔuu nɛ Kristo, nɛ gu neneene mumi ɔ nɔ ngɔ e he nɛ piami ko be he ngɔ ha Mawu ɔ muɔ be wa he ni lemi he fɔe kɛ je ni tsumi gbogboehi a mi, konɛ wa sɔmɔ Mawu hɛ kalɔ ɔ?
15Enɛ ɔ nɔuu he je nɛ e ji somi he ɔ mi dalɔ ɔ nɛ, benɛ pee nɛ e gu gbenɔ nɔ kɛ kpata kekle somi ɔ nɔ tɔmi ɔmɛ, konɛ nihi nɛ a tsɛ ɔmɛ a nine nɛ su neneene gbo si ni ɔmɛ a he si womi ɔ nɔ.
16Ejakaa he nɛ si womi nɛ haa a yeɔ gbo si ni ngɛ ɔ, e hia kaa nɔ nɛ wo si ɔ e gbo lolo, 17ejakaa si womi nɛ haa a yeɔ gbo si ni ɔ, ja si wolɔ ɔ gbo loko e naa he wami, se ke e hɛ ngɛ kɛ mwɔ ɔ, e be he wami. 18Enɛ ɔ he nɛ kekle nɔ́ ɔ hu a si we muɔ se kɛ wui ɔ nɛ. 19Ejakaa benɛ Mose fiɛ kita amɛ tsuo ngɔ tsɔɔ ma mluku ɔ kulaa ngɛ mlaa a nya a, e ngɔ na bimɛ kɛ tokuhi a muɔ kɛ nyu kɛ jijɔ he bwɔmi tsutsu kɛ hisopo, nɛ e kɛ fia womi ɔ nitsɛ kɛ ma mluku ɔ kulaa nɔ, 20e ke: “Oʼɛ, somi ɔ nɛ Mawu kã nyɛ he kita a muɔ ɔ ji nɛ ɔ nɛ.” 21Nɛ bo tsu ɔ hu kɛ Mawu jami he ni ɔmɛ kulaa, e kɛ muɔ ɔ fia nɔ ja nɔuu. 22Nɛ anɔkuale mi ɔ, e piɛ bɔɔ nɛ a kɛ muɔ tsukɔɔ nihi kulaa he ngɛ mlaa a nya; nɛ ke a pue we muɔ si ɔ, a kɛ pɛ́.
Kristo bɔsami ɔ jeɔ yayami
23Lɛɛ e hia kaa nihi nɛ ji hiɔwe ni ɔmɛ a henɔ nɛ ɔmɛ ɔ, a ngɔ enɛ ɔmɛ kɛ tsukɔ he; se hiɔwe ni ɔmɛ nitsɛmɛ ɔ, bɔhi nɛ hi pe kɔlɔ ɔmɛ a kɛ tsukɔɔ he. 24Ejakaa pi he klɔuklɔu nɛ a kɛ ninehi pee nɛ ji nɔ́ ɔ nitsɛ henɔ kɛkɛ mi nɛ Kristo ya sɛ ɔ, se mohu hiɔwe nitsɛ e ya sɛ, konɛ jehanɛ ya je e he kpo ngɛ Mawu hɛ mi ha wɔ. 25Pohu e ya sɛ we lejɛ ɔ konɛ e ngɔ e he ngɔ ha daa daa, kaa bɔ nɛ osɔfo nɔkɔtɔma a ya sɛɛ he klɔuklɔu ɔ daa jeha kɛ muɔ nɛ pi lɛ nitsɛ e nɔ ɔ; 26ejakaa ke ja a, jinɛ sa kaa e na amanehlu kpiti kpiti kɛ je je mi siiije lokoo; se jehanɛ ɔ, si kake kɛkɛ a je lɛ kpo ngɛ je mi be ɔmɛ a nyagbe mi, konɛ e ngɔ lɛ nitsɛ e he nɛ e kɛ sa bɔ ɔ kɛ je yayami ɔ. 27Nɛ be abɔ nɛ e fɔɔ si ha nimli kaa si kake a gboɔ nɛ lɔ ɔ se ɔ a maa kojo mɛ ɔ, 28ja nɔuu Kristo hu, a ngɔ lɛ ngɔ ha si kake, konɛ e tloo nihi fuu a he yayami kɛ ho. E ma je e he kpo nɔ́ nɛ ji si enyɔ, pi ngɛ yayami he, se mohu konɛ e ba he ninɛmɛ nɛ ngɛ lɛ blɔ hyɛe ɔ a yi wami.

english_text:
1The Law of Moses is like a shadow of the good things to come. This shadow isn't the good things themselves, because it cannot free people from sin by the sacrifices offered year after year. 2If there were worshipers who already have their sins washed away and their consciences made clear, there would not be any need to go on offering sacrifices. 3-4But the blood of bulls and goats cannot take away sins. It only reminds people of their sins from one year to the next.
5 When Christ came into the world, he said to God,
“Sacrifices and offerings
are not what you want,
but you have given me
my body.
6No, you are not pleased
with animal sacrifices
and offerings for sin.”
7Then Christ said,
“And so, my God,
I have come to do
what you want,
as the Scriptures say.”
8The Law teaches that offerings and sacrifices must be made because of sin. But why did Christ mention these things and say that God did not want them? 9Well, it was to do away with offerings and sacrifices and to replace them. This is what he meant by saying to God, “I have come to do what you want.” 10So we are made holy because Christ obeyed God and offered himself once for all.
11 The priests do their work each day, and they keep on offering sacrifices that can never take away sins. 12 But Christ offered himself as a sacrifice that is good forever. Now he is sitting at God's right side, 13and he will stay there until his enemies are put under his power. 14By his one sacrifice he has forever set free from sin the people he brings to God.
15The Holy Spirit also speaks of this by telling us that the Lord said,
16 “When the time comes,
I will make an agreement
with them.
I will write my laws
on their minds and hearts.
17 Then I will forget
about their sins
and no longer remember
their evil deeds.”
18When sins are forgiven, there is no more need to offer sacrifices.
Encouragement and Warning
19My friends, the blood of Jesus gives us courage to enter the most holy place 20by a new way that leads to life! And this way takes us through the curtain that is Christ himself.
21We have a great high priest who is in charge of God's house. 22 So let's come near God with pure hearts and a confidence that comes from having faith. Let's keep our hearts pure, our consciences free from evil, and our bodies washed with clean water. 23We must hold tightly to the hope we say is ours. After all, we can trust the one who made the agreement with us. 24We should keep on encouraging each other to be thoughtful and to do helpful things. 25Some people have given up the habit of meeting for worship, but we must not do that. We should keep on encouraging each other, especially since you know that the day of the Lord's coming is getting closer.
26No sacrifices can be made for people who decide to sin after they find out about the truth. 27 They are God's enemies, and all they can look forward to is a terrible judgment and a furious fire. 28 If two or more witnesses accused someone of breaking the Law of Moses, that person could be put to death. 29 But it is much worse to dishonor God's Son and to disgrace the blood of the promise that made us holy. And it is just as bad to insult the Holy Spirit, who shows us mercy. 30 We know that God has said he will punish and take revenge. We also know that the Scriptures say the Lord will judge his people. 31It is a terrible thing to fall into the hands of the living God!
32Don't forget all the hard times you went through when you first received the light. 33Sometimes you were abused and mistreated in public, and at other times you shared in the sufferings of others. 34You were kind to people in jail. And you gladly let your possessions be taken away, because you knew you had something better, something that would last forever.
35Keep on being brave! It will bring you great rewards. 36Learn to be patient, so you will please God and be given what he has promised. 37 As the Scriptures say,
“God is coming soon!
It won't be very long.
38The people God accepts
will live because
of their faith.
But he isn't pleased
with anyone
who turns back.”
39We are not like those people who turn back and get destroyed. We will keep on having faith until we are saved.
translation_text:
1Ejakaa ni kpakpahi nɛ maa ba amɛ a nini kɛkɛ Mlaa a hɛɛ, se pi ni ɔmɛ a subai nitsɛ, lɔ ɔ he ɔ, e be nyɛe nɛ e kɛ daa jeha bɔhi nɛ a saa nɔtonɔto ɔ nɛ ha nihi nɛ baa Mawu ngɔ ɔ nɛ a hi kɛ pi si. 2Jinɛ a ko jɔɔ bɔ ɔmɛ sami, ejakaa nihi nɛ ba jaa Mawu ɔ, ke a tsukɔ a he si kake pɛ ɔ, a be fɔ ko nɛ a yeɔ ngɛ a he yayamihi a he kulaa hu. 3Se mohu bɔ ɔmɛ ɔ, kaimi a kɛ kaii yayamihi daa jeha, 4ejakaa a be nyɛe maa ngɔ nahi kɛ tokuhi a muɔ kɛ je yayamihi.
5Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, benɛ Kristo ma je nɔ mi ɔ, ye de Mawu ke:
“Bɔ kɛ nike ni ɔmɛ ɔ, o sume,
Se nɔmlɔ tso o dla ha mi
6Bɔ nɛ a kɛ lohwehi saa kɛ yayami he bɔ ɔmɛ
Sɛ́ o hɛ mi.
7Kɛkɛ nɛ i de ke: ‘Oʼɛ, i ba, Oo Mawu,
Nɛ ma ba pee o suɔmi nya ni
Kaa bɔ nɛ a ngma ngɛ ye he ngɛ Mlaa womi ɔ mi ɔ.’ ”
8Kekle ɔ e ke: “Bɔ kɛ nike nihi kɛ lohwehi a bɔhi kɛ yayami he bɔ ɔmɛ ɔ o sume, nɛ e sɛ́ o hɛ mi hulɔ,” (nihi nɛ a kɛ ba haa ngɛ Mlaa a nya a); 9kɛkɛ nɛ e ke: “Oʼɛ, i ba nɛ ma ba pee mo, Mawu, o suɔmi nya ni.” Lɔ ɔ Mawu jeɔ kekle bɔ sami ni ɔmɛ konɛ e ngɔ Kristo nɔ ɔ ngɔ ma nane mi. 10A kɛnɛ Yesu Kristo pee Mawu suɔmi nya ni he je ɔ, a tsukɔ wa he kɛ gu e nɔmlɔ tso nɛ e kɛ ha si kake nyɔngloo ɔ nɔ.
11Osɔfo tsuaa osɔfo ɔ, ligbi tsuaa ligbi ɔ, e daa si nɛ e sɔmɔɔ, nɛ e saa jamɛ a bɔ ɔmɛ nɔuu kpitikpiti, nihi nɛ nyɛ we yayami nɛ a je ligbi ko ligbi ko ɔ. 12Kristo lɛɛ e sa yayamihi a he bɔ si kake nyɔngloo, nɛ e ya hi si ngɛ Mawu hiɛ ɔ nɔ; 13nɛ nɔ́ nɛ piɛ ji kaa, e ngɛ mlɛe kɛ maa su be nɛ a maa ngɔ e henyɛli ɔmɛ kɛ maa pee e nane si maangoo. 14Ejakaa bɔ kake nɛ e sa a, e kɛ ha nihi nɛ a tsukɔ a he ɔ hi kɛ pi si nyɔngloo.
15Mumi Klɔuklɔu ɔ hu yeɔ wɔ odase. Kekleekle ɔ, e ke:
16“Enɛ ɔ ji somi nɛ i kɛ mɛ maa so
Ngɛ jamɛ a ligbi ɔmɛ a se, Nyɔmtsɛ ɔ lɛ de:
I kɛ ye mlaa amɛ maa wo a tsui mi,
Nɛ ma ngma ngɔ wo a juɛmi mi
17Nɛ a he yayami ɔmɛ kɛ a nɔ tɔmi ɔmɛ ɔ, i be kaie kulaa hu.”
18Nɛ he nɛ a kɛ enɔmɛ pa ngɛ ɔ, yayami he bɔ sami ko be hu.
Nyɛ ha waa hɛ kɛ su Mawu he
19Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, mamimɛ, akɛnɛ wa ngɛ he blɔ ngɛ Yesu muɔ ɔ nya nɛ wa kɛ maa sɛ he klɔuklɔu ɔ 20ngɛ blɔ he nɛ hɛ ngɛ nɛ e je ha wɔ ɔ kɛ gu tsu mi pomi bo ɔ nɛ ji lɛ nitsɛ e he lo ɔ mi, 21nɛ jehanɛ wa ngɛ osɔfo nɔkɔtɔma ngua nɛ yeɔ Mawu we ɔ nɔ he je ɔ, 22nyɛ ha waa hɛ kɛ su Mawu he kɛ tsui klɔuu ngɛ hemi kɛ yemi nɛ wa ngɛ he wami ngɛ nɔ ɔ mi, kɛ tsui hu nɛ a tsukɔ he nɛ e be he ni lemi yaya ko hulɔ, kɛ nɔmlɔ tso nɛ a kɛ nyu nɛ mi tsɔ du he. 23Nyɛ ha waa pɛtɛ wa hɛ kɛ nɔ fɔmi nɛ wa jaje ɔ mi wawɛɛ, ejakaa nɔ nɛ wo si ɔ anɔkualetsɛ ji lɛ. 24Nyɛ ha wa susu wa sibi a he, konɛ wa hɛ nɛ e dɔ ngɛ suɔmi kɛ ni tsumi kpakpahi a he. 25Nyɛ ko ha waa jɔɔ wa he nya buami, kaa bɔ nɛ ni komɛ pɔɔ peemi ɔ, se mohu waa wo wa he ga, nɛ titli ɔ, akɛnɛ nyɛ na kaa Ligbi ɔ ngɛ sue nɛ ɔ.
