E binyumu ɔmɛ ngɔ muɔ ɔ kɛ ba ha lɛ, nɛ e tsɛ̃ kɛ pue bɔ sami la tɛ ɔ he kɛ kpe. 19Na ku ɔ zɔ ɔ, agbosu ɔ zɔ ɔ, kɛ hlemi ɔ, kɛ se tso mi ngmɛ ɔmɛ, kɛ fafali ɔ he nɛ hi pe kulaa a, 20Aaron ngɔ mɛ ngɔ pue lohwe ɔmɛ a gugue ɔmɛ a nɔ, nɛ e ya sã mɛ ngɛ bɔ sami la tɛ ɔ nɔ. 21Kaa bɔ nɛ Mose fa ke a pee ɔ, gugue ɔmɛ, kɛ hiɔ nɔ fiɔ ɔ lɛɛ Aaron wo a nɔ kaa bɔ nɛ a fɔɔ kɛ yaa kɛ baa ngɛ Yawɛ hɛ mi.
22 Benɛ Aaron sã yayami pami bɔ ɔ, sami bɔ ɔ, kɛ tue mi jɔmi bɔ ɔ gbe nya a, e wo e nine nɔ ngɛ ma a nɔ nɛ e gbaa mɛ. Lɔ ɔ se ɔ, e kple si kɛ je he nɛ e sã bɔ ɔmɛ ngɛ ɔ. 23Jehanɛ, Mose kɛ Aaron sɛ kpe he bo tsu ɔ mi, nɛ benɛ a je kpo ɔ, a gbaa ma a. Kɛkɛ nɛ Yawɛ hɛ mi nyami ɔ je kpo, nɛ ma a tsuo pɛpɛɛpɛ na. 24Tlukaa a, Yawɛ ha nɛ la ba, nɛ e ba sã sami bɔ ɔ, kɛ zɔ ɔ nɛ ngɛ bɔ sami la tɛ ɔ nɔ ɔ. Benɛ ni ɔmɛ tsuo na nɔ́ nɛ ɔ, a he ose, nɛ a kɛ a hɛ mi bu si.

english_text:
Nadab and Abihu
1Nadab and Abihu were two of Aaron's sons, but they disobeyed the Lord by burning incense to him on a fire pan, when they were not supposed to. 2Suddenly the Lord sent fiery flames and burned them to death. 3Then Moses told Aaron that this was exactly what the Lord had meant when he said:
“I demand respect
from my priests,
and I will be praised
by everyone!”
Aaron was speechless.
4Moses sent for Mishael and Elzaphan, the two sons of Aaron's uncle Uzziel. Then he told them, “Take these two dead relatives of yours outside the camp far from the entrance to the sacred tent.” 5So they dragged the dead men away by their clothes.
6Then Moses told Aaron and his other two sons, Eleazar and Ithamar:
Don't show your sorrow by messing up your hair and tearing your priestly clothes, or the Lord will get angry. He will kill the three of you and punish everyone else. It's all right for your relatives, the people of Israel, to mourn for those he destroyed by fire. 7But you are the Lord's chosen priests, and you must not leave the sacred tent, or you will die.
Aaron and his two sons obeyed Moses.
8The Lord said to Aaron:
9When you or your sons enter the sacred tent, you must never drink beer or wine. If you do, you will die right there! This law will never change. 10You must learn the difference between what is holy and what isn't holy and between the clean and the unclean. 11You must also teach the people of Israel everything that I commanded Moses to say to them.
12 Moses told Aaron and his two sons, Eleazar and Ithamar:
The grain sacrifice that was offered to give thanks to the Lord is very holy. So make bread without yeast from the part that wasn't sent up in smoke and eat it beside the altar. 13The Lord has said that this belongs to you and your sons, and that it must be eaten in a holy place. 14-15 But the choice ribs and the hind leg that were lifted up may be eaten by your entire family, as long as you do so in an acceptable place. These parts are yours from the sacrifices that the people offer to ask the Lord's blessing. This is what the Lord has commanded, and it will never change.
16When Moses asked around and learned that the ram for the sin sacrifice had already been burned on the altar, he became angry with Eleazar and Ithamar and said, 17 “Why didn't you eat the meat from this sacrifice in an acceptable place? It is very holy, and the Lord has given you this sacrifice to remove Israel's sin and guilt. 18Whenever an animal's blood isn't brought into the sacred tent, I commanded you to eat its meat in an acceptable place, but you burned it instead.”
19Their father Aaron replied, “Today two of my sons offered the sacrifice for sin and the sacrifice to please the Lord, and look what has happened to me! Would the Lord have approved if I had eaten the sacrifice for sin?”
20Moses was satisfied with Aaron's reply.
translation_text:
Nadab kɛ Abihu pee yayami
1Aaron binyumuhi, Nadab kɛ Abihu a ti nɔ tsuaa nɔ ngɔ e ngɛyu, nɛ e je la ngɔ wo mi, nɛ e ngɔ tsopa kɛ e he via ngɔ pue nɔ, nɛ e kɛ ba Yawɛ hɛ mi; se la nɛ ɔ he tsɔ we, ejakaa Yawɛ fa we mɛ ke a pee ja. 2Tlukaa a, la je Yawɛ ngɔ ba sã mɛ, nɛ a gbo ngɛ lejɛ ɔ. 3Kɛkɛ nɛ Mose de Aaron ke, “Enɛ ɔ ji nɔ́ nɛ Yawɛ de ɔ nɛ. E ke, ‘Nihi nɛ hɛ mɛ kɛ su ye he ɔ, ma tsɔɔ mɛ bɔ nɛ i ngɛ klɔuklɔu ha, nɛ a maa wo ye hɛ mi nyami ngɛ ma a tsuo hɛ mi.’ ” Se Aaron de we nɔ́ ko.
4Mose tsɛ Aaron tsɛ nyɛminyumu Uziel bimɛ, Mishael kɛ Elzafan kɛ ba, nɛ e de mɛ ke, “Nyɛɛ ba hiɛ ɔ nɛ nyɛ ba muɔ nyɛ nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ kɛ je he klɔuklɔu ɔ kɛ ho ma a sito he ɔ se ya.” 5A ba muɔ mɛ kɛ a he tade ɔmɛ kɛ ho ma sito he ɔ se ya kaa bɔ nɛ Mose de mɛ ɔ.
6Lɔ ɔ se ɔ, Mose de Aaron kɛ e binyumu ɔmɛ, Eleazar kɛ Itamar ke, “Nyɛ ko ngmɛɛ nyɛ yi bwɔmi he kɛ pue nyɛ nɔ, nɛ nyɛ ko hía nyɛ tadehi ngɛ nyɛ he hulɔ kɛ tsɔɔ kaa nyɛ ngɛ kɔmɔ yee. Ke nyɛ pee ja a, nyɛ ma gbo, nɛ Yawɛ mi mi ma fu ma a tsuo. Se nyɛ nyɛmimɛ ɔmɛ, kɛ Israel we ɔ tsuo kulaa ma nyɛ maa ye kɔmɔ nɛ a nyɛ ya ha gbogboe ɔmɛ nɛ Yawɛ la sã a. 7Nyɛ ko je kpe he bo tsu ɔ sinya a nya kɛ ya he ko. Ke nyɛ pee ja a, nyɛ ma gbo; ejakaa a kɛ Yawɛ nu pɔ nyɛ.” Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, a pee kaa bɔ nɛ Mose de ɔ.
Mlaa nɛ a wo osɔfo ɔmɛ
8Yawɛ kɛ Aaron tu munyu, nɛ e de lɛ ke, 9“O kɛ o binyumu ɔmɛ nyɛ ti nɔ ko nɔ ko kó nu wai, loo dã nɛ nya wa kɛ ya kpe he bo tsu ɔ mi. Ke nyɛ pee ja a, nyɛ ma gbo. Enɛ ɔ maa pee mlaa nɛ fɔɔ si ha nyɛ kɛ yaa neneene. 10Nyɛɛ le slɔɔto nɛ ngɛ nɔ́ klɔuklɔu, kɛ nɔ́ gu a kpɛti, nɔ́ nɛ he tsɔ, kɛ nɔ́ nɛ he tsɔ we. 11Nyɛɛ tsɔɔ Israel bi ɔmɛ mlaa amɛ tsuo kulaa nɛ́ imi Yawɛ, i wo mɛ kɛ gu Mose nɔ ɔ.”
12 Jehanɛ, Mose de Aaron kɛ e binyumuhi enyɔ ɔmɛ nɛ piɛ, nɛ ji Eleazar kɛ Itamar ke, “Niye ní bɔhi nɛ a kɛ la sãã ha Yawɛ ɔ, nyɛɛ ngɔ nɔ́ nɛ piɛ ɔ; nyɛ ko wo mi masa nɛ nyɛɛ ye ngɛ bɔ sami la tɛ ɔ kasa nya, ejakaa e he tsɔ saminya. 13Nyɛɛ ye ngɛ he ko nɛ ngɛ klɔuklɔu, ejakaa bɔhi nɛ a kɛ la sãã kɛ haa Yawɛ ɔ, nyɛɛ nyɛ blɔ fami nɔ́ nɛ Yawɛ to ji lɔ ɔ nɛ. 14 Se lohwe ɔ gugue nɛ a fɔɔ, kɛ fiɔ ɔ nɛ a woɔ nɔ́ ɔ, o kɛ o binyumu ɔmɛ, kɛ o biyi ɔmɛ nɛ ye ngɛ he ko nɛ tsɔ; ejakaa tue mi jɔmi bɔ ɔmɛ nɛ Israel bi ɔmɛ ba sãã a, o kɛ o bimɛ ɔmɛ nyɛ blɔ fa mi nɔ́ ji lɔ ɔ nɛ. 15Fiɔ ɔ, kɛ gugue ɔ nɛ a fɔɔ kɛ yaa kɛ baa ngɛ Yawɛ hɛ mi ɔ, á ngɔ kɛ piɛ zɔ ɔ nɛ a kɛ la sãã a he kɛ ba kaa bɔ nɛ a fɔɔ kɛ yaa kɛ baa ngɛ Yawɛ hɛ mi. Fiɔ ɔ, kɛ gugue ɔ maa pee o kɛ o binyumu ɔmɛ nyɛ nɔ́ kɛ yaa neneene kaa bɔ nɛ Yawɛ fa a.”
16Enɛ ɔmɛ tsuo a se ɔ, Mose hla mi fitsofitso konɛ e le nɔ́ ko ngɛ apletsi ɔ nɛ a kɛ maa sã yayami pami bɔ ɔ he. Benɛ e na le kaa a sã lɛ momo ɔ, e mi mi fu Eleazar kɛ Itamar, Aaron bimɛ ɔmɛ nɛ piɛ ɔ, nɛ e bi mɛ ke, 17 “Mɛni he je nɛ nyɛ yi yayami pami bɔ ɔ ngɛ he klɔuklɔu ɔ? Nyɛ li kaa e ji nɔ́ ko nɛ ngɛ klɔuklɔu, nɛ Mawu kɛ ha nyɛ nɛ nyɛ kɛ je ma a he yayami kɛ kpata Yawɛ kɛ ha mɛ lo? 18Nɛ nyɛ ngɔɛ e muɔ ɔ kɛ yɛ he klɔuklɔu ɔ, jinɛ e sa kaa nyɛɛ ye bɔ sami ní ɔ ngɛ he klɔuklɔu ɔ kɛkɛ kaa bɔ nɛ i fa nyɛ ɔ.”
19Aaron he nɔ ke, “O nɛ, mwɔnɛ ɔ, ma a ngɔ a he yayami pami bɔ ɔ, kɛ a sami bɔ ɔ ba ha Yawɛ, nɛ nɔ́ nɛ ba ye nɔ ji nɛ ɔ nɛ! Kaa i ye yayami pami bɔ nɛ ɔ eko mwɔnɛ ɔ, e ko sa Yawɛ hɛ mi lo?” 20Benɛ Mose nu munyu nɛ ɔ, munyu ɔ da ha lɛ.

english_text:
Clean and Unclean Animals
(Deuteronomy 14.3-21)
1 The Lord told Moses and Aaron 2to say to the community of Israel:
You may eat 3any animal that has divided hoofs and chews the cud. 4-8But you must not eat animals such as camels, rock badgers, and rabbits that chew the cud but don't have divided hoofs. And you must not eat pigs—they have divided hoofs, but don't chew the cud. All of these animals are unclean, and you are forbidden even to touch their dead bodies.
9-12You may eat anything that lives in water and has fins and scales. But it would be disgusting for you to eat anything else that lives in water, and you must not even touch their dead bodies.
13-19Eagles, vultures, buzzards, crows, ostriches, hawks, sea gulls, owls, pelicans, storks, herons, hoopoes, and bats are also disgusting, and you are forbidden to eat any of them.
20-23The only winged insects you may eat are locusts, grasshoppers, and crickets. All other winged insects that crawl are too disgusting for you to eat.
24-28Don't even touch the dead bodies of animals that have divided hoofs but don't chew the cud. And don't touch the dead bodies of animals that have paws. If you do, you must wash your clothes, but you are still unclean until evening.
29-30Moles, rats, mice, and all kinds of lizards are unclean. 31Anyone who touches their dead bodies or anything touched by their dead bodies becomes unclean until evening. 32If something made of wood, cloth, or leather touches one of their dead bodies, it must be washed, but it is still unclean until evening. 33If any of these animals is found dead in a clay pot, the pot must be broken to pieces, and everything in it becomes unclean. 34If you pour water from this pot on any food, that food becomes unclean, and anything drinkable in the pot becomes unclean.
35If the dead body of one of these animals touches anything else, including ovens and stoves, that thing becomes unclean and must be destroyed. 36A spring or a cistern where one of these dead animals is found is still clean, but anyone who touches the animal becomes unclean. 37If the dead body of one of these animals is found lying on seeds that have been set aside for planting, the seeds remain clean. 38But seeds that are soaking in water become unclean, if the dead animal is found in the water.
39If an animal that may be eaten happens to die, and you touch it, you become unclean until evening. 40If you eat any of its meat or carry its body away, you must wash your clothes, but you are still unclean until evening.
41-42Don't eat any of those disgusting little creatures that crawl or walk close to the ground. 43If you eat any of them, you will become just as disgusting and unclean as they are. 44 I am the Lord your God, and you must dedicate yourselves to me and be holy, just as I am holy. Don't become disgusting by eating any of these unclean creatures. 45I brought you out of Egypt so that I could be your God. Now you must become holy, because I am holy!
46-47I have given these laws so that you will know what animals, birds, and fish are clean and may be eaten, and which ones are unclean and may not be eaten.
translation_text:
Lohwehi nɛ á ye
(Mose V, 14.3-21)
1Yawɛ wo mlaa nɛ ɔmɛ kɛ gu Mose kɛ Aaron nɔ kɛ ha 2Israel bi ɔmɛ. Lohwe nane eywiɛɛywiɛtsɛmɛ nɛ nyɛ ma nyɛ maa ye ji nɛ ɔmɛ nɛ. 3Lohwe tsuaa lohwe nɛ a gba e nane koklotohi a mi, nɛ e gɔleɔ nɔ́ nɛ e ye ɔ nɛ e kpaleɔ taa ekohu ɔ, nyɛ ma nyɛ maa ye. 4-6Se nyɛ ko ye enɛ ɔmɛ: afukpɔngɔ, tɛ sa nɔ kpi, kɛ alɔngɔ, ejakaa a gɔleɔ nɔ́ nɛ a ye ɔ nɛ a kpaleɔ taa ekohu lɛɛ, se a gba we a nane kokloto mi, lɔ ɔ he ɔ, a he tsɔ we. 7Nyɛ ko ye kpotoo, e he tsɔ we, ejakaa a gba e nane kokloto mi lɛɛ, se e gɔle we nɔ́ nɛ e ye ɔ nɛ e ta ekohu. 8Nyɛ ko ye lohwe nɛ ɔmɛ, nɛ nyɛ ko ta a gbogboe he hulɔ; a he tsɔ we.
9Nyɛ ma nyɛ maa ye lo nɛ ɔmɛ: lo tsuaa lo nɛ ngɛ se ngmo kɛ toto. 10Se nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ wami ngɛ e mi ngɛ wo loo pa mi, nɛ e be se ngmo kɛ toto ɔ, nyɛ ko ye. 11A he tsɔ we; lɔ ɔ he ɔ, nyɛ ko ye, nɛ nyɛ ko ta a gbogboe he hulɔ. 12Nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ ngɛ nyu mi nɛ wami ngɛ e mi, se e be se ngmo kɛ toto ɔ, nyɛ ko ye; a he tsɔ we.
13-19Nyɛ ko ye lohwe pɛlitsɛmɛ kɛ a henɔ nɛ ɔmɛ: kɔle, okpoku, pa nɔ kɔle, kayo, kɔɔkɔmite, duguma, anuma, nyɔ mi kayo, klomi, nga mi kpakpahe, pa nɔ kayo, omiɔhɔɔ, kpokukpoku, godo, kɔne, loo apani.
20Nyɛ ko ye lohwe tsɔwi nane eywiɛtsɛmɛ nɛ tee, 21ja ní nɛmɛ nɛ tuu ɔ. 22Nyɛ ma nyɛ maa ye baalɛ, apã, adodo, kɛ a henɔ ɔmɛ. 23Se lohwe tsɔwi nane eywiɛtsɛmɛ nɛ tee kpahi ɔ, nyɛ ko ye; a he tsɔ we.
24-28Nɔ tsuaa nɔ nɛ maa ta lohwe nɛ ɔmɛ eko gbogboe he ɔ, e he be tsɔe kɛ yaa si du ma bu: lohwehi tsuo nɛ a gba we a nane kokloto mi, nɛ a gɔle we nɔ́ nɛ a ye ɔ nɛ a ta ekohu, kɛ lohwe nane eywiɛɛywiɛtsɛmɛ nɛ be kokloto, se a nyɛɛ ngɛ a nine a nɔ ɔ, mɛ tsuo a he tsɔ we. Nɔ tsuaa nɔ nɛ maa ta eko gbogboe he ɔ bleɔ e he. Ke nɔ ko ble e he ja a, é fɔ e tade ɔmɛ a he; se kɛ ɔ, e he be tsɔe kɛ yaa si du ma bu.
29Lohwehi nɛ sãã si ngɛ zugba a nɔ nɛ a he tsɔ we ha nyɛ ji kɔkɔbo, kɔkue, ve, kɛ e henɔ ɔmɛ, 30tsunyɛ, nyaka, akɔtɔku, angmlɔ, kɛ akpasi. 31A he tsɔ we, lɔ ɔ he ɔ, nɔ tsuaa nɔ nɛ maa ta eko gbogboe he ɔ, e he be tsɔe kɛ yaa si du ma bu. 32Nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ lohwe nɛ ɔmɛ eko gbogboe maa sa he ɔ, e he be tsɔe; tso a kɛ pee nɔ ɔ jio, bo jio, lohwe he womi jio, kotoku jio, nɔ́ saisaa jio. Á kɛ nyu nɛ fɔ he, se nɔ́ ɔ he be tsɔe kɛ yaa si du ma bu. 33Ke lohwe nɛ ɔmɛ eko gbogboe ko ya nɔ buɛ mi ɔ, e bleɔ nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ ngɛ buɛ ɔ mi ɔ; lɔ ɔ he ɔ, á ywia buɛ ɔ. 34Ke buɛ nɛ ɔ mi nyu ɔ eko pue niye ní ko nɔ ɔ, niye ní ɔ he be tsɔe. Nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ a nuu nɛ ngɛ kikɛmɛ a buɛ ɔ mi ɔ he be tsɔe. 35Jehanɛ, nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ kikɛmɛ a lohwe nɛ ɔmɛ eko gbogboe maa nɔ nɔ ɔ, nɔ́ ɔ he be tsɔe, la tɛ jio, flɔɔnɔɔ jio, á ywia nɔ́ ɔ wɔtsɔwɔtsɔ. 36Ke lohwe nɛ ɔmɛ eko gbogboe ya nɔ nyu hɛngmɛ, loo nyu nɔ́ ko mi ɔ, nyu ɔ he tsɔ; se nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ maa sa a gbogboe he ɔ he tsɔ we. 37Ke lohwe gbogboe ɔ he ko nɔ wu nɛ a yaa du nɔ ɔ, e be wu ɔ blee, 38se ke a wo wu ɔ nyu nɛ lohwe gbogboe nɔ nɔ ɔ, e bleɔ lɛ.
39Jehanɛ, ke lohwehi nɛ a yeɔ ɔ eko gbo ɔ, nɔ nɛ maa ta e gbogboe ɔ he ɔ, e he be tsɔe kɛ yaa si du ma bu. 40Ke nɔ ko ye lo nɛ ɔ eko ɔ, é fɔ e tade ɔmɛ a he. Se lɛ nitsɛ lɛɛ e he be tsɔe kɛ yaa si du ma bu. Nɔ tsuaa nɔ nɛ maa kɛ̃ e gbogboe ɔ bleɔ e he; ke nɔ ko ble e he ja a, nɔ ɔ nɛ fɔ e tade ɔmɛ a he, se e he be tsɔe kɛ yaa si du ma bu.
41Lohwehi nɛ sãã si ɔ, a he tsɔ we; nyɛ ko ye. 42Ke a sãã si ngɛ a mi nɔ jio, a nane eywiɛ nɔ jio, a nane babauu nɔ jio, nyɛ ko ye; a he tsɔ we. 43Nyɛ ko ta lohwehi nɛ sãã si ɔ eko he. Ke nyɛ pee ja a, nyɛ bleɔ nyɛ he, nɛ nyɛ he tsɔ we. 44 Imi ji Yawɛ, nyɛ Mawu ɔ nɛ. Nyɛɛ pee nyɛ he klɔuklɔu; ejakaa Nɔ Klɔuklɔu ji mi. Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, lohwehi nɛ sãã si ɔ, nyɛ ko ngɔ ekoeko kɛ ble nyɛ he. 45Imi ji Yawɛ. Imi nɛ I je nyɛ kɛ je Egipt zugba a nɔ, konɛ ma ba pee nyɛ Mawu. Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, nyɛɛ pee nyɛ he klɔuklɔu; ejakaa Nɔ Klɔuklɔu ji mi.
46Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, lohwe nane eywiɛɛywiɛtsɛmɛ, lohwe pɛlitsɛmɛ, kɛ adebɔ níhi tsuo nɛ ngɛ nyu mi, kɛ adebɔ níhi tsuo nɛ sãã si ngɛ zugba a nɔ ɔ, mlaa nɛ kɔɔ a he ji nɛ ɔmɛ nɛ. 47Mlaa nɛ ɔ tsɔɔ slɔɔto nɛ ngɛ lohwehi nɛ a he tsɔ, kɛ lohwehi nɛ a he tsɔ we a kpɛti, kɛ slɔɔto nɛ ngɛ lohwehi nɛ a yeɔ, kɛ lohwehi nɛ a yi a kpɛti.

english_text:
What Women Must Do after Giving Birth
1The Lord told Moses 2to say to the community of Israel:
If a woman gives birth to a son, she is unclean for seven days, just as she is during her monthly period. 3 Her son must be circumcised on the eighth day, 4but her loss of blood keeps her from being completely clean for another 33 days. During this time she must not touch anything holy or go to the place of worship. 5Any woman who gives birth to a daughter is unclean for two weeks, just as she is during her period. And she won't be completely clean for another 66 days.
6When the mother has completed her time of cleansing, she must come to the front of the sacred tent and bring to the priest a year-old lamb as a sacrifice to please me and a dove or a pigeon as a sacrifice for sin. 7After the priest offers the sacrifices to me, the mother will become completely clean from her loss of blood, whether her child is a boy or a girl. 8 If she cannot afford a lamb, she can offer two doves or two pigeons, one as a sacrifice to please me and the other as a sacrifice for sin.
translation_text:
Yihi a he tsukɔmi ngɛ fɔmi se
1Mlaahi nɛ Yawɛ wo 2Israel bi ɔmɛ kɛ gu Mose nɔ ji nɛ ɔmɛ nɛ. Ke yo ko ngɔ hɔ nɛ e fɔ binyumu ɔ, e he be tsɔe ligbi kpaago, kaa bɔ nɛ e he be tsɔe, ke e ku nine ɔ. 3 Ke binyumu ɔ ye ligbi kpaanyɔ ɔ, á po lɛ. 4Lɔ ɔ se ɔ, bi nyɛ ɔ he be tsɔe kɛ yaa si ligbi nyingmi etɛ kɛ etɛ se loko e he ma tsɔ. Be nɛ ɔ mi tsuo ɔ, e ko ta nɔ́ ko nɛ ngɛ klɔuklɔu he, nɛ e ko ya he klɔuklɔu ɔ hulɔ, kɛ yaa si be nɛ e maa tsukɔ e he kɛ gbe nya, ngɛ muɔ nɛ be ngɛ e he ɔ he.
5Se ke biyo e fɔ ɔ, lɛɛ e he be tsɔe otsi enyɔ, kaa bɔ nɛ e he be tsɔe, ke e ku nine ɔ. E he be tsɔe kɛ yaa si ligbi nyingmi ekpa kɛ ekpa nɛ e maa tsukɔ e he kɛ gbe nya.
6Ke yo ɔ gbe e he tsukɔmi ɔ nya ngɛ binyumu, loo biyo fɔmi se ɔ, e ngɔ jijɔ nɛ ye jeha kake, kɛ lahuɛ, loo beleku lahuɛ kake kɛ ba ha osɔfo ɔ ngɛ kpe he bo tsu ɔ sinya a nya. Osɔfo ɔ nɛ ngɔ jijɔ ɔ kɛ sã sami bɔ. Lahuɛ, loo beleku lahuɛ ɔ lɛɛ e kɛ sã yayami pami bɔ. 7Osɔfo ɔ nɛ ngɔ ní nɛ ɔmɛ kɛ ba ha Yawɛ, nɛ e pee kusumi kɛ tsukɔ yo ɔ he; kɛkɛ ɔ, e he ma tsɔ. Enɛ ɔ ji mlaa nɛ fɔɔ si ha yihi tsuo nɛ ma fɔ binyumu, loo biyo.
8 Ke yo ɔ be nyɛe nɛ e kɛ jijɔ bi ma ba sã bɔ ɔ, lɛɛ e ngɔ lahuɛ enyɔ, loo beleku lahuɛ enyɔ kɛ ba. E ngɔ kake kɛ ba sã sami bɔ, nɛ e ngɔ kake hu kɛ ba sã yayami pami bɔ. Osɔfo ɔ nɛ pee kusumi kɛ tsukɔ yo ɔ he; kɛkɛ ɔ, e he ma tsɔ.

english_text:
Skin Diseases
1The Lord told Moses and Aaron to say to the people:
2If sores or boils or a skin rash should break out and start spreading on your body, you must be brought to Aaron or to one of the other priests. 3If the priest discovers that the hair in the infected area has turned white and that the infection seems more than skin deep, he will say, “This is leprosy—you are unclean.”
4But if the infected area is white and only skin deep, and if the hair in it hasn't turned white, the priest will order you to stay away from everyone else for seven days. 5If the disease hasn't spread by that time, he will order you to stay away from everyone else for another seven days. 6Then if the disease hasn't become any worse or spread, the priest will say, “You are clean. It is only a sore. After you wash your clothes, you may go home.”
7However, if the disease comes back, you must return to the priest. 8If it is discovered that the disease has started spreading, he will say, “This is leprosy—you are unclean.”
9Any of you with a skin disease must be brought to a priest. 10If he discovers that the sore spot is white with pus and that the hair around it has also turned white, 11he will say, “This is leprosy. You are unclean and must stay away from everyone else.” 12-13But if the disease has run its course and only the scars remain, he will say, “You are clean.” 14-15If the sores come back and turn white again, he will say, “This is leprosy—you are unclean.”
16-17However, if the sores heal and only white spots remain, the priest will say, “You are now clean.”
18-19If you have a sore that either swells or turns reddish-white after it has healed, then you must show it to a priest. 20If he discovers that the hair in the infected area has turned white and that the infection seems more than skin deep, he will say, “This is leprosy—you are unclean.” 21But if the white area is only on the surface of the skin and hasn't become any worse, and if the hair in it hasn't turned white, he will tell you to stay away from everyone else for seven days.
22If the sore begins spreading during this time, the priest will say, “You are unclean because you have a disease.” 23But if it doesn't spread, and only a scar remains, he will say, “You are now clean.”
24If you have a burn that gets infected and turns red or reddish-white, 25a priest must examine it. Then if he discovers that the hair in the infected area has turned white and that the infection seems more than skin deep, he will say, “The burn has turned into leprosy, and you are unclean.” 26But if the priest finds that the hair in the infected area hasn't turned white and that the sore is only skin deep and it is healing, he will tell you to stay away from everyone else for seven days. 27On the seventh day the priest will examine you again, and if the infection is spreading, he will say, “This is leprosy—you are unclean.” 28However, if the infection hasn't spread and has begun to heal, and if only a scar remains, he will say, “Only a scar remains from the burn, and you are clean.”
29If you have a sore on your head or chin, 30it must be examined by a priest. If the infection seems more than skin deep, and the hair in it has thinned out and lost its color, he will say, “This is leprosy—you are unclean.” 31On the other hand, if he discovers that the itchy spot is only skin deep, but that the hair still isn't healthy, he will order you to stay away from everyone else for seven days. 32By that time, if the itch hasn't spread, if the hair seems healthy, and if the itch is only skin deep, 33you must shave off the hair around the infection, but not those on it. Then the priest will tell you to stay away from everyone else for another seven days. 34By that time, if the itch hasn't spread and seems no more than skin deep, he will say, “You are clean; now you must wash your clothes.”
35-36Later, if the itch starts spreading, even though the hair is still healthy, the priest will say, “You are unclean.” 37But if he thinks you are completely well, he will say, “You are clean.”
38If white spots break out on your skin, 39but the priest discovers that it is only a rash, he will say, “You are clean.”
40-41If you become bald on any part of your head, you are still clean. 42-43But if a priest discovers that a reddish-white sore has broken out on the bald spot and looks like leprosy, he will say, 44“This is leprosy—you are unclean.”
45If you ever have leprosy, you must tear your clothes, leave your hair uncombed, cover the lower part of your face, and go around shouting, “I'm unclean! I'm unclean!” 46As long as you have the disease, you are unclean and must live alone outside the camp.
47-50If a greenish or reddish spot appears anywhere on any of your clothing or on anything made of leather, you must let the priest examine the clothing or the leather. He will put it aside for seven days, 51and if the mildew has spread in that time, he will say, “This is unclean 52because the mildew has spread.” Then he will burn the clothing or the piece of leather.
53If the priest discovers that the mildew hasn't spread, 54he will tell you to wash the clothing or leather and put it aside for another seven days, 55after which he will examine it again. If the spot hasn't spread, but is still greenish or reddish, the clothing or leather is unclean and must be burned. 56But if the spot has faded after being washed, he will tear away the spot. 57Later, if the spot reappears elsewhere on the clothing or the leather, you must burn it. 58Even if the spot completely disappears after being washed, it must be washed again before it is clean.
59These are the rules for deciding if clothing is clean or unclean after a spot appears on it.
translation_text:
He womi nɔ hiɔ yaya he mlaahi
1Yawɛ wo Mose kɛ Aaron mlaa nɛ ɔmɛ. 2Ke nɔfu nɔ́ ko, aloo pa, loo loholoho ba nɔ ko he, nɛ́ ma nyɛ maa pee he womi nɔ hiɔ yaya a, a ngɔ hiɔtsɛ ɔ kɛ ba osɔfo ɔ, nɛ ji Aaron nina a ngɔ. 3Osɔfo ɔ nɛ hyɛ e he womi ɔ he nɛ hiɔ ɔ ngɛ ɔ. Ke bwɔmi nɛ ngɛ lejɛ ɔ tsake pee futaa, nɛ lejɛ ɔ lo ɔ hu nɔ mi ɔ, lɛɛ e ji he womi nɔ hiɔ yaya. Ke osɔfo ɔ hyɛ lɛ ta a, e ma ha nɛ a le kaa nɔ ɔ he tsɔ we. 4Se ke he womi ɔ nɔ he nɛ hiɔ ɔ ngɛ ɔ ngɛ futaa, nɛ ke a hyɛ ɔ, e nɔɛ lo mi, nɛ pohu bwɔmi ɔ be futaa hulɔ ɔ, osɔfo ɔ nɛ tsi hiɔtsɛ ɔ nya ligbi kpaago. 5Ligbi kpaagone ɔ nɔ ɔ, osɔfo ɔ nɛ hyɛ lɛ ekohu. Ke osɔfo ɔ hyɛ nɛ e na kaa hiɔ ɔ hɛ́ si, se he kake ɔ kɛ̃ nɛ e ngɛ ɔ, e tsi e nya ligbi kpaago ekohu. 6Ligbi nɛ ji kpaago ɔ, e hyɛ lɛ ekohu. Ke e na kaa he nɛ hiɔ ɔ ngɛ ɔ yu, nɛ hiɔ ɔ hɛ́ si ngɛ hiɔtsɛ ɔ he womi nɔ ɔ, osɔfo ɔ nɛ ha nɛ a le kaa hiɔtsɛ ɔ he tsɔ; ejakaa e ji nɔfu nɔ́ kɛkɛ. Hiɔtsɛ ɔ nɛ fɔ e tade ɔmɛ a he, kɛkɛ e he ma tsɔ. 7Se ke osɔfo ɔ hyɛ lɛ nɛ e ha a le kaa e he tsɔ, nɛ pee se ɔ, nɔfu nɔ́ ɔ bɔni si hami ɔ, hiɔtsɛ ɔ nɛ ngɔ e he ba tsɔɔ osɔfo ɔ ekohu. 8Ke osɔfo ɔ hyɛ lɛ, nɛ e na kaa nɔfu nɔ́ ɔ ha si ɔ, e ha nɛ a le kaa e he tsɔ we; he womi nɔ hiɔ yaya e ngɛ nue ɔ nɛ.
9Ke nɔ ko ngɛ he womi nɔ hiɔ yaya nue ɔ, a ngɔ lɛ kɛ ba ha osɔfo ɔ, 10nɛ e hyɛ lɛ. Ke e na nɔfu nɔ́ ko ngɛ e he womi nɔ, nɛ bwɔmi nɛ ngɛ lejɛ ɔ pee futaa, nɛ bua ba nɔfu nɔ́ ɔ mi ɔ, 11lɛɛ he womi nɔ hiɔ yaya nɛ se kɛ nɔ ɔ ngɛ nue ɔ nɛ. Osɔfo ɔ nɛ ha nɛ a nu sisi kaa e he tsɔ we. A ko tsi e nya; ejakaa e fɔɔ si paa kaa e he tsɔ we. 12Ke osɔfo ɔ na kaa hiɔ ɔ je kpo ngɛ e he womi nɔ, nɛ e ha hiɔtsɛ ɔ he womi nɔ kulaa kɛ je e yi je kɛ ya pue e nanewɛɛ ɔ, 13e hyɛ lɛ ekohu. Ke e na nɔ́ ɔ kaa e ha e nɔmlɔ tso ɔ tsuo he ɔ, e ha nɛ hiɔtsɛ ɔ nɛ le kaa e he tsɔ. Ke e he womi ɔ tsuo pee futaa a, e he tsɔ ji lɔ ɔ nɛ. 14Se ke pa he je kpo ngɛ e he womi ɔ nɔ ɔ, lɛɛ e he tsɔ we. 15Osɔfo ɔ nɛ hyɛ nɔ ɔ pa he ɔ, e ha nɛ nɔ ɔ nɛ le kaa e he tsɔ we. Pa he ɔ nɛ je kpo ɔ tsɔɔ kaa he womi nɔ hiɔ yaya e ngɛ nue ɔ nɛ; nɔ ɔ he tsɔ we. 16Ke pa a gbo, nɛ e he womi lo ɔ pee futaa ekohu ɔ, hiɔtsɛ ɔ nɛ kpale ba na osɔfo ɔ. 17Osɔfo ɔ nɛ hyɛ lɛ ekohu. Ke e na kaa hiɔtsɛ ɔ he womi ɔ pee futaa a, e ha nɛ e le kaa e he tsɔ. E he tsɔ niinɛ.
18Ke tslɔɔ pa doku ngɛ nɔ ko he womi nɔ, 19nɛ nɔfu nɔ́ futaa, loo nɔ́ futaa nɛ tsutsuu su bɔɔ ngɛ mi je kpo ngɛ pa doku ɔ mi ɔ, e kɛ ya tsɔɔ osɔfo ɔ. 20Ke osɔfo ɔ hyɛ, nɛ e na kaa lejɛ ɔ nɔ lo mi, nɛ bwɔmi nɛ ngɛ lejɛ ɔ pee futaa a, e ha nɛ e le kaa e he tsɔ we; he womi nɔ hiɔ yaya nɛ́ je kpo ngɛ tslɔɔ mi nɔ ɔ ngɛ nue ɔ nɛ. 21Se ke osɔfo ɔ hyɛ lɛ, nɛ e na kaa bwɔmi nɛ ngɛ lejɛ ɔ pee we futaa, nɛ e nɔɛ lo mi hulɔ, se nɔ́ ɔ fani ɔ, lɛɛ e tsi hiɔtsɛ ɔ nya ligbi kpaago. 22Ke nɔfu nɔ́ ɔ ha si ngɛ e he womi ɔ nɔ ɔ, lɛɛ hiɔ ɔ e ngɛ nue ɔ nɛ; osɔfo ɔ nɛ ha nɛ e le kaa e he tsɔ we. 23Se ke nɔfu nɔ́ ɔ ngɛ he kake, nɛ e hɛ́ si ɔ, lɛɛ e ji tslɔɔ pa doku kɛkɛ; osɔfo ɔ nɛ ha nɛ nɔ ɔ nɛ le kaa e he tsɔ.
24Ke la sã nɔ ko nɛ e pee pa, nɛ pa a pee loholoho futaa, loo futaa nɛ tsutsuu bɔɔ ngɛ mi ɔ, 25osɔfo ɔ nɛ hyɛ lɛ. Ke e na kaa lejɛ ɔ nɔ lo mi, nɛ bwɔmi nɛ ngɛ loholoho ɔ mi ɔ pee futaa a, lɛɛ he womi nɔ hiɔ yaya lɛ je e he kpo ngɛ la pa a mi ɔ nɛ; osɔfo ɔ nɛ ha nɛ e le kaa e he tsɔ we. 26Ke osɔfo ɔ hyɛ nɔ ɔ, nɛ e na kaa bwɔmi nɛ ngɛ lejɛ ɔ pee we futaa, nɛ lejɛ ɔ nɔɛ lo mi hulɔ, se e fani ɔ, osɔfo ɔ nɛ tsi e nya ligbi kpaago. 27Osɔfo ɔ nɛ hyɛ lɛ ekohu ligbi kpaagone ɔ, nɛ ke e na kaa nɔ́ ɔ ngɛ si hae ngɛ e he womi ɔ nɔ ɔ, lɛɛ e ha nɛ e le kaa e he tsɔ we; ejakaa he womi nɔ hiɔ yaya e ngɛ nue ɔ nɛ. 28Ke nɔ́ ɔ ngɛ he kake, nɛ e hɛ́ si ngɛ e he womi ɔ nɔ, se e fani mohu ɔ, lɛɛ nɔfu nɔ́ nɛ je kpo ngɛ pa a mi ji lɔ ɔ nɛ. Osɔfo ɔ nɛ ha nɛ e le kaa e he tsɔ, ejakaa e ji la pa doku kɛkɛ.
29Ke nɔ́ ko pue nyumu ko, loo yo ko yi mi, loo e kpɛni he ɔ, 30osɔfo ɔ nɛ hyɛ. Ke he nɛ hiɔ ɔ ngɛ ɔ nɔ lo mi, nɛ bwɔmi nɛ ngɛ lejɛ ɔ hɛɛ kungwɔ zɔ su, nɛ e pee dleledlele ɔ, osɔfo ɔ nɛ ha nɛ e le kaa yi mi, loo kpɛni mi he womi nɔ hiɔ yaya nɛ plɛɛ nɔ e ngɛ nue ɔ nɛ; e he tsɔ we. 31Se ke osɔfo ɔ hyɛ hiɔ ɔ, nɛ e na kaa lejɛ ɔ nɔɛ lo mi, nɛ bwɔmi yumu hu be mi ɔ, lɛɛ osɔfo ɔ nɛ tsi hiɔtsɛ ɔ nya ligbi kpaago. 32Ligbi nɛ ji kpaago ɔ, e hyɛ hiɔtsɛ ɔ ekohu. Ke hiɔ ɔ hɛ́ si, nɛ bwɔmi nɛ hɛɛ kungwɔ zɔ su be mi, nɛ lejɛ ɔ hu nɔɛ lo mi ɔ, 33lɛɛ hiɔtsɛ ɔ nɛ sɛ lejɛ ɔ bwɔmi ɔ pɛ kɛ bɔle nɔ́ ɔ nɛ ngɛ lɛ plɛe ɔ. Osɔfo ɔ nɛ tsi hiɔtsɛ ɔ nya ligbi kpaago ekohu. 34Ligbi nɛ ji kpaago ɔ, osɔfo ɔ nɛ hyɛ hiɔ ɔ ekohu. Ke hiɔ ɔ hɛ́ si, nɛ e nɔɛ lo mi hulɔ ɔ, osɔfo ɔ nɛ ha nɛ hiɔtsɛ ɔ nɛ le kaa e he tsɔ. Hiɔtsɛ ɔ nɛ fɔ e tade ɔmɛ a he, kɛkɛ ɔ, e he ma tsɔ. 35Ke benɛ a ha nɛ e le kaa e he tsɔ se nɛ hiɔ ɔ bɔni si hami ɔ, 36osɔfo ɔ nɛ hyɛ lɛ ekohu. Ke e na kaa hiɔ ɔ ha si ɔ, osɔfo ɔ ko hao e he kaa e ma pa hla bwɔmi nɛ hɛɛ kungwɔ zɔ su nɛ e na; e fɔɔ si paa kaa hiɔtsɛ ɔ he tsɔ we. 37Se ke osɔfo ɔ ma nɔ mi kaa hiɔ ɔ ta, nɛ bwɔmi yumu puɛ ngɛ mi ɔ, lɛɛ hiɔ ɔ jɔ niinɛ, nɛ hiɔtsɛ ɔ he tsɔ. Osɔfo ɔ nɛ ha nɛ hiɔtsɛ ɔ nɛ le kaa e he tsɔ.
38Ke ngmo pue nyumu ko, loo yo ko he, nɛ e he womi ɔ pee huataa a, 39osɔfo ɔ nɛ hyɛ lɛ. Ke ngmo ɔ su ngɛ kaa la zu huataa a, lɛɛ e ji kó kɛkɛ nɛ je kpo ngɛ e he womi nɔ; nɔ ɔ he tsɔ.
40Ke bwɔmi ta nyumu yi mi ɔ, e yi mi kɛkɛ lɛ kpa; se e he tsɔ. 41Ke bwɔmi ta nyumu hɛ nya a, e hɛ nya kɛkɛ lɛ kpa; se e he tsɔ. Ke nɔ́ ɔ tsuɔ, loo e hɛɛ ba mumu su ɔ, lɛɛ he womi nɔ hiɔ yaya lɛ pue e yi ɔ he nɛ kpa a nɛ. 42Se ke nɔ́ ko futaa nɛ tsutsuu bɔɔ fia mi pue nɔ ɔ yi mi, loo e hɛ nya he nɛ kpa a, lɛɛ he womi nɔ hiɔ yaya lɛ je kpo ngɛ e yi ɔ mi, kɛ e hɛ nya he nɛ kpa a nɛ. 43Osɔfo ɔ nɛ hyɛ lɛ. Ke e na kaa nɔ́ nɛ pue nɔ ɔ yi mi, loo e hɛ nya a ngɛ futaa nɛ tsutsuu bɔɔ fia mi ɔ, 44osɔfo ɔ nɛ ha nɛ e le kaa e he tsɔ we; ejakaa he womi nɔ hiɔ yaya lɛ ngɛ e yi mi ɔ nɛ.
45Ke nɔ ko ngɛ he womi nɔ hiɔ yaya nue ɔ, é wo tade gbagbɛ, é ngmɛɛ e yi bwɔmi he kɛ pue e nɔ, e ha e nya nɔ, nɛ e hi ngmlaa kpae ke, “Ye he tsɔ we oo, ye he tsɔ we!” 46E he be tsɔe kɛ yaa si be nɛ e hiɔ ɔ maa ta; nɛ lɛ nɔ kake nɛ e maa hi si ngɛ ma sito he ɔ se.
Mlaahi nɛ kɔɔ nɔ́ nɛ fu ja he
47Ke he hami nɔ́ ko fu ja a, kuutu jio, kploba jio, 48bo nɛ a kɛ kuutu kpa, loo kploba kpa lo jio, lohwe he womi, loo nɔ́ ko nɛ a kɛ lohwe he womi pee jio, 49ke nɔ́ fu ja a tsuɔ, loo e hɛɛ ba mumu su ɔ, e maa pee kaa nɔ́ yaya lɛ ngɛ ja fue ngɛ he hami nɔ́ ɔ mi ɔ nɛ; a ngɔ kɛ ya tsɔɔ osɔfo ɔ. 50Osɔfo ɔ nɛ hyɛ nɔ́ ɔ, nɛ e tsi heha nɔ́ ɔ nya ligbi kpaago. 51Ligbi kpaagone ɔ, osɔfo ɔ nɛ hyɛ nɔ́ ɔ ekohu. Ke nɔ́ fu ja a ha si ngɛ he hami nɔ́ ɔ mi ɔ lɛɛ e ji nɔ fu ja yaya, e he tsɔ we. 52Osɔfo ɔ nɛ sã he hami nɔ́ ɔ. Hiɔ yaya ji nɔ́ nɛ sɛ nɔ́ ɔ mi ɔ nɛ; e hia kaa a sã.
53Se ke osɔfo ɔ hyɛ nɔ́ ɔ, nɛ e na kaa nɔ́ fu ja a hɛ́ si ngɛ he hami nɔ́ ɔ mi ɔ, 54e ha nɛ a fɔ he, nɛ e tsi nya ligbi kpaago ekohu. 55Osɔfo ɔ nɛ hyɛ nɔ́ ɔ; ke nɔ́ fu ja a su tsakee we, nɛ e hɛ́ si hulɔ ɔ, nɔ́ ɔ he tsɔ we; nyɛɛ sã. Nɔ́ ɔ hɛ mi nɛ fu ja a jio, e se mi jio, á sã.
56Se ke a fɔ nɔ́ ɔ he se, nɛ osɔfo ɔ hyɛ ekohu nɛ e na kaa nɔ́ nɛ sɛ mi ɔ ngɛ laae ɔ, e hia he nɛ fu ja a kɛ je nɔ́ ɔ he, he hami nɔ́ jio, lohwe he womi jio. 57Jehanɛ, ke nɔtsɛ ɔ na kaa nɔ́ ɔ ngɛ ja fue kɛ ngɛ si hae ngɛ he hami nɔ́, loo lohwe he womi ɔ mi kɛ mwɔɔ ɔ, a sã nɔ́ ɔ. 58Ke e fɔ nɔ́ ɔ he, nɛ e na kaa nɔ́ yaya a je mi pɛsɛɛ ɔ, e fɔ he ekohu si enyɔne, kɛkɛ ɔ, nɔ́ ɔ he ma tsɔ kulaa.
59Mlaa nɛ ɔ ngɛ kɛ ha nɔ́ fu ja ngɛ he hami ní nɛ ɔmɛ a mi: he hami nɔ́ nɛ a kɛ kuutu, loo kploba pee jio, bo nɛ a kɛ kuutu, loo kploba kpa lo jio, lohwe he womi, loo nɔ́ ko nɛ a kɛ lohwe he womi pee jio. Enɛ ɔ nɛ maa tsɔɔ kaa nɔ́ ɔ he tsɔ, loo e he tsɔ we.

english_text:
The Ceremony for People Healed of Leprosy
1The Lord told Moses to say to the people:
2-3 After you think you are healed of leprosy, you must ask for a priest to come outside the camp and examine you. And if you are well, 4he will order someone to bring out two live birds that are acceptable for sacrifice, together with a stick of cedar wood, a piece of red yarn, and a branch from a hyssop plant. 5The priest will order someone to kill one of the birds over a clay pot of spring water. 6Then he will dip the other bird, the cedar, the red yarn, and the hyssop in the blood of the dead bird. 7Next, he will sprinkle you seven times with the blood and say, “You are now clean.” Finally, he will release the bird and let it fly away.
8After this you must wash your clothes, shave your entire body, and take a bath before you are completely clean. You may move back into camp, but you must not enter your tent for seven days. 9Then you must once again shave your head, face, and eyebrows, as well as the hair on the rest of your body. Finally, wash your clothes and take a bath, and you will be completely clean.
10On the eighth day you must bring to the priest two rams and a year-old female lamb that have nothing wrong with them; also bring 300 milliliters of olive oil and 3 kilograms of your finest flour mixed with oil. 11Then the priest will present you and your offerings to me at the entrance to my sacred tent. 12There he will offer one of the rams, together with the oil, as a sacrifice to make things right. He will also lift them up to show that they are dedicated to me. 13This sacrifice is very holy. It belongs to the priest and must be killed in the same place where animals are killed as sacrifices for sins and as sacrifices to please me.
14The priest will smear some of the blood from this sacrifice on your right ear lobe, some on your right thumb, and some on the big toe of your right foot. 15He will then pour some of the olive oil into the palm of his left hand, 16dip a finger of his right hand into the oil, and sprinkle some of it seven times toward the sacred tent. 17Next, the priest will smear some of the oil on your right ear lobe, some on your right thumb, and some on the big toe of your right foot, 18-20and he will pour the rest of the oil from his palm on your head. Then he will offer the other two animals—one as a sacrifice for sin and the other as a sacrifice to please me, together with a grain sacrifice. After this you will be completely clean.
21If you are poor and cannot afford to offer this much, you may offer a ram as a sacrifice to make things right, together with 300 milliliters of olive oil and one kilogram of flour mixed with oil as a grain sacrifice. The priest will then lift these up to dedicate them to me. 22Depending on what you can afford, you must also offer either two doves or two pigeons, one as a sacrifice for sin and the other as a sacrifice to please me. 23The priest will offer these to me in front of the sacred tent on the eighth day.
24-25The priest will kill this ram for the sacrifice to make things right, and he will lift it up with the olive oil in dedication to me. Then he will smear some of the blood on your right ear lobe, some on your right thumb, and some on the big toe of your right foot.
26The priest will pour some of the olive oil into the palm of his left hand, 27then dip a finger of his right hand in the oil and sprinkle some of it seven times toward the sacred tent. 28He will smear some of the oil on your right ear lobe, some on your right thumb, and some on the big toe of your right foot, just as he did with the blood of the sacrifice to make things right. 29-31And he will pour the rest of the oil from his palm on your head.
Then, depending on what you can afford, he will offer either the doves or the pigeons together with the grain sacrifice. One of the birds is the sacrifice for sin, and the other is the sacrifice to please me. After this you will be completely clean.
32These are the things you must do if you have leprosy and cannot afford the usual sacrifices to make you clean.
When There Is Mildew in a House
33The Lord told Moses and Aaron to say to the people:
34After I have given you the land of Canaan as your permanent possession, here is what you must do, if I ever put mildew on the walls of any of your homes. 35First, you must say to a priest, “I think there is mildew on the wall of my house.”
36The priest will reply, “Empty the house before I inspect it, or else everything in it will be unclean.”
37If the priest discovers greenish or reddish spots that go deeper than the surface of the walls, 38he will have the house closed for seven days. 39Then he will return and check to see if the mildew has spread. 40-41If so, he will order someone to scrape the plaster from the walls, remove the stones covered with mildew, then haul everything off and dump it in an unclean place outside the town. 42Afterwards the wall must be repaired with new stones and fresh plaster.
43If the mildew appears a second time, 44the priest will come and say, “This house is unclean. It's covered with mildew that can't be removed.” 45Then he will have the house torn down and every bit of wood, stone, and plaster hauled off to an unclean place outside the town. 46Meanwhile, if any of you entered the house while it was closed, you will be unclean until evening. 47And if you either slept or ate in the house, you must wash your clothes.
48On the other hand, if the priest discovers that mildew hasn't reappeared after the house was newly plastered, he will say, “This house is clean—the mildew has gone.” 49Then, to show that the house is now clean, he will get two birds, a stick of cedar wood, a piece of red yarn, and a branch from a hyssop plant and bring them to the house. 50He will kill one of the birds over a clay pot of spring water 51-52and let its blood drain into the pot. Then he will dip the cedar, the hyssop, the yarn, and the other bird into the mixture of blood and water. Next, he will sprinkle the house seven times with the mixture, then the house will be completely clean. 53Finally, he will release the bird and let it fly away, ending the ceremony for purifying the house.
54-57These are the things you must do if you discover that you are unclean because of an itch or a sore, or that your clothing or house is unclean because of mildew.
translation_text:
He womi nɔ hiɔ yaya numi se he tsukɔmi
1-2 Yawɛ wo Mose mlaa nɛ ɔmɛ nɛ tsɔɔ kusumi nɛ a pee kɛ tsukɔ nɔ ko nɛ nu he womi nɔ hiɔ yaya nɛ a tsa lɛ ɔ he. Ligbi nɛ a ma ha nɛ e le kaa e he tsɔ ɔ, a kɛ lɛ nɛ ba osɔfo ɔ ngɔ. 3Osɔfo ɔ nɛ ngɔ lɛ kɛ je ma sito he ɔ, nɛ e ya hyɛ lɛ. Ke e na kaa hiɔ ɔ ta ngɛ nɔ ɔ he ɔ, 4e fa nɛ a kɛ lohwe pɛlitsɛmɛ nɛ a he tsɔ enyɔ, seda tso, kɔjai, kɛ nga nɛ a fi kɛ bla kaa bɛ nɛ ba. 5Osɔfo ɔ nɛ fa nɛ a gbe lohwe pɛlitsɛ ɔ kake ngɛ zu buɛ nɛ nyu mua ngɛ mi nɔ, 6konɛ e ngɔ lohwe pɛlitsɛ hɛngmengmletsɛ ɔ, seda tso ɔ, kɔjai ɔ, kɛ nga nɛ a fi kɛ bla kaa bɛ ɔ, nɛ e kɛ sɔ lohwe pɛlitsɛ nɛ a gbe ɔ ngɛ nyu mua nɔ ɔ muɔ ɔ mi. 7Jehanɛ, é fĩa muɔ ɔ si kpaago kɛ pue nɔ nɛ nu he womi nɔ hiɔ yaya nɛ ma e he tsukɔmi ɔ nɔ, nɛ é ha nɛ e le kaa e he tsɔ. Lɔ ɔ se ɔ, é ngmɛɛ lohwe hɛngmengmletsɛ ɔ he nɛ é te kɛ ho nga mi ya. 8Enɛ ɔ se ɔ, nɔ nɛ ma e he tsukɔmi ɔ nɛ fɔ e tade ɔmɛ a he, nɛ é sɛ e he bwɔmi tsuo, nɛ é du e he; kɛkɛ e he ma tsɔ. E ma nyɛ maa ba ma sito he ɔ, se e be e bo tsu ɔ mi hwɔe; e maa hi e bo tsu ɔ se ligbi kpaago. 9Ligbi kpaagone ɔ, nɔ ɔ nɛ sɛ e yi kpalokpalo; é sɛ e kpɛni kɛ e hɛngmɛ se bwɔmi, kɛ e he bwɔmi tsuo kulaa. Enɛ ɔ se ɔ, é fɔ e tade ɔmɛ a he, nɛ é du e he, kɛkɛ e he ma tsɔ.
10Ligbi nɛ ji kpaanyɔ ɔ, é ngɔ agbosu enyɔ nɛ kpa ko be a he, kɛ jijɔ yo nɛ ye jeha kake, nɛ lɛ hu kpa ko be e he, kɛ níye ní bɔ mamu bukɔbukɔ kilo etɛ nɛ a kɛ nu futu mi, kɛ nu lita fa kɛ ba. 11Osɔfo ɔ nɛ maa tsukɔ nɔ ɔ he ha lɛ ɔ nɛ ngɔ lɛ, kɛ e ní ɔmɛ tsuo kɛ ba Yawɛ hɛ mi ngɛ kpe he bo tsu ɔ sinya a nya. 12Osɔfo ɔ nɛ ngɔ agbosu enyɔ ɔmɛ a ti kake kɛ piɛ nu lita fa a he kɛ ba kaa fɔ yemi bɔ, nɛ e ngɔ mɛ kɛ ba kaa bɔ nɛ a fɔɔ kɛ yaa kɛ baa ngɛ Yawɛ hɛ mi. 13É gbe agbosu ɔ ngɛ he klɔuklɔu ɔ, he nɛ a gbee lohwe nɛ a kɛ sãã yayami pami bɔ, kɛ sami bɔ ngɛ ɔ. Ejakaa yayami pami bɔ ɔ, osɔfo ɔmɛ a nɔ́ kaa bɔ nɛ fɔ yemi bɔ ɔ ngɛ ɔ; e ngɛ klɔuklɔu saminya. 14Osɔfo ɔ nɛ ngɔ lohwe nɛ a kɛ ba sã fɔ yemi bɔ ɔ e muɔ eko kɛ kpa nɔ nɛ ma e he tsukɔmi ɔ hiɔ nɔ tue nya lo, kɛ e hiɔ nine nguɛ gɔleku, kɛ e hiɔ nane nguɛ gɔleku he. 15Jehanɛ, osɔfo ɔ nɛ plɛ nu ɔ eko kɛ wo lɛ nitsɛ e muɔ dɛ kɔkɔ mi. 16É kɛ e hiɔ nine nguɛ kake nɛ sɔ nu ɔ mi, nɛ é fĩa si kpaago ngɛ Yawɛ hɛ mi. 17É ngɔ nu ɔ nɛ ngɛ e dɛ mi ɔ eko nɛ e kɛ kpa nɔ nɛ ma e he tsukɔmi ɔ hiɔ nɔ tue nya lo, hiɔ nine nguɛ gɔleku, kɛ e hiɔ nane nguɛ gɔleku he. E ngɔ lohwe ɔ nɛ a kɛ ba sã fɔ yemi bɔ ɔ hu muɔ kɛ pee ja nɔuu. 18Nu ɔ nɛ maa piɛ ngɛ osɔfo ɔ dɛ mi ɔ, e kɛ pue nɔ nɛ ma e he tsukɔmi ɔ yi mi. Ke nɔ ko nu he womi nɔ hiɔ yaya a, kusumi nɛ osɔfo ɔ maa pee kɛ kpata Yawɛ ha lɛ ji nɛ ɔ nɛ.
19Jehanɛ, osɔfo ɔ nɛ sã yayami pami bɔ kɛ kpata Yawɛ ha nɔ nɛ ma e he tsukɔmi ɔ. Lɔ ɔ se ɔ, é gbe lohwe ɔ nɛ a kɛ maa sã sami bɔ ɔ. 20Osɔfo ɔ nɛ ngɔ sami bɔ ɔ, kɛ niye ní bɔ ɔ, nɛ e sã mɛ ngɛ bɔ sami la tɛ ɔ nɔ. Kusumi nɛ osɔfo ɔ maa pee kɛ kpata Yawɛ ha lɛ ji nɛ ɔ nɛ, kɛkɛ ɔ, e he ma tsɔ.
21Ke ohiatsɛ ji nɔ ɔ, nɛ e be ní ɔmɛ tsuo nyɛe ma ha a, e ngɔ agbosu kake pɛ kɛ pee fɔ yemi bɔ, nɛ a fɔ kɛ ya kɛ ba ngɛ Yawɛ hɛ mi. Níhi nɛ e ngɔ kɛ piɛ he ji mamu bukɔbukɔ kilo kake, nɛ a kɛ nu futu mi ha niye ní bɔ, nu tɔ kake, 22kɛ lahuɛ enyɔ, aloo beleku lahuɛ enyɔ. Kake maa pee yayami pami bɔ, nɛ kake hu maa pee sami bɔ. 23E he tsukɔmi be ɔ, ligbi kpaanyɔne ɔ nɔ ɔ, e ngɔ ní nɛ ɔmɛ kɛ ba ha osɔfo ɔ ngɛ Yawɛ hɛ mi ngɛ kpe he bo tsu ɔ sinya a nya. 24Osɔfo ɔ nɛ ngɔ agbosu ɔ nɛ a kɛ maa sã fɔ yemi bɔ ɔ, kɛ nu ɔ kɛ ba kaa bɔ nɛ a fɔɔ kɛ yaa kɛ baa ngɛ Yawɛ hɛ mi. 25Jehanɛ, é gbe agbosu ɔ, nɛ é ngɔ e muɔ ɔ eko kɛ kpa nɔ nɛ ma e he tsukɔmi ɔ hiɔ nɔ tue nya lo, kɛ e hiɔ nine nguɛ gɔleku, kɛ e hiɔ nane nguɛ gɔleku he. 26Enɛ ɔ se ɔ, osɔfo ɔ nɛ plɛ nu ɔ eko kɛ wo lɛ nitsɛ e muɔ nine dɛ kɔkɔ mi, 27nɛ e ngɔ e hiɔ nine nguɛ kake kɛ sɔ nu ɔ mi nɛ e fĩa si kpaago ngɛ Yawɛ hɛ mi. 28Osɔfo ɔ nɛ ngɔ nu nɛ ngɛ e dɛ mi ɔ eko kɛ kpa nɔ nɛ ma e he tsukɔmi ɔ hiɔ nɔ tue nya lo, e hiɔ nine nguɛ gɔleku, kɛ e hiɔ nane nguɛ gɔleku ɔmɛ a he kaa bɔ nɛ e kɛ muɔ ɔ pee ɔ. 29Nu nɛ maa piɛ ngɛ osɔfo ɔ dɛ mi ɔ, e kɛ pue nɔ ɔ nɛ a ngɛ e he tsukɔe ɔ yi mi. Kusumi nɛ osɔfo ɔ maa pee kɛ kpata Yawɛ ha lɛ ji nɛ ɔ nɛ. 30Jehanɛ e ngɔ lahuɛ ɔ kake, loo beleku lahuɛ ɔ kake 31kɛ ba sã yayami pami bɔ, nɛ a kɛ kake ɔ hu nɛ sã sami bɔ kɛ piɛ niye ní bɔ ɔ he. Kusumi nɛ osɔfo ɔ maa pee kɛ kpata Yawɛ ha nɔ nɛ ma e he tsukɔmi ɔ ji nɛ ɔ nɛ. 32Nɔ nɛ ngɛ he womi nɔ hiɔ yaya nue, nɛ be nyɛe ma ha ní ɔmɛ tsuo nɛ a kɛ maa pee kusumi kɛ tsukɔ e he ɔ, mlaa nɛ fɔɔ si ha lɛ ji nɛ ɔ nɛ.
Wehi nɛ a he fu ja
33Yawɛ ha Mose kɛ Aaron 34mlaa nɛ ɔmɛ nɛ kɔɔ wehi nɛ a he fu ja a he. Ke Israel bi ɔmɛ ya su zugba a nɛ Yawɛ ngɔ ha mɛ kaa a weto ní ɔ nɔ ɔ, mlaa nɛ sa kaa a ye nɔ ji nɛ ɔ nɛ. 35Nɔ tsuaa nɔ nɛ maa na nɔ́ ko nɛ fu ja ngɛ e we he ɔ, e ha nɛ osɔfo nɛ le. 36Osɔfo ɔ nɛ fa nɛ a je nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ kpo, loko e ya hyɛ he nɛ fu ja a, bɔ nɛ pee nɛ a ko bu nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ ngɛ we ɔ mi ɔ kaa e he tsɔ we. Ke a je ní ɔmɛ kpo ta a, osɔfo ɔ nɛ ya we ɔ mi 37nɛ e ya hyɛ he nɛ fu ja a. Ke e na nɔ́ tsu, loo nɔ́ nɛ hɛɛ ba mumu su nɛ ha si ngɛ gli ɔ he ɔ, 38osɔfo ɔ nɛ je lejɛ ɔ, nɛ e ha nɛ a nga we ɔ nya ligbi kpaago. 39Ligbi kpaagone ɔ, osɔfo ɔ nɛ kpale ya hyɛ ekohu. Ke e na kaa nɔ́ ɔ ha si ngɛ gli ɔ he ɔ, 40e fa nɛ a je tɛhi nɛ nɔ́ ɔ ngɛ a he ɔ kɛ je gli ɔ mi, nɛ a ya sake mɛ ngɔ pue kuku nɔ ngɛ ma a se. 41Lɔ ɔ se ɔ, osɔfo ɔ nɛ ha nɛ a ngmla gli ɔ tsuo he ngɛ tsu ɔmɛ a mi, nɛ a bua zu ɔ nya kɛ ya pue he ngɛ kuku nɔ ngɛ ma a se. 42Jehanɛ, á ngɔ tɛ kpahi kɛ tsi puɔ ɔmɛ, nɛ́ a ngɔ zu kpa kɛ kã gli ɔmɛ a he.
43Se ke a tsake tɛ ɔmɛ, nɛ a ngmla gli ɔ he, nɛ a kpale kã gli ɔmɛ a he, nɛ lɔ ɔ se a na kaa lejɛ ɔ fu ja ekohu ɔ, 44osɔfo ɔ nɛ kpale ya hyɛ ekohu. Ke e na kaa nɔ́ ɔ ha si ngɛ gli ɔ he ɔ, lɛɛ e ji nɔ́ yaya nɛ maa ye awi; we ɔ he tsɔ we. 45Osɔfo ɔ nɛ ha nɛ a ku we ɔ kɛ pue si nɛ a muɔ tɛ ɔmɛ, tso ɔmɛ, kɛ zu ɔ kɛ je ma a mi kɛ ya pue kuku nɔ. 46Nɔ tsuaa nɔ nɛ maa sɛ we ɔ mi, be mi nɛ a nga we ɔ nya a, e he be tsɔe kɛ yaa si du ma bu. 47Nɔ tsuaa nɔ nɛ maa hwɔ we ɔ mi, loo e maa ye ní ngɛ we ɔ mi ɔ, é fɔ e tade ɔmɛ a he.
48Se ke a kɛ zu kpa kã gli ɔ he, nɛ lɔ ɔ se osɔfo ɔ ba hyɛ, nɛ e nɛ nɔ́ ko ngɛ he ɔ, e ha nɛ a le kaa we ɔ he tsɔ; ejakaa a je nɔ́ nɛ fu ja a tsuo kɛ je gli ɔ mi. 49Osɔfo ɔ nɛ ngɔ lohwe pɛlitsɛ enyɔ, seda tso, kɔjai, kɛ nga nɛ a fi kɛ bla kaa bɛ kɛ ba, konɛ a kɛ julaa we ɔ. 50É gbe lohwe pɛlitsɛ ɔmɛ a ti kake ngɛ zu buɛ nɛ nyu mua ngɛ mi nɔ. 51Jehanɛ, é ngɔ seda tso ɔ, nga nɛ a fi kɛ bla kaa bɛ ɔ, kɔjai ɔ, kɛ lohwe pɛlitsɛ hɛngmengmletsɛ ɔ, nɛ e kɛ sɔ lohwe pɛlitsɛ nɛ a gbe ɔ muɔ ɔ, kɛ nyu mua a mi, nɛ e kɛ fĩa we ɔ he si kpaago. 52Bɔ nɛ e kɛ lohwe pɛlitsɛ ɔ muɔ, nyu mua a, lohwe pɛlitsɛ hɛngmengmletsɛ ɔ, seda tso ɔ, nga nɛ a fi kɛ bla kaa bɛ ɔ, kɛ kɔjai ɔ maa julaa we ɔ ji nɛ ɔ nɛ. 53Lɔ ɔ se ɔ, osɔfo ɔ nɛ ngmɛɛ lohwe pɛlitsɛ hɛngmengmletsɛ ɔ he nɛ e te kɛ ya nga mi. Kusumi nɛ e maa pee kɛ julaa we ɔ ji nɛ ɔ nɛ. Kɛkɛ ɔ, we ɔ he ma tsɔ.
54Mlaa nɛ ɔmɛ ngɛ kɛ ha he womi nɔ hiɔ yaya, 55-56sakpa, loo nɔfu nɔ́, loo tslɔɔ, he hami nɔ́ nɛ fu ja, loo we nɛ hiɔ yaya nɛ ɔ sɛ gli ɔ mi. 57Mlaa nɛ ɔmɛ tsɔɔ be mi nɛ nɔ́ ko he tsɔ we kɛ be mi nɛ nɔ́ ɔ he tsɔ.

english_text:
Sexual Uncleanness
1The Lord told Moses and Aaron 2to say to the community of Israel:
Any man with an infected penis is unclean, 3whether it is stopped up or keeps dripping. 4Anything that he rests on or sits on is also unclean, 5-7and if you touch either these or him, you must wash your clothes and take a bath, but you still remain unclean until evening.
8If you are spit on by the man, you must wash your clothes and take a bath, but you still remain unclean until evening. 9-10Any saddle or seat on which the man sits is unclean. And if you touch or carry either of these, you must wash your clothes and take a bath, but you still remain unclean until evening. 11If the man touches you without first washing his hands, you must wash your clothes and take a bath, but you still remain unclean until evening. 12Any clay pot that he touches must be destroyed, and any wooden bowl that he touches must be washed.
13Seven days after the man gets well, he will be considered clean, if he washes his clothes and takes a bath in spring water. 14On the eighth day he must bring either two doves or two pigeons to the front of my sacred tent and give them to a priest. 15The priest will offer one of the birds as a sacrifice for sin and the other as a sacrifice to please me, then I will consider the man completely clean.
16Any man who has a flow of semen must take a bath, but he still remains unclean until evening. 17If the semen touches anything made of cloth or leather, these must be washed, but they still remain unclean until evening. 18After having sex, both the man and the woman must take a bath, but they still remain unclean until evening.
19When a woman has her monthly period, she remains unclean for seven days, and if you touch her, you must take a bath, but you remain unclean until evening. 20-23Anything that she rests on or sits on is also unclean, and if you touch either of these, you must wash your clothes and take a bath, but you still remain unclean until evening. 24Any man who has sex with her during this time becomes unclean for seven days, and anything he rests on is also unclean.
25Any woman who has a flow of blood outside her regular monthly period is unclean until it stops, just as she is during her monthly period. 26Anything that she rests on or sits on during this time is also unclean, just as it would be during her period. 27If you touch either of these, you must wash your clothes and take a bath, but you still remain unclean until evening.
28Seven days after the woman gets well, she will be considered clean. 29On the eighth day, she must bring either two doves or two pigeons to the front of my sacred tent and give them to a priest. 30He will offer one of the birds as a sacrifice for sin and the other as a sacrifice to please me; then I will consider the woman completely clean.
31When any of you are unclean, you must stay away from the rest of the community of Israel. Otherwise, my sacred tent will become unclean, and the whole nation will die.
32-33These are the things you men must do if you become unclean because of an infected penis or if you have a flow of semen. And these are the things you women must do when you become unclean either because of your monthly period or an unusual flow of blood. This is also what you men must do if you have sex with a woman who is unclean.
translation_text:
Nyu yaya nɛ bee ngɛ nɔmlɔ he
1Mlaahi nɛ Yawɛ wo Mose kɛ Aaron 2kɛ ha Israel bi ɔmɛ ji nɛ ɔmɛ nɛ. Ke nyu ngɛ bee ngɛ nyumu ko he ɔ, nyu ɔ nɛ ngɛ bee ɔ ha nyumu ɔ he tsɔ we. 3Ke nyu yaya a ngɛ bee jio, e ha e nyumu tso mi tsi jio, nɔ ɔ he tsɔ we. 4Sa tsuaa sa nɛ nyumu nɛ nyu yaya ngɛ bee ngɛ e he ɔ maa hwɔ nɔ, loo nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ e maa hi nɔ ɔ, nɔ́ ɔ he tsɔ we. 5Nɔ tsuaa nɔ nɛ maa ta sa a he ɔ, é fɔ e tade ɔmɛ a he, nɛ e du e he. E he be tsɔe kɛ yaa si du ma bu. 6Nɔ tsuaa nɔ nɛ maa hi nɔ́ ko nɛ nɔ nɛ nyu yaya ngɛ bee ngɛ e he ɔ hi nɔ ɔ nɔ ɔ, é fɔ e tade ɔmɛ a he, nɛ é du e he. E he be tsɔe kɛ yaa si du ma bu. 7Nɔ tsuaa nɔ nɛ maa ta nɔ nɛ nyu ngɛ bee ngɛ e nyumu tso mi ɔ he ɔ, é fɔ e tade ɔmɛ a he, nɛ e du e he. E he be tsɔe kɛ yaa si du ma bu. 8Ke nɔ nɛ nyu ngɛ bee ngɛ e he ɔ la lada pue nɔ ko nɛ he tsɔ nɔ ɔ, nɔ ɔ nɛ fɔ e tade ɔmɛ a he, nɛ e du e he. E he tsɔ we kɛ yaa si du ma bu. 9Lohwe se mi sɛ nɛ nɔ nɛ nyu yaya ngɛ bee ngɛ e he ɔ maa hi nɔ ɔ he be tsɔe. 10Nɔ tsuaa nɔ nɛ maa ta nɔ́ ko nɛ nɔ ɔ hi nɔ he ɔ, e he be tsɔe kɛ yaa si du ma bu, nɛ nɔ tsuaa nɔ nɛ maa tloo jamɛ a nɔ́ ɔ, é fɔ e tade ɔmɛ a he, nɛ e du e he. E he be tsɔe kɛ yaa si du ma bu. 11Ke nyu yaya ngɛ bee ngɛ nɔ ko he, nɛ e fɔ we e dɛ, nɛ e ta nɔ ko he ɔ, nɔ ɔ nɛ e ta e he ɔ nɛ fɔ e tade ɔmɛ a he, nɛ e du e he. E he be tsɔe kɛ yaa si du ma bu. 12Zu buɛ saisaa nɛ nɔ nɛ nyu ngɛ bee ngɛ e he ɔ maa ta he ɔ, a ywia lɛ, se tso sowe nɛ e maa ta he lɛɛ a fɔ he.
13Ke nɔ nɛ nyu yaya ngɛ bee ngɛ e he ɔ hiɔ ɔ ta a, e mlɛ ligbi kpaago loko e tsukɔ e he, nɛ e fɔ e tade ɔmɛ a he. Lɔ ɔ se ɔ, e ya du e he ngɛ pa mi, kɛkɛ e he ma tsɔ. 14Ligbi nɛ ji kpaanyɔ ɔ, e ngɔ lahuɛ enyɔ, loo beleku lahuɛ enyɔ kɛ ba Yawɛ hɛ mi ngɛ kpe he bo tsu ɔ sinya a nya, nɛ e ngɔ mɛ kɛ ha osɔfo ɔ. 15Osɔfo ɔ maa ngɔ kake kɛ sã yayami pami bɔ, nɛ e maa ngɔ kake hu kɛ sã sami bɔ kɛ kpata Yawɛ ha lɛ ngɛ nyu yaya nɛ be ngɛ e he ɔ he. 16Ke nyumu ko he nyu be ngɛ e he ɔ, e du e nɔmlɔ tso ɔ kulaa he. E he be tsɔe kɛ yaa si du ma bu. 17Sa nɔ bo, loo nɔ́ ko nɛ a kɛ lohwe he womi pee, nɛ nyumu ɔ he nyu nɛ ɔ ma pue nɔ ɔ, á fɔ he. E he be tsɔe kɛ yaa si du ma bu. 18Ke nyumu kɛ yo na bɔmi nɛ nyumu ɔ he nyu be ɔ, mɛ ni enyɔ ɔmɛ tsuo a du a he. A he be tsɔe kɛ yaa si du ma bu.
19Ke yo ko ku nine ɔ, e he be tsɔe ligbi kpaago; nɛ nɔ tsuaa nɔ nɛ maa ta e he ɔ, e he be tsɔe kɛ yaa si du ma bu. 20Nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ e maa hi nɔ, loo e maa hwɔ nɔ be mi nɛ e ku nine ɔ, nɔ́ ɔ he be tsɔe. 21-23Nɔ tsuaa nɔ nɛ maa ta sa, loo nɔ́ ko nɛ yo nɛ ɔ hi nɔ ɔ he ɔ, é fɔ e tade ɔmɛ a he, nɛ é du e he. E he be tsɔe kɛ yaa si du ma bu. 24Ke nyumu ko kɛ yo nɛ ɔ na bɔmi be mi nɛ e ku nine ɔ, jamɛ a nyumu ɔ ble e he, nɛ e he be tsɔe ligbi kpaago. Sa tsuaa sa nɛ e maa hwɔ nɔ ɔ hu he be tsɔe.
25Ke muɔ be ngɛ yo ko he be saii, be mi nɛ e nine kumi be sui lolo, aloo ke e be ɔ su, nɛ muɔ ɔ be kɛ be nɔ ɔ, e he be tsɔe ligbi ɔmɛ tsuo nɛ muɔ ɔ ngɛ bee ɔ, kaa bɔ nɛ e he be tsɔe, be mi nɛ e ku nine ɔ. 26Sa tsuaa sa nɛ e maa hwɔ nɔ, kɛ nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ e maa hi nɔ be nɛ ɔ mi ɔ he be tsɔe. 27Nɔ tsuaa nɔ nɛ maa ta ní nɛ ɔmɛ a he ɔ, e he be tsɔe. Nɔ ɔ nɛ fɔ e tade ɔmɛ a he, nɛ e du e he. E he be tsɔe kɛ yaa si du ma bu. 28Ke muɔ ɔ nɛ ngɛ bee ngɛ yo nɛ ɔ he ɔ se po ɔ, e maa hi si ligbi kpaago loko e he ma tsɔ. 29Ligbi kpaanyɔne ɔ, yo ɔ nɛ ngɔ lahuɛ enyɔ, loo beleku lahuɛ enyɔ kɛ ba ha osɔfo ɔ ngɛ kpe he bo tsu ɔ sinya a nya. 30Osɔfo ɔ maa ngɔ kake kɛ sã yayami pami bɔ, nɛ e maa ngɔ kake ɔ hu kɛ sã sami bɔ. Kusumi nɛ osɔfo ɔ maa pee kɛ kpata Yawɛ ha yo ɔ ji nɛ ɔ nɛ.
31Yawɛ de Mose ke e slɔ Israel bi ɔmɛ ngɛ a he nɛ tsɔ we ɔ he, konɛ a ko ble Yawɛ kpe he bo tsu ɔ ngɛ ma a sito he ɔ. Ke pi ja a, a ma gbo.
32Enɛ ɔmɛ ji mlaahi nɛ fɔɔ si kɛ ha nyumu nɛ nyu yaya, loo nyumu he nyu ngɛ bee ngɛ e he, nɛ haa e he tsɔ we ɔ, 33kɛ yo hu nɛ ku nine, loo nyumu nɛ e kɛ yo na bɔmi be mi nɛ yo ɔ ku nine, nɛ e he tsɔ we ɔ.

english_text:
The Great Day of Forgiveness
1-2 Two of Aaron's sons had already lost their lives for disobeying the Lord, so the Lord told Moses to say to Aaron:
I, the Lord, appear in a cloud over the place of mercy on the sacred chest, which is behind the inside curtain of the sacred tent. And I warn you not to go there except at the proper time. Otherwise, you will die!
3 Before entering this most holy place, you must offer a bull as a sacrifice for your sins and a ram as a sacrifice to please me. 4You will take a bath and put on the sacred linen clothes, including the underwear, the robe, the sash, and the turban. 5Then the community of Israel will bring you a ram and two goats, both of them males. The goats are to be used as sacrifices for sin, and the ram is to be used as a sacrifice to please me.
6Aaron, you must offer the bull as a sacrifice of forgiveness for your own sins and for the sins of your family. 7Then you will lead the two goats into my presence at the front of the sacred tent, 8where I will show you which goat will be sacrificed to me and which one will be sent into the desert to the demon Azazel. 9After you offer the first goat as a sacrifice for sin, 10the other one must be presented to me alive, before you send it into the desert to take away the sins of the people.
11You must offer the bull as a sacrifice to ask forgiveness for your own sins and for the sins of your family. 12Then you will take a fire pan of live coals from the bronze altar, together with two handfuls of finely ground incense, into the most holy place. 13There you will present them to me by placing the incense on the coals, so that the place of mercy will be covered with a cloud of smoke. Do this, or you will die right there! 14Next, use a finger to sprinkle some of the blood on the place of mercy, which is on the lid of the sacred chest; then sprinkle blood seven times in front of the chest.
15 Aaron, you must next sacrifice the goat for the sins of the people, and you must sprinkle its blood inside the most holy place, just as you did with the blood of the bull. 16By doing this, you will take away the sins that make both the most holy place and the people of Israel unclean. Do the same for the sacred tent, which is here among the people. 17Only you are allowed in the sacred tent from the time you enter until the time you come out. 18After leaving the tent, you will purify the bronze altar by smearing each of its four corners with some of the blood from the bull and from the goat. 19Use a finger to sprinkle the altar seven times with the blood, and it will be completely clean from the sins of the people.
20After you have purified the most holy place, the sacred tent, and the bronze altar, you must bring the live goat to the front of the tent. 21 There you will lay your hands on its head, while confessing every sin the people have committed, and you will appoint someone to lead the goat into the desert, so that it can take away their sins. 22Finally, this goat that carries the heavy burden of Israel's sins must be released deep in the desert.
23-24 Aaron, after this you must go inside the sacred tent, take a bath, put on your regular priestly clothes, and leave there the clothes you put on before entering the most holy place. Then you will come out and offer sacrifices to please me and sacrifices for your sins and for the sins of the people. 25The fat from these sacrifices for sin must be sent up in smoke on the bronze altar.
26The one who led the goat into the desert and sent it off to the demon Azazel must take a bath and wash his clothes before coming back into camp. 27 The remains of the bull and the goat whose blood was taken into the most holy place must be taken outside the camp and burned. 28And whoever does this must take a bath and change clothes before coming back into camp.
The Lord told Moses to say to the people:
29 On the tenth day of the seventh month of each year, you must go without eating to show sorrow for your sins, and no one, including foreigners who live among you, is allowed to work. 30This is the day on which the sacrifice for the forgiveness of your sins will be made in my presence, 31and from now on, it must be celebrated each year. Go without eating and make this a day of complete rest just like the Sabbath. 32The high priest must offer the sacrifices for cleansing from sin, while wearing the sacred linen clothes. 33He will offer these sacrifices for the most holy place, the sacred tent, the bronze altar, all the priests, and for the whole community. 34You must celebrate this day each year—it is the Great Day of Forgiveness for all the sins of the people of Israel.
Moses did exactly as the Lord had commanded.
translation_text:
Kpatami ligbi ɔ
1Benɛ Aaron binyumu enyɔ ɔmɛ ngɔ la nɛ he tsɔ we kɛ ya Yawɛ hɛ mi nɛ a gbo se ɔ, Yawɛ kɛ Mose tu munyu. 2 E de lɛ ke, “De o nyɛminyumu Aaron ke e ko ya he klɔuklɔu pe kulaa a ngɛ tsu mi pomi bo ɔ se be saisaa, konɛ e ko gbo. Ejakaa lejɛ ɔ ji he nɛ i jeɔ ye he kpo ngɛ ngɛ bɔku mi, ngɛ somi daka a nya nɔ́ ɔ nɔ. 3 E ma nyɛ maa ya he klɔuklɔu pe kulaa a ke e hɛɛ na niheyo kɛ ha yayami pami bɔ sami, nɛ e hɛɛ agbosu hu kɛ ha sami bɔ.”
4Jehanɛ Yawɛ wo mlaa nɛ ɔmɛ. Be tsuaa be nɛ Aaron maa sɛ he klɔuklɔu pe kulaa a, é du e he, nɛ é wo osɔfo tade klɔuklɔu nɛ ɔmɛ: kploba yi nɔ tade klɔuklɔu ɔ, sisi tade ɔmɛ, kɛ kploba mlɛ mi fimi nɔ́ ɔ, nɛ é bu kploba pɛɛ ɔ.
5Aaron nɛ he akpakpo enyɔ nɛ a kɛ maa sã yayami pami bɔ, kɛ agbosu kake nɛ a kɛ maa sã sami bɔ ngɛ Israel ma a tsuo dɛ. 6É sã na ku ɔ kaa yayami pami bɔ kɛ ha lɛ nitsɛ e he, nɛ é kpata Yawɛ ha lɛ nitsɛ kɛ e we ɔ. 7Jehanɛ, é ngɔ akpakpo enyɔ ɔmɛ kɛ ba Yawɛ hɛ mi ngɛ kpe he bo tsu ɔ sinya a nya. 8É fɔ a nɔ sɔ. Yawɛ nɔ́ kake, kɛ Azazel nɔ́ kake. 9Nɔ́ nɛ Yawɛ sɔ ɔ je ɔ, a kɛ sã yayami pami bɔ. 10Nɔ́ nɛ Azazel nɔ́ ɔ je ɔ, a kɛ ba Yawɛ hɛ mi hɛ ngmengmle, nɛ a kɛ ba kpata Yawɛ ha ma a. Lɔ ɔ se ɔ, a je lɛ we kɛ ho nga a nɔ ya kɛ ya ha Azazel.
11Ke Aaron maa sã na ku ɔ kaa yayami pami bɔ kɛ ha lɛ nitsɛ e he kɛ e we ɔ, 12e ngɔ ngɛyu kɛ je la ngɛ bɔ sami la tɛ ɔ nɔ, nɛ e piti tsopa kɛ e he via nɛ a wɛɛ lɛ bukɔbukɔ dɛ kɔkɔ enyɔ, nɛ e kɛ sɛ he klɔuklɔu pe kulaa a. 13E ngɔ tsopa kɛ e he via a ngɔ pue la a mi ngɛ Yawɛ hɛ mi, nɛ e wo la su ku nɛ mi ti kɛ tsi somi daka nya nɔ́ ɔ nɔ, bɔ nɛ pee nɛ Aaron ko na somi daka nya nɔ́ ɔ, nɛ e ba gbo. 14É ngɔ na ku ɔ muɔ eko, nɛ e kɛ e nine nguɛ nɛ sɔ mi nɛ e kɛ fĩa somi daka nya nɔ ɔ hɛ mi. É kɛ muɔ ɔ nɛ fĩa somi daka nitsɛ hu hɛ mi si kpaago.
15 Jehanɛ, é gbe akpakpo ɔ nɛ a kɛ ma yayami pami bɔ sami ha ma a. É ngɔ muɔ ɔ kɛ ba he klɔuklɔu pe kulaa a, nɛ e ya fĩa kɛ pue somi daka a nya nɔ́ ɔ nɔ, kɛ somi daka a he kɛ kpe kaa bɔ nɛ a kɛ na ku ɔ muɔ ɔ pee ɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ. 16É pee kusumi nɛ ɔ kɛ kpata Yawɛ ngɛ he klɔuklɔu pe kulaa a ngɛ Israel bi ɔmɛ a musuhi nɛ a bɔ, mlaahi a nɔ nɛ a tɔ, kɛ yayamihi nɛ a pee ɔ tsuo kulaa he. É pee kusumi nɛ ɔ kɛ ha kpe he bo tsu ɔ hulɔ; ejakaa e ngɛ ma sito he ɔ he nɛ a ble ɔ. 17Kɛ je be nɛ Aaron maa sɛ he klɔuklɔu pe kulaa a nɛ e ya pee kusumi nɛ ɔ, kɛ yaa si e maa je kpo ɔ, nɔ ko nɔ ko nɛ ko ya bo tsu ɔ mi. Ke e pee kusumi nɛ e kɛ kpata Yawɛ kɛ ha lɛ nitsɛ e he kɛ e we ɔ, kɛ ma a tsuo gbe nya a, 18é je kpo kɛ ya bɔ sami la tɛ nɛ ngɛ Yawɛ hɛ mi ɔ he, nɛ e ya kpata Yawɛ kɛ ha la tɛ ɔ. É ngɔ na ku ɔ muɔ ɔ eko, kɛ akpakpo ɔ hu muɔ ɔ eko kɛ kpa bɔ sami la tɛ ɔ koli ɔmɛ a he. 19É ngɔ e nine nguɛ kɛ fĩa muɔ ɔ eko kɛ pue bɔ sami la tɛ ɔ nɔ si kpaago. É tsukɔ he, nɛ é pee lɛ klɔuklɔu ngɛ yayamihi nɛ Israel bi ɔmɛ pee kɛ ble la tɛ ɔ he.
Musu kpami to
20Ke Aaron pee kusumi ɔ kɛ tsukɔ he klɔuklɔu pe kulaa a, kpe he bo tsu ɔ, kɛ bɔ sami la tɛ ɔ he gbe nya a, é ngɔ akpakpo hɛngmengmletsɛ ɔ kɛ ba Yawɛ hɛ mi. 21É ngɔ e nine enyɔ ɔmɛ tsuo ngɔ pue akpakpo ɔ yi mi, nɛ e jaje kaa Israel bi ɔmɛ pee yayami, a tɔ mlaa, nɛ a gbo tue. Aaron nɛ ngɔ yayami nɛ ɔmɛ ngɔ pue akpakpo ɔ nɔ. Lɔ ɔ se ɔ, e ngɔ akpakpo ɔ kɛ ha nɔ ko nɛ a hla kɛ to, nɛ e fie lɛ kɛ ho nga nɔ ya, nɛ e ya ngmɛɛ e he ngɛ lejɛ ɔ. 22Akpakpo ɔ maa tloo Israel bi ɔmɛ a he musu tsuo kɛ maa ho zugba nɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko be nɔ ɔ nɔ ya.
23 Jehanɛ, Aaron nɛ sɛ kpe he bo tsu ɔ mi, nɛ é je e we osɔfo tade ɔmɛ nɛ e wo kɛ ya sɛ he klɔuklɔu pe kulaa kɛ pue lejɛ ɔ. 24É du e he ngɛ he ko nɛ tsɔ, nɛ é wo lɛ nitsɛ e tade ɔmɛ. Jehanɛ, é je kpo nɛ e ya sã sami bɔ kɛ kpata Yawɛ ha lɛ nitsɛ e he, kɛ ma a hulɔ. 25Lohwe ɔ nɛ a kɛ ma yayami pami bɔ ɔ sami ɔ, e sã e zɔ ɔ ngɛ bɔ sami la tɛ ɔ nɔ. 26Nɔ ɔ nɛ fie to ɔ kɛ ya ha Azazel ngɛ nga a nɔ ɔ nɛ fɔ e tade ɔmɛ nɛ e wo ɔ a he, nɛ e du e he loko e ba ma sito he ɔ. 27 Na ku ɔ, kɛ akpakpo ɔ nɛ a kɛ ba sã yayami pami bɔ, nɛ a kɛ a muɔ ɔ ba kpata Yawɛ ngɛ he klɔuklɔu pe kulaa a, a ngɔ mɛ kɛ je ma sito he ɔ, nɛ a ya sã mɛ. A sã lohwe he womi ɔmɛ, lo ɔ, kɛ a fĩ ɔ tsuo. 28Nɔ nɛ maa sã ní nɛ ɔmɛ ɔ, é fɔ e tade ɔmɛ a he, nɛ é du e he loko é ba ma sito he ɔ.
Kpatami ligbi ɔ yemi
29 Enɛ ɔ maa pee mlaa nɛ fɔɔ si kɛ yaa neneene. Nyɔhiɔ kpaagone ɔ we ligbi nɛ ji nyɔngma a, Israel fɔfɔɛ, kɛ nibwɔhi nɛ ngɛ a kpɛti tsuo maa ha hwɔ, nɛ a be nɔ́ ko nɔ́ ko tsue. 30Jamɛ a ligbi ɔ, a maa pee kusumi kɛ kpata Yawɛ ha mɛ kɛ tsukɔ a he kɛ je a he yayami ɔmɛ tsuo kulaa mi, konɛ a he nɛ tsɔ. 31Jamɛ a ligbi ɔ maa pee Hejɔɔmi ligbi nɛ a be nɔ́ ko nɔ́ ko tsue; nɔ tsuaa nɔ maa ha hwɔ. Mlaa nɛ ɔmɛ fɔɔ si ha mɛ kɛ yaa neneene. 32Osɔfo nɔkɔtɔma pe kulaa nɛ a pɔ lɛ nu, nɛ a tsukɔ e he, nɛ a wo lɛ osɔfo ngɛ e tsɛ nane mi ɔ nɛ wo osɔfo tade ɔmɛ, nɛ é pee kpatami kusumi ɔmɛ. 33E maa tsukɔ he klɔuklɔu pe kulaa a, kpe he bo tsu ɔ, bɔ sami la tɛ ɔ, osɔfo ɔmɛ, kɛ ma kpekpemi ɔ tsuo a he. 34Á ye mlaa nɛ ɔmɛ a nɔ kɛ ya neneene. Daa jeha a, a maa pee kusumi nɛ ɔ si kake kɛ kpata Mawu ha Israel bi ɔmɛ ngɛ a he yayami ɔmɛ a he.
Mose pee kaa bɔ nɛ Yawɛ fa lɛ ɔ.

english_text:
Where To Offer Sacrifices
1The Lord told Moses 2to tell Aaron, his sons, and everyone else in Israel:
3-4Whenever you kill any of your cattle, sheep, or goats as sacrifices to me, you must do it at the entrance to the sacred tent. If you don't, you will be guilty of pouring out blood, and you will no longer belong to the community of Israel. 5And so, when you sacrifice an animal to ask my blessing, it must not be done out in a field, 6but in front of the sacred tent. Then a priest can splatter its blood against the bronze altar and send its fat up in smoke with a smell that pleases me. 7Don't ever turn from me again and offer sacrifices to goat-demons. This law will never change.
8Remember! No one in Israel, including foreigners, is to offer a sacrifice anywhere 9except at the entrance to the sacred tent. If you do, you will no longer belong to my people.
Do Not Eat Blood
The Lord said:
10 I will turn against any of my people who eat blood. This also includes any foreigners living among you. 11 Life is in the blood, and I have given you the blood of animals to sacrifice in place of your own. 12That's also why I have forbidden you to eat blood. 13Even if you should hunt and kill a bird or an animal, you must drain out the blood and cover it with soil.
14The life of every living creature is in its blood. That's why I have forbidden you to eat blood and why I have warned you that anyone who does will no longer belong to my people.
15If you happen to find a dead animal and eat it, you must take a bath and wash your clothes, but you are still unclean until evening. 16If you don't take a bath, you will suffer for what you did wrong.
translation_text:
Mlaahi nɛ kɔɔ muɔ he
1Yawɛ de Mose ke 2e de Aaron, kɛ e binyumu ɔmɛ, kɛ Israel ma a tsuo ke mlaahi nɛ Yawɛ wo mɛ ji nɛ ɔmɛ nɛ. 3-4Ke Israel fɔfɔɛ ko gbe na, loo jijɔ, loo apletsi ngɛ he kpa ko nɛ pi kpe he bo tsu ɔ sinya a nya, nɛ e kɛ ba sã bɔ ha Yawɛ ɔ, e tɔ mlaa. Jamɛatsɛ ɔ pue muɔ si. Á je lɛ we, nɛ a ko bu lɛ ngɔ si ye ma a mi bi ɔmɛ a nɔ hu. 5Mlaa nɛ ɔ tsɔɔ kaa jehanɛ lɛɛ Israel bi ɔmɛ nɛ a ngɔ lohwe ɔmɛ nɛ a gbee ngɛ nga nɔ ɔ kɛ ba ha osɔfo ɔ ngɛ kpe he bo tsu ɔ sinya a nya. Á gbe lohwe ɔ ngɛ lejɛ ɔ kɛ sã tue mi jɔmi bɔ ha Yawɛ. 6Osɔfo ɔ nɛ fĩa muɔ ɔ kɛ pue Yawɛ bɔ sami la tɛ ɔ nɔ ngɛ kpe he bo tsu ɔ sinya a nya, konɛ é sã zɔ ɔ kaa bɔ nɛ jee via ngɛ Yawɛ hɛ mi. 7Enɛ ɔ ma ha Israel bi ɔmɛ maa jɔɔ bɔ sami ha mumi yayamihi nɛ hɛɛ apletsi su nɛ a jee Mawu se nɛ a ya jaa a. Enɛ ɔ maa pee mlaa nɛ fɔɔ si ha mɛ, kɛ a nina kɛ yaa neneene.
8Jehanɛ hu, de mɛ ke, ke Israel fɔfɔɛ, aloo nɔ ko nɛ ba to mɛ nubwɔ maa sã sami bɔ, loo bɔ kpa ko kɛ ha Yawɛ, nɛ e ngɔɛ kɛ bɛ kpe he bo tsu ɔ sinya a nya a, 9jamɛ a nɔ ɔ, a je lɛ we, nɛ a ko bu lɛ ngɔ si ye ma a mi bi ɔmɛ a nɔ hu.
10 Ke Israel fɔfɔɛ ko, aloo nɔ ko nɛ ba to nyɛ nubwɔ ye muɔ ɔ, ye hɛ maa dɔ kɛ wo jamɛ a nɔ ɔ. Ma je lɛ we, nɛ a ko bu lɛ ngɔ si ye ma a mi bi ɔmɛ a nɔ hu. 11 Muɔ ji nɔ́ nɛ haa he lo tsuaa he lo wami. Lɔ ɔ he nɛ Yawɛ fa ke a ngɔ muɔ kɛ pue bɔ sami la tɛ ɔ nɔ nɛ a kɛ kpa musu ɔ nɛ. Muɔ ji nɔ́ nɛ a kɛ kpaa musu, ejakaa wami ngɛ mi. 12Enɛ ɔ he je nɛ i de Israel bi ɔmɛ ke a ko ye muɔ ɔ nɛ; mɛ jio, nɔ ko nɛ ba to mɛ nubwɔ jio.
13Ke Israel fɔfɔɛ, loo nɔ ko nɛ ba to mɛ nubwɔ ya da de nɛ e gbe lohwe nane eywiɛtsɛ, loo pɛlitsɛ nɛ a yeɔ ɔ, é dɛ muɔ ɔ kɛ pue si, nɛ e ngɔ zu ngɔ pue nɔ. 14Ejakaa muɔ ji nɔ́ nɛ haa he lo tsuaa he lo wami. Lɔ ɔ he nɛ Yawɛ de Israel bi ɔmɛ ke a ko ye muɔ ɔ nɛ. Nɔ tsuaa nɔ nɛ maa pee ja a, á je lɛ we, nɛ a ko bu lɛ ngɔ si ye ma a mi bi ɔmɛ a nɔ hu.
15Israel no tsuaa Israel no, loo nubwɔ kó ye lohwe ko nɛ lɛ nitsɛ e gbo, aloo nɔ́ nɛ nga mi lohwe tsɔtslɔɔ e mi. Ke e ba mi kaa nɔ ko tɔ mlaa nɛ ɔ nɔ ɔ, é fɔ e tade ɔmɛ a he, nɛ é du e he. E he be tsɔe kɛ yaa si du ma bu; lɔ ɔ se loko e he ma tsɔ. 16Ke e fɔ we e tade ɔmɛ a he, nɛ́ e du e he ɔ, e musu maa tloo lɛ.

english_text:
Forbidden Sex
1The Lord told Moses 2to tell the people of Israel:
I am the Lord your God! 3So don't follow the customs of Egypt where you used to live or those of Canaan where I am bringing you. 4I am the Lord your God, and you must obey my teachings. 5 Obey them and you will live. I am the Lord.
6Don't have sex with any of your close relatives, 7especially your own mother. This would disgrace your father. 8 And don't disgrace him by having sex with any of his other wives. 9 Don't have sex with your sister or stepsister, whether you grew up together or not. 10Don't disgrace yourself by having sex with your granddaughter 11or half sister 12-13 or a sister of your father or mother. 14Don't disgrace your uncle by having sex with his wife. 15 Don't have sex with your daughter-in-law 16 or sister-in-law. 17 And don't have sex with the daughter or granddaughter of any woman that you have earlier had sex with. You will be having sex with her closest relatives, and that would make you unclean. 18As long as your wife is alive, don't cause trouble for her by taking one of her sisters as a second wife.
19 When a woman is having her monthly period, she is unclean, so don't have sex with her.
20 Don't have sex with another man's wife—that would make you unclean.
21 Don't sacrifice your children on the altar fires to the god Molech. I am the Lord your God, and that would disgrace me.
22 It is disgusting for a man to have sex with another man.
23 Anyone who has sex with an animal is unclean.
24Don't make yourselves unclean by any of these disgusting practices of those nations that I am forcing out of the land for you. They made themselves 25and the land so unclean, that I punished the land because of their sins, and I made it vomit them up. 26-27Now don't do these sickening things that make the land filthy. Instead, obey my laws and teachings. 28Then the land won't become sick of you and vomit you up, just as it did them. 29-30If any of you do these vulgar, disgusting things, you will be unclean and no longer belong to my people. I am the Lord your God, and I forbid you to follow their sickening way of life.
translation_text:
Nyumu kɛ yo bɔmi nɛ a hĩɔ
1Yawɛ de Mose ke 2e de Israel bi ɔmɛ ke, “Imi ji, Yawɛ nyɛ Mawu ɔ nɛ. 3Egipt bi ɔmɛ nɛ nyɛ hi a zugba a nɔ ɔ, kɛ Kanaan bi ɔmɛ nɛ i ngɔ nyɛ kɛ yaa a zugba a a nɔ ɔ, nyɛ ko pee a kusumi níhi. 4Nyɛɛ pee ye suɔmi nya ní, nɛ nyɛɛ ye ye mlaa amɛ a nɔ. Imi ji Yawɛ, nyɛ Mawu ɔ nɛ. 5 Mlaahi nɛ i wo nyɛ, kɛ blɔ nyahi nɛ i to ha nyɛ ɔ, nyɛɛ ye a nɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Ke nyɛ pee ja a, nyɛ yi ma na wami. Imi ji Yawɛ.”
6Yawɛ wo mlaa nɛ ɔmɛ. Nyɛ ti nɔ ko nɔ ko kɛ lɛ nitsɛ e nyɛmi tutuutu kó na nyumu kɛ yo bɔmi. Imi ji Yawɛ. 7Nɔ ko kɛ e nyɛ kó na nyumu kɛ yo bɔmi nɛ e ba pue e tsɛ hɛ mi si. Kó pue mo nitsɛ o nyɛ hɛ mi si. 8 O kɛ o tsɛ e yo kpa ko kó na nyumu kɛ yo bɔmi nɛ o ba pue o tsɛ hɛ mi si. 9 O kɛ o nyɛmiyo kó na nyumu kɛ yo bɔmi, o nyɛbi ji lɛ jio, o tsɛbi ji lɛ jio, nɔ nɛ a fɔ lɛ ngɛ we jio, nɔ nɛ a fɔ lɛ ngɛ ma se jio. 10O kɛ o bibi kó na nyumu kɛ yo bɔmi, o binyumu bi ji lɛ jio, o biyo bi ji lɛ jio; e ji hɛ mi si puemi nɔ́ kɛ ha nyɛ tsuo. 11O kɛ o tsɛ yo e biyo kó na nyumu kɛ yo bɔmi, ejakaa lɛ hu o nyɛmi ji lɛ. 12 O kɛ o nyɛko kó na nyumu kɛ yo bɔmi, ejakaa o tsɛ nitsɛ nyɛmiyo ji lɛ. 13O kɛ o nyɛwayo, loo o nyɛngua kó na nyumu kɛ yo bɔmi, ejakaa lɛ hu e ngɛ kaa o nyɛ kɛ̃. 14O kɛ o tsɛngua, loo o tsɛwayo e yo kó na nyumu kɛ yo bɔmi, ejakaa o nyɛnyua, loo o nyɛwayo ji lɛ. 15 O kɛ o binyumu e yo kó na nyumu kɛ yo bɔmi, ejakaa o nganyɛ ji lɛ. 16 O kɛ o nyɛminyumu e yo kó na nyumu kɛ yo bɔmi, ejakaa e ji hɛ mi si puemi ha o nyɛminyumu ɔ. 17 O kɛ yo kɛ e biyo tsuo kó na nyumu kɛ yo bɔmi. O kɛ yo ɔ e bibi hu kó na nyumu kɛ yo bɔmi, e binyumu biyo jio, e biyo ɔ biyo jio. Ke o pee ja a, o bɔ musu, ejakaa nyɛmimɛ tutuutu ji mɛ. 18Koo ngɔ nɔ kɛ e nyɛmi nɛ a ba pee huno yihi, be mi nɛ e nyɛmi ɔ ngɛ je mi kɛ mwɔɔ.
19 “O kɛ yo nɛ ku nine kó na nyumu kɛ yo bɔmi, ejakaa e he tsɔ we. 20 O kɛ o nyɛmi e yo kó na nyumu kɛ yo bɔmi nɛ o kó ba ble o he. 21 Koo ngɔ o bimɛ ɔmɛ eko kɛ ha nɛ a sã ha mawu ɔ nɛ a tsɛɛ lɛ Molek ɔ. Ke o pee ja a, o gbe Yawɛ, o Mawu ɔ he guɛ. 22 Nyumu kɛ nyumu kó na bɔmi kaa yo kɛ nyumu; a hĩɔ. 23 O kɛ lohwe kó na bɔmi nɛ o ba ble o he. Yo hu kɛ lohwe kó hwɔ nɛ e ba ble e he ja nɔuu. A hĩɔ.
24“Je ma amɛ nɛ i ngɛ fiee kɛ ngɛ nyɛ blɔ mi jee ɔ, níhi nɛ a pee nɛ a kɛ ble a he, 25nɛ a kɛ ble zugba a hulɔ ɔ ji nɛ ɔmɛ nɛ. Lɔ ɔ he je nɛ i ngɛ zugba a tue gblae, nɛ zugba a hu ngɛ ni ɔmɛ fiee ɔ nɛ. 26Se nyɛ nitsɛmɛ, kɛ nibwɔhi nɛ ba to nyɛ ɔ lɛɛ nyɛɛ ye ye mlaa amɛ, kɛ ye blɔ nya tomi ɔmɛ a nɔ, nɛ nyɛ ko pee níhi nɛ a hĩɔ nɛ ɔ eko. 27Nihi nɛ hi hiɛmɛ nɛ ɔ loko nyɛ ba a bɔ musu nɛ ɔmɛ tsuo kɛ ble zugba a. 28Ke nyɛ hu nyɛ pee ní nɛ ɔmɛ kɛ ble zugba a, zugba a maa fie nyɛ kaa bɔ nɛ e fie nihi nɛ hi lejɛ ɔ loko nyɛ ba a. 29Nɔ tsuaa nɔ nɛ maa pee níhi nɛ a hĩɔ nɛ ɔ eko ɔ, a je lɛ we, nɛ a ko bu lɛ ngɔ si ye ma a mi bi ɔmɛ a nɔ hu.”
30Yawɛ de kɛ gbe nya ke, “Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, nyɛɛ ye ye mlaa amɛ a nɔ. Musu bɔmi níhi nɛ ni nɛmɛ nɛ hi zugba a nɔ kekle ɔ pee ɔ, nyɛ ko pee nɛ nyɛ ba ble nyɛ he. Imi ji Yawɛ, nyɛ Mawu ɔ nɛ.”

english_text:
Moral and Religious Laws
1The Lord told Moses 2 to say to the community of Israel:
I am the Lord your God. I am holy, and you must be holy too! 3-4 Respect your father and your mother, honor the Sabbath, and don't make idols or images. I am the Lord your God.
5When you offer a sacrifice to ask my blessing, be sure to follow my instructions. 6You may eat the meat either on the day of the sacrifice or on the next day, but you must burn anything left over on the third day. 7If you eat any of it on the third day, the sacrifice will be disgusting to me, and I will reject it. 8In fact, you will be punished for not respecting what I say is holy, and you will no longer belong to the community of Israel.
9 When you harvest your grain, always leave some of it standing along the edges of your fields and don't pick up what falls on the ground. 10Don't strip your grapevines clean or gather the grapes that fall off the vines. Leave them for the poor and for those foreigners who live among you. I am the Lord your God.
11 Do not steal or tell lies or cheat others.
12 Do not misuse my name by making promises you don't intend to keep. I am the Lord your God.
13 Do not steal anything or cheat anyone, and don't fail to pay your workers at the end of each day.
14 I am the Lord your God, and I command you not to make fun of the deaf or to cause a blind person to stumble.
15 Be fair, no matter who is on trial—don't favor either the poor or the rich.
16Don't be a gossip, but never hesitate to speak up in court, especially if your testimony can save someone's life.
17 Don't hold grudges. On the other hand, it's wrong not to correct someone who needs correcting. 18 Don't be angry or try to take revenge. I am the Lord, and I command you to love others as much as you love yourself.
19 Breed your livestock animals only with animals of the same kind, and don't plant two kinds of seed in the same field or wear clothes made of different kinds of material.
20If a man has sex with a slave woman who is promised in marriage to someone else, he must pay a fine, but they are not to be put to death. After all, she was still a slave at the time. 21-22The man must bring a ram to the entrance of the sacred tent and give it to a priest, who will then offer it as a sacrifice to me, so the man's sins will be forgiven.
23After you enter the land, you will plant fruit trees, but you are not to eat any fruit from them for the first three years. 24In the fourth year the fruit must be set apart, as an expression of thanks 25to me, the Lord God. Do this, and in the fifth year, those trees will produce an abundant harvest of fruit for you to eat.
26 Don't eat the blood of any animal.
Don't practice any kind of witchcraft.
27-28 I forbid you to shave any part of your head or beard or to cut and tattoo yourself as a way of worshiping the dead.
29 Don't let your daughters serve as temple prostitutes—this would bring disgrace both to them and the land.
30 I command you to respect the Sabbath and the place where I am worshiped.
31 Don't make yourselves disgusting to me by going to people who claim they can talk to the dead.
32I command you to show respect for older people and to obey me with fear and trembling.
33 Don't mistreat any foreigners who live in your land. 34Instead, treat them as well as you treat your own people and love them as much as you love yourself. Remember, you were once foreigners in the land of Egypt. I am the Lord your God.
35-36 Use honest scales and don't cheat when you weigh or measure anything.
I am the Lord your God. I rescued you from Egypt, 37and I command you to obey my laws.
translation_text:
Mlaahi nɛ kɔɔ klɔuklɔu peemi kɛ dami sane yemi he
1Yawɛ de Mose ke 2 e de Israel ma kpekpemi ɔ tsuo ke, “Nyɛɛ pee nyɛ he klɔuklɔu, ejakaa imi Yawɛ, nyɛ Mawu ɔ, i ngɛ klɔuklɔu. 3 Nyɛ ti nɔ tsuaa nɔ nɛ bu e nyɛ kɛ e tsɛ; nɛ e ye Hejɔɔmi ligbi ɔ kaa bɔ nɛ i fa nyɛ ɔ. Imi ji Yawɛ, nyɛ Mawu ɔ nɛ.
4 “Nyɛ ko je ye se nɛ nyɛ ya ja amagahi; nɛ nyɛ ko pee dade mawuhi ha nyɛ he. Imi ji Yawɛ, nyɛ Mawu ɔ nɛ.
5“Ke nyɛ gbe lohwe nɛ a kɛ maa sã tue mi jɔmi bɔ ha imi Yawɛ, nyɛ Mawu ɔ, mlaahi nɛ i wo nyɛ ɔ, nyɛɛ ye a nɔ, konɛ e sa ye hɛ mi. 6Á ye lo ɔ ligbi nɛ a maa gbe lohwe ɔ, aloo e nɔ jena. Ke eko piɛ nɛ ye ligbi etɛ ɔ, á sã, 7Ke kaa nɔ ko ye eko ligbi etɛne ɔ, i be e bɔ ngɔe, ejakaa a hĩɔ. 8Nɔ tsuaa nɔ nɛ maa ye eko ɔ, a gbla e tue, ejakaa e ble Yawɛ nɔ́ klɔuklɔu ɔ. A ma je lɛ we, nɛ a be lɛ bue ngɔ si ye ma a mi bi ɔmɛ a nɔ hu.
9 “Ke nyɛ ngɛ nyɛ ngmɔ ní kpae ɔ, nyɛ ko kpa ní ɔ kɛ ya su ngmɔ ɔ tue haa. Nyɛ ko muɔ nɔ́ nɛ ma pue si ngɛ ní kpami ɔ se hulɔ. 10Wai ngmɔtsɛ kó kpa wai yiblii ɔmɛ tsuo ngɛ e wai tso ɔmɛ a nɔ. Wai yiblii nɛ maa nɔɔ si ngɛ wai ngmɔ ɔ mi ɔ hu e ko ya kukuɔ. E si ha ohiatsɛmɛ, kɛ nibwɔhi. Imi ji Yawɛ, nyɛ Mawu ɔ nɛ.
11 “Nyɛ ko ju; nyɛ ko sisi nɔ, nɛ nyɛ ko ye nyɛ sibi lakpa.
12 “Nyɛ ko ngɔ ye biɛ kɛ ka lakpa kita kɛ wo ye biɛ he mu. Imi ji Yawɛ, nyɛ Mawu ɔ nɛ.
13 “Koo fia o nyɛmi ojo, nɛ koo ju e nɔ́ ko hulɔ. Ke o ya bɔ nɔ ko apaa ke e ba tsu ní ha mo ɔ, wo lɛ hiɔ loko je nɛ na nɔ. 14 Koo gbiɛ tue kpokutsɛ, nɛ koo fɔ hɛ yuyuilɔ blɔ mi tso. Ye o Mawu ɔ gbeye. Imi ji Yawɛ.
15 “Nyɛɛ ye dami sane ngɛ kojomi mi; nyɛ ko hyɛ nɔ ko hɛ mi, ohiatsɛ ji lɛ jio, niatsɛ ji lɛ jio. 16Koo pee o he sieku yelɔ kɛ hi yae kɛ hi bae ngɛ o ma mi bi ɔmɛ a kpɛti. Koo ye lakpa odase kɛ si o nyɛmi, nɛ́ a pue e muɔ si yaka gu. Imi ji Yawɛ.
17 “Koo nyɛ o nyɛmi ngɛ o tsui mi. Ke sane ko ba a, o kɛ lɛ nɛ hla mi, konɛ e he ɔ, mo mohu o ko ba pee yayami. 18 Koo ye mo nitsɛ o he lue, nɛ koo nyɛ o ma a mi bi ɔmɛ a ti nɔ ko nɔ ko; se mohu, moo suɔ o nyɛmi nɔmlɔ kaa bɔ nɛ o suɔ mo nitsɛ o he ɔ. Imi ji Yawɛ.
19 “Nyɛɛ ye ye mlaa amɛ a nɔ. Nyɛ ko ha nɛ nyɛ we mi lohwehi nɛ kuɔ henɔ kpahi nɛ a kɛ mɛ nɛ fɔ. Nyɛ ko du wu munomuno enyɔ ngɛ ngmɔ kake mi; nɛ nyɛ ko wo tade nɛ a kɛ nɔ́ slɔɔto enyɔ lo bo ɔ.
20“Ke nyumu ko kɛ nyɔguɛ yo ko nɛ a bi e si ha nyumu kpa na bɔmi be mi nɛ a kpɔ̃ we lɛ, loo e yi e he lolo ɔ, a hla munyu ɔ mi. A ko gbe mɛ, ejakaa nyɔguɛ ɔ yi e he lolo. 21Se nyumu ɔ lɛɛ lɛ nitsɛ e ngɔ agbosu kɛ ba ha Yawɛ ngɛ kpe he bo tsu ɔ sinya a nya, nɛ a kɛ ba sã fɔ yemi bɔ. 22Osɔfo ɔ nɛ ngɔ agbosu ɔ nɛ a kɛ ma fɔ yemi bɔ ɔ sami ɔ kɛ ya Yawɛ hɛ mi, nɛ e kɛ ya pee kusumi kɛ kpata Yawɛ ngɛ yayami nɛ nɔ ɔ pee ɔ he, nɛ Mawu kɛ maa pa lɛ.
23“Ke nyɛ ya su Kanaan zugba a nɔ, nɛ nyɛ du tso slɔɔtoslɔɔtohi nɛ woɔ yiblii slɔɔtoslɔɔtohi nɛ a yeɔ ɔ, nyɛɛ bu a yiblii ɔmɛ kaa níhi nɛ a tsi nya kekleekle jeha etɛ ɔmɛ; jamɛ a be ɔ mi ɔ, nyɛ ko ye eko. 24Jeha eywiɛne ɔ mi ɔ, nyɛɛ ngɔ yiblii ɔmɛ tsuo ngɔ pee sina bɔ klɛdɛɛ ha imi Yawɛ. 25Jeha enuɔne ɔ mi lɛɛ nyɛ ma nyɛ maa ye a yiblii ɔmɛ. Ke nyɛ pee ní nɛ ɔmɛ ɔ, tso ɔmɛ maa wo yiblii babauu ha nyɛ. Imi ji Yawɛ, nyɛ Mawu ɔ nɛ.
26 “Nyɛ ko ye lo nɛ muɔ ngɛ mi kɛ mwɔɔ. Nyɛ ko klaa, nɛ nyɛ ko ye kunya hulɔ. 27 Nyɛ ko po huɛ ngɛ nyɛ yi kpɛti, nɛ nyɛ ko sua nyɛ kpɛni hulɔ. 28Ke nɔ ko gbo ɔ, nyɛ ko po nyɛ he ha, nɛ nyɛ ko ngmaangmaa nyɛ he kɛ ye kɔmɔ. Imi ji Yawɛ.
29 “Ko ha nɛ o biyo nɛ pee e he yaholɔ, nɛ e ba puɛ. Ke e pee ja a, yahomi kɛ musu bɔmi ma ba hiɛ ngɛ zugba a nɔ. 30 Nyɛɛ ye ye Hejɔɔmi ligbi ɔmɛ, nɛ nyɛɛ ngɔ bu kɛ ha ye he klɔuklɔu ɔ; imi ji Yawɛ.
31 “Nyɛ ko ya bi ní ngɛ klaali, kɛ kunya yeli a ngɔ; ke nyɛ pee ja a, nyɛ ma ble nyɛ he. Imi ji Yawɛ, nyɛ Mawu ɔ nɛ.
32“Buu nɔkɔtɔma, nɛ o wo e hɛ mi nyami. Ye mi gbeye. Imi ji Yawɛ, o Mawu ɔ nɛ.
33 “Ke nɔ ko ba to nyɛ nubwɔ ngɛ zugba a nɔ ɔ, nyɛ ko pee lɛ yayami. 34Ke nɔ ko ba to nyɛ nubwɔ ɔ, nyɛɛ bu lɛ kaa ma a mi no nɔuu. Moo suɔ lɛ kaa bɔ nɛ o suɔ mo nitsɛ o he ɔ; ejakaa nyɛ hu nyɛ ya to nubwɔ hyɛ ngɛ Egipt zugba a nɔ. Imi ji Yawɛ, nyɛ Mawu ɔ nɛ.
35 “Nyɛ ko sisi nɔ ngɛ nɔ́ ko kami, e jiimi, loo e hiɛmi kalemi mi. 36Nyɛɛ ngɔ sɛnihi, sɛni tɛhi, kɛ susumi níhi nɛ da kɛ tsu ní. Imi ji Yawɛ, nyɛ Mawu ɔ nɛ je nyɛ kɛ je Egipt zugba a nɔ ɔ nɛ. 37Nyɛ hɛ nɛ hi ye mlaa amɛ, kɛ ye blɔ nya tomi ɔmɛ tsuo nɔ, konɛ nyɛɛ ye a nɔ. Imi ji Yawɛ.”

english_text:
Penalties for Disobeying God's Laws
1The Lord told Moses 2to say to the community of Israel:
Death by stoning is the penalty for any citizens or foreigners in the country who sacrifice their children to the god Molech. 3They have disgraced both the place where I am worshiped and my holy name, and so I will turn against them and no longer let them belong to my people. 4Some of you may let them get away with human sacrifice, 5but not me. If any of you worship Molech, I will turn against you and your entire family, and I will no longer let you belong to my people.
6I will be your enemy if you go to someone who claims to speak with the dead, and I will destroy you from among my people. 7Dedicate yourselves to me and be holy because I am the Lord your God. 8I have chosen you as my people, and I expect you to obey my laws.
9 If you curse your father or mother, you will be put to death, and it will be your own fault.
10 If any of you men have sex with another man's wife, both you and the woman will be put to death.
11 Having sex with one of your father's wives disgraces him. So both you and the woman will be put to death, just as you deserve. 12 It isn't natural to have sex with your daughter-in-law, and both of you will be put to death, just as you deserve. 13 It's disgusting for men to have sex with one another, and those who do will be put to death, just as they deserve. 14 It isn't natural for a man to marry both a woman and her daughter, and so all three of them will be burned to death. 15-16 If any of you have sex with an animal, both you and the animal will be put to death, just as you deserve.
17 If you marry one of your sisters, you will be punished, and the two of you will be disgraced by being openly forced out of the community. 18 If you have sex with a woman during her monthly period, both you and the woman will be cut off from the people of Israel. 19 The sisters of your father and mother are your own relatives, and you will be punished for having sex with any of them. 20If you have sex with your uncle's wife, neither you nor she will ever have any children. 21 And if you marry your sister-in-law, neither of you will ever have any children.
22Obey my laws and teachings. Or else the land I am giving you will become sick of you and throw you out. 23The nations I am chasing out did these disgusting things, and I hated them for it, so don't follow their example. 24I am the Lord your God, and I have promised you their land that is rich with milk and honey. I have chosen you to be different from other people. 25That's why you must make a difference between animals and birds that I have said are clean and unclean—this will keep you from becoming disgusting to me. 26I am the Lord, the holy God. You have been chosen to be my people, and so you must be holy too.
