and we'll see what happens.
14I will be responsible
for what happens to me.
15God may kill me, but still
I will trust him
and offer my defense.
16This may be what saves me,
because no guilty person
would come to his court.
17Listen carefully to my words!
18I have prepared my case well,
and I am certain to win.
19If you can prove me guilty,
I will give up and die.
Job Prays
I Ask Only Two Things
20I ask only two things
of you, my God,
and I will no longer
hide from you—
21stop punishing
and terrifying me!
22Then speak, and I will reply;
or else let me speak,
and you reply.
23Please point out my sins,
so I will know them.
24Why have you turned your back
and count me your enemy?
25Do you really enjoy
frightening a fallen leaf?
26Why do you accuse me
of horrible crimes
and make me pay for sins
I did in my youth?
27 You have tied my feet down
and keep me surrounded;
28I am rotting away like cloth
eaten by worms.
translation_text:
1-2Ní nɛ ɔmɛ tsuo nɛ nyɛ ngɛ dee ɔ,
i na, nɛ i nu hyɛ; i nu lɛ tsuo sisi.
Nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ nyɛ le ɔ, imi hu i le;
nyɛ pi mi.
3Imi lɛɛ Mawu Ope ɔ lɛ i kɛ na, se pi nyɛ;
ma suɔ nɛ i kɛ lɛ wa hla níhi a nya.
4Nyɛɛ lɛɛ pe nyɛ poɔ sane deɔ;
nyɛ tsuo nyɛ ngɛ kaa tsopatsɛmɛ
nɛ a he be se nami.
5I na nɛ nyɛ ma nyɛ nya mohu,
jinɛ a ko tsɛ nyɛ ní leli.
6Nyɛɛ bu ye sane ɔ tue,
konɛ nyɛɛ na bɔ nɛ ma je ye nya ha.
7Mɛni he je nyɛ ngɛ lakpa yee?
Nyɛ susu kaa nyɛ lakpa a he maa ba se nami ha Mawu lo?
8Mawu he lɛ nyɛ ngɛ pɛe ɔ?
Nyɛ maa ye e sane ɔ ha lɛ lo?
9Ke Mawu ke e ma hla nyɛ níhi a mi fitsofitso ɔ,
anɛ e maa hi ha nyɛ lo?
Anɛ nyɛ susu kaa nyɛ maa sisi Mawu
kaa bɔ nɛ nyɛ sisiɔ nimli adesahi lo?
10Ke nyɛ hyɛɛ nimli a hɛ mi ngɛ laami mi ɔ,
e ma ka nyɛ hɛ mi kɛ̃.
11E he wami kpetekpleenyɛ ɔ maa wo nyɛ he gbeye,
nɛ sawale maa nu nyɛ.
12Abɛhi nɛ nyɛ ngɛ bue ɔ,
a he be se nami ko;
munyuhi nɛ nyɛɛ kɛ ngɛ Mawu he fae ɔ
ngɛ kaa kɔɔhiɔ kɛkɛ.
13Nyɛɛ pee dii nɛ ma tu munyu,
konɛ nɔ́ nɛ maa ba ye nɔ nɛ ba.
14E wɛ ha mi kaa ma ngɔ ye wami kɛ ha
ngɛ enɛ ɔ he.
15Bɔ tsuaa bɔ nɛ pee ɔ,
e maa gbe mi sa;
i be hɛ nɔ kami ko.
Se kɛ̃ ɔ, ma fa ye he ngɛ e hɛ mi.
16Enɛ ɔ nɔuu ma he ye yi wami,
ejakaa yayami peelɔ ko be
nyɛe maa ba Mawu hɛ mi.
17Nyɛɛ bu mi tue saminya,
konɛ nɔ́ nɛ ma de ɔ nɛ sɛ nyɛ tue mi.
18Jehanɛ, i dla ye he konɛ ma jaje ye sane ɔ,
ejakaa i le kaa i yeɔ nguɔ.
19Mɛnɔ lɛ ma ye nya pomi ɔ?
Mo Mawu lo?
Ke ja a,
lɛɛ ma pee dii nɛ ma gbo mohu.
20Ha nɛ ma bi mo nɔ́ enyɔ pɛ, nɛ o ha mi,
kɛkɛ i be ye he laae ngɛ o hɛ mi.
21Kpa ye tue gblami, kɛ ye he gbeye womi.
22Mawu, moo tu munyu kekle, konɛ ma he nɔ;
aloo ke o suɔ ɔ, imi ma de kekle,
konɛ moo o he nɔ.
23Mɛni ji ye he yayami ɔmɛ?
Mɛni tɔmihi nɛ i pee?
Tsɔɔ mi ye yayami ɔmɛ, kɛ ye tɔmi ɔmɛ.
24Mɛni he je o kɛ o hɛ mi laa mi ɔ?
Mɛni he je o kɛ mi ngɛ
ní toe kaa o he nyɛlɔ ɔ?
25O ngɛ hlae nɛ o wo ye he gbeye lo?
Imi lɛɛ i ngɛ kaa ba kɛkɛ;
tsakati gbigbli se lɛ o ngɛ nyɛe ɔ nɛ.
26O po ye nya wawɛɛ nitsɛ;
yayamihi nɛ i pee ye nihe be mi hu
o ngɔ kɛ piɛ he.
27 O ngɔ ye nanehi kɛ wo pã mi.
Nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ i ngɛ pee ɔ,
o ngɛ hyɛe;
ye nane nya po o hyɛɛ fitsofitso.
28I pee kaa tso nɛ sa, nɛ hule nɔ si,
aloo bo nɛ wɔyewɔye ye.

english_text:
Job Continues His Prayer
Life Is Short and Sorrowful
1 Life is short and sorrowful
for every living soul.
2We are flowers that fade
and shadows that vanish.
3And so, I ask you, God,
why pick on me?
4There's no way a human
can be completely pure.
5Our time on earth is brief;
the number of our days
is already decided by you.
6Why don't you leave us alone
and let us find some happiness
while we toil and labor?
When a Tree Is Chopped Down
7When a tree is chopped down,
there is always the hope
that it will sprout again.
8Its roots and stump may rot,
9but at the touch of water,
it sprouts once again.
10Humans are different—
we die, and that's the end.
11We are like streams and lakes
after the water has gone;
12we fall into the sleep of death,
never to rise again,
until the sky disappears.
13Please hide me, God,
deep in the ground—
and when you are angry no more,
remember to rescue me.
Will We Humans Live Again?
14Will we humans live again?
I would gladly suffer
and wait for my time.
15My Creator, you would want me;
you would call out,
and I would answer.
16You would take care of me,
but not count my sins—
17you would put them in a bag,
tie it tight,
and toss them away.
18But in the real world,
mountains tumble,
and rocks crumble;
19streams wear away stones
and wash away soil.
And you destroy our hopes!
20You change the way we look,
then send us away,
wiped out forever.
21We never live to know
if our children are praised
or disgraced.
22We feel no pain but our own,
and when we mourn,
it's only for ourselves.
translation_text:
1Nɔmlɔ adesa wami be ngɛ kpiti kɛkɛ,
se e mi haomi hiɛ babauu.
2Nɔmlɔ waa esɔesɔ, nɛ e gboɔ tlukaa
kaa bɔ nɛ mɔmɔ hu puɛɔ nɛ e nglaa a.
E ngɛ kaa nini; bɔɔ kɛkɛ e laa nɛ a nɛ lɛ hu.
3Anɛ o kɛ imi, nɔ kaa kikɛ nɛ ɔ
maa ye sane lo?
4Anɛ nɔmlɔ adesa ko ngɛ nɛ
he tsɔ kɛ pi si lo?
Dɛbi! Nɔ ko be.
5Nɔmlɔ adesa wami se kɛmi,
kɛ hlami abɔ nɛ e maa ye ngɛ je mi ɔ,
a to ngɔ fɔ si momo.
Mo nitsɛ o ma nɔ́ nɛ ɔ nya si momo,
nɛ e be hie tsakemi.
6Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, je o hɛ ngɛ e he
nɛ e na he jɔmi.
Ha nɛ e na bua jɔmi bɔ nɛ e ma nyɛ
ngɛ e si himi nɛ he wa nɛ ɔ mi.
7Ke a po tso ngɔ fɔ si ɔ,
hɛ nɔ kami ngɛ kaa e ma tsɛ̃ ekohu;
ejakaa e hɛngmɛ ɔmɛ lɛɛ a gbo we.
8Ke sipoku ɔmɛ a se kɛ ngɛ zu mi,
nɛ tso ku ɔ sa tete po,
9ke tso ɔ na nyu ɔ, e ma tsɛ̃ ekohu,
nɛ e ma gba kɔni kaa tso nɛ a du ehe.
10Se nɔmlɔ lɛɛ ke e gbo ɔ,
e nyagbe ji lɔ ɔ nɛ.
Ke nɔmlɔ adesa gbo ɔ,
jije o maa na lɛ ngɛ ekohu?
11Kaa bɔ nɛ taku mi nyu taa,
nɛ pa mi nyu miiɔ nɛ e gbliɔ ɔ,
12jã kɛ̃ nɔmlɔ adesa hwɔɔ mahe,
nɛ e ti si hu.
E be si tee hu,
nɛ kɛ yaa si be mi nɛ hiɔwe be hu ɔ,
a be lɛ tsɛ̃ɛ̃e hu kɔkɔɔkɔ.
13I na nɛ o ngɔ mi ya laa ngɛ gbeje
kɛ yaa si o mi mi fumi ɔ se maa po;
nɛ lɔ ɔ se ɔ, o maa to be nɛ a kɛ ma kai mi.
14Ke nɔmlɔ gbo ɔ,
e kpaleɔ kɛ baa ekohu jinɛ
i ko mlɛ kɛ yaa si ye haomi be nɛ ɔ se maa po,
nɛ be kpakpa ma ba na mi.
15Jinɛ o ma tsɛ mi, nɛ ma he nɔ,
nɛ o ma na imi,
nɔmlɔ nɛ o bɔ ɔ,
ye he bua jɔmi.
16Jinɛ o maa hyɛ ye nyɛɛmi,
nɛ o be ye he yayami ɔmɛ a se die.
17O kɛ ye he yayami ɔmɛ maa pa mi,
nɛ o maa ngmɛɛ he kulaa.
Tɔmihi babauu nɛ i pee ɔ,
o maa gbe lɛ tsuo pɛpɛɛpɛ.
18Se, kaa bɔ nɛ yohi tete po huleɔ kɛ nɔɔ si,
nɛ tɛ sahi jeɔ a blɔ hehi;
19kaa bɔ nɛ nyu haa tɛ yeɔ,
nɛ pa nɛ hia muɔɔ tabo zu kɛ yaa a,
jã nɛ o haa nɛ nɔmlɔ adesa hɛ nɔ kami peeɔ yaka.
20Ke o fia lɛ nɔ́, kɛkɛ e hɛ mi tsake;
kɛkɛ a wo lɛ blɔ, nɛ e be bae hu gblegbleegble.
21Ke e gbo ɔ, e bimɛ a hɛ mi ba nyami jio,
e bimɛ a hɛ mi pue si jio, e li.
22Lɛ nitsɛ e he lo ɔ kɛkɛ nɛ e nuu he kaa
e ngɛ lɛ yee; nɛ e yeɔ kɔmɔ.

english_text:
Eliphaz's Second Speech
If You Had Any Sense
1Eliphaz from Teman said:
* 2Job, if you had any sense,
3you would stop spreading
all of this hot air.
4Your words are enough
to make others turn from God
and lead them to doubt.
5And your sinful, scheming mind
is the source of all you say.
6I am not here as your judge;
your own words are witnesses
against you.
7Were you the first human?
Are you older than the hills?
8Have you ever been present
when God's council meets?
Do you alone have wisdom?
9Do you know and understand
something we don't?
10We have the benefit of wisdom
older than your father.
11And you have been offered
comforting words from God.
Isn't this enough?
12Your emotions are out of control,
making you look fierce;
13that's why you attack God
with everything you say.
14 No human is pure and innocent,
15and neither are angels—
not in the sight of God.
If God doesn't trust his angels,
16what chance do humans have?
We are so terribly evil
that we thirst for sin.
Just Listen to What I Know
17Just listen to what I know,
and you will learn
18wisdom known by others
since ancient times.
19Those who gained such insights
also gained the land,
and they were not influenced
by foreign teachings.
20But suffering is in store
each day for those who sin.
21Even in times of success,
they constantly hear
the threat of doom.
22Darkness, despair, and death
are their destiny.
23They scrounge around for food,
all the while dreading
the approaching darkness.
24They are overcome with despair,
like frightened soldiers facing
a fearsome king in battle.
25This is because they rebelled
against God All-Powerful
26and have attacked him
with their weapons.
27They may be rich and fat,
28but they will live in the ruins
of deserted towns.
29Their property and wealth
will shrink and disappear.
30They won't escape the darkness,
and the blazing breath of God
will set their future aflame.
* 31They have put their trust
in something worthless;
now they will become worthless
32like a date palm tree
without a leaf.
33Or like vineyards or orchards
whose blossoms and unripe fruit
drop to the ground.
34Yes, the godless and the greedy
will have nothing but flames
feasting on their homes,
35because they are the parents
of trouble and vicious lies.
translation_text:
Ní sɛɛmi enyɔne
(15.1—21.34)
Elifaz
1-2Ní lelɔ pee we nya puu!
Ní lelɔ ha we sane heto kikɛ nɛ ɔ.
3Ní lelɔ tu we munyu kaa
bɔ nɛ o ngɛ munyu tue ɔ.
Ní lelɔ fa we e he kɛ munyu
nɛ he be se nami.
4E je mo nɔ kake o he jinɛ
nɔ ko nɔ ko be Mawu gbeye yee hu;
jinɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko be kue fae ha lɛ hu.
5Nɔ́ nɛ o ngɛ dee ɔ
yeɔ o he yayami ɔmɛ a he odase;
lakpa sɔuu lɛ o ngɛ yee ɔ nɛ.
6Mo nitsɛ o nya mi munyu ngɛ mo fɔ bue;
mo nitsɛ o lilɛ ngɛ odase yee kɛ ngɛ mo sie,
se pi imi.
7Mo ji kekleekle nɔmlɔ nɛ a fɔ lo?
A fɔ mo loko Mawu pee yoku ɔmɛ lo?
8O nu Mawu laami sanehi hyɛ lo?
Mo pɛ ji ní lelɔ lo?
9Mɛni o le nɛ wɔɔ lɛɛ wa li?
Mɛni o kpa si nɛ wɔɔ lɛɛ wa juɛmi sui he?
10Nihi nɛ a yi mi je mua, kɛ nikɔtɔmahi ngɛ wa kpɛti
nɛ a wa kulaa pe o tsɛ.
11Bua jɔmi nɛ Mawu ha mo ɔ,
e pi ha mo lo?
Bɔ nɛ e kɛ mo tuɔ munyu blɛuu ɔ,
lɔ ɔ sɛ́ o hɛ mi lo?
12Mɛni he je o mi mi fu kikɛ nɛ ɔ?
Mɛni he je o hɛ dɔ kikɛ nɛ ɔ?
13Mɛni he je o mi mi fu Mawu,
nɛ o ha nɛ munyuhi kaa kikɛ nɛ ɔ je o nya mi?
14 Anɛ nɔmlɔ ko ngɛ nɛ e he tsɔ lo?
Nɔmlɔ nɛ yo fɔ lɛ ɔ,
anɛ dalɔ ji lɛ ngɛ Mawu hɛ mi lo?
15Hyɛ, Mawu bɔfo klɔuklɔu ɔmɛ po
e kɛ e hɛ fɔ we a nɔ;
mɛ nitsɛmɛ tete po a he tsɔ we ngɛ e hɛ mi.
16Nɛ mo, nɔmlɔ adesa
nɛ o sa, nɛ se nami be o he ɔ!
Mo nɛ o peeɔ yayami kaa bɔ nɛ a nuu nyu kumakuma a,
kɛ maa pee kɛɛ nɛ moo o he ma tsɔ ngɛ Mawu hɛ mi?
17Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, Hiob, bu tue
nɛ ma sɛɛ mo nɔ́ nɛ i le.
Ha ma tsɔɔ mo nɔ́ nɛ i kase
kɛ je ní leli a ngɔ.
18I kase anɔkuale nɛ ɔ kɛ je ní leli a ngɔ.
Mɛ hu a kase kɛ je a tsɛmɛ a ngɔ;
a laa we nɔ́ ko nɔ́ ko nɔ.
19Mɛ pɛ lɛ a ngɔ zugba a ngɔ ha;
nubwɔ ko nubwɔ ko be a kpɛti.
20Yiwutsotsɛ, nɔ nɛ waa nihi yi mi ɔ,
e maa na nɔ́ e wami be ɔ tsuo.
21E tue mi maa hi ngmlɛ fiae kɛ wo e he gbeye.
Be mi nɛ e susu kaa e ngɛ he jɔmi mi ɔ,
ojo fiali ma ba tua lɛ tlukaa.
22Hɛ nɔ kami ko be ha lɛ kaa
e maa tu fo kɛ je diblii ɔ mi;
ejakaa klaate ji nɔ́ nɛ ngɛ lɛ mlɛe nɛ e gbe lɛ,
23nɛ okpokuhi hu ngɛ mlɛe nɛ a ye lɛ.
Nɔmlɔ kaa kikɛ nɛ ɔ le kaa
e hɛ mi kpatami be ɔ su ta.
24Fimi kɛ amanehlu woɔ e he gbeye.
E le kaa ní nɛ ɔmɛ maa ba e nɔ tlukaa
kaa matsɛ ngua ko nɛ mia kɛ ha ta.
25Nɔmlɔ nɛ teɔ si kɛ siɔ Ope ɔ,
nɛ hiaa kɔ̃ kɛ woɔ Mawu he ɔ,
nɔ́ nɛ maa ba e nɔ ji nɛ ɔ nɛ.
26-27Jamɛ a nɔmlɔ ɔ,
he nɔ wolɔ, kɛ atuã tsɔlɔ ji lɛ;
e kɛ he nɔ womi woɔ e tsɛ̃i nɔ,
nɛ e he sɔɔ nɛ e kɛ Mawu ya hwu ta.
28Jamɛ a nɔmlɔ ɔ ya ngɔ mahi, kɛ wehi
nɛ nɔtsɛmɛ tu fo kɛ je a mi.
Se a de to kaa ta ma kpata
jamɛ a ma amɛ, kɛ we ɔmɛ a hɛ mi.
29E ní nami ɔ se be kɛe;
e nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ hɛ mi ma kpata.
Lɛ nitsɛ e nini tete po maa laa,
30nɛ diblii maa wo lɛ.
E maa pee kaa tso nɛ la sã e kɔnihi,
nɛ kɔɔhiɔ muɔ e mɔmɔ ɔmɛ kɛ ho.
31Ke e ya sisi e he,
nɛ e ngɔ e hɛ ngɔ fɔ níhi nɛ a he be se nami a nɔ ɔ,
e maa je mi dɛ gu.
32Loko e nyagbe ɔ maa su ɔ,
e ma na e hiɔwo sisiisi;
e maa pee kaa tso
nɛ ba mumu be e yi mi.
33E maa pee kaa wai tso
nɛ e yi mi wai yiblii ngmlikiti kplɔ pue si,
aloo oliv tso nɛ e mɔmɔhi kplɔ pue si.
34Nimli nɛ li Mawu ɔ,
a be ngmɛdu woe.
Wehi nɛ a he nyɔ mi ní nɛ a kɛ ma mɛ ɔ,
la maa sã mɛ pue si.
35Nimli nɛ ɔmɛ ji ni nɛmɛ nɛ toɔ ga yaya,
nɛ a peeɔ yayami;
sisimi hyi a tsui mi tɔtɔɔtɔ.

english_text:
Job's Reply to Eliphaz
I Have Often Heard This
1Job said:
2I have often heard this,
and it offers no comfort.
3So why don't you keep quiet?
What's bothering you?
4If I were in your place,
it would be easy to criticize
or to give advice.
5But I would offer hope
and comfort instead.
6If I speak, or if I don't,
I hurt all the same.
My torment continues.
7God has worn me down
and destroyed my family;
8my shriveled up skin proves
that I am his prisoner.
9God is my hateful enemy,
glaring at me and attacking
with his sharp teeth.
10Everyone is against me;
they sneer and slap my face.
11And God is the one
who handed me over
to this merciless mob.
Everything Was Going Well
12Everything was going well,
until God grabbed my neck
and shook me to pieces.
God set me up as the target
13for his arrows,
and without showing mercy,
he slashed my stomach open,
spilling out my insides.
14God never stops attacking,
15and so, in my sorrow
I dress in sackcloth
and sit in the dust.
16My face is red with tears,
and dark shadows
circle my eyes,
17though I am not violent,
and my prayers are sincere.
18If I should die,
I beg the earth not to cover
my cry for justice.
19 Even now, God in heaven
is both my witness
and my protector.
20My friends have rejected me,
but God is the one I beg
21to show that I am right,
just as a friend should.
22Because in only a few years,
I will be dead and gone.
translation_text:
Hiob
1-2I nu munyuhi babauu kaa kikɛ nɛ ɔ hyɛ;
ye bua nɛ nyɛ ke nyɛ ma womi ɔ,
haomi mohu lɛ nyɛ ba ngɛ mi haoe.
3Nyɛ maa hi yaka munyu nɛ ɔmɛ tue
nɛ nyɛ be kpae lo?
Mɛni hiɔ lɛ nyɛ ngɛ nue
nɛ nyɛ maa hi munyu tue kpamisa kikɛ nɛ ɔ?
4Níhi nɛ nyɛ ngɛ dee nɛ ɔ,
imi hu i ko de ja nɔuu.
I ko mimiɛ ye yi,
nɛ ma ha nyɛ munyu nguahi.
5Jinɛ ma wo nyɛ ga,
nɛ ma tu munyu kɛ wo nyɛ bua.
6Se amlɔ nɛ ɔ, i tu munyu jio,
i ma ye nya jio,
haomi kake too ɔ mi lɛ i ngɛ kpamisa.
7Mawu, jehanɛ lɛɛ o ha nɛ pɔ tɔ mi;
o gbe ye he nihi tsuo ta.
8O ha nɛ ye he womi tsuo hlũɛ, nɛ i ta he lo,
nɛ enɛ ɔmɛ yeɔ odase kɛ siɔ mi.
9Mawu mi mi fu mi, nɛ e tsɔtslɔɔ ye mi.
E kpɔ lungu ngɔ wo mi,
nɛ e muɔ e hɛngmɛ ngɔ pue ye nɔ
kaa a peeɔ nɔ he nyɛlɔ.
10Nihi yeɔ ye he fɛu.
A buaa kɛ woɔ ye he, nɛ a gbaa ye tue mi ma.
Nɛ a bɔɔ mi ahlua.
11Mawu ngɔ mi ngɔ ha nihi nɛ li Mawu;
e ngɔ mi ngɔ wo yiwutsotsɛmɛ a dɛ mi.
12Jinɛ i ngɛ he mi jɔmi,
se Mawu tsɔtslɔɔ ye mi.
Mawu nu ye kuɛ, nɛ e ku mi dukuduku.
E je hɛ pi mi kaa nɔ́ ko
nɛ e kɛ maa kase dɛ nya dami.
13E tsɛ̃ɔ mi kɛ̃ɛ̃ kɛ jeɔ he tsuaa he.
Kɛ̃ɛ̃ mi bi ɔmɛ sɛɛ ye he womi mi, nɛ a plaa mi;
se Mawu nɛ mi mɔbɔ.
14E he sɔɔ kɛ ba tuaa mi nɔtonɔto,
nɛ e plaa mi kaa tatsɛ nɛ hɛ dɔ.
15I kpɛ kpekpe ngɔ ha ye he,
nɛ i hii si ngɛ zugba kɛ
ngɛ kɔmɔ yee.
16I fo ya hluu kɛ ya si ye hɛngmɛ ɔmɛ fuu
nɛ a pee kɔu kaa nɔ́ nɛ nɔ́ ko ha a nɔ.
17Se i yi nɔ ko amimi;
i faa kue haa Mawu kɛ jeɔ ye tsui mi.
18Zugba, yayamihi nɛ a pee mi ɔ, koo ha a nɔ!
Ngmlaa nɛ i ngɛ kpae kaa a ye dami sane ha mi ɔ,
ko ha nɛ ngmlaa a nya nɛ ba si!
19 Amlɔ nɛ ɔ tete po,
ye we odase ngɛ hiɔwe;
nɔ nɛ ma fa ye he ɔ
ngɛ hiɔwe lokoo.
20Ye huɛmɛ ɔmɛ yeɔ ye he fɛu,
se i faa kue haa Mawu kɛ vo nyu.
21I na nɛ nɔ ko ma fa ye he ngɛ Mawu hɛ mi
kaa bɔ nɛ nɔmlɔ adesa faa e nyɛmi he ɔ.
22Jehahi bɔɔ komɛ a se ɔ,
ma hia blɔ kɛ ya he ko
nɛ i be kpalee kɛ ba hu.

english_text:
Job Complains to God
My Hopes Have Died
1My hopes have died,
my time is up,
and the grave is ready.
2All I can see are angry crowds,
making fun of me.
3If you, Lord, don't help,
who will pay the price
for my release?
4My friends won't really listen,
all because of you,
and so you must be the one
to prove them wrong.
5They have condemned me,
just to benefit themselves;
now blind their children.
6You, God, are the reason
I am insulted and spit on.
7I am almost blind with grief;
my body is a mere shadow.
8People who are truly good
would feel so alarmed,
that they would become angry
with my worthless friends.
9They would do the right thing
and because they did,
they would grow stronger.
10But none of my friends
show any sense.
11My life is drawing to an end;
hope has disappeared.
12But all my friends can do
is offer empty hopes.
13I could tell the world below
to prepare me a bed.
14Then I could greet the grave
as my father
and say to the worms,
“Hello, mother and sisters!”
15But what kind of hope is that?
16Will it keep me company
in the world of the dead?
translation_text:
1Ye wami be ɔ ta; i nyɛ we nɛ i ngɛ mumi woe.
Amlɔ nɛ ɔ lɛɛ nɔ́ nɛ ngɛ mi mlɛe ji yɔkɔ.
2He fɛu yeli bɔle mi kɛ kpe;
niinɛ, i naa mɛ nɛ a hii ye he fɛu yee.
3Mawu, anɔkualetsɛ ji mi;
mo he mi nɛ o ye.
Nɔ́ nɛ i ngɛ dee ɔ,
nɔ kpa ko be nɛ ma fi se.
4O ha nɛ nimli adesahi biɛ,
nɛ a susuu we a yi mi;
lɔ ɔ he ɔ, ko ha nɛ a ye ye nɔ.
5Nimeli ke, “Nɔ nɛ tsɔɔ e huɛmɛ a se blɔ,
nɛ e nine suu a weto ní nɔ ɔ,
e bimɛ a hɛngmɛ ma yu.”
6Mwɔnɛ ɔ, i plɛ pee abɛ bumi nɔ́ ha nihi,
nɛ a laa lada kɛ pueɔ ye hɛ mi.
7Aywilɛho sɔuu ha nɛ ye hɛngmɛ nɔ pee kɔu,
nɛ ye kɔnihi, kɛ ye nanehi pee legelege kaa nini.
8Ke dali na nɔ́ nɛ ɔ, a he mi jɔ̃ɔ̃,
nɛ a tuɔ a hɛ mi kɛ woɔ nihi nɛ li Mawu.
9Se bɔ tsuaa bɔ nɛ pee ɔ,
dalɔ hii e blɔ nɔ kɛ̃.
Nɔmlɔ nɛ yayami ko be e he ɔ,
e naa he wami he ekohu.
10Se nyɛɛ lɛɛ, i nɛ ní lelɔ kake ngmelu
ngɛ nyɛ tsuo nyɛ kpɛti.
11Ye ligbi ɔmɛ ta; ye yi mi tomi ɔmɛ puɛ;
ye hɛ kɛ nɔ fɔmi ɔ ta.
12Se ye huɛmɛ ɔmɛ ngɔɔ nyɔ kɛ peeɔ piani.
La a nɛ a ngɛ dee ɔ hu ngɛ kaa diblii.
13Ye hɛ nɔ kami kɛkɛ ji gbeje;
lejɛ ɔ ji he nɛ ma hwɔ ngɛ diblii mi.
14Ma tsɛ yɔkɔ ɔ ke tsaatsɛ;
gɔgɔhi nɛ maa ye mi ɔ,
ma tsɛ mɛ maa, kɛ ye nyɛmiyihi.
15Jije hɛ nɔ kami pa ngɛ ha mi?
Mɛnɔ lɛ maa na jamɛ a hɛ nɔ kami ɔ?
16Anɛ hɛ nɔ kami kɛ mi maa ya gbeje lo?
Anɛ e kɛ mi maa ya zu mi lo?

english_text:
Bildad's Second Speech
How Long Will You Talk?
1Bildad from Shuah said:
2How long will you talk?
Be sensible! Let us speak.
3Or do you think that we
are dumb animals?
4You cut yourself in anger.
Will that shake the earth
or even move the rocks?
* 5 The lamps of sinful people
soon are snuffed out,
6leaving their tents dark.
7Their powerful legs become weak,
and they stumble on schemes
of their own doing.
* 8Before they know it,
9they are trapped in a net,
10hidden along the path.
11Terror strikes and pursues
from every side.
12Starving, they run,
only to meet disaster,
13then afterwards to be eaten alive
by death itself.
14Those sinners are dragged
from the safety of their tents
to die a gruesome death.
15Then their tents and possessions
are burned to ashes,
16and they are left like trees,
dried up from the roots.
17They are gone and forgotten,
18thrown far from the light
into a world of darkness,
19without any children
to carry on their name.
20Everyone, from east to west,
is overwhelmed with horror.
21Such is the fate of sinners
and their families
who don't know God.
translation_text:
Bildad
1-2Hiob, mɛni be lɛ o maa hi munyu tue kɛ yaa si?
Ke o pee dii ɔ, waa kɛ mo maa tu munyu.
3Mɛni he je a buɔ wɔ kaa lohwehi ɔ?
Mɛni he je o susuɔ kaa wa be juɛmi ɔ?
4Nɛ o ngɔ abofu kɛ ngɛ mo nitsɛ o he tsɔtslɔɔe ɔ nɛɛ!
Ke o mi mi fu ɔ, enɛ ɔ tsɔɔ kaa
nihi nɛ a je je ɔ mi lo?
Aloo o ngɛ hlae nɛ a hia tɛ sahi
kɛ je a blɔ hehi lo?
5 Ee, yayami peelɔ kane ɔ ma gbo,
nɛ e la a be kpɛe hu gblegbleegble.
6E kane ɔ ma gbo ngɛ e kasa nya,
nɛ e bo tsu ɔ mi maa wo diblii.
7Bɔ nɛ e hiaa nane kam, kam, kam be ko nɛ be ɔ,
amlɔ nɛ ɔ lɛɛ e hii si tɛe;
lɛ nitsɛ e yi mi tomi maa tsɛ̃ lɛ kɛ nɔ si.
8Lɛ nitsɛ e maa ngɔ e nane kɛ ya du ya;
lɛ nitsɛ e maa nyɛɛ kɛ ya nɔ muɔ mi.
9E nane se ja ma ya sɛ klama mi,
nɛ klama a maa nu lɛ.
10A maa tsɔ̃ lɛ klama kɛ laa ngɛ zugba;
a maa tsɔ̃ lɛ klama ngɛ e blɔ mi.
11Gbeye níhi maa bɔle lɛ kɛ kpe,
nɛ daa nɛ ɔ, e maa hi fo nɔ kpla, kpla, kpla!
12Hwɔ maa ye lɛ hluu kɛ yaa si e he wami maa ta.
Amanehlu maa tsɛ̃ lɛ kɛ fɔ si bum!
13Hiɔ yaya maa ha e he womi tsuo nɔ,
nɛ e kɔnihi, kɛ e nanehi maa sa ngɛ e he.
14E bo tsu ɔ nɛ e ngɔ e hɛ ngɔ fɔ nɔ ɔ,
a maa gbla lɛ kɛ je lejɛ ɔ
kɛ ba he ko nɛ ngɛ gbeyegbeye.
15Nɔ́ ko nɔ́ ko be piɛe
ngɛ e sihi he ɔ.
La nɛ ngɛ tsoe plamplam maa sã e bo tsu ɔ.
16E sipoku ma gbli ngɛ e sisi,
nɛ e kɔnihi maa ylɔ.
17E biɛ maa laa ngɛ ma a mi, kɛ ma se tsuo,
nɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko be lɛ kaie hu.
18A maa fie lɛ kɛ je je ɔ mi,
kɛ je la he kɛ ya diblii mi.
19E be bi, loo nina ngɛ e ma mi bi ɔmɛ a kpɛti;
he nɛ e hi be ko ɔ, e nina ko be lejɛ ɔ.
20Kɛ je beleku je kɛ yaa si bonyoku je ɔ;
nihi nɛ maa nu e haomi ɔmɛ a he ɔ,
mɛ tsuo pɛpɛɛpɛ a he mi maa po.
21Yayami peelɔ, aloo nɔmlɔ nɛ li Mawu ɔ,
nɔ́ nɛ maa ba e nɔ ji nɛ ɔ nɛ.

english_text:
Job's Reply to Bildad
How Long Will You Torture Me?
1Job said:
2How long will you torture me
with your words?
3Isn't ten times enough
for you to accuse me?
Aren't you ashamed?
4Even if I have sinned,
you haven't been harmed.
5You boast of your goodness,
claiming I am suffering
because I am guilty.
6But God is the one at fault
for finding fault with me.
7Though I pray to be rescued
from this torment,
no whisper of justice
answers me.
8God has me trapped
with a wall of darkness
9and stripped of respect.
10God rips me apart,
uproots my hopes,
11and attacks with fierce anger,
as though I were his enemy.
12His entire army advances,
then surrounds my tent.
I Am Forgotten
* 13God has turned relatives
and friends against me,
14and I am forgotten.
15My guests and my servants
consider me a stranger,
16and when I call my servants,
they pay no attention.
17My breath disgusts my wife;
everyone in my family
turns away.
18Young children can't stand me,
and when I come near,
they make fun.
19 My best friends and loved ones
have turned from me.
20I am skin and bones—
just barely alive.
21My friends, I beg you for pity!
God has made me his target.
22Hasn't he already done enough?
Why do you join the attack?
23I wish that my words
could be written down
24or chiseled into rock.
25I know that my Protector lives,
and at the end
he will stand on this earth.
26My flesh may be destroyed,
yet from this body
I will see God.
27Yes, I will see him for myself,
and I long for that moment.
28My friends, you think up ways
to blame and torment me, saying
I brought it on myself.
29But watch out for the judgment,
when God will punish you!
translation_text:
Hiob
1-2Mɛni be nyɛ maa ngɔ munyuhi
kɛ hao mi kɛ yaa si?
3Kpamisa nɛ ɔ,
jɛmi kɛkɛ nyɛ ngɛ mi jɛe.
Anɛ e pee we nyɛ zo kaa
nyɛ ngɛ mi nisɛ ní pee lo?
4Ke e ngɛ mi tete po kaa i pee yayami ɔ,
mɛni enɛ ɔ kɔɔ ngɛ nyɛ he?
5Nyɛ woɔ nyɛ he nɔ,
nɛ nyɛ susuɔ kaa nyɛ hi pe mi.
Nyɛ deɔ ke ye yayami ɔmɛ
a he hiɔ lɛ a ngɛ mi woe ɔ nɛ.
6Se nyɛ li kaa Mawu lɛ pee nɔ́ nɛ ɔ lo?
Lɛ nɛ tsɔ klama kɛ bɔle mi kɛ kpe.
7Hyɛ, i kpaa ngmlaa nɛ i deɔ ke Mawu ngɛ mi awi yee,
se nɔ ko nɔ ko he we nɔ.
Ngmlaa nɛ i ngɛ kpae ke a ye dami sane ha mi ɔ,
nɔ ko nɔ ko nui.
8Mawu tsi mi blɔ nɛ i nyɛ we ma be;
e ha nɛ diblii wo ngɛ ye blɔ nɔ.
9E je ye hɛ mi nyami ɔ ngɛ ye he,
nɛ e kpɔ ye jlasi ɔ ngɛ ye yi mi.
10E kpata ye hɛ mi,
nɛ e kɛ mi gbe nya pɛsɛpɛsɛ.
I pee kaa tso nɛ a hia lɛ kɛ e sipoku tsuo;
ye hɛ kɛ nɔ fɔmi ta.
11Mawu mi mi fu mi wawɛɛ nitsɛ,
nɛ e buɔ mi e he nyɛlɔ.
12E ta buli babauu ba tua mi;
a bɔle mi kɛ kpe,
nɛ a sa ye yi kɛ wo ye sihi he ɔ.
13Mawu ha nɛ ye nyɛmimɛ kua mi;
i plɛ pee nubwɔ ngɛ nihi
nɛ i le mɛ ɔ a kpɛti.
14Ye weku li je ye he,
nɛ ye huɛ kpakpahi a hɛ je ye nɔ.
15Nibwɔhi nɛ ngɛ ye we mi ɔ,
a hɛ je ye nɔ;
i plɛ pee nubwɔ, loo ma se no
ngɛ ye mawayihi a hɛ mi.
16Ke i tsɛ ye tsɔlɔ ɔ, e he we nɔ;
ke i kpa lɛ pɛɛ tete po, e bui.
17Ye nya mi mumi jeɔ fu kɛ haa ye yo;
imi nitsɛ ye nyɛ mi mi bimɛ
bɛ ye kasa nya.
18Jokuɛwi tete po hiee mi;
ke a na mi pɛ,
kɛkɛ a bɔni ye he munyu tumi.
19Ye huɛmɛ kpakpahi tsuo ngɛ mi hiee;
ni nɛmɛ nɛ i suɔ mɛ saminya po te si wo mi.
20I ta he lo nɛ i pee kanyakanya;
i kɛ gbenɔ wa kpɛti kɛ we kulaa.
21Nyɛɛ na mi mɔbɔ;
ye huɛmɛ nyɛɛ na mi mɔbɔ,
ejakaa Mawu nine sa ye he.
22Mɛni he je nyɛ ngɛ mi yi mi wae
kaa bɔ nɛ Mawu peeɔ mi ɔ?
Bɔ nɛ nyɛ hao mi ɔ,
e pi ha nyɛ lo?
23Níhi nɛ i ngɛ dee ɔ,
i na nɛ nɔ ko kai
nɛ e ngma kɛ wo womi mi!
24I ná nɛ a kɛ dade kpɛ́ ye munyu
ɔmɛ ngɛ tɛ sa mi,
nɛ a kɛ sumui wo mi,
konɛ a hi lejɛ ɔ daa.
25Ejakaa i le kaa nɔ ko ngɛ hiɔwe
nɛ nyagbenyagbe ɔ,
e ma ba kpɔ mi.
26Ke ye he womi hɛ mi kpata kikɛ nɛ ɔ,
nɛ he lo ko be ye he po,
ma na Mawu.
27Imi nitsɛ na lɛ paa kɛ ye hɛngmɛ.
Imi nitsɛnitsɛ,
se pi nɔ kpa ko.
Ye tsui ta!
28Benɛ nyɛ bi ke,
“Kɛ wa maa pee kɛɛ kɛ wa lɛ yi mi?” ɔ,
nyɛ hla nɔ ko nyɛ da nɔ,
nɛ nyɛ ba tua mi.
29Nyɛ na nɛ nyɛɛ le
kaa tue gblami fɔɔ si ha nyɛ.
A maa gbla nyɛ tue ngɛ nyɛ he yayami ɔmɛ a he,
konɛ nyɛɛ le kaa kojolɔ ko ngɛ.

english_text:
Zophar's Second Speech
Your Words Are Disturbing
1Zophar from Naamah said:
2Your words are disturbing;
now I must speak.
3You have accused
and insulted me,
and reason requires a reply.
4Since the time of creation,
everyone has known
5that sinful people are happy
for only a while.
6Though their pride and power
may reach to the sky,
7they will disappear like dust,
and those who knew them
will wonder what happened.
8 They will be forgotten
like a dream
9and vanish from the sight
of family and friends.
10Their children will have to repay
what the parents took
from the poor.
11Indeed, the wicked will die
and go to their graves
in the prime of life.
Sinners Love the Taste of Sin
12Sinners love the taste of sin;
they relish every bite
13and swallow it slowly.
14But their food will turn sour
and poison their stomachs.
15Then God will make them lose
the wealth they gobbled up.
16They will die from the fangs
of poisonous snakes
17and never enjoy rivers flowing
with milk and honey.
18Their hard work will result
in nothing gained,
19because they cheated the poor
and took their homes.
20Greedy people want everything
and are never satisfied.
21But when nothing remains
for them to grab,
they will be nothing.
22Once they have everything,
distress and despair
will strike them down,
23and God will make them swallow
his blazing anger.
24 While running from iron spears,
they will be killed
by arrows of bronze,
25whose shining tips go straight
through their bodies.
They will be trapped by terror,
26and what they treasure most
will be lost in the dark.
God will send flames
to destroy them in their tents
with all their property.
27The heavens and the earth
will testify against them,
28and all their possessions
will be dragged off
when God becomes angry.
29This is what God has decided
for those who are evil.
translation_text:
Zofar
1-2Hiob, o ha nɛ ye yi mi pee basaa,
enɛ ɔ he je ɔ, ma ha mo heto nɔuu.
3Jɛmi munyuhi lɛ o tu ɔ nɛ,
se mumi ɔ tsɔɔ mi bɔ nɛ ma ha mo heto ha.
4I heɔ yeɔ kaa o le nɔ́ nɛ ɔ,
kaa kɛ je blema lokoo nɛ a
bɔ nɔmlɔ kɛ wo je ɔ mi ɔ,
5yiwutsotsɛ hɛ mi nyami ɔ,
e se kɛ we;
nɛ nɔmlɔ nɛ li Mawu ɔ,
e bua jɔmi peeɔ kuku kɛkɛ.
6Ke e nɔ kuɔ kɛ ya su hiɔwe,
nɛ e yi ya pi bɔku po,
7e hɛ mi ma kpata
kɛ maa ya neneene
kaa lɛ nitsɛ e fĩ.
Nihi nɛ le lɛ ɔ ma bi ke,
“Jije e ngɛ?”
8E maa laa kaa nlami,
aloo nina nɛ a na nyɔ mi;
nɛ nɔ ko be lɛ nae hu.
9Nɔ ko nɔ ko be lɛ nae hu;
e sihi he ɔ maa fɔ si gu.
10Níhi nɛ e ju ngɛ ohiatsɛmɛ a dɛ ɔ,
e bimɛ maa kpale kɛ ha mɛ ekohu.
11Nɔmlɔ tso kɛ e he nihe nyu tsuaa a
ma plɛ pee zu.
12-13Yayami ngɔɔ e nya.
E ngɛ kaa dɔkɔdɔkɔ nɔ́ ko
nɛ e ngɔ kɛ laa ngɛ e lilɛ kuɔ si.
E hii he gbugbɔe,
nɛ e sume kaa e ma je ngɛ e nya mi.
14Se niye ní nɛ ɔ plɛɔ peeɔ sinɔ duɔ
nɛ nya wa ngɛ e mi mi.
15Ní kpakpahi nɛ yayami peelɔ mi ɔ,
e vieɔ kɛ pueɔ si ekohu.
Mawu nitsɛ jeɔ ní ɔmɛ
kɛ jeɔ e mi mi.
16Nɔ́ nɛ yayami peelɔ gbugbɔ ɔ
ngɛ kaa sinɔ duɔ;
e maa gbe lɛ kaa
nɔ́ nɛ sinɔ duɔtsɛ nɛ kɔ lɛ.
17E be je mi hie nɛ́ e maa na
nyɔ nyu, kɛ hwo nɛ ngɛ bee kaa paa.
18Nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ e gbo he dengme
nɛ e na a maa je e dɛ,
nɛ e be e mi ngɔɔmi ko yee.
E be bua jɔmi ko nae kɛ je e ní nɛ e na a mi.
19Ejakaa e wa ohiatsɛmɛ yi mi,
nɛ e kua mɛ;
wehi nɛ nihi ma a,
e kpɔ ngɛ a dɛ pani nya.
20Akɛnɛ e li tɔ biɛ he je ɔ,
nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ e na a,
e yeɔ tsuatsuaatsua.
21Ke e ye ní ɔ,
eko kulaa píɛ ngɛ se.
Enɛ ɔ he je ɔ,
ní nami ɔ se maa po.
22Be mi nɛ e na e he ɔ,
jamɛ a be ɔ,
haomi nɛ nya wa maa ba e nɔ tlukaa.
23Mawu ma ha e mi mi la nɛ nya wa a ma kple e nɔ
kaa niye ní nɛ e ye nɛ e tɔ.
24Ke e ka kaa e maa tu fo kɛ je dade nya a,
a ma tsɛ̃ lɛ akɔblee kɛ̃ɛ̃ kɛ fɔ si.
25A maa gbla kɛ̃ɛ̃ mi bi kɛ je e nɔmlɔ tso mi.
Muɔ maa dɛ kɛ je kɛ̃ɛ̃ mi bi ɔ nya piɔpiɔ
nɛ ngɛ kpɛe ɔ he kɛ pue si,
nɛ gbeye maa nu lɛ.
26E juetli tsuo hɛ mi ma kpata.
La, nɛ pi nɔmlɔ nɛ slɛ maa sã lɛ,
nɛ e we mi nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ hɛ mi ma kpata.
27Hiɔwe ma je nyumu nɛ ɔ yayami ɔ kpo,
nɛ zugba maa ye odase kɛ si lɛ.
28Ligbi ɔ nɛ Mawu mi mi ma fu ɔ,
a ma kpata nɔmlɔ nɛ ɔ weto ní tsuo hɛ mi
kaa bɔ nɛ pa muɔɔ níhi kɛ yaa a.
29Enɛ ɔ ji yayami peelɔ blɔ fa mi nɔ́;
gbosi ní nɛ Mawu to
kɛ ha yayami peelɔ ji nɛ ɔ nɛ.

english_text:
Job's Reply to Zophar
If You Want To Offer Comfort
1Job said:
2If you want to offer comfort,
then listen to me.
3And when I have finished,
you can start your insults
all over again.
4My complaint is against God;
that's why I am impatient.
5Just looking at me is enough
to make you sick,
6and the very thought of myself
fills me with disgust.
7Why do evil people live so long
and gain such power?
8Why are they allowed to see
their children grow up?
9They have no worries at home,
and God never punishes them.
10Their cattle have lots of calves
without ever losing one;
11their children play and dance
safely by themselves.
12These people sing and celebrate
to the sound of tambourines,
small harps, and flutes,
13and they are successful,
without a worry,
until the day they die.
Leave Us Alone!
14Those who are evil say
to God All-Powerful,
“Leave us alone! Don't bother us
with your teachings.
15What do we gain from praying
and worshiping you?
16We succeeded all on our own.”
And so, I keep away from them
and their evil schemes.
17How often does God become angry
and send disaster and darkness
to punish sinners?
18How often does he strike them
like a windstorm
that scatters straw?
19You say, “God will punish
those sinners' children
in place of those sinners.”
But I say, “Let him punish
those sinners themselves
until they really feel it.
20Let God All-Powerful force them
to drink their own destruction
from the cup of his anger.
21Because after they are dead,
they won't care what happens
to their children.”
Who Can Tell God What To Do?
22Who can tell God what to do?
He judges powerful rulers.
* 23Some of us die prosperous,
24enjoying good health,
25while others die in poverty,
having known only pain.
26But we all end up dead,
beneath a blanket of worms.
27My friends, I know that you
are plotting against me.
28You ask, “Where is the home
of that important person
who does so much evil?”
29Everyone, near and far, agrees
30that those who do wrong
never suffer disaster,
when God becomes angry.
31No one points out their sin
or punishes them.
32Then at their funerals,
they are highly praised;
33the earth welcomes them home,
while crowds mourn.
34But empty, meaningless words
are the comfort you offer me.
translation_text:
Hiob
1-2Nyɛɛ bu nɔ́ nɛ ma de nɛ ɔ tue saminya;
ke nyɛ pee ja a,
e ngɛ kaa nɔ́ nɛ nyɛ ba jɔɔ ye bua.
3Nyɛɛ ngmɛ mi blɔ nɛ imi hu ma tu munyu;
ke i de nɔ́ nɛ ma de ɔ ta a,
nyɛ ma nyɛ maa ye ye he fɛu faa.
4Imi ɔ, tsa pi nɔmlɔ adesa nɛ i kɛ na;
i kɛ Mawu lɛ na.
Mɛni he je e sɛ kaa ye susuma haoɔ mɔ?
5Nyɛɛ hyɛ mi ha! Anɛ bɔ nɛ i ngɛ nɛ ɔ
ha we nɛ nyɛ he mi nɛ po,
nɛ nyɛɛ pee dii lo?
6Nɔ́ nɛ ba ye nɔ nɛ ɔ,
ke i susu he ɔ,
ye he mi poɔ,
nɛ ye nɔmlɔ tso ɔ doɔ blibliibli.
7Mɛni he je yayami peeli a se kɛɔ ngɛ je mi?
Mɛni he je a peeɔ nimli nguahi,
nɛ a bwɔɔ kotokoto loko a gboɔ ɔ?
8A hii je mi kɛ ya siɔ a bimɛ,
kɛ a bibimɛ waa ba naa mɛ.
9Mawu ngɔɛ haomi ko kɛ bɛ a wehi a mi;
nɔ́ ko nɔ́ ko wui a he gbeye.
10Niinɛ, a na ku ɔmɛ, kɛ na yi ɔmɛ naa bɔmi pɛpɛɛpɛ,
nɛ na yi ɔmɛ fɔɔ nɛ nɔ́ ko pee we mɛ.
11A bi tsɔwitsɔwihi jeɔ kpo babauu
nɛ a hii hlue kaa to bihi.
12A fiɛɔ do, a fiaa saku,
nɛ a laa kɛ toɔ he;
nɛ a naa bua jɔmi bɔ nɛ sa.
13A yeɔ a be ɔ ngɛ kplɔkɔtɔ mi,
nɛ a gboɔ ngɛ tue mi jɔmi mi.
14Yayami peeli deɔ Mawu ke e je a nɔ,
ejakaa a hla we e blɔ ɔmɛ nɛ a le.
15A biɔ ke,
“Mɛnɔ ji Ope ɔ
nɛ saa kaa wa sɔmɔɔ lɛ ɔ?
Ke wa fa kue ha lɛ ɔ,
mɛni se wa ma na?”
16A deɔ ke,
“Tsa pi nɔ ko nɛ wo wɔ ní;
wɔ nitsɛmɛ lɛ wa tsu nɛ wa na.”
Se a susumi nɛ ɔ,
imi i ngɔɛ.
17Anɛ yayami peelɔ ko kane gbo hyɛ lo?
Anɛ haomi ba a ti nɔ ko nɔ hyɛ lo?
Anɛ Mawu kɛ abofu gbla yayami peelɔ ko tue hyɛ lo?
18Anɛ Mawu muɔ yayami peeli kɛ ho hyɛ
kaa bɔ nɛ kɔɔhiɔ muɔɔ bunyuku,
aloo bɔ nɛ ahumi muɔɔ tsakati kɛ yaa a lo?
19Nyɛ deɔ ke Mawu gblaa bimɛ a tue
ngɛ a tsɛmɛ a he yayamihi a he.
Dɛbi! Ha nɛ Mawu ɔ nɛ gbla yayami peeli ɔmɛ
nitsɛmɛ a tue,
konɛ a na kaa a he yayami
ɔmɛ a he lɛ a ngɛ a tue gblae ɔ nɛ.
20Ha nɛ yayami peeli ɔmɛ nitsɛmɛ
nɛ a ná a tue gblami ɔ.
Ha nɛ Mawu Ope ɔ we abofu ɔ
nɛ kple mɛ nitsɛmɛ a nɔ.
21Ke nɔ ko gbo ɔ,
anɛ e pa susuɔ
bimɛ nɛ e si ngɛ se ɔ a he lo?
22Mawu nɛ tsɔɔ nimli nguahi po nile ɔ,
anɛ nɔ ko ma nyɛ maa kojo lɛ lo?
23-24Ni komɛ hii nɔmlɔ tso he wami
hluu kɛ ya siɔ a gbenɔ be.
A plɔkeɔ nɛ a peeɔ tɔfutɔfu,
nɛ a gboɔ kɛ bua jɔmi ngɛ tue mi jɔmi mi.
25Ni komɛ hu gboɔ kɛ aywilɛho
nɛ a na we bua jɔmi ko hyɛ.
26Nimli nɛ ɔmɛ tsuo gboɔ,
nɛ a puɔ mɛ ngɛ zu mi,
nɛ gɔgɔ ba haa mɛ tsuo a nɔ.
27Hyɛ, i le nyɛ juɛmi ɔmɛ!
Ga nɛ nyɛ to nɛ nyɛɛ
kɛ maa wa mi yi mi ɔ, i le.
28Nyɛ biɔ ke,
“Jehanɛ lɛɛ jije ganɔ ɔ we ɔ ngɛ?
Jije yiwutsotsɛmɛ ɔmɛ a sihi he ɔmɛ ngɛ?”
29Anɛ nyɛɛ kɛ blɔ hiali sɛɛ we ní lo?
Níhi nɛ a ba deɔ nyɛ ɔ,
nyɛ ngɔɛ lo?
30Anɛ nyɛ li kaa ke
amanehlu ba a, yiwutsotsɛmɛ
lɛɛ a jeɔ mɛ kɛ jeɔ mi,
nɛ a yeɔ a he lo?
31Mɛnɔ lɛ ma ka yiwutsotsɛ hɛ mi?
Níhi nɛ e peeɔ ɔ,
mɛnɔ lɛ maa pee lɛ kɛ to nane mi?
32Benɛ a hɛɛ lɛ kɛ yaa gɔ ɔ mi ɔ,
jamɛ a be ɔ, nihi daa si
nɛ a ngɛ e yɔkɔ ɔ he bue.
33Nimli babauu nyɛɛɔ e hɛ mi,
nɛ babauu hu nyɛɛɔ e se;
tabo zu ɔ po peeɔ huyɛhuyɛ ngɛ e nɔ.
34Nɛ nyɛɛ lɛɛ nyɛɛ
kɛ munyu gu ba ngɛ ye bua jɔɔe!
Hetohi nɛ nyɛ ha mi ɔ, lakpa sɔuu;
anɔkuale kake ngmelu be mi.

english_text:
Eliphaz's Third Speech
What Use Are We Humans to God?
1Eliphaz from Teman said:
2 What use are we humans
to God,
even the wisest of us?
3If you were completely sinless,
that would still mean nothing
to God All-Powerful.
4Is he correcting you
for worshiping him?
5No! It's because of
your terrible and endless sins.
6To guarantee payment of a debt,
you have taken clothes
from innocent people.
7And you refused bread and water
to the hungry and thirsty,
8although you were rich,
respected, and powerful.
9You have turned away widows
and have broken the arms
of orphans.
10That's why you were suddenly
trapped by terror,
11blinded by darkness,
and drowned in a flood.
God Lives in the Heavens
12God lives in the heavens
above the highest stars,
where he sees everything.
13Do you think the deep darkness
hides you from God?
14Do thick clouds cover his eyes,
as he walks around heaven's dome
high above the earth?
15Give up those ancient ideas
believed by sinners,
16who were swept away
without warning.
17They rejected God All-Powerful,
feeling he was helpless,
18although he had been kind
to their families.
The beliefs of these sinners
are truly disgusting.
19When God's people see
the godless swept away,
they celebrate, 20saying,
“Our enemies are gone,
and fire has destroyed
their possessions.”
Surrender to God All-Powerful
21Surrender to God All-Powerful!
You will find peace
and prosperity.
22Listen to his teachings
and take them to heart.
23If you return to God
and turn from sin,
all will go well for you.
24So get rid of your finest gold,
as though it were sand.
25Let God All-Powerful
be your silver and gold,
26and you will find happiness
by worshiping him.
27God will answer your prayers,
and you will keep the promises
you made to him.
28He will do whatever you ask,
and life will be bright.
29When others are disgraced,
God will clear their names
in answer to your prayers.
30Even those who are guilty
will be forgiven,
because you obey God.
translation_text:
Ní sɛɛmi etɛne
(22.1—27.23)
Elifaz
1-2 Anɛ nɔmlɔ adesa ko he ngɛ se nami ha Mawu lo?
Ní lelɔ ɔ,
lɛ nitsɛ e nile ɔ he se lɛ e naa.
3Ke o peeɔ nɔ́ nɛ da a,
anɛ Ope ɔ naa bua jɔmi ko ngɛ lɔ ɔ he lo?
Ke sé ko be o he ɔ,
anɛ Mawu naa nɔ́ ko ngɛ mi lo?
4O susu kaa Mawu gbeye nɛ o yeɔ ɔ,
lɔ ɔ he lɛ e ngɛ o hɛ mi kae,
nɛ e ngɛ o tue gblae ɔ lo?
5Dɛbi, a ngɛ o tue gblae,
ejakaa o he yayami ɔmɛ hiɛ tsɔ;
o he yayami ɔ, a li nya.
6Ke o nyɛmi hɛɛ mo hiɔ
nɛ e nyɛ we nɛ e wo mo ɔ,
o kpaa bo ngɛ e he,
nɛ o haa nɛ e hɛɛɔ e he gu.
7Nihi nɛ pɔ tɔ mɛ ɔ,
o ha we mɛ nyu nɛ a nu;
ni nɛmɛ nɛ hwɔ ngɛ mɛ yee ɔ,
o ha we mɛ ní nɛ a ye.
8Pohu o ngɔ o he wami,
kɛ bu nɛ a buu mo ɔ
kɛ kpɔ zugba a tsuo.
9O fieɔ yalɔyihi kɛ jeɔ o ngɔ
kɛ a dɛ mi gu,
nɛ awusahi hu o waa mɛ yi mi.
10Enɛ ɔ he je ɔ,
a tsɔ mo klama kɛ bɔle si,
nɛ amlɔ nɛ ɔ,
sawale nu mo.
11Diblii kpii wo mo,
nɛ o hyɛ we nɔ́ hu;
nyu kpekpemi bɔle mo kɛ kpe.
12Niinɛ, Mawu ngɛ hiɔwe lokoo!
Se dodoehi nɛ ngɛ hiɔwe lokoo ɔ,
anɛ Mawu lɛɛ e hyɛ we mɛ
kaa nɔ́ nɛ zugba lɛ a ngɛ lo?
13Se kɛ̃ ɔ, o biɔ ke,
“Mawu ɔ, mɛni e le?
Nɔ nɛ bɔku kpii ha e hɛ mi ɔ,
kɛ e maa pee
kɛ kojo wɔ kɛɛ?”
14O susuɔ kaa ke Mawu ngɛ nyɛɛe
ngɛ je ɔ, kɛ hiɔwe a kpe he ɔ,
e hyɛ we nɔ́ ngɛ bɔku kpii ɔ mi lo?
15Blɔ nɛ yiwutsotsɛmɛ nyɛɛɔ nɔ ɔ,
o maa nyɛɛ jamɛ a blɔ ɔ nɔ kɛ mwɔɔ lo?
16Loko jamɛatsɛmɛ ɔmɛ a be maa su ɔ,
pa nɛ hia kɛ bee ba sa mɛ
kɛ a sipoku tsuo kɛ ho momo.
17Nimli nɛ ɔmɛ ji nihi nɛ kua Mawu,
nɛ a biɔ a he ke,
“Mɛni Ope ɔ ma nyɛ maa pee wɔ?”
18Se Mawu ɔ nɔuu lɛ haa
a wehi hyi ɔ kɛ ní kpakpahi.
Anɔkuale mi ɔ,
yiwutsotsɛmɛ a yi mi tomi ɔ,
imi lɛɛ i sume saasaa!
19Ke a ngɛ yiwutsotsɛmɛ a tue gblae ɔ,
nimli kpakpahi a bua jɔɔ,
nɛ ni nɛmɛ nɛ pee we yayami ko ɔ yeɔ a he fɛu.
20Yiwutsotsɛmɛ a níhi
tsuo pɛpɛɛpɛ a hɛ mi kpataa,
nɛ nɔ́ nɛ piɛ ɔ, la ba sãã.
21Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, Hiob,
yaa nɛ o kɛ Mawu ya pee kake
nɛ o na tue mi jɔmi.
Blɔ nɔ nɛ o maa gu
nɛ e maa hi ha mo ji nɛ ɔ nɛ.
22Moo kplɛɛ nɛ Mawu nɛ tsɔɔ mo ní,
nɛ o ngɔ e munyu ɔmɛ kɛ to o tsui mi.
23Ee, ba o he si nɛ o kpale
kɛ ya Mawu ngɔ.
Yayamihi tsuo nɛ a peeɔ
ngɛ o we ɔ mi ɔ, a kpa peemi.
24Mo sake o sika tsu ngɔ fɔ he;
o sika tsu kpakpa a,
hɛɛ ngɔ pue pa mi,
ngɛ tɛhi a kpɛ.
25Ha nɛ Mawu Ope ɔ nɛ pee o sika tsu;
ha nɛ e pee o sika hiɔ kpakpa.
26Ngɔɔ o hɛ kɛ fɔ Mawu Ope ɔ nɔ daa,
nɛ o maa na kaa e ma ha mo bua jɔmi.
27Ke o fa kue ha lɛ ɔ,
e ma he nɔ,
nɛ o maa ye o siwo ɔ nɔ.
28Nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ o to o yi mi ke o maa pee ɔ,
e maa ba mi ja pɛpɛɛpɛ ha mo,
nɛ la ma kpɛ ngɛ o blɔ mi.
29Nɔ nɛ woɔ e he nɔ ɔ,
Mawu baa lɛ si,
se nɔ nɛ baa e he si ɔ,
Mawu heɔ e yi wami.
30Nihi nɛ pee we yayami ko ɔ,
Mawu heɔ a yi wami.
Mo hu ke o he tsɔ ɔ,
Mawu ma he o yi wami ja nɔuu.

english_text:
Job's Reply to Eliphaz
Today I Complain Bitterly
1Job said:
2Today I complain bitterly,
because God has been cruel
and made me suffer.
3If I knew where to find God,
I would go there
4and argue my case.
5Then I would discover
what he wanted to say.
6Would he overwhelm me
with his greatness?
No! He would listen
7because I am innocent,
and he would say,
“I now set you free!”
8I cannot find God anywhere—
in front or back of me,
9to my left or my right.
God is always at work,
though I never see him.
10But he knows what I am doing,
and when he tests me,
I will be pure as gold.
* 11I have never refused to follow
any of his commands,
12and I have always treasured
his teachings.
13But he alone is God,
and who can oppose him?
God does as he pleases,
14and he will do exactly
what he intends with me.
* 15Merely the thought
of God All-Powerful
16makes me tremble with fear.
17God has covered me
with darkness,
but I refuse to be silent.
translation_text:
Hiob
1-2Mwɔnɛ ɔ hu i kɛ Mawu na ekohu;
i ngɛ kɛmɛe,
se e ngɛ ye tue gblae kɛ mwɔɔ.
3I na nɛ i le he nɛ ma na lɛ ngɛ;
i na nɛ i le bɔ nɛ ma pee kɛ ya lejɛ ɔ.
4Jinɛ ma ngɔ ye sane ɔ kɛ ya fɔ e hɛ mi,
nɛ ma je ye nya bɔ nɛ ma nyɛ.
5Ma suɔ nɛ ma le nɔ́ nɛ e ma de,
kɛ bɔ nɛ e ma ha mi heto ha.
6Anɛ Mawu kɛ mi maa to ní
ngɛ e he wami kpetekpleenyɛ ɔ nya lo?
Dɛbi, e maa bu mi tue kɛ̃.
7Anɔkualetsɛ ji mi;
i kɛ Mawu ma hla níhi a nya;
nyagbe ɔ, e maa wo mi nguɔ kɛ̃.
8I hla Mawu ngɛ beleku je,
se e be lejɛ ɔ;
i ba bonyoku je hu, i nɛ lɛ.
9I hla lɛ ngɛ omleyi je, se i nɛ lɛ;
i kpale kɛ ba leneyi je hu,
i nɛ lɛ ja nɔuu.
10Se Mawu le blɔ nɛ i nyɛɛɔ nɔ ɔ;
ke e ka mi ɔ,
e maa na kaa ye he tsɔ kaa sika tsu.
11Mawu blɔ ɔ,
lɔ ɔ nɔ i nyɛɛɔ daa nɛ;
i gba we kɛ yɛ muɔ nɔ,
loo hiɔ nɔ.
12Nɔ́ nɛ Mawu fa mi ke ma pee ɔ,
lɔ ɔ i peeɔ.
I pee we imi nitsɛ ye suɔmi nya ní;
Mawu suɔmi nya ní lɛ i peeɔ.
13Mawu ɔ,
bɔ nɛ e ngɛ ɔ, jã kɛ̃ e ngɛ; e tsakee we.
Nɔ́ nɛ e suɔ ɔ,
lɔ ɔ e peeɔ.
Mɛnɔ ma nyɛ ma tsake e yi mi tomi?
14Nɔ́ nɛ e to ha mi ɔ,
lɔ ɔ e ngɛ pee ɔ nɛ;
níhi kaa kikɛ nɛ ɔ babauu hu ngɛ e yi mi.
15Ke i susu ní nɛ ɔmɛ a he ɔ,
i yeɔ Mawu gbeye,
nɛ ye he doɔ blibliibli ngɛ e hɛ mi.
16Mawu ha nɛ ye nine mi jɔ̃;
Ope ɔ wo ye he gbeye.
17Ejakaa diblii bɔle mi kɛ kpe;
diblii kpii ha ye hɛ mi.

english_text:
Job Continues
Why Doesn't God Set a Time?
1Why doesn't God
set a time for court?
Why don't his people know
where he can be found?
2Sinners remove boundary markers
and take care of sheep
they have stolen.
3They cheat orphans and widows
by taking their donkeys
and oxen.
4The poor are trampled
and forced to hide
5in the desert,
where they and their children
must live like wild donkeys
and search for food.
6If they want grain or grapes,
they must go to the property
of these sinners.
7They sleep naked in the cold,
because they have no cover,
8and during a storm
their only shelters are caves
among the rocky cliffs.
9Children whose fathers have died
are taken from their mothers
as payment for a debt.
10Then they are forced to work
naked in the grain fields
because they have no clothes,
and they go hungry.
11They crush olives to make oil
and grapes to make wine—
but still they go thirsty.
12And along the city streets,
the wounded and dying cry out,
yet God does nothing.
Some Reject the Light
13Some rebel and refuse
to follow the light.
14Soon after sunset they murder
the poor and the needy,
and at night they steal.
15Others wait for the dark,
thinking they won't be seen
if they sleep with the wife
or husband of someone else.
16Robbers hide during the day,
then break in after dark
because they reject the light.
17They prefer night to day,
since the terrors of the night
are their friends.
Sinners Are Filthy Foam
18Those sinners are filthy foam
on the surface of the water.
And so, their fields and vineyards
will fall under a curse
and won't produce.
19Just as the heat of summer
swallows the snow,
the world of the dead
swallows those who sin.
20Forgotten here on earth,
and with their power broken,
they taste sweet to worms.
21Sinners take advantage of widows
and other helpless women.
22But God's mighty strength
destroys those in power.
Even if they seem successful,
they are doomed to fail.
23God may let them feel secure,
but they are never
out of his sight.
24Great for a while; gone forever!
Sinners are mowed down
like weeds,
then they wither and die.
25If I haven't spoken the truth,
then prove me wrong.
translation_text:
1Mɛni he je lɛ Ope ɔ to we be
nɛ a kɛ maa kojo nihi?
Mɛni he je lɛ e ngɔ be ɔ kɛ laa
nihi nɛ sɔmɔɔ lɛ po?
2Nihi hiaa ni komɛ a bunahi kɛ yaa se,
konɛ mɛɛ a zugba a nɛ e kle.
A juɔ nihi a tohi nɛ a lɛɛ.
3A kpɔɔ awusahi a tejihi ngɛ a dɛ,
nɛ yalɔyihi lɛɛ a ngɔɔ a na amɛ kɛ toɔ awaba.
4A fieɔ ohiatsɛmɛ kɛ jeɔ a blɔ nɔ,
nɛ ohiatsɛmɛ ɔmɛ ya buaa
a he nya nɛ a laa a he.
5Enɛ ɔ he je ɔ,
ohiatsɛmɛ ɔmɛ ya hlaa niye ní
ngɛ nga kplanaa a nɔ kɛ haa a bimɛ,
kaa bɔ nɛ nga mi tejihi ya nuɔ lohwe
ngɛ pu mi ba haa a bimɛ ɔ.
6Ke nihi kpa ní ta a, ohiatsɛmɛ
ya kukuɔɔ bibliwi ngɛ wai ngmɔ ɔmɛ a nɔ.
A ya kukuɔɔ wai yiblii
ngɛ yiwutsotsɛmɛ po a wai ngmɔhi a nɔ.
7Nyɔ ɔ mi tsuo a hwɔɔ si kɛ a he gu
nɛ bo be a he;
fĩɛ be hu nɔ́ ko be nɛ a kɛ maa ha a he.
8Hiɔmi nɛɛ mɛ ngɛ yo ɔmɛ a nɔ,
nɛ a pɔɔ kpanyaa.
Akɛnɛ a be hi he ko he je ɔ,
a hɔɔ tɛ sahi a kpɛ.
9Nimli yayami komɛ kpɔɔ bimwɔwi nɛ be tsɛmɛ
pani nya ngɛ a nyɛmɛ a nyɔ nya.
A kɛ bimwɔwi nɛ ɔmɛ toɔ a tsɛmɛ ɔmɛ
a hiɔhi a nya.
10Nimli nɛ ɔmɛ haa
nɛ ohiatsɛmɛ ɔmɛ hɛɛɔ a he gu
nɛ bo be a he;
a haa nɛ a kɛ mi mi hwɔ
tsuɔ ní ngɛ ngmɔ nɔ.
11A naa nu kɛ jeɔ oliv tso mi,
nɛ a ngaa wai kɛ jeɔ wai yiblii mi.
Se mɛ nitsɛmɛ lɛɛ kuma yeɔ mɛ.
12O maa nu nɛ nihi ngɛ kɛmɛe ngɛ ma a mi;
o maa nu nɛ nihi nɛ plaa a ngɛ ngmlaa kpae,
nɛ a ngɛ yemi kɛ buami hlae.
Se Mawu bui mɛ tue fɛɛ.
13Nimli yayamihi ji ni nɛmɛ nɛ kua la a nɛ;
a nui la a sisi,
nɛ he nɛ la a ngɛ kpɛe ngɛ hu,
a be lejɛ ɔ.
14Awi yelɔ teɔ si mɔtu kpla
konɛ e gbe ohiatsɛ,
aloo nɔ nɛ be nɔ́ ko.
Nyɔ mi kɛkɛ e pee e he julɔ.
15Gba puɛlɔ hu hii mlɛe konɛ du nɛ bu.
E deɔ e he ke, “Nɔ ko be mi nae,”
kɛkɛ e ngɔ nɔ́ kɛ ha e hɛ mi.
16Ke diblii wo ɔ,
juli ya sɛɛ nihi a wehi a mi ya juɔ.
Piani lɛɛ a laa a he,
nɛ a sume nɛ a baa la hɛ mi.
17Ejakaa a yeɔ piani la a gbeye;
diblii kpii ɔ mohu wui a he gbeye.
Zofar
18Yiwutsotsɛ ɔ,
pa nɛ hia ba ngɔɔ lɛ kɛ yaa.
A gbiɛ e weto ní
nɛ ji e zugba a,
nɛ e be ní tsue ngɛ e wai ngmɔ ɔ mi hu.
19Gbeje ngɔɔ yayami peelɔ kɛ yaa
kaa bɔ nɛ sapu kɛ latsa miiɔ nyu ɔ.
20E nyɛ po hɛ maa je e nɔ.
Gɔgɔ maa ye lɛ,
nɛ e hɛ mi ma kpata
kaa tso nɛ ku pue si.
Nɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko be lɛ kaie hu.
21Nɔ́ nɛ ɔ maa ba e nɔ,
ejakaa e wa yosahi yi mi;
yalɔyihi hu e nɛ́ mɛ mɔbɔ.
22Se kɛ̃ ɔ,
Mawu kɛ e he wami haa nɛ
nɔmlɔ nɛ he wa a yaa nɔ.
E tee si be mi
nɛ e hɛ be wami ko nɔ hu.
23Mawu ma ha nɛ e maa hi si
ngɛ tue mi jɔmi mi,
se daa nɛ ɔ, e hɛngmɛ ngɛ e he.
24Yayami peelɔ yaa nɔ nɛ e plɔkeɔ;
se be bɔɔ se ɔ, e be hu.
E hɛ mi kpataa kaa bɔ nɛ
nimlihi tsuo a hɛ mi kpataa a,
nɛ e peeɔ kaa blɛfo tso nɛ a po.
25Ke ní nɛ ɔmɛ be mi ɔ,
mɛnɔ ma nyɛ maa tsɔɔ kaa
i ngɛ lakpa yee?
Anɛ nɔ ko ma nyɛ maa tsɔɔ kaa
munyu gu lɛ i ngɛ tue ɔ lo?

english_text:
Bildad's Third Speech
God Is the One To Fear
1Bildad from Shuah said:
2God is the one to fear,
because God is in control
and rules the heavens.
3Who can count his army of stars?
Isn't God the source of light?
4How can anyone be innocent
in the sight of God?
5To him, not even the light
of the moon and stars
can ever be pure.
6So how can we humans,
when we are merely worms?
translation_text:
Bildad
1-2Mawu kle, nɛ e he ngɛ gbeye.
E hiɔwe ma a lɛɛ
tue mi jɔmi sɔuu ji lejɛ ɔ.
3Bɔfohi nɛ sɔmɔɔ Mawu ɔ,
nɔ ko ma nyɛ maa kane mɛ lo?
E la a nɛ́,
ni komɛ ngɛ nɛ e tsui ha mɛ lo?
4Lɛɛ kɛ a maa pee kɛ bu nɔmlɔ dalɔ
ngɛ Mawu hɛ mi kɛɛ?
Nɔmlɔ nɛ yo fɔ lɛ ɔ,
kɛ e maa pee kɛɛ nɛ e he ma tsɔ?
5Nyɔhiɔ tete kpɛ we ha Mawu,
nɛ dodoehi po a hɛ mi tsɔ we ha lɛ.
6Nɔmlɔ nɛ ngɛ kaa aklɔku,
aloo gɔgɔ ɔ,
kɛ lɛɛ e maa pee
kɛ sa Mawu hɛ mi kɛɛ?

english_text:
Job's Reply to Bildad
You Have Really Been Helpful
1Job said:
2You have really been helpful
to someone weak and weary.
3You have given great advice
and wonderful wisdom
to someone truly in need.
4How can anyone possibly speak
with such understanding?
5Remember the terrible trembling
of those in the world of the dead
below the mighty ocean.
6Nothing in that land
of death and destruction
is hidden from God,
7who hung the northern sky
and suspended the earth
on empty space.
8God stores water in clouds,
but they don't burst,
9and he wraps them around
the face of the moon.
10On the surface of the ocean,
God has drawn a boundary line
between light and darkness.
11And columns supporting the sky
tremble at his command.
12By his power and wisdom,
God conquered the force
of the mighty ocean.
13The heavens became bright
when he breathed,
and the escaping sea monster
died at his hands.
14These things are merely a whisper
of God's power at work.
How little we would understand
if this whisper
ever turned into thunder!
translation_text:
Hiob
1-2Balɔ kpakpa!
Mo lɛ o piɛ ye he.
Imi nɛ i gbɔjɔ!
Imi nɛ ye he wami ta!
3Imi kuasia
nɛ i li nɔ́ ko nɔ́ ko ɔ,
o wo mi ga,
nɛ o tu nile munyu kpakpahi
kɛ tsɔɔ mi!
4Mɛnɔ lɛ piɛ o he nɛ o
kɛ tu munyu nɛ ɔmɛ?
Mɛnɔ mumi lɛ je o mi ɔ?
Bildad
5Kpade ɔmɛ a he mi ngɛ mɛ hiae
ngɛ zu mi ngɛ nyu ɔ sisi.
6Gbeje fɔɔ si paa ngɛ Mawu hɛ mi.
He hami nɔ́ be he
nɛ maa tsi lɛ blɔ.
7Mawu gbla omleyi je hiɔwe ɔ mi,
nɛ e ngɔ je ɔ ngɔ kpla si
nɛ nɔ́ ko hɛɛ we lɛ.
8Mawu lɛ e kɛ nyu woɔ bɔku kpii ɔmɛ a mi;
lɛ nɛ e fii bɔku ɔmɛ a nya,
nɛ e ha we nɛ a pɛ́.
9Mawu lɛ e ngɔɔ nyɔhiɔ
kɛ laa ngɛ bɔku ɔmɛ a se.
10E po huzu ngɛ wo hɛ mi
kɛ gba piani kɛ nyɔ a kpɛti.
11Ke e kuɛ́ ɔ,
titimahi nɛ hɛɛ hiɔwe ɔ hosoɔ,
nɛ a he wami taa.
12E kɛ e he wami jɔɔ wo ɔ he,
nɛ e kɛ juɛmi kpata
wo mi lohwe ɔ nɛ a tsɛɛ Rahab ɔ hɛ mi.
13E mumi ɔ lɛ ha nɛ hiɔwe tsɔ,
nɛ e pee saminyayoo.
E nine lɛ e kɛ tsɔtslɔɔ
wo mi lohwe ngua a mi.
14Mawu blɔ ɔmɛ a he níhi bɔɔ kɛkɛ
nɛ́ wa nu kɛ wa tue ji nɛ ɔmɛ nɛ.
E he wami kpetekpleenyɛ nitsɛnitsɛ ɔ lɛɛ
mɛnɔ ma nyɛ maa le?

english_text:
Job Continues
I Am Desperate
1Job said:
2I am desperate because
God All-Powerful refuses
to do what is right.
As surely as God lives,
3and while he gives me breath,
4I will tell only the truth.
5Until the day I die,
I will refuse to do wrong
by saying you are right,
6because each day my conscience
agrees that I am innocent.
7I pray that my enemies
will suffer no less
than the wicked.
8Such people are hopeless,
and God All-Powerful
will cut them down,
9without listening
when they beg for mercy.
10And that is what God should do,
because they don't like him
or ever pray.
11Now I will explain in detail
what God All-Powerful does.
12All of you have seen these things
for yourselves.
So you have no excuse.
How God Treats the Wicked
13Here is how God All-Powerful
treats those who are wicked
and brutal.
14They may have many children,
but most of them will go hungry
or suffer a violent death.
15Others will die of disease,
and their widows
won't be able to weep.
16The wicked may collect riches
and clothes in abundance
as easily as clay.
17But God's people will wear
clothes taken from them
and divide up their riches.
18No homes built by the wicked
will outlast a cocoon
or a shack.
19Those sinners may go to bed rich,
but they will wake up poor.
20Terror will strike at night
like a flood or a storm.
21Then a scorching wind
will sweep them away
22without showing mercy,
as they try to escape.
23At last, the wind will celebrate
because they are gone.
translation_text:
Hiob
1-2I na Mawu Ope nɛ hɛ ngɛ ɔ,
nɔ nɛ kua dami sane yemi ha mi,
nɛ e ha nɛ i na amanehlu kikɛ nɛ ɔ,
3kaa be abɔ nɛ i ngɛ wami mi,
nɛ Mawu mumi ngɛ ye mi nɛ ɔ,
4lakpa munyu be ye nya mi jee gblegbleegble;
i kɛ ye lilɛ hu be nɔ ko sisie kɔkɔɔkɔ.
5I be kplɛɛe kɔkɔɔkɔ kaa nɔ́
nɛ nyɛ ngɛ dee ɔ ngɛ mi;
kɛ yaa si ye gbenɔ ligbi ɔ,
nɔ́ nɛ i ngɛ dee kɛkɛ ji i yi fɔ.
6Nɔ́ nɛ i ngɛ dee ke
i pee we nɔ́ ko nɛ dɛ blɔ ɔ,
jamɛ a munyu kake too ɔ i ngɛ tue;
ye he nile bui mi fɔ ligbi ko ligbi ko.
7Ye he nyɛlɔ ɔ,
á gbla e tue kaa yiwutsotsɛ;
nɔ nɛ teɔ si kɛ woɔ mi ɔ,
á gbla e tue kaa yayami peelɔ.
8Ke yayami peelɔ be su,
nɛ Mawu ba ngɔ lɛ ɔ,
mɛni hɛ kɛ nɔ fɔmi pa ngɛ ha lɛ?
9Ke haomi ba e nɔ, nɛ e fa kue ha Mawu ɔ,
anɛ Mawu maa nu e kue fami ɔ lo?
10Anɛ e náá Ope ɔ he bua jɔmi lo?
Anɛ e faa kue kɛ haa lɛ daa lo?
11Nyɛ ha nɛ ma tsɔɔ nyɛ bɔ nɛ Mawu kle ha;
nɔ́ nɛ Mawu Ope ɔ to ke e maa pee ɔ,
i be nyɛ ba laae ngɛ he.
12Se tse nyɛ nitsɛmɛ nyɛ na
ní nɛ ɔmɛ momo kɛ nyɛ hɛngmɛ.
Lɛɛ mɛni he je lɛ nyɛ tsuo nyɛ ngɛ
munyuhi nɛ a he be se nami tue kikɛ nɛ ɔ mɔ?
Zofar
13Bɔ nɛ Mawu gblaa yayami peelɔ tue ji nɛ ɔ nɛ.
Hiɔwo nɛ yiwutsotsɛ naa
kɛ jeɔ Ope ɔ dɛ mi ji nɛ ɔ nɛ.
14E ma fɔ bimɛ babauu,
se mɛ tsuo pɛpɛɛpɛ a ma gbo ngɛ ta mi;
e bimɛ na we niye ní
nɛ suu a nya gblegbleegble.
15Nihi nɛ a he maa je mi ɔ,
gbenɔ hiɔ maa gbe mɛ,
nɛ a yalɔyi ɔmɛ be ya nyɛe ha mɛ.
16Yayami peelɔ ma bua sika hiɔ babauu nya kaa bunyuku
nɛ be hie kanemi;
e ma bua he hami níhi babauu nya
kaa tabo zu.
17Se nɔmlɔ kpakpa ko lɛ ma ba ha bo ɔmɛ;
nɔ kpakpa ko lɛ ma ba wo tade ɔmɛ,
nɛ e maa ngɔ sika hiɔ ɔ.
18Yayami peelɔ we nɛ e po ɔ
ngɛ kaa anani ya,
aloo tsu wayoo nɛ bulɔ pee.
19E ma ya hwɔ si kaa niatsɛ;
se ke e te si ɔ,
e maa na kaa e sika a tsuo ta.
20Sawale maa nu lɛ kaa pa nɛ hia kɛ bee.
Kɔɔhiɔ nɛ nya wa maa fia lɛ kɛ ho nyɔ mi.
21Beleku kɔɔhiɔ maa fia lɛ kɛ ho;
e maa bɛɛ lɛ kɛ je he nɛ e hii ɔ.
22Mawu ma ha nɛ beleku kɔɔhiɔ maa fia lɛ wawɛɛ nitsɛ;
nɛ e be lɛ mɔbɔ nae kulaa,
be mi nɛ e ngɛ mɔde bɔe kaa e maa tu fo kɛ je nya.
23Kɔɔhiɔ nɛ nya wa nɛ ɔ ma kpa fiifii
kɛ nyɛɛ e se kɛ fo
kɛ wo e he gbeye.
E maa pee lɛ kaa nihi lɛ a ngɛ a dɛ fiae
kɛ ngɛ lɛ fiee kɛ je he nɛ e hii ɔ.

english_text:
Job Continues
Gold and Silver Are Mined
1Gold and silver are mined,
then purified;
2the same is done
with iron and copper.
3Miners carry lanterns
deep into the darkness
to search for these metals.
4They dig tunnels
in distant, unknown places,
where they dangle by ropes.
5Far beneath the grain fields,
fires are built
to break loose those rocks
6that have jewels or gold.
7Miners go to places unseen
by the eyes of hawks;
8they walk on soil unknown
to the proudest lions.
9With their own hands
they remove sharp rocks
and uproot mountains.
10They dig through the rocks
in search of jewels
and precious metals.
11They also uncover
the sources of rivers
and discover secret places.
Where Is Wisdom Found?
12 But where is wisdom found?
13 No human knows the way.
14Nor can it be discovered
in the deepest sea.
* 15It is worth much more
than silver or pure gold
16or precious stones.
17Nothing is its equal—
not gold or costly glass.
18Wisdom is worth much more than
coral, jasper, or rubies.
19All the topaz of Ethiopia
and the finest gold
cannot compare with it.
20Where then is wisdom?
21It is hidden from human eyes
and even from birds.
22Death and destruction
have merely heard rumors
about where it is found.
23 God is the only one who knows
the way to wisdom;
24he alone sees everything
beneath the heavens.
25When God divided out
the wind and the water,
26and when he decided the path
for rain and lightning,
27 he also determined the truth
and defined wisdom.
28 God told us, “Wisdom means
that you respect me, the Lord,
and turn from sin.”
translation_text:
Nile yi jemi la
1Niinɛ, muɔhi ngɛ nɛ a tsuaa sika hiɔ ngɛ a mi.
Sika tsu he tsumi hehi hu ngɛ.
2A tsuaa dade ngɛ zu mi,
nɛ a sileɔ tɛ, nɛ a jeɔ akɔblee kɛ jeɔ mi.
3Nihi suɔ kane ngɛ diblii mi,
nɛ a kɛ hlaa tɛ kpakpahi
ngɛ zugba a sisi hehi nɛ wo diblii kpii,
kɛ hehi nɛ ngɛ gbeye.
4Kɔ̃ mi hehi nɛ nimli be,
hehi nɛ blɔ hiali nyɛɛ we ɔ,
lejɛ ɔ sika tsuali ya tsuaa muɔ ngɛ.
O maa na mɛ nɛ a kplaa si ngɛ kpahi a he,
nɛ a ngɛ asɛkɛ wue kɛ ngɛ yae kɛ ngɛ bae.
5Niye ní jeɔ zu mi,
se zu ɔ sisi lɛɛ e pee kaa nɔ́ nɛ la sã.
6Tɛhi nɛ ngɛ zu ɔ mi ɔ,
safiro ngɛ mi.
Bibliwi ɔmɛ hu, sika tsu sɔuu.
7Blɔ nɛ yaa sika muɔ ɔmɛ a mi ɔ,
kayo ko hɛngmɛ nɛ hyɛ;
okpoku ko hu ti kɛ ya bi ngɛ lejɛ ɔ hyɛ.
8Jata, loo lohwe awi yelɔ ko
bi ngɛ jamɛ a blɔ ɔ nɔ.
9Nimli adesahi tsuaa tɛ sahi nɛ a he wa,
a hiaa yokuhi kɛ jeɔ a hi hehi.
10Ke a ngɛ tɛ sa amɛ a mi kpɛe ɔ,
a naa tɛhi nɛ a he jua wa.
11A tsuaa pa mi kɛ yaa pa a je he tɔɔ,
nɛ níhi nɛ a kɛ laa ngɛ lejɛ ɔ,
a ngɔɔ kɛ baa la hɛ mi.
12Se nile lɛɛ jije a maa na lɛ ngɛ?
Juɛmi ɔ, jije e hii?
13A nɛ nile ngɛ nimli a kpɛti.
Nɔ ko nɔ ko li bɔ nɛ e he jua wa ha.
14Muɔ voovoo ɔmɛ ke nile be a ngɔ;
wo hu ja nɔuu lɛ e ngɛ dee.
15Nile ɔ,
a ngɔɛ sika tsu, loo sika hiɔ kɛ he we.
16E he jua a,
sika tsu, loo juetli kpakpa po sui nya.
17E he jua wa pe sika tsu,
e he jua wa pe sika tsu kplu,
aloo ahuhuɛ kpakpa.
18Nile he jua wa pe huazi, loo kɔli,
loo adiagba.
19Etiopia topasion tɛ,
aloo sika tsu ngmingmiingmi kɛ nile sɔɛ.
20Lɛɛ jije a naa nile ngɛ mɔ?
Jije ji juɛmi hi he?
21A ngɔ kɛ laa nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ hɛ ngɛ.
Lohwe pɛlitsɛmɛ ngɛ hiɔwe po,
a li he nɛ nile ngɛ.
22Gbenɔ kɛ hɛ mi kpatami po de ke,
“Oo, e biɛ kɛkɛ lɛ wa nu kɛ wa tue.”
23He nɛ nile ngɛ,
kɛ blɔ nɛ a maa gu kɛ ya na lɛ ɔ,
Mawu pɛ lɛ le.
24Ejakaa lɛɛ e hɛngmɛ hyɛɛ nɔ́
kɛ yaa je mi nyagbe he ɔmɛ tɔɔ;
e naa níhi tsuo nɛ ngɛ hiɔwe sisi.
25Benɛ Mawu susu kɔɔhiɔ jiimi,
kɛ he nɛ wo ɔ yi ma bli kɛ ya su ɔ,
26benɛ Mawu to he nɛ hiɔmi maa nɛ ngɛ,
kɛ he nɛ hiɔwe ma si kɛ ya be ngɛ ɔ,
27jamɛ a be ɔ mi nɛ e na nile, nɛ e wo nɔ ta.
E hla mi fitsofitso, nɛ e to lɛ sisi.
28 Mawu de nɔmlɔ ke,
“Nyɔmtsɛ ɔ gbeye yemi ɔ, lɔ ɔ ji nile;
yayami he jemi ɔ, lɔ ɔ ji juɛmi.”

english_text:
Job Continues
I Long for the Past
1Job said:
2I long for the past,
when God took care of me,
3and the light from his lamp
showed me the way
through the dark.
4I was in the prime of life,
God All-Powerful
was my closest friend,
5and all of my children
were nearby.
6My herds gave enough milk
to bathe my feet,
and from my olive harvest
flowed rivers of oil.
* 7When I sat down at the meeting
of the city council,
8the young leaders stepped aside,
* 9while the older ones stood
10and remained silent.
Everyone Was Pleased
11Everyone was pleased
with what I said and did.
12When poor people or orphans
cried out for help,
I came to their rescue.
13And I was highly praised
for my generosity to widows
and others in poverty.
14Kindness and justice
were my coat and hat;
15I was helpful to the blind
and to the lame.
16I was a father to the needy,
and I defended them in court,
even if they were strangers.
17When criminals attacked,
I broke their teeth
and set their victims free.
18I felt certain that I would live
a long and happy life,
then die in my own bed.
19In those days I was strong
like a tree with deep roots
and with plenty of water,
20or like an archer's new bow.
21Everyone listened in silence
to my welcome advice,
22and when I finished speaking,
nothing needed to be said.
23My words were eagerly accepted
like the showers of spring,
24and the smile on my face
renewed everyone's hopes.
25My advice was followed
as though I were a king
leading my troops,
or someone comforting
those in sorrow.
translation_text:
Hiob je e nya nyagbe nɔ́
1Hiob tsa e munyu ɔ nɔ nɛ e de ke,
2I na nɛ i ngɛ kaa bɔ nɛ i ngɛ sa a
nɛ Mawu buɔ ye he ɔ.
3Jamɛ a be ɔ, Mawu kɛ mi ngɛ saminya,
nɛ ke i ngɛ diblii mi nyɛɛe ɔ, e haa mi la.
4Jamɛ a be ɔ, ye he hi,
nɛ Mawu kɛ mi ngɛ kaa nɔ kɛ e huɛ.
5Jamɛ a be ɔ, Ope ɔ kɛ mi ngɛ,
nɛ ye bimɛ bɔle mi kɛ kpe.
6Jamɛ a be ɔ,
ye na amɛ, kɛ to ɔmɛ haa mi nyɔ nyu babauu;
nɛ hehi nɛ tɛ sa hiɛ ngɛ po,
i naa oliv tsohi babauu nɛ haa mi nu bɔ nɛ sa.
7Be tsuaa be nɛ ma nimeli ma bua a he nya
ngɛ ma agbo ɔ nya, nɛ ma ho ya hi
ye blɔ he ngɛ lejɛ ɔ,
8ke nihewi na mi pɛ kɛkɛ a gba ha mi;
nikɔtɔmahi maa te nɛ a maa da si ha mi.
9Ganɔ ɔmɛ maa jɔɔ munyu tumi,
nɛ a kɛ a nine maa wo a nya mi.
10Odehehi tete a lilɛ maa mɛtɛ a nya mi,
nɛ a maa pee dii.
11Ke nihi nu ye he ɔ,
a jeɔ ye yi,
nɛ ke a na mi ɔ,
a tuɔ ye he munyu kpakpa.
12Ejakaa ke ohiatsɛmɛ kpa ngmlaa
kɛ tsɛ balɔ ɔ, i jeɔ mɛ;
awusahi hu i piɛɔ a he ja nɔuu.
13I je nihi kɛ je haomi mi,
nɛ a gbaa mi;
nɛ i ha nɛ yalɔyihi na bua jɔmi.
14Be tsuaa be ɔ, i yeɔ dami sane,
nɛ i peeɔ nɔ́ nɛ da.
15I plɛ pee hɛngmɛ ha hɛ yuyuili,
kɛ nane ha glɔtsɛmɛ.
16I pee kaa tsɛ kɛ ha dɛgutsɛmɛ,
nɛ nihi nɛ i li mɛ po,
i ye a sane ha mɛ.
17I ku yiwutsotsɛmɛ a tsitsa,
nɛ i kpɔ nihi nɛ a ngɛ yi mi wae ɔ
kɛ je a nya mi.
18I hyɛ blɔ kaa ye wami ligbi ɔmɛ
maa hiɛ babauu kaa zia,
nɛ ma gbo ngɛ we,
ngɛ he jɔmi mi.
19I ngɛ kaa tso nɛ sipoku naa nyu be tsuaa be,
nɛ bɔ́ pɔɔ e kɔnihi a he daa.
20Nihi tuɔ ye he munyu kpakpa daa,
nɛ be tsuaa be ɔ,
i naa he wami he.
21Ke i ngɛ nihi ga woe ɔ,
a peeɔ dii nɛ a buɔ nɔ́
nɛ i ngɛ dee ɔ tue.
22Ke i tu munyu gbe nya a,
nɔ ko de we nɔ́ ko hu;
ejakaa a nuɔ ye munyu ɔmɛ a sisi saminya.
23Ke pee ɔ,
a hyɛɛ mi blɔ nɛ ma ba tu mɛ munyu
kaa bɔ nɛ nihi nɛ nyu he hia mɛ
hyɛɛ gbo hiɔmi nɛmi blɔ ɔ.
24Ke a ngɛ a tsui yee ɔ,
kɛkɛ i muɔ hɛlii ha mɛ.
Ke i tsɔ ye hɛ mi ha mɛ ja
kɛkɛ a nɔ gbagba te.
25I kɛ mɛ hi si kaa a hɛ mi nyɛɛlɔ;
nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ hia kaa a pee ɔ, i tsɔɔ mɛ.
I kɛ mɛ hi si kaa matsɛ ngɛ e ta buli a kpɛti,
aloo bua wolɔ ngɛ kɔmɔ yeli a kpɛti.

english_text:
Job Continues
Young People Now Insult Me
1Young people now insult me,
although their fathers
would have been a disgrace
to my sheep dogs.
2And those who insult me
are helpless themselves.
3They must claw the desert sand
in the dark for something
to satisfy their hunger.
4They gather tasteless shrubs
for food and firewood,
5and they are run out of towns,
as though they were thieves.
6Their only homes are ditches
or holes between rocks,
7where they bray like donkeys
gathering around shrubs.
8And like senseless donkeys
they are chased away.
Those Worthless Nobodies
9Those worthless nobodies
make up jokes and songs
to disgrace me.
10They are hateful
and keep their distance,
even while spitting
in my direction.
11God has destroyed me,
and so they don't care
what they do.
12Their attacks never stop,
though I am defenseless,
and my feet are trapped.
13Without any help,
they prevent my escape,
destroying me completely
14and leaving me crushed.
15Terror has me surrounded;
my reputation and my riches
have vanished like a cloud.
I Am Sick at Heart
16I am sick at heart!
Pain has taken its toll.
17Night chews on my bones,
causing endless torment,
18and God has shrunk my skin,
choking me to death.
19I have been thrown in the dirt
and now am dirt myself.
20I beg God for help,
but there is no answer;
and when I stand up,
he simply stares.
21God has turned brutal,
22stirring up a windstorm
to toss me about.
23Soon he will send me home
to the world of the dead,
where we all must go.
24No one refuses help to others,
when disaster strikes.
25I mourned for the poor
and those who suffered.
26But when I beg for relief
and light,
all I receive are disaster
and darkness.
27My stomach is tied in knots;
pain is my daily companion.
28My days are dark and gloomy
and in the city council
I stand and cry out,
29making mournful sounds
like jackals and owls.
30My skin is so parched,
that it peels right off,
and my bones are burning.
31My only songs are sorrow
and sadness.
translation_text:
1Se mwɔnɛ ɔ,
nihi nɛ i wa pe mɛ po ngɛ mi muɔe.
Nimli nɛ ɔmɛ a tsɛmɛ nɛ fɔ mɛ ɔ,
i bui mɛ fɛɛ;
gbehi nɛ buu ye tohi a he pohu
i kɛ mɛ be gbe ɔmɛ futue.
2Nimli nɛ a he wami tsuo ta nɛ ɔ,
mɛni se ma na ngɛ a he?
3Ohia kɛ hwɔ ha nɛ a ta he lo,
nɛ a pee kanyakanya;
sa a, tso sipoku gbigbli lɛ
a kpeɔ ngɛ nga kplanaa nɔ.
4Tso sipoku, kɛ ba ji a niye ní.
5A fie mɛ kɛ je nimli a kpɛti;
a huɔ mɛ kaa a huɔɔ julɔ.
6A hi hehi ji muɔhi,
tɛ sahi, kɛ dɔhi a mi.
7A ya buaa a he nya ngɛ mio tsohi a sisi ngɛ pu mi,
nɛ a hii huãe kaa lohwe awi yeli.
8Yakayaka nimli, kɛ ni guhi ji mɛ tsuo,
nihi nɛ a fia a nane si tu kɛ je ma a mi.
9Amlɔ nɛ ɔ, a ba konɛ a ba muɔ mi;
i plɛ pee a nya mi la.
10A hɛ mɛ kɛ je ye kasa nya;
a hiee mi.
Ke a hyɛ mi kɛkɛ a la lada pue ye nɔ.
11Akɛnɛ Mawu gbla ye tue nɛ i gbɔjɔ
he je ɔ, a bui mi fɛɛ;
nɔ́ nɛ a suɔ lɛ a peeɔ mi.
12Yakayaka nimli nɛ ɔmɛ ba tuaa mi basabasa,
nɛ a hlaa kaa a ma kpata ye hɛ mi.
13A tsi mi blɔ nɛ ma ko ma fo;
a bɔ mɔde kaa a ma kpata ye hɛ mi,
nɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko tsi we a nya.
14A hiɛ babauu kɛ ba tua mi
kaa nɔ́ nɛ puɔ agbo ko mi lɛ a gu kɛ ba.
15Sawale nu mi; ye hɛ mi nyami laa mi
kaa kɔɔhiɔ muɔɔ ní kɛ yaa.
Ye ní nami ɔ se po kaa bɔku.
16Amlɔ nɛ ɔ, ye gbenɔ be su ta;
jehanɛ lɛɛ, ye haomi ɔ nya ba wa tsɔ.
17Nyɔ mi ɔ,
ye wuhi a mi kpeɔ mi wawɛɛ nitsɛ
nɛ he jɔmi be mi.
18E ngɛ kaa nɔ́ nɛ
Mawu mia ye yi nɔ tade ɔ
kɛ wo ye kuɛ kpɛii
nɛ mumi womi he be mi.
19Mawu tsitsɛɛ mi kɛ wo mɔsɔ mi,
nɛ i pee kaa tabo zu,
aloo la zu.
20Mawu, ke i tsɛ mo ɔ, o he we nɔ;
ke i fa kue ha mo ɔ,
o bui mi tue.
21O ngɛ mi yi mi wae;
o kɛ nine si wami ngɛ mi yi mi wae wawɛɛ nitsɛ.
22O wo ye nɔ nɛ o fɔ mi
kɛ ya kɔɔhiɔ mi.
Kɔɔhiɔ nɛ nya wa a fia mi
kɛ ya kɛ ba.
23Niinɛ, i le kaa o ngɔ mi kɛ yaa gbeje,
he nɛ a to kɛ ha nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ hɛ ngɛ ɔ.
24Se kɛ̃ ɔ,
imi nɛ ye he wami ta,
imi nɛ i nyɛ we nɔ́ ko peemi,
nɛ pɛɛ kɛkɛ i ngɛ mo kpae
ke o na mi mɔbɔ ɔ,
mɛni he je lɛ o kɛ mi
ye sane kikɛ nɛ ɔ?
25Anɛ i fo we ya ha nihi nɛ
ngɛ haomi mi lo?
Anɛ ohiatsɛmɛ a sane pee we mi mɔbɔ lo?
26Se benɛ i ngɛ nɔ́ kpakpa blɔ hyɛe ɔ,
nɔ́ yayami mohu lɛ ba na mi.
Benɛ i ngɛ la blɔ hyɛe ɔ,
diblii mohu lɛ ba.
27Ye tsui ngɛ fiae wawɛɛ ngɛ ye mi mi;
ye haomi ligbi ɔmɛ hiɛ tsɔ.
28I ngɛ kaa nɔ ko nɛ ngɛ diblii mi nyɛɛe
nɛ e nɛ pu hɛ mi.
I teɔ si ngɛ gua mi,
nɛ i biɔ yemi kɛ buami.
29I plɛ pee nga mi gbehi
a nyɛmi, kɛ klomihi a huɛ.
30Ye he womi pee tuu,
nɛ ye wuhi a he dɔ la.
31Ye gbi nɛ jijeɔ kaa saku, aloo bɛ ɔ,
mwɔnɛ ɔ, e pɛɛ kaa nihi nɛ a wo yana kɛ ngɛ kɔmɔ yee.

english_text:
Job Continues
I Promised Myself
1I promised myself
never to stare with desire
at a young woman.
2God All-Powerful punishes
men who do that.
3In fact, God sends disaster
on all who sin,
4and he keeps a close watch
on everything I do.
5I am not dishonest or deceitful,
6and I beg God to prove
my innocence.
7If I have disobeyed him
or even wanted to,
8then others can eat my harvest
and uproot my crops.
9If I have desired someone's wife
and chased after her,
10then let some stranger
steal my wife from me.
11If I took someone's wife,
it would be a horrible crime,
12sending me to destruction
and my crops to the flames.
13When my servants
complained against me,
I was fair to them.
14Otherwise, what answer
would I give to God
when he judges me?
15After all, God is the one
who gave life to each of us
before we were born.
I Have Never Cheated Anyone
16 I have never cheated widows
or others in need,
17and I have always shared
my food with orphans.
18Since the time I was young,
I have cared for orphans
and helped widows.
19I provided clothes for the poor,
20and I was praised
for supplying woolen garments
to keep them warm.
21If I have ever raised my arm
to threaten an orphan
when the power was mine,
22I hope that arm will fall
from its socket.
23I could not have been abusive;
I was terrified at the thought
that God might punish me.
24 I have never trusted
the power of wealth,
25or taken pride in owning
many possessions.
* 26I have never openly or secretly
27worshiped the sun or moon.
28Such horrible sins
would have deserved
punishment from God.
29I have never laughed
when my enemies
were struck by disaster.
30Neither have I sinned
by asking God
to send down on them
the curse of death.
31No one ever went hungry
at my house,
32and travelers
were always welcome.
33Many have attempted to hide
their sins from others—
but I refused.
34And the fear of public disgrace
never forced me to keep silent
about what I had done.
Why Doesn't God Listen?
35Why doesn't God All-Powerful
listen and answer?
If God has something against me,
let him speak up
or put it in writing!
36Then I would wear his charges
on my clothes and forehead.
37And with my head held high,
I would tell him everything
I have ever done.
38I have never mistreated
the land I farmed
and made it mourn.
39Nor have I cheated
my workers
and caused them pain.
40If I had, I would pray
for weeds instead of wheat
to grow in my fields.
After saying these things,
Job was silent.
translation_text:
1I ka kita kaa i kɛ akɔnɔ hɛngmɛ
be zangmayo ko hyɛe gblegbleegble.
2Mɛni hiɔwo lɛ ma na kɛ je Mawu
nɛ ngɛ hiɔwe ɔ dɛ mi?
Mɛni weto ní lɛ ma na
kɛ je Ope ɔ dɛ mi?
3Anɛ e kpataa we yiwutsotsɛmɛ a hɛ mi lo?
Anɛ e gbla we yayami peeli a tue lo?
4Mawu le nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ i peeɔ;
e le ye blɔ ɔmɛ tsuo.
5I ngɛ kita kae kaa i yi nɔ ko lakpa;
i sisi we nɔ ko hulɔ.
6Mawu nɛ́ ngmɛ mi ngɛ sɛni nɛ da nɔ,
nɛ e maa na kaa i pee we yayami ko.
7Ke i je blɔ kpakpa a nɔ
kɛ ya nyɛɛ níhi nɛ ye tsui suɔ a se,
nɛ i kɛ nɔ́ nɛ ɔ peemi ble ye he ɔ,
8lɛɛ níhi nɛ i du ɔ,
ni kpahi nɛ a ba ye;
aloo ní ɔmɛ a hɛ mi nɛ kpata.
9Ke ye nyɛmi ko e yo he pee mi akɔnɔ hyɛ,
nɛ i ya wo lɛ ka ngɛ ye nyɛmi
nɛ ɔ sinya se ɔ,
10lɛɛ ye yo nɛ e hoo gba ní ha nɔ kpa,
nɛ nyumu kpa kɛ lɛ nɛ hwɔ.
11Yayami kaa kikɛ nɛ ɔ, e ji zo;
e sa kaa kojoli
nɛ a gbla nɔ tue ngɛ he.
12E ngɛ kaa la nɛ sãã nɔ́ kɛ yaa tsitsaa;
e ma kpata ye nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ hɛ mi.
13Ke ye tsɔlɔ nyumu,
aloo ye mawayo ko kɛ mi na sane ɔ,
i yeɔ sane ɔ ngɛ blɔ nɛ da nɔ.
14Ke i pee we ja a,
kɛ ma pee kɛ da Mawu hɛ mi kɛɛ?
Ke Mawu ba nɛ́ e ba kojo mi ɔ,
kɛ ma de kɛɛ?
15Mawu ɔ nɛ bɔ mi ɔ,
lɛ kɛ̃ lɛ e bɔ ye tsɔli nyumu ɔmɛ,
kɛ ye mawayi ɔmɛ.
16Ke nɔ́ ko hia ohiatsɛ ɔ,
i haa lɛ; yalɔyihi hu,
i ha we nɛ a hɛngmɛ nɔ daa nyu.
17Ke i ngɛ ní yee ɔ,
i ha we nɛ hwɔ yeɔ awusahi.
18I hyɛɔ awusahi a nɔ kaa a tsɛ ye wami be ɔ tsuo.
I ye bua yalɔyihi kɛ je ye nihe mi.
19Ke i na nɔ ko nɛ yi fi,
nɛ nɔ́ ko be e dɛ
nɛ e kɛ ma he bo nɛ e ha,
ke i na dɛgutsɛ ko kaa kikɛ nɛ ɔ,
20i haa lɛ he hami nɔ́
nɛ a kɛ imi nitsɛ ye to he bwɔmi pee.
Ke e he dɔ la a,
kɛkɛ e maa na mi si babauu.
21Ke i ya ye awusa ko amimi,
ejakaa i le kaa bɔ tsuaa bɔ nɛ pee ɔ,
a maa wo mi nguɔ ngɛ kojomi he ɔ,
22lɛɛ ye nine nɛ ku;
ye kɔni nɛ kplɔ kɛ je kɔni wu ɔ he.
23Se akɛnɛ i yeɔ Mawu Hewamitsɛ ɔ
tue gblami ɔ gbeye he je ɔ,
i be nyɛe ma pee nɔ́ ko kaa ja.
24I ngɔɛ ye hɛ fɔ we sika nɔ.
25Ní babauu nɛ i na a,
i fĩa we ngɔ fɔ nɔ.
26Pu nɛ tsoɔ saminyayoo,
kɛ nyɔhiɔ nɛ kpɛɔ saminyayoo nɛ ɔ,
i ja we mɛ hyɛ.
27Nɔ́ ko mlɔɔ we mi hyɛ
kaa ma fiɔ ye nine he
kɛ wo a hɛ mi nyami.
28Nɔ́ nɛ ɔ hu maa pee yayami
nɛ sa kaa kojoli
nɛ a gbla nɔ tue ngɛ he.
Ke i pee ja a,
kɛkɛ i kua Mawu nɛ ngɛ hiɔwe ɔ.
29Ke haomi ba ye he nyɛlɔ nɔ,
aloo ye he nyɛlɔ hɛ mi kpata a,
i nya we.
30I sɔle we hyɛ ke ye he nyɛli nɛ a gbo,
nɛ́ enɛ ɔ ba pee yayami ha mi.
31Nihi tsuo nɛ tsuɔ ní ha mi ɔ
le kaa hwɔ yi a ti nɔ ko hyɛ.
32I ha we nɛ nibwɔhi hwɔɔ gbɛjegbɛ nɔ;
mohu ɔ, i ngɔɔ mɛ kɛ baa we mi.
33I laa we ye yayamihi a nɔ
kaa bɔ nɛ Adam pee ɔ.
34I yi nihi babauu a hɛ mi gbeye.
Ke ye weku li muɔ mi ɔ,
e pee we mi nɔ́ ko
nɛ lɔ ɔ he ɔ, ma pee dii
nɛ ma ko je kpo.
35Anɛ nɔ ko be nɔ́ nɛ
i ngɛ dee ɔ tue bue lo?
I ngɛ kita kae kaa anɔkuale sisiisi lɛ
i ngɛ tue ɔ nɛ.
Mawu Ope ɔ nɛ ha mi heto.
Sanehi nɛ ye nya polɔ ɔ kɛ fɔ ye nɔ ɔ,
a ngma sane nɛ ɔmɛ kɛ wo womi mi jinɛ
36i kɛ maa fɔ ye konɔ,
nɛ ma fi kɛ wo ye yi kaa jlasi.
37Jinɛ ma nyɛɛ kam kam kaa ganɔ kɛ ya Mawu ngɔ,
nɛ ma ya bɔ lɛ nihi tsuo nɛ i pee ɔ.
38Ke ye zugba a,
aloo ngmɔ nɛ i pee
ngɛ zugba a nɔ ɔ maa po ye nya
39kaa i ye zugba a nɔ niba ní yaka
nɛ i wui he hiɔ,
aloo kaa i gbe zugbatsɛmɛ ɔmɛ,
konɛ ye nine nɛ su a zugba amɛ a nɔ ɔ,
40lɛɛ ngma nane mi ɔ,
mio nɛ puɛ;
akoko nane mi ɔ,
nga nɛ puɛ.
Hiob munyu ɔmɛ a nyagbe ji nɛ ɔ nɛ.

english_text:
Elihu Is Upset with Job's Friends
1Finally, these three men stopped arguing with Job, because he refused to admit he was guilty.
2Elihu from Buz was there, and he had become upset with Job for blaming God instead of himself. 3He was also angry with Job's three friends for not being able to prove that Job was wrong. 4Elihu was younger than these three, and he let them speak first. 5But he became irritated when they could not answer Job, 6and he said to them:
I am much younger than you,
so I have shown respect
by keeping silent.
7I once believed age
was the source of wisdom;
8now I truly realize
wisdom comes from God.
9Age is no guarantee of wisdom
and understanding.
10That's why I ask you
to listen to me.
I Eagerly Listened
* 11I eagerly listened
to each of your arguments,
12but not one of you proved
Job to be wrong.
13You shouldn't say,
“We know what's right!
Let God punish him.”
14Job hasn't spoken against me,
and so I won't answer him
with your arguments.
15All of you are shocked;
you don't know what to say.
16But am I to remain silent,
just because you
have stopped speaking?
17No! I will give my opinion,
18because I have so much to say,
that I can't keep quiet.
19I am like a swollen wineskin,
and I will burst
20if I don't speak.
* 21I don't know how to be unfair
or to flatter anyone—
22if I did, my Creator
would quickly destroy me!
translation_text:
Elihu tu munyu
(32.1—37.24)
1Jehanɛ lɛɛ nyumuhi etɛ nɛ ɔmɛ ha we Hiob e munyu ɔmɛ a heto hu, ejakaa a na kaa e buu e he kaa nɔmlɔ nɛ da. 2Kɛkɛ nɛ Elihu mi mi fu Hiob wawɛɛ nitsɛ kaa e pia Mawu, nɛ e wo lɛ nitsɛ e he nguɔ. (Elihu nɛ ɔ, Buz no ɔ nɛ a tsɛɛ lɛ Barakel ɔ binyumu ji lɛ. E je Ram weku ɔ mi, nɛ lɛɛ e bee ngɛ lejɛ ɔ kɛkɛ.) 3Elihu mi mi fu Hiob huɛmɛ etɛ ɔmɛ hulɔ, ejakaa a bu Hiob fɔ, be mi nɛ mɛ nitsɛmɛ a nɛ heto kpakpa ko nɛ a ha lɛ. 4E mlɛ kɛ ya si ni ɔmɛ tsuo tu munyu gbe nya loko e kɛ Hiob tu munyu, ejakaa lɛ ji a kpɛti nɔ wayoo pe kulaa. 5Benɛ Elihu na kaa nyumuhi etɛ nɛ ɔmɛ pa nyɛ we nɛ a ha Hiob e sane ɔmɛ a heto hu ɔ, e mi mi wo la, 6nɛ e tu munyu.
Elihu
Niheyo kɛkɛ ji mi;
nyɛɛ lɛɛ nikɔtɔmahi ji nyɛ.
Enɛ ɔ he je ɔ, i ya ye gbeye, nɛ i nyɛ we
nɛ ma de nyɛ bɔ nɛ imi hu i susu ha.
7I de ngɛ ye yi mi ke,
nyɛ lɛ e sa kaa nyɛɛ tu munyu;
nyɛ nimeli ɔmɛ lɛ
e sa kaa nyɛ je nyɛ juɛmi kpo.
8Se, Mawu Ope mumi ɔ
nɛ ngɛ nɔmlɔ adesa mi ɔ,
lɛ nɛ e haa nɔmlɔ nile.
9Pi wami nɛ peeɔ nɔ ní lelɔ;
pi bwɔmi nɛ haa nɛ nɔ leɔ nɔ́ nɛ da.
10Lɔ ɔ he ɔ,
i kpa nyɛ pɛɛ nɛ nyɛɛ bu mi tue,
konɛ imi hu ma je ye juɛmi kpo.
11Benɛ nyɛ ngɛ ní sɛɛe,
nɛ nyɛ ti nɔ tsuaa nɔ
ngɛ mɔde bɔe kaa
e maa tu nile munyu ɔ, i ngmɛ dii,
nɛ i ngɛ nyɛ tue bue.
12Nɛ́ i bu nyɛ tue hluu ɔ,
i na kaa nyɛ ti nɔ ko nɔ ko nyɛ we
nɛ e ha Hiob munyu ɔmɛ a heto bɔ nɛ sa.
13Nyɛɛ hyɛ saminya nɛ
e ko pee nyɛ kaa nyɛ le ní.
Mawu lɛ maa bu Hiob fɔ,
se pi nɔmlɔ adesa.
14Hiob ɔ, pi imi nɛ e kɛ ngɛ munyu tue.
Kaa imi lɛ e kɛ ngɛ munyu tue ɔ, jinɛ
bɔ nɛ nyɛ ha lɛ heto ɔ,
imi lɛɛ pi ja nɛ ma de lɛ.
15Hiob hyɛ, ní leli ɔmɛ pee yaa;
a pee dii, a pa be nɔ́ ko nɛ a ma de hu.
16I mlɛ hluu kaa a ma pa de nɔ́ ko lo;
i mlɛ kaa a ma ha mo heto kpa ko lo.
Se a daa si dii kɛkɛ.
17Lɔ ɔ he ɔ,
imi hu ma de ye nɔ́;
ma je imi hu ye juɛmi kpo.
18I ngɛ níhi babauu nɛ ma de.
Mumi nɛ ngɛ ye mi ɔ ngɛ ye yi se tsitsɛɛe.
19Ke i na we he blɔ nɛ ma tu munyu ɔ,
lɛɛ ma pɛ́ kaa wai tɔ
nɛ wai he hyi lɛ tɔtɔɔtɔ.
20Ma tu munyu, konɛ ma na he jɔmi;
ma pa ye nya mi,
nɛ ma ha mo o munyu ɔmɛ a heto.
21I be nɔ ko hɛ mi hyɛe kɛ tu munyu;
nɛ i be munyu dɔkɔdɔkɔ tue ngɛ nɔ ko he.
22I li munyu dɔkɔdɔkɔ tumi.
Ke i pee ja a,
ye bɔlɔ ɔ maa gbla ye tue amlɔ.

english_text:
Elihu Speaks
Job, Listen to Me!
1Job, listen to me!
Pay close attention.
* 2Everything I will say
3is true and sincere,
4just as surely as the Spirit
of God All-Powerful
gave me the breath of life.
5Now line up your arguments
and prepare to face me.
6We each were made from clay,
and God has no favorites,
7so don't be afraid of me
or what I might do.
I Have Heard You Argue
8I have heard you argue
9that you are innocent,
guilty of nothing.
10You claim that God
has made you his enemy,
11 that he has bound your feet
and blocked your path.
12But, Job, you're wrong—
God is greater
than any human.
13So why do you challenge God
to answer you?
14God speaks in different ways,
and we don't always
recognize his voice.
* 15 Sometimes in the night,
he uses terrifying dreams
16to give us warnings.
17God does this to make us turn
from sin and pride
18and to protect us
from being swept away
to the world of the dead.
19Sometimes we are punished
with a serious illness
and aching joints.
20Merely the thought
of our favorite food
makes our stomachs sick,
21and we become so skinny
that our bones stick out.
22We feel death and the grave
taking us in their grip.
23One of a thousand angels
then comes to our rescue
by saying we are innocent.
24The angel shows kindness,
commanding death to release us,
because the price was paid.
25Our health is restored,
we feel young again,
26and we ask God to accept us.
Then we joyfully worship God,
and we are rewarded
because we are innocent.
27When that happens,
we tell everyone,
“I sinned and did wrong,
but God forgave me
28and rescued me from death!
Now I will see the light.”
29God gives each of us
chance after chance
30to be saved from death
and brought into the light
that gives life.
31So, Job, pay attention
and don't interrupt,
32though I would gladly listen
to anything you say
that proves you are right.
33Otherwise, listen in silence
to my wisdom.
translation_text:
1Jehanɛ Hiob, i kpa mo pɛɛ
nɛ o bu nɔ́ nɛ ma de mo ɔ tue saminya.
2I pee klaalo nɛ i kɛ mo maa tu munyu,
nɛ nɔ́ nɛ ngɛ ye nya mi ɔ, ma de mo.
3Anɔkuale ɔ nɛ i le ɔ,
lɔ ɔ ma de mo
kɛ je ye tsui mi faa.
4Mawu mumi ɔ lɛ pee mi;
Ope ɔ mumi ɔ lɛ ha mi wami.
5Ke o ma nyɛ ɔ, ha mi heto.
Moo pee klaalo kɛ o munyu ɔmɛ,
konɛ o kɛ mi nɛ kpe.
6Bɔ nɛ o ngɛ ɔ,
ja nɔuu imi hu i ngɛ ngɛ Mawu hɛ mi.
Imi hu tabo zu ɔ kɛ̃ lɛ a kɛ puɛ mi.
7Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, koo ye mi gbeye;
pi nɔmlɔ nɛ ke e daa si ngɛ o hɛ mi
nɛ o tsui maa po ji mi.
8Munyu nɛ o tu
nɛ i nu kɛ ye tue ji,
9“Ye he tsɔ; i pee we nɔ́ ko nɛ dɛ blɔ.
I yeɔ nguɔ; yayami ko be ye he.
10Se kɛ̃, Mawu bu mi kaa e he nyɛlɔ,
nɛ e ngɛ tɔmihi hlae ngɛ ye he.
11 E bɔ ye nane pã,
nɛ e hɛ ngɛ ye he be tsuaa be.”
12Hyɛ, nɔ́ nɛ i ngɛ mo dee ji o nɔ́ be mi;
Mawu kle pe nɔmlɔ adesa.
13Mɛni he je mɔ lɛ o kɛ lɛ ngɛ pɛe
kaa e bui níhi nɛ e ngɛ pee ɔ ekoeko
he akɔtaa kɛ tsɔɔ we nɔ ko?
14Mawu ngɛ munyu tue daa be tsuaa be,
se nɔmlɔ adesa bui nɔ́ nɛ e ngɛ dee ɔ tue.
15 Nyɔ mi benɛ nimli adesahi hwɔ mahe vii ngɛ sa nɔ ɔ,
Mawu kɛ mɛ tuɔ munyu
kɛ guu nlamihi, kɛ ninahi a mi.
16Jamɛ a be ɔ, e bliɔ nimli adesahi a tue,
konɛ a nu nɔ́ nɛ e ngɛ mɛ dee ɔ.
Ke e bɔ mɛ kɔkɔ ɔ, a yeɔ gbeye.
17Mawu kɛ nimli adesahi tuɔ munyu
bɔ nɛ pee nɛ a kpa yayami peemi,
nɛ a ko wo a he nɔ.
18E hla we kaa a hɛ mi nɛ kpata;
e heɔ a yi wami kɛ jeɔ gbenɔ mi tete.
19Nɔmlɔ kaseɔ ní ngɛ hiɔ sa nɔ,
be mi nɛ e wuhi a mi ngɛ lɛ kpee
nɛ he jɔmi be mi.
20Ke e ba lɛ ja kɛkɛ e nya mi gbo,
nɛ e pee we lɛ kaa e ye nɔ́ ko hu;
niye ní ngɔngɔɛ tete po jlo we lɛ.
21E tãã he lo kanyakanya nɛ hi hyɛmi;
nɛ e wuhi nɛ a nɛ be ko nɛ be ɔ jeɔ kpo.
22Lɔ ɔ ji e miɔ nɛ e ma gbo ɔ nɛ.
23Alini, Mawu bɔfo akpe ɔmɛ
nɛ tsɔɔ nimli adesahi nɔ́ nɛ da a,
a ti nɔ kake ma ba je lɛ.
24Mawu bɔfo ɔ maa na lɛ mɔbɔ.
E ma de ke, “Nyɛɛ ngmɛɛ e he;
e be gbeje yae!
Nɔ́ nɛ a kɛ ma kpɔ lɛ konɛ
e ye e he ji nɛ ɔ nɛ.”
25E ma tsake maa pee niheyo ekohu,
nɛ e he womi maa pee tlotlootlo
kaa jokuɛyo he womi.
26Ke e fa kue ha Mawu ɔ,
Mawu ma he nɔ.
E ma sɔmɔ Mawu kɛ bua jɔmi,
nɛ Mawu ma ha nɛ níhi a mi maa hi ha lɛ ekohu.
27E kɛ bua jɔmi ma de ngɛ ma hɛ mi ke,
“I pee yayami.
I pee we nɔ́ nɛ da blɔ,
se kɛ̃ ɔ,
Mawu na mi mɔbɔ.
28Mawu kplɛɛ we nɛ ma ya gbeje,
nɛ i ngɛ je mi kɛ mwɔɔ.”
29Nɔ́ nɛ Mawu peeɔ ha nɔmlɔ si abɔ ji nɛ ɔ nɛ:
30e heɔ nɔmlɔ yi wami,
nɛ e haa lɛ bua jɔmi ngɛ je mi.
31Hiob, jehanɛ bu nɔ́ nɛ i ngɛ mo dee ɔ tue;
pee dii konɛ ma tu munyu.
32Ke o ngɛ nɔ́ ko nɛ o ma de ɔ,
de nɛ ma nu;
ma suɔ kaa ma wo mo nguɔ.
33Se ke o be nɔ́ ko nɛ o ma de ɔ,
lɛɛ pee dii, nɛ o bu mi tue,
nɛ ma tsɔɔ mo nile.

english_text:
Elihu Continues
You Men Think You Are Wise
1Elihu said:
2You men think you are wise,
but just listen to me!
3Think about my words,
as you would taste food.
4Then we can decide the case
and give a just verdict.
5Job claims he is innocent
and God is guilty
of mistreating him.
6Job also argues that God
considers him a liar
and that he is suffering severely
in spite of his innocence.
7But to tell the truth,
Job is shameless!
8He spends his time with sinners,
9because he has said,
“It doesn't pay to please God.”
If Any of You Are Smart
10If any of you are smart,
you will listen and learn
that God All-Powerful
does what is right.
11 God always treats everyone
the way they deserve,
12and he is never unfair.
13From the very beginning,
God has been in control
of all the world.
14If God took back the breath
that he breathed into us,
15we humans would die
and return to the soil.
16So be smart and listen!
17The mighty God is the one
who brings about justice,
and you are condemning him.
18Indeed, God is the one
who condemns unfair rulers.
19And God created us all;
he has no favorites,
whether rich or poor.
20Even powerful rulers die
in the darkness of night
when they least expect it,
just like the rest of us.
God Watches Everything We Do
21God watches everything we do.
22No evil person can hide
in the deepest darkness.
23And so, God doesn't need
to set a time for judgment.
24Without asking for advice,
God removes mighty leaders
and puts others in their place.
25He knows what they are like,
and he wipes them out
in the middle of the night.
26And while others look on,
he punishes them
because they were evil
27and refused to obey him.
28The persons they mistreated
had prayed for help,
until God answered
their prayers.
29When God does nothing,
can any person or nation
find fault with him?
30But still, he punishes rulers
who abuse their people.
31Job, you should tell God
that you are guilty
and promise to do better.
32Then ask him to point out
what you did wrong,
so you won't do it again.
33Do you make the rules,
or does God?
You have to decide—
I can't do it for you;
now make up your mind.
34Job, anyone with good sense
can easily see
35that you are speaking nonsense
and lack good judgment.
36So I pray for you to suffer
as much as possible
for talking like a sinner.
37You have rebelled against God,
time after time,
and have even insulted us.
