translation_text:
1-2Nyɛ ní leli, nyɛɛ bu mi tue.
3 Munyu kpakpa, loo munyu yaya a,
tue nɛ leɔ,
kaa bɔ nɛ lilɛ hu leɔ niye ní
nɛ ngɔɔ, kɛ nɔ́ nɛ ngɔɛ ɔ.
4Nyɛ ha nɛ waa hyɛ sane ɔ mi,
nɛ waa na anɔkuale ɔ.
5Hiob ngɛ tsɔɔe kaa dalɔ ji lɛ,
se Mawu mohu lɛ yi dami sane ha lɛ.
6E ke e pee we nɔ́ ko nɛ dɛ blɔ,
se a bu lɛ lakpatsɛ.
E ngɛ mi kaa a plaa lɛ yeyee mohu,
se e le kaa e pee we yayami ko.
7Anɛ nyɛ na nyumu ko hyɛ kaa Hiob lo?
Nɔmlɔ nɛ bɔɔ musu bɔ nɛ e suɔ
kaa bɔ nɛ a nuu nyu ɔ.
8E kɛ nimli yayamihi lɛ bɔɔ.
9E deɔ ke e he be se nami
kaa nɔ ko nɛ pee Mawu suɔmi nya ní.
10Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, nyɛɛ bu mi tue,
nyɛ juɛmitsɛmɛ!
Anɛ Mawu maa pee yi wu tso ní lo?
Anɛ Ope ɔ maa pee nɔ́ nɛ dɛ blɔ lo?
11 Mawu lɛɛ nɔ́ nɛ o tsu ɔ,
lɔ ɔ he hiɔ lɛ e woɔ mo;
Mawu woɔ nɔ tsuaa nɔ hiɔ bɔ nɛ sa lɛ.
12Niinɛ, Mawu pee we nɔ́ nɛ dɛ blɔ;
Ope ɔ plɛ we nɔ ko sane hɛ mi ngɔ bu si.
13Mɛnɔ nɛ ha Mawu e he wami ɔ?
Mɛnɔ nɛ tu je ɔ tsuo kɛ wo e dɛ mi?
14Ke Mawu kpɔ mumi nɛ haa nɔ wami ngɛ nɔmlɔ dɛ ɔ,
15nimli adesahi tsuo ma gbo,
nɛ a ma plɛ pee tabo zu ekohu.
16Lɔ ɔ he ɔ,
ke ní leli ji nyɛ ɔ, nyɛɛ bu mi tue.
17Nɔ nɛ he wa nɛ e yeɔ dami sane ɔ,
o maa bu lɛ fɔ,
konɛ nɔ nɛ sume dami sane yemi ɔ mohu
nɛ ye tsɛ lo?
18Mɛnɔ lɛ deɔ matsɛ ke, “Yaka nɔmlɔ ji mo!”
Mɛnɔ lɛ deɔ odehehi ke, “Yiwutsotsɛmɛ ji nyɛ!”
19Mawu hyɛ we ganɔhi a hɛ mi.
E bui niatsɛmɛ pe ohiatsɛmɛ;
ejakaa lɛ nɛ e bɔ mɛ tsuo.
20Nɔmlɔ gboɔ tlukaa,
Mawu fiaa nimli adesahi nɔ́
nyɔ mi kɛkɛ a hɛ mi kpata.
Nimli nguahi po Mawu gbeɔ mɛ
nɛ adesa nine be mi.
21E hɛ ngɛ nɔmlɔ he be tsuaa be.
E náá e ní peemi níhi tsuo.
22Diblii ko be nɛ nya tsa
bɔ nɛ yayami peeli maa laa a he ngɛ mi.
23E hia we kaa Mawu nɛ to be ha nimli adesahi
nɛ a ba e ngɔ loko e kojo mɛ.
24E jeɔ nimli nguahi kɛ jeɔ a blɔ hehi,
nɛ e ngɔɔ ni kpahi kɛ daa a nane mi;
e hia we kaa e hla a sane ɔmɛ a mi.
25Akɛnɛ Mawu le nɔ́ nɛ a tsuɔ he je ɔ,
e ba tuaa mɛ nyɔ mi, nɛ e kpataa a hɛ mi.
26Mawu gblaa yayami peeli a tue ngɛ ma hɛ mi,
27ejakaa a kpa e se nyɛɛmi,
nɛ e mlaa amɛ hu a yi ekoeko nɔ.
28A ha nɛ ohiatsɛmɛ kpa ngmlaa
kɛ ba Mawu yemi kɛ buami,
nɛ Mawu nu nɔ́ nali ɔmɛ a kue fami ɔ.
29Ke Mawu pee dii ɔ,
mɛnɔ maa pa e nya mi?
Ke e ngɔ e hɛ mi kɛ laa a,
mɛnɔ maa na lɛ; ma ko loo,
aloo nɔmlɔ adesa ko?
30Lɔ ɔ lɛɛ ma ko be nyɛe maa pee nɔ ko,
konɛ nɔmlɔ yayami ko ye tsɛ
nɛ e ba kpata e ma a hɛ mi.
31Hiob, anɛ o jaje o yayami ɔmɛ kɛ tsɔɔ Mawu lo?
Anɛ o wo lɛ si kaa o be yayami pee hu lo?
32Anɛ o fa kue ha Mawu
ke e tsɔɔ mo o tɔmi ɔmɛ lo?
Anɛ o kplɛɛ kaa o ma kpa yayami peemi lo?
33Nɛ́ o kua Mawu ɔ,
o ngɛ lɛ blɔ hyɛe
kaa e pee moo o suɔmi nya ní ha mo lo?
Mo lɛ o ma ha munyu nɛ ɔ heto; pi imi.
Kɛ o susuɔ kɛɛ?
34Nihi nɛ ngɛ juɛmi,
kɛ ní leli tsuo
nɛ ngɛ mi tue bue ɔ,
nɔ́ nɛ a ma de ji,
35“Munyuhi nɛ Hiob ngɛ tue ɔ,
juɛmi be mi;
e li nɔ́ nɛ e ngɛ dee ɔ.”
36E je imi nɔ kake ye he jinɛ
a ko gbla Hiob tue wawɛɛ nitsɛ
ngɛ munyu yayahi nɛ e tu kɛ si Mawu ɔ he.
37Hiob tsɔ atuã kɛ piɛ e yayami ɔmɛ a he,
nɛ e tu munyuhi babauu ngɛ wa hɛ mi
kɛ si Mawu.

english_text:
Elihu Continues
Are You Really Innocent?
1Elihu said:
2Job, are you really innocent
in the sight of God?
3Don't you honestly believe
it pays to obey him?
4I will give the answers
to you and your friends.
* 5Look up to the heavens
6 and think!
Do your sins hurt God?
7Is any good you may have done
at all helpful to him?
8The evil or good you do
only affects other humans.
9In times of trouble,
everyone begs the mighty God
to have mercy.
10But after their Creator
helps them through hard times,
they forget about him,
11though he makes us wiser
than animals or birds.
12God won't listen to the prayers
of proud and evil people.
13If God All-Powerful refuses
to answer their empty prayers,
14he will surely deny
your impatient request
to face him in court.
15Job, you were wrong to say
God doesn't punish sin.
16Everything you have said
adds up to nonsense.
translation_text:
1-2Hiob, e sɛ kaa o deɔ ke
o pee we yayami ko ngɛ Mawu hɛ mi.
3E sɛ po kaa o biɔ Mawu ke,
“Ke i pee yayami ɔ,
mɛni lɔ ɔ kɔɔ ngɛ o he?
Mɛni se i naa kaa i pee we yayami ko?”
4Ma ha mo heto,
mo kɛ o huɛmɛ ɔmɛ tsuo.
5Hyɛ hiɔwe; hyɛ bɔ nɛ o
kɛ bɔku ɔmɛ a he kɛ ha!
6 Ke o pee yayami ɔ,
kɛ lɔ ɔ saa Mawu he kɛɛ?
Aloo ke o pee yayami nɔtonɔto ɔ,
mɛni lɔ ɔ peeɔ ha Mawu?
7Ke o pee nɔ́ nɛ da a,
mɛni ji nɔ́ nɛ o pee kɛ ha Mawu?
Mɛni ji nɔ́ nɛ Mawu ma na ngɛ o dɛ?
8Ke o pee yayami ɔ,
o nyɛmi nɔmlɔ adesa lɛ naa nɔ́;
ke o pee kpakpa a,
o nyɛmi nɔmlɔ adesa lɛ naa he se.
9Ke a ngɛ nimli adesahi yi mi wae ɔ,
a kpaa ngmlaa kɛ tsɛɔ balɔ.
10Se Mawu nɛ bɔ mɛ ɔ,
nɔ nɛ baa a yi nyɔ mi tete po ɔ,
lɛɛ nɔ ko hla we e se blɔ.
11Mawu ɔ nɛ pee wɔ ní leli pe lohwehi tsuo ɔ,
a hla we e se blɔ.
12A kpaa ngmlaa kɛ tsɛɔ balɔ,
se Mawu bui mɛ tue;
ejakaa he nɔ woli, kɛ yayami peeli ji mɛ.
13Niinɛ, Mawu bui yaka ngmlaa tue;
Mawu Ope ɔ bui he akɔtaa.
14Hiob, mo lɛ o ke o be Mawu nae ɔ?
O sane ɔ ngɛ e hɛ mi;
moo hyɛ lɛ blɔ.
15Amlɔ nɛ ɔ, o susuɔ kaa Mawu gbla we nɔ tue,
nɛ ke nɔ pee yayami hu e di se tsɔ.
16Enɛ ɔ he je ɔ,
mo Hiob, o paa o nya mi
nɛ o tuɔ munyu bɔ nɛ o suɔ.
O tuɔ munyuhi babauu nɛ juɛmi be mi.

english_text:
Elihu Continues
Be Patient a While Longer
1Elihu said:
2Be patient a while longer;
I have something else to say
in God's defense.
3God always does right—
and this knowledge
comes straight from God.
4You can rest assured
that what I say is true.
5Although God is mighty,
he cares about everyone
and makes fair decisions.
6The wicked are cut down,
and those who are wronged
receive justice.
7God watches over good people
and places them in positions
of power and honor forever.
8But when people are prisoners
of suffering and pain,
* 9God points out their sin
and their pride,
10then he warns them
to turn back to him.
11And if they obey,
they will be successful
and happy from then on.
12But if they foolishly refuse,
they will be rewarded
with a violent death.
Godless People Are Too Angry
13Godless people are too angry
to ask God for help
when he punishes them.
14So they die young
in shameful disgrace.
15Hard times and trouble
are God's way
of getting our attention!
16And at this very moment,
God deeply desires
to lead you from trouble
and to spread your table
with your favorite food.
17Now that the judgment
for your sins
has fallen upon you,
18don't let your anger
and the pain you endured
make you sneer at God.
19Your reputation and riches
cannot protect you
from distress,
20nor can you find safety
in the dark world below.
21Be on guard! Don't turn to evil
as a way of escape.
22God's power is unlimited.
He needs no teachers
23to guide or correct him.
Others Have Praised God
24Others have praised God
for what he has done,
so join with them.
25From down here on earth,
everyone has looked up and seen
26how great God is—
God is more than we imagine;
no one can count the years
he has lived.
* 27God gathers moisture
into the clouds
28and supplies us with rain.
29Who can understand
how God scatters the clouds
and speaks from his home
in the thunderstorm?
30And when God sends lightning,
it can be seen
at the bottom of the sea.
31By producing such rainstorms,
God rules the world
and provides us with food.
32Each flash of lightning
is one of his arrows
striking its target,
33and the thunder tells
of his anger against sin.
translation_text:
1-2Moo to o tsui si nɛ o bu mi tue!
Níhi nɛ i ngɛ mo dee ngɛ Mawu nane mi ɔ,
i gbi nya lolo.
3Ma ngɔ ye nile nɛ hiɛ babauu ɔ
kɛ tsɔɔ mo kaa Mawu
nɛ bɔ mi ɔ, dalɔ ji lɛ.
4Anɔkuale i ngɛ tue ɔ nɛ, pi lakpa;
ní lelɔ kpanaa lɛ daa si ngɛ o hɛ mi ɔ nɛ.
5Mawu kle! E nyɛ́ nɔ.
Nɔ́ ko nɔ́ ko be nɛ e juɛmi sui he.
6E ha we nɛ yayami peeli a se kɛɛ ngɛ je mi;
e yeɔ ohiatsɛmɛ a sane kɛ haa mɛ.
7Mawu hɛngmɛ ngɛ dali a he be tsuaa be.
E hyɛɛ a nɔ kaa matsɛmɛ,
nɛ e woɔ a hɛ mi nyami daa.
8Se ke a bɔ nihi pã,
nɛ a ngɛ nɔ́ nae
ngɛ nɔ́ ko nɛ a pee he ɔ,
9Mawu tsɔɔ mɛ a nɔ́ nami ɔ sisi,
kaa a wo a he nɔ,
nɛ a pee yayami.
10E kaa a hɛ mi saminya,
nɛ e deɔ mɛ ke a kpa yayami peemi.
11Ke a bu Mawu tue nɛ a sɔmɔ lɛ ɔ,
a ma na tue mi jɔmi, kɛ kplɔkɔtɔ.
12Se ke a bui tue ɔ,
lɛɛ a ma gbo ngɛ klaate nya kaa nihi nɛ li nɔ́.
13Nihi nɛ li Mawu ɔ,
mɛɛ lɛɛ a woɔ a mi mi la kɛ yaa nɔ.
Ke a gbla a tue po,
a fa we kue kɛ tsɛ balɔ.
14A gboɔ ngɛ a nihe mi,
ejakaa a hyɛ we a nɔmlɔ tso ɔ nɔ saminya.
A gbenɔ peeɔ hɛ mi si puemi.
15Mawu tsɔɔ nihi ní kɛ guu nɔ́ nami mi;
e ngɔɔ amanehlu kɛ bliɔ nihi a hɛngmɛ.
16Mawu je mo kɛ je amanehlu mi,
nɛ e ha mo tue mi jɔmi,
kɛ niye ní kpakpa.
17Se, jehanɛ lɛɛ
a ngɛ o tue gblae bɔ nɛ sa mo.
18Hyɛ saminya nɛ o mi mi nɛ fu ɔ
kó ha nɛ o ya gbe Mawu he guɛ.
Ko ha ní nami nɛ je o juɛmi kɛ je Mawu he.
19Ke o fa kue kɛ tsɛ balɔ hu, yaka gu;
o he wami tsuo be nyɛe ma tsu nɔ́ ko.
20Ko de ke o na nɛ e su nyɔ mi,
be mi nɛ nihi a hɛ mi ma kpata.
21Hyɛ saminya nɛ o ko ya nyɛɛ yayami se.
A kɛ amanehlu nɛ ɔ ba o nɔ,
konɛ o ko pee yayami.
22Na nɛ o le kaa Mawu ngɛ he wami;
e kle pe tsɔɔli tsuo.
23Mɛnɔ lɛ maa tsɔɔ Mawu nɔ́ nɛ sa nɛ e pee?
Mɛnɔ lɛ maa po e nya ke e pee yayami?
24Nihi ngɛ Mawu yi jee
ngɛ e ní tsumi kpetekpleenyɛ ɔmɛ a he;
mo hu mo je e yi koo.
25Níhi nɛ Mawu tsuɔ ɔ, nɔ tsuaa nɔ naa,
se nɔ ko nɔ ko nui sisi.
26Hyɛ, Mawu kle! Wa li lɛ kulaa;
jeha nɛ e ye hu wa juɛmi sui he.
27Mawu lɛ gblaa nyu kɛ jeɔ zugba,
nɛ e haa nɛ e plɛɔ peeɔ hiɔmi nɛ nɛɛ.
28E haa nɛ hiɔmi nɛɛ babauu kɛ jeɔ bɔku mi
kɛ pueɔ si ha nimli adesahi tsuo.
29Bɔ nɛ bɔku haa si,
kɛ bɔ nɛ hiɔwe siɔ
ngɛ lɛ Mawu ɔ e hi he ɔ,
mɛnɔ lɛ le?
30E haa nɛ oslabai gbaa ngɛ hiɔwe ɔ tsuo,
se wo ɔ sisi lɛɛ e ngɛ diblii mi.
31Bɔ nɛ Mawu peeɔ kɛ hyɛɛ e ma a nɔ ji nɛ ɔ nɛ:
e haa mɛ niye ní babauu.
32E kɛ e nine nuɔ oslabai,
nɛ he tsuaa he nɛ e fa lɛ ke e ya a,
kɛkɛ e gba kɛ ya lejɛ ɔ.
33Ke hiɔwe si ɔ,
lɔ ɔ tsɔɔ kaa kɔɔhiɔ
nɛ nya wa ma ngɛ se.
Lohwehi tete po le enɛ ɔ.

english_text:
Elihu Continues
I Am Frightened
1I am frightened
and tremble all over,
2when I hear the roaring voice
of God in the thunder,
3and when I see his lightning
flash across the sky.
4God's majestic voice
thunders his commands,
5creating miracles too marvelous
for us to understand.
6Snow and heavy rainstorms
7make us stop and think
about God's power,
8and they force animals
to seek shelter.
9The windstorms of winter strike,
10and the breath of God
freezes streams and rivers.
11Rain clouds filled with lightning
appear at God's command,
12traveling across the sky
13to release their cargo—
sometimes as punishment for sin,
sometimes as kindness.
Consider Carefully
14Job, consider carefully
the many wonders of God.
15Can you explain why lightning
flashes at the orders
16of God who knows all things?
Or how he hangs the clouds
in empty space?
17You almost melt in the heat
of fierce desert winds
when the sky is like brass.
18God can hammer out the clouds
in spite of the oppressive heat,
but can you?
19Tell us what to say to God!
Our minds are in the dark,
and we don't know how
to argue our case.
20Should I risk my life
by telling God
that I want to speak?
21No one can stare at the sun
after a breeze has blown
the clouds from the sky.
22Yet the glorious splendor
of God All-Powerful
is brighter by far.
23God cannot be seen—
but his power is great,
and he is always fair.
24And so we humans fear God,
because he shows no respect
for those who are proud
and think they know so much.
translation_text:
1Nɔ́ nɛ ɔ ha ye tsui po, nɛ e ngɛ fiae kplakplaakpla.
2Nyɛɛ bu tue! Mawu wo gbi, nyɛɛ bu tue;
nyɛɛ bu hoo nɛ ngɛ pɛe kɛ je e nya mi ɔ tue.
3E haa oslabai gbaa ngɛ hiɔwe,
nɛ e kpɛɔ ngɛ je ɔ kɔ nya he tsuaa he.
4Kɛkɛ ɔ, hiɔwe siɔ wawɛɛ kɛ nyɛɛɔ se.
Jamɛ a be ɔ tsuo oslabai ɔ ngɛ la pae plamplam.
5Ke Mawu wo gbi kikɛ nɛ ɔ,
e peeɔ ní nguahi nɛ wa juɛmi sui he.
6E faa ke snoo nɛ nɛ ngɔ pue zugba a nɔ,
nɛ e haa nɛ hiɔmi nɛ nya wa hu nɛɔ ja nɔuu.
7Ke e ba kikɛ nɛ ɔ,
nimli adesahi kpaa ní tsumi,
konɛ nimli adesahi ngɛ je ɔ mi tsuo
nɛ a na e he wami ɔ.
8Kɛkɛ ɔ, nga mi lohwehi beɔ kɛ yaa a hi hehi.
9Kɔɔhiɔ nɛ nya wa fiaa kɛ jeɔ leneyi je,
nɛ fĩɛ nɛ nya wa jeɔ omleyi je kɛ baa.
10Mumi nɛ jeɔ Mawu gugwɔ mi ɔ
haa nɛ nyu babauu ɔ wluaa gaganii kaa tɛ.
11Mawu haa bɔku ɔmɛ hyi ɔ kɛ nyu.
Oslabai hii la pae ngɛ bɔku ɔmɛ a mi,
12be mi nɛ a ngɛ nyɛɛe nɛ a ngɛ Mawu ní tsue ɔ.
Nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ Mawu fa mɛ ke a pee
ngɛ je ɔ mi tsuo kɛ bɔle si ɔ,
a peeɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ.
13Mawu haa hiɔmi nɛɛ, konɛ nyu nɛ
ba zugba a nɔ;
e haa hiɔmi nɛɛ
nɛ e kɛ gblaa nimli adesahi a tue,
aloo nɛ e kɛ naa mɛ mɔbɔ.
14Hiob, bu tue!
Da si dii nɛ o susu Mawu nyakpɛ ní ɔmɛ a he.
15Anɛ o le bɔ nɛ Mawu faa,
nɛ e haa oslabai gbaa kɛ jeɔ bɔku mi lo?
16Bɔ nɛ bɔkuhi plɛɔ kɛ beɔ kɛ a he sɔmi
ngɛ nyakpɛ blɔ nɔ ɔ, anɛ o le lo?
Ee, ní lelɔ kpanaa a,
e ní tsumi ji lɔ ɔ nɛ.
17Ke leneyi je kɔɔhiɔ ngɛ fiae,
nɛ je mi ngmɛ dii ɔ,
anɛ o le bɔ nɛ peeɔ loko moo o he mi dɔɔ la lo?
18Hiɔwe ɔ nɛ he wa kpakpataa
kaa ahuhuɛ nɛ a sile,
nɛ a puɛ ngɔ ma si ɔ,
anɛ o ma nyɛ maa gbla mi
kaa bɔ nɛ lɛ
Mawu ɔ, e pee ɔ lo?
19Hiob, moo tsɔɔ wɔ nɔ́ nɛ wa ma de Mawu.
Wɔɔ lɛɛ wa juɛmi mi wo diblii,
nɛ nɔ́ ko be wa nya mi nɛ wa ma de.
20I be suɔe nɛ i kɛ Mawu nɛ tu munyu.
Ke i pee ja a,
ye hɛ mi ma kpata.
21Amlɔ nɛ ɔ, la nɛ ngɛ hiɔwe ɔ
ngɛ kpɛe nylamnylam nɛ e hi hyɛmi,
ejakaa kɔɔhiɔ muɔ bɔku ɔmɛ kɛ ho.
22Je mi tsɔ hleii kaa sika tsu ngɛ omleyi je;
Mawu hɛ mi nyami ɔ ngɛ gbeye.
23Mawu Ope ɔ loo, wa be nyɛe maa su e he.
E ngɛ he wami, e yeɔ dami sane,
nɛ e pee we nɔ́ nɛ dɛ kɔkɔɔkɔ.
24Enɛ ɔ he je ɔ, nihi tsuo yeɔ lɛ gbeye;
ni nɛmɛ nɛ mɛɛ a buɔ a he ní leli ɔ,
Mawu lɛɛ e bui mɛ fɛɛ.

english_text:
The Lord Speaks
From Out of a Storm
1From out of a storm,
the Lord said to Job:
2Why do you talk so much
when you know so little?
3Now get ready to face me!
Can you answer
the questions I ask?
4How did I lay the foundation
for the earth?
Were you there?
5Doubtless you know who decided
its length and width.
6What supports the foundation?
Who placed the cornerstone,
7 while morning stars sang,
and angels rejoiced?
8 When the ocean was born,
I set its boundaries
9and wrapped it in blankets
of thickest fog.
10Then I built a wall around it,
locked the gates, 11and said,
“Your powerful waves stop here!
They can go no farther.”
Did You Ever Tell the Sun To Rise?
12Did you ever tell the sun to rise?
And did it obey?
13Did it take hold of the earth
and shake out the wicked
like dust from a rug?
14Early dawn outlines the hills
like stitches on clothing
or sketches on clay.
15But its light is too much
for those who are evil,
and their power is broken.
16Job, have you ever walked
on the ocean floor?
17Have you seen the gate
to the world of the dead?
18And how large is the earth?
Tell me, if you know!
19Where is the home of light,
and where does darkness live?
20Can you lead them home?
21I'm certain you must be able to,
since you were already born
when I created everything.
22Have you been to the places
where I keep snow and hail,
23until I use them to punish
and conquer nations?
24From where does lightning leap,
or the east wind blow?
25Who carves out a path
for thunderstorms?
Who sends torrents of rain
26on empty deserts
where no one lives?
27Rain that changes barren land
to meadows green with grass.
28Who is the father of the dew
and of the rain?
29Who gives birth to the sleet
and the frost
30that fall in winter,
when streams and lakes
freeze solid as a rock?
Can You Arrange Stars?
31 Can you arrange stars in groups
such as Orion
and the Pleiades?
32Do you control the stars
or set in place the Big Dipper
and the Little Dipper?
33Do you know the laws
that govern the heavens,
and can you make them rule
the earth?
34Can you order the clouds
to send a downpour,
35or will lightning flash
at your command?
36Did you teach birds to know
that rain or floods
are on their way?
37Can you count the clouds
or pour out their water
38on the dry, lumpy soil?
39When lions are hungry,
do you help them hunt?
40Do you send an animal
into their den?
41And when starving young ravens
cry out to me for food,
do you satisfy their hunger?
translation_text:
Yawɛ ha Hiob heto
1Kɛkɛ nɛ Yawɛ kɛ Hiob tu munyu
kɛ je kɔɔhiɔ nɛ nya wa mi.
Yawɛ
2Mɛnɔ ji mo nɛ o kɛ munyu puu nɛ juɛmi be mi
biɔ mi ye nile he sane?
3Da si kaa nyumu, nɛ o ha mi
sanehi nɛ ma bi mo ɔ a heto.
4Benɛ i to je ɔ sisi ɔ,
jije o ngɛ?
Ke o le ɔ, ha mi heto.
5Je ɔ kami kɛ e blimi ɔ,
mɛnɔ lɛ tsɔɔ?
Mɛnɔ lɛ fɔ kpa kɛ susu?
Tse o ma nyɛ ma ha heto!
6Mɛni nɔ a fia e sisi tomi ɔmɛ kɛ ma?
Mɛnɔ lɛ to kɔ nya tɛ ɔ?
7Jamɛ a ligbi ɔ mɔtu ɔ,
dodoe ɔmɛ tsuo la,
nɛ Mawu bimɛ ɔmɛ tsuo hwɔ lele.
8 Benɛ wo ɔ hia kɛ ma babaaba
kaa nɔ́ nɛ zugba a nitsɛ mi mi lɛ e je ɔ,
mɛnɔ lɛ nga sinya a kɛ tsi wo ɔ nya?
9Imi lɛ i ngɔ bɔku kɛ ha wo ɔ he;
imi lɛ i ngɔ diblii kpii kɛ blaa lɛ.
10Imi lɛ i po huzu kɛ wo wo ɔ he,
nɛ i ma nya agbo kɛ e se dade.
11I de wo ɔ ke,
“Moo fia kɛ ba su hiɛ ɔ pɛ;
koo be he!
O we oslɔke ngua amɛ ɔ,
he nɛ a ma ba ta ji nɛ ɔ nɛ.”
12Hiob, o wami be ɔ tsuo mi ɔ,
anɛ o fa hyɛ ke je nɛ na,
nɛ je na lo?
13Anɛ o fa hyɛ ke mɔtu la a nɛ nu je ɔ
kɛ yaa si a ma huanya yiwutsotsɛmɛ
kɛ je a laami hehi lo?
14Piani la haa nɛ a naa yoku ɔmɛ, kɛ kɔ̃ ɔmɛ saminya
kaa bɔ nɛ a naa zahi ngɛ bo mi,
aloo nya sɔumi nɔ́ ngɛ tabo zu mi ɔ.
15Piani la nya wa tsɔ ha yayami peeli.
E tsiɔ mɛ blɔ nɛ a nyɛ we nɛ a tsuɔ yi wu tso ní.
16Pahi nɛ ngɛ wo ɔ sisi ɔ,
anɛ o ya a kasa nya hyɛ lo?
O nyɛɛ ngɛ muɔ voo ɔ
nɛ ngɛ lejɛ ɔ mi hyɛ lo?
17Agbohi nɛ ngɛ ni gbogboehi a je,
he nɛ wo diblii kpii ɔ,
anɛ nɔ ko bli nya kɛ tsɔɔ mo hyɛ lo?
18Anɛ o le je ɔ blimi lo?
Ke o le ɔ, ha mi heto.
19Jije a guu kɛ yaa la hi he?
Diblii hu jije e hi he ngɛ?
20Anɛ o ma nyɛ maa tsɔɔ mɛ a huzu nya,
nɛ o kpale mɛ kɛ ba a hi he ekohu lo?
21Ee, o ma nyɛ; nɔkɔtɔma ji mo.
Jamɛ a be ɔ, tse a fɔ mo!
22Hehi nɛ i toɔ snoo, kɛ gbiɛ ngo ngu ngɛ ɔ,
o ya lejɛ ɔmɛ hyɛ lo?
23I ngɔ mɛ ngɔ to lejɛ ɔ
ngɛ haomi, loo ta nɛ maa ba he.
24Jije a guu kɛ yaa he nɛ pu jeɔ kɛ baa,
aloo he nɛ beleku kɔɔhiɔ fiaa kɛ jeɔ?
25Mɛnɔ lɛ gba nyu dɔ
kɛ ha hiɔmi nɛ nɛɛ piapiaapia a?
Mɛnɔ lɛ je blɔ
ha hiɔwe simi, kɛ oslabai gbami?
26Mɛnɔ lɛ haa nɛ hiɔmi nɛɛ ngɛ zugba nɔ he nɛ
nɔmlɔ adesa ko be
kaa nga kplanaa nɔ kikɛ nɛ ɔ?
27Zugba nɛ gbo,
aloo zugba nɛ pee nga kplanaa a,
mɛnɔ lɛ haa lɛ nyu loko nga puɛɔ ngɛ nɔ?
28Hiɔmi nɛ nɛɛ ɔ,
e ngɛ tsɛ lo?
Bɔ́ hu, mɛnɔ lɛ fɔ lɛ?
29Mɛnɔ muklii mi nyu tɛ je?
Hiɔwe bɔ́ ɔ, mɛnɔ lɛ fɔ lɛ?
30Nyu ɔ wluaa gaganii,
nɛ e he waa kaa tɛ.
31 Dodoehi nɛ a tsɛɛ ke Kungwɔ
kɛ e bimɛ ɔ,
anɛ o ma nyɛ maa fi mɛ kɔsɔkɔsɔ lo?
Huɛ etɛ ɔ, o ma nyɛ maa pɛne
e mi mi fimi nɔ́ ɔ lo?
32Anɛ o ma nyɛ maa tsɔɔ dodoehi blɔ
ngɛ a be mi lo?
O ma nyɛ maa tsɔɔ Je kpaago kɛ
e bimɛ ɔmɛ blɔ lo?
33Anɛ o le mlaahi nɛ a kɛ tsuɔ ní ngɛ hiɔwe lo?
O ma nyɛ ma ha jamɛ a mlaa amɛ
nɛ tsu ní ngɛ zugba a nɔ lo?
34Anɛ o ma nyɛ maa wo gbi
nɛ nyu babauu maa je bɔku ɔmɛ a mi ba pɔ mo lo?
35Anɛ o ma nyɛ ma fa oslabai ke e gba,
nɛ e ma he nɔ ke,
“Ma pee kaa bɔ nɛ o fa mi ɔ” lo?
36Mɛnɔ lɛ ha nɔmlɔ adesa nile?
Mɛnɔ kɛ juɛmi wo nɔmlɔ yi mi?
37Mɛnɔ lɛ le ní bɔ nɛ sa
nɛ e ma nyɛ maa kane bɔkuhi ngɛ hiɔwe?
Mɛnɔ ma nyɛ ma plɛ nyu buɛ mi bɔku ɔmɛ
a nya ngɔ ka si,
38nɛ tabo zu ɔ ma pɔtɔ maa pee mɔsɔ;
nɛ lɔ ɔ se ɔ, e maa pee zu kpɔ longolongohi?
39Mo lɛ o haa jata niye ní nɛ e yeɔ lo?
Mo lɛ o haa jata bimɛ ní nɛ a yeɔ nɛ a tɔɔ,
40be mi nɛ a buu si ngɛ tɛ puɔhi a mi,
loo a wo ka ngɛ a muɔhi a mi?
41Mɛnɔ lɛ haa kuakualabite niye ní?
Ke hwɔ ngɛ kuakualabite bimɛ yee,
nɛ a ngɛ niye ní hlae kɛ bee,
nɛ a kpa ngmlaa tsɛ mi ɔ,
mɛnɔ lɛ haa mɛ niye ní?

english_text:
The Lord Continues
When Do Mountain Goats Give Birth?
1When do mountain goats
and deer give birth?
Have you been there
when their young are born?
* 2How long are they pregnant
3before they deliver?
4Soon their young grow strong
and then leave
to be on their own.
5Who set wild donkeys free?
6I alone help them survive
in salty desert sand.
7They stay far from crowded cities
and refuse to be tamed.
8Instead, they roam the hills,
searching for pastureland.
9Would a wild ox agree
to live in your barn
and labor for you?
10Could you force him to plow
or to drag a heavy log
to smooth out the soil?
11Can you depend on him
to use his great strength
and do your heavy work?
12Can you trust him
to harvest your grain
or take it to your barn
from the threshing place?
An Ostrich Proudly Flaps Her Wings
13An ostrich proudly
flaps her wings,
but not because
she loves her young.
14She abandons her eggs
and lets the dusty ground
keep them warm.
15And she doesn't seem to worry
that the feet of an animal
could crush them all.
16She treats her eggs as though
they were not her own,
unconcerned that her work
might be for nothing.
17I myself made her foolish
and without common sense.
18But once she starts running,
she laughs at a rider
on the fastest horse.
Did You Give Horses Their Strength?
19Did you give horses their strength
and the flowing hair
along their necks?
20Did you make them able
to jump like grasshoppers
or to frighten people
with their snorting?
21Before horses are ridden
into battle,
they paw at the ground,
proud of their strength.
22Laughing at fear, they rush
toward the fighting,
23while the weapons of their riders
rattle and flash in the sun.
24Unable to stand still,
they gallop eagerly into battle
when trumpets blast.
25Stirred by the distant smells
and sounds of war, they snort
in reply to the trumpet.
26Did you teach hawks to fly south
for the winter?
* 27Did you train eagles to build
28their nests on rocky cliffs,
29where they can look down
to spot their next meal?
30 Then their young gather to feast
wherever the victim lies.
translation_text:
1Anɛ o le be nɛ pu mi apletsihi fɔɔ lo?
O na odabɔ nɛ ngɛ fɔe hyɛ lo?
2Anɛ o le nyɔhiɔ abɔ nɛ a hɛɛɔ mi lo?
O le be nɛ a fɔɔ lo?
3O le bɔ nɛ a buɔ si, nɛ a fɔɔ,
nɛ a haomi ɔmɛ jeɔ a nɔ lo?
4A bimɛ ɔmɛ waa saminya ngɛ nga a nɔ;
a jeɔ a nyɛmɛ ɔmɛ a he,
nɛ a kpale we kɛ bɛ hu.
5Nga mi teji ɔmɛ ɔ,
mɛnɔ lɛ ha nɛ a ye a he?
Mɛnɔ lɛ ngmɛɛ a he loko a ngɛ kpae ɔ?
6Imi lɛ i ha mɛ nga kplanaa a,
nɛ a kɛ pee a hi he,
kɛ ngo zugba a hulɔ,
konɛ a hi lejɛ ɔ.
7A sume ma nguahi a mi he nɛ huhui ngɛ;
a hla we nɛ nɔ ko nɛ jɔɔ a kã he
nɛ a tsu ní ha lɛ.
8Yo ɔmɛ a nɔ ji a ní yemi he;
a yeɔ ba mumu tsuaa ba mumu ngɛ lejɛ ɔ.
9Anɛ pu mi okpɔngɔ maa suɔ nɛ e tsu ní ha mo lo?
Anɛ e maa suɔ nɛ e hwɔ o lohwehi a ní yemi he lo?
10Anɛ o ma nyɛ maa wo pu mi okpɔngɔ kpa
nɛ e hu ha mo lo?
Anɛ o ma nyɛ ma ha nɛ e gbla dade kpakplaa
kɛ hu o ngmɔ mi lo?
11Anɛ o maa ngɔ o hɛ ngɔ fɔ e he wami ɔ nɔ,
konɛ e tsu o ní tsumi kpakpataa a ha mo lo?
12Anɛ o heɔ yeɔ kaa e ma kpa ní ha mo,
nɛ e kɛ o blɛfo ɔ ma ba wo blɛfo gba mi ha mo lo?
13Mo lɛ o ha pu mi klakumi e pɛli saminyayoo ɔ lo?
Duguma tsɛli, kɛ e pɛli ɔmɛ nɛɛ,
mo lɛ o ha lɛ?
14Duguma siɔ e hluihi ngɛ zugba,
konɛ la nɛ jeɔ zu mi ɔ
nɛ ha a he nɛ dɔ la.
15E hɛ jeɔ nɔ kaa nane ko ma nyɛ maa ywia mɛ,
loo pu mi lohwe ko ma ba naa nɔ.
16E waa e bimɛ ɔmɛ yi mi kaa nɔ́
nɛ pi e bimɛ ji mɛ.
E hia we lɛ tete kaa e gbo yaka dengme.
17Imi Mawu lɛ i pee lɛ kuasia,
nɛ i ha nɛ nile bɔ lɛ kikɛ nɛ ɔ nɛ.
18Se ke e bɔni fo tumi kikɛ nɛ ɔ,
e muɔɔ okpɔngɔ kɛ e nɔ hilɔ.
19Mo Hiob lɛ o ha okpɔngɔ e he wami ɔ lo?
Mo lɛ o ha lɛ bwɔmi gagaa ngɛ e kuɛ he ɔ lo?
20Mo lɛ o haa nɛ e tuɔ kaa baalɛ ɔ lo?
Mo lɛ o haa nɛ e fliɔ e gugwɔ mi wawɛɛ
kɛ woɔ nɔ he gbeye ɔ lo?
21E kɛ bua jɔmi siɔ si glɛi glɛi glɛi ngɛ kɔ̃ ɔ mi,
nɛ e kɛ e he wami tsuo gbɔɔ fo kɛ yaa ta.
22E li nɔ́ nɛ a tsɛɛ ke fɔ̃;
e tui klaate nya fo.
23Kɛ̃ɛ̃ mi bihi hii a sibi a he hae ngɛ e se mi;
akplɔ kɛ tsɛ̃i hii kpɛe nylamnylam.
24Ke titimati ɔ pɛ kikɛ nɛ ɔ,
e dɛ si dii;
e kɛ hɛdɔ kɛ mi mi fumi nɛ nya wa
gbɔɔ fo kɛ yaa ta.
25Ke titimati ɔ pɛ kɛkɛ e fli e gugwɔ mi wawɛɛ.
E nuɔ ta he fu ngɛ tsitsaa lokoo.
E nuɔ nɛ asafoatsɛmɛ ɔmɛ ngɛ gbi woe,
nɛ ose ngɛ pɛe ngɛ ta a mi.
26Mo lɛ o tsɔɔ kayo temi
loko e gbɛɛ e pɛlihi a mi,
nɛ e teɔ kɛ yaa leneyi je ɔ lo?
27Mo lɛ o deɔ kɔle loko e ya peeɔ e tsu
ngɛ hiɔwe lokoo ɔ lo?
28Tɛ sa mi e hiiɔ; lejɛ ɔ ji e we;
tɛ sa kɛ e nya piɔpiɔɔpiɔ ɔ ji e mɔ.
29Ke e ngɛ lejɛ ɔ,
e hɛngmɛ hyɛɛ nɔ́
kɛ yaa tsitsaa
kaa e maa na lohwe ko
nɛ e ye lo.
30 Ke e na lohwe gbogboe ko kikɛ nɛ ɔ,
e ya maa si ngɛ lejɛ ɔ,
nɛ e bimɛ ɔmɛ nuɔ muɔ.

english_text:
The Lord Continues
I Am the Lord All-Powerful
* 1I am the Lord All-Powerful,
2but you have argued
that I am wrong.
Now you must answer me.
3Job said to the Lord:
4Who am I to answer you?
5I did speak once or twice,
but never again.
6Then out of the storm
the Lord said to Job:
7Face me and answer
the questions I ask!
8Are you trying to prove
that you are innocent
by accusing me of injustice?
9Do you have a powerful arm
and a thundering voice
that compare with mine?
10If so, then surround yourself
with glory and majesty.
* 11Show your furious anger!
Throw down and crush
12all who are proud and evil.
13Wrap them in grave clothes
and bury them together
in the dusty soil.
14Do this, and I will agree
that you have won
this argument.
I Created You
15I created both you
and the hippopotamus.
It eats only grass like an ox,
16but look at the mighty muscles
in its body 17and legs.
Its tail is like a cedar tree,
and its thighs are thick.
18The bones in its legs
are like bronze or iron.
19I made it more powerful
than any other creature,
yet I am stronger still.
20Undisturbed, it eats grass
while the other animals
play nearby.
* 21It rests in the shade of trees
along the riverbank
22or hides among reeds
in the swamp.
23It remains calm and unafraid
with the Jordan River rushing
and splashing in its face.
24There is no way to capture
a hippopotamus—
not even by hooking its nose
or blinding its eyes.
translation_text:
1-2Hiob, o ke o kɛ Mawu Ope ɔ maa hua munyu he.
Anɛ o ma ha yi,
aloo o maa ya nɔ?
Ha mi heto!
Hiob
3-4I kpa mo pɛɛ,
pi nɔ ko kulaa ji mi.
Mɛni heto ma ha mo?
I be munyu tue hu.
5I tu munyu pe bɔ nɛ sa nɛ ma tu;
i pa be nɔ́ ko dee hu.
6Kɛkɛ nɛ Yawɛ kɛ Hiob tu munyu ekohu
kɛ je kɔɔhiɔ nɛ nya wa mi.
Yawɛ
7Jehanɛ, da si kaa nyumu!
Ma bi mo sane, nɛ o ha mi heto.
8Anɛ o ngɛ hlae nɛ o bu mi fɔ kaa i yi dami sane,
konɛ moo lɛɛ o wo o he nguɔ kaa o nɔ́ da lo?
9Anɛ o ngɛ he wami kaa imi Mawu ɔ lo?
Anɛ o ma nyɛ maa wo gbi kaa imi lo?
10Ke ja a, dla o he,
nɛ o he nɛ pee fɛu.
Wo ablade tade saminyayoo,
konɛ o hɛ mi nɛ ba nyami.
11Hyɛ he woli!
O mi mi nɛ fu mɛ nɛ o ba mɛ si.
12Ee, hyɛ mɛ nɛ o ba mɛ si.
Moo naa yiwutsotsɛmɛ a nɔ ngɛ a hi he ɔmɛ.
13Moo pu mɛ tsuo ngɛ tabo zu mi,
nɛ o fi a hɛ mi ngɛ gbeje.
14Ke o pee ja a, lɛɛ imi hu ma je o yi,
nɛ ma de ke o ma nyɛ ma he mo nitsɛ o yi wami.
15Hyɛ pa mi suɔ!
I bɔ lɛ, kɛ mo tsuo.
E kpeɔ nga kaa na.
16Se hyɛ bɔ nɛ e nɔmlɔ tso ɔ he wa ha;
hyɛ bɔ nɛ e pani ɔmɛ ti ha!
17E hlemi ngɛ tlɔmɔɔ kaa seda tso.
Panihi nɛ hɛɛ e fiɔ ɔmɛ ɔ a he wa saminya.
18E wuhi a he wa kaa akɔblee,
nɛ e nanehi ngɛ kaa dade.
19Lɛ ji ye nibɔ ní ɔmɛ a kpɛti
nɔ́ nɛ ngɛ nyakpɛ pe mɛ tsuo.
E bɔlɔ ɔ pɛ ji nɔ nɛ ma nyɛ maa ye e nɔ.
20E naa niye ní ngɛ yo ɔmɛ a nɔ;
lejɛ ɔ lɛ pu mi lohwehi tsuo ya fiɛɔ ngɛ.
21E buɔ si ngɛ mio tsohi a sisi,
nɛ e laa e he ngɛ ngɔwuhi a kpɛti ngɛ pa mi.
22Mio tso ɔmɛ peeɔ hɔ̃ kɛ haa lɛ,
nɛ ngɔwu ɔmɛ bɔleɔ lɛ kɛ kpeɔ ngɛ nyu ɔ mi.
23Ke pa a he wa tete po, e yi gbeye.
Ke Yordan pa a nitsɛ fia kɛ ba pue e hɛ mi pohu,
e bui tete.
24Anɛ nɔ ko ma nyɛ maa nu lɛ kɛ gbowe lo?
Anɛ nɔ ko ma nyɛ maa wo e gugwɔ mi ga lo?

english_text:
The Lord Continues
Can You Catch a Sea Monster?
1 Can you catch a sea monster
by using a fishhook?
Can you tie its mouth shut
with a rope?
2Can it be led around
by a ring in its nose
or a hook in its jaw?
3Will it beg for mercy?
4Will it surrender
as a slave for life?
5Can it be tied by the leg
like a pet bird
for little girls?
6Is it ever chopped up
and its pieces bargained for
in the fish-market?
7Can it be killed
with harpoons or spears?
8Wrestle it just once—
that will be the end.
9Merely a glimpse of this monster
makes all courage melt.
10And if it is too fierce
for anyone to attack,
who would dare oppose me?
11I am in command of the world
and in debt to no one.
12What powerful legs,
what a stout body
this monster possesses!
13Who could strip off its armor
or bring it under control
with a harness?
14Who would try to open its jaws,
full of fearsome teeth?
* 15Its back is covered
with shield after shield,
16firmly bound and closer together
17than breath to breath.
When This Monster Sneezes
18When this monster sneezes,
lightning flashes, and its eyes
glow like the dawn.
19Sparks and fiery flames
explode from its mouth.
20And smoke spews from its nose
like steam
from a boiling pot,
21while its blazing breath
scorches everything in sight.
22Its neck is so tremendous
that everyone trembles,
23the weakest parts of its body
are harder than iron,
24and its heart is stone.
25When this noisy monster appears,
even the most powerful
turn and run in fear.
26No sword or spear can harm it,
27and weapons of bronze or iron
are as useless as straw
or rotten wood.
28Rocks thrown from a sling
cause it no more harm
than husks of grain.
This monster fears no arrows,
29it simply smiles at spears,
and striking it with a stick
is like slapping it with straw.
30As it crawls through the mud,
its sharp and spiny hide
tears the ground apart.
31And when it swims down deep,
the sea starts churning
like boiling oil,
32and it leaves behind a trail
of shining white foam.
33No other creature on earth
is so fearless.
34It is king of all proud creatures,
and it looks upon the others
as nothing.
translation_text:
1 Anɛ o ma nyɛ ma sá nyaka kɛ gbowe lo?
Anɛ o ma nyɛ maa ngɔ kpa kɛ fi
e lilɛ kɛ muɔ si lo?
2Anɛ o ma nyɛ maa ngɔ tangme
kɛ wo e gugwɔ mi lo?
Anɛ o ma nyɛ maa ngɔ gbowe
kɛ wo e tsitsa mi lo?
3Anɛ e ma kpa mo pɛɛ ke o ngmɛɛ e he lo?
Anɛ e maa fa kue ha mo ke o na lɛ mɔbɔ lo?
4Anɛ e kɛ mo maa so
kaa e ma sɔmɔ mo daa lo?
5Anɛ o kɛ lɛ ma fiɛ kaa
a kɛ lohwe pɛlitsɛ fiɛɔ,
aloo o maa fi lɛ ha o mawayi ɔmɛ
nɛ a kɛ lɛ nɛ fiɛ lo?
6Anɛ jua yeli ma nyɛ maa wo e he jua lo?
Anɛ a maa poo lɛ kpɔ nya kpɔ nya
nɛ a jua ha jua yeli lo?
7Anɛ o ma nyɛ ma tsɛ̃ kɛ̃ɛ̃hi babauu
kɛ wo e he womi mi lo?
Anɛ o ma nyɛ maa ngɔ akplɔ
kɛ gbɔ e yi mi lo?
8Moo ta e he si kake nɛ o hyɛ,
nɛ e be mo jloe kaa o ta e he si enyɔne;
o hɛ be nɔ jee gblegbleegble.
9Nɔ tsuaa nɔ nɛ maa na nyaka kikɛ nɛ ɔ,
sawale maa nu lɛ,
nɛ e maa nɔ si bum ngɛ zugba.
10Katsɛ ko katsɛ ko be
nɛ ma nyɛ maa wo e hɛ mi la.
Ke ja a, lɛɛ mɛnɔ lɛ ma nyɛ
maa da imi ye hɛ mi?
11Mɛnɔ lɛ e kɛ nyaka ya kpe kunɔ hyɛ
nɛ e he je mi?
Dɛbi! Je ɔ mi tsuo ɔ,
nɔ ko nɔ ko be!
12Nyaka a, tsa pi fiɛmi lohwe ji lɛ;
a je blɔ bɔ lɛ,
nɛ e ngɛ he wami saminya.
E nɔmlɔ tso ɔ he níhi, e nanehi,
kɛ e kpɔhi yeɔ ní nɛ ɔmɛ a he odase.
13Mɛnɔ ma nyɛ ma kpɔ e he toto ɔ?
E he womi ɔ nɛ ngɛ kaa gbaja nɛ e kpla a,
mɛnɔ ma nyɛ maa hɛ lɛ nɔ́ nɛ maa gbu lɛ kɛ je kpo?
14E nya kɛ e mi lunguhi gbeyegbeye ɔ,
mɛnɔ ma nyɛ ma bli?
15E he toto saminyawiiwi ɔmɛ ngɛ kaa tsɛ̃ihi
nɛ a fi ngɔ bla,
nɛ a to mɛ za nɔ za nɔ.
A he wa pe tɛ.
16A tsa a sibi a nya pɛpɛɛpɛ,
bɔ nɛ kɔɔhiɔ po be nyɛe maa gu a kpɛti.
17A tsa, nɛ a mɛtɛ a sibi a he saminya,
bɔ nɛ nɔ́ ko nɔ́ ko be nyɛe ma gba mi.
18Ke e tsile kɛkɛ la kpɛ;
e hɛngmɛhi ngɛ hleii kaa mɔtu pu la.
19La hii tsoe ngɛ e nya mi,
nɛ la lilɛhi tuɔ kɛ jeɔ mi pueɔ si.
20La su ku jeɔ e gugwɔ puɔhi a mi
kaa lamuɔ nɛ jeɔ buɛ,
loo kutu nɛ ngɛ fiae mi.
21Ke e wo mumi kikɛ nɛ ɔ,
e haa nɛ hã tsɛ̃ɔ,
nɛ la lilɛhi tuɔ kɛ jeɔ e nya mi.
22E kuɛ ngɛ kpakpataa;
ke o kɛ lɛ kpe ɔ,
ja sawale nu mo.
23E he womi he wa kpɛkpɛtɛɛ;
e be bɔdɔbɔdɔ,
nɛ e be tsuãã hulɔ.
24E tsui he wa kaa tɛ!
Ee, e tsui he wa kaa wɛ.
25Ke e wó e he nɔ kikɛ nɛ ɔ,
katsɛmɛ tete po yeɔ gbeye;
sawale nuɔ mɛ tsuo pɛpɛɛpɛ.
26Klaate ko klaate ko be nɛ maa plaa lɛ.
Akplɔ, loo kɛ̃ɛ̃ ko be nɛ maa ye lɛ awi.
27Dade ngɛ kaa nga ha lɛ;
akɔblee hu ngɛ kaa tso nɛ sa kɛkɛ.
28Kɛ̃ɛ̃ mi bi ko be nyɛe maa wo lɛ fo;
amlami tɛ ngɛ kaa nga ha lɛ.
29Tsokpoti ngɛ kaa nga ha lɛ,
nɛ ke akplɔ ngɛ pɛe kɛ ma a, e muɔɔ.
30Totohi nɛ ngɛ e mi si ɔ
ngɛ kaa buɛ kokoehi nɛ a nya ba.
E ngmlãã si ngɛ mɔsɔ mi
kaa nɔ́ nɛ blɛfo lɛ e ngɛ gblɛe.
31E haa nɛ wo fiaa kaa nyu ngɛ buɛ mi,
nɛ e fiaa hwɔli kaa nu ngɛ tɔ mi.
32Ke e be kikɛ nɛ ɔ,
e jeɔ blɔ ngɛ e se futaa.
Bɔ nɛ blɔ ɔ nɔ hii kpɛe ha a,
o ma de ke wo ɔ puɛ mua.
33Nɔ́ ko nɔ́ ko be je nɛ ɔ mi
nɛ ngɛ kaa lɛ;
e li nɔ́ nɛ a tsɛɛ ke fɔ̃.
34E bui lohwe ko lohwe ko;
lohwe nɛ kle kaa mɛni po, e bui.
Lohwehi nɛ a he ngɛ gbeye tsuo
a matsɛ ji lɛ.

english_text:
Job's Reply to the Lord
No One Can Oppose You
1Job said:
2No one can oppose you,
because you have the power
to do what you want.
3 You asked why I talk so much
when I know so little.
I have talked about things
that are far beyond
my understanding.
4 You told me to listen
and answer your questions.
5I heard about you from others;
now I have seen you
with my own eyes.
6That's why I hate myself
and sit here in dust and ashes
to show my sorrow.
The Lord Corrects Job's Friends
7The Lord said to Eliphaz:
What my servant Job has said about me is true, but I am angry with you and your two friends for not telling the truth. 8So I want you to go over to Job and offer seven bulls and seven goats on an altar as a sacrifice to please me. After this, Job will pray, and I will agree not to punish you for your foolishness.
9Eliphaz, Bildad, and Zophar obeyed the Lord, and he answered Job's prayer.
A Happy Ending
10 After Job had prayed for his three friends, the Lord made Job twice as rich as he had been before. 11Then Job gave a feast for his brothers and sisters and for his old friends. They expressed their sorrow for the suffering the Lord had brought on him, and they each gave Job some silver and a gold ring.
12The Lord now blessed Job more than ever; he gave him 14,000 sheep, 6,000 camels, 1,000 pair of oxen, and 1,000 donkeys.
13In addition to seven sons, Job had three daughters, 14whose names were Jemimah, Keziah, and Keren Happuch. 15They were the most beautiful women in that part of the world, and Job gave them shares of his property, along with their brothers.
16Job lived for another 140 years—long enough to see his great-grandchildren have children of their own— 17and when he finally died, he was very old.
translation_text:
1Kɛkɛ nɛ Hiob he nɔ nɛ e kɛ Yawɛ tu munyu.
Hiob
2Yawɛ, i le kaa he walɔ kpetekpleenyɛ ji mo;
o nyɛɔ nɛ o peeɔ nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ o suɔ.
3 O bi ke kɛ peeɔ kɛɛ nɛ i biɔ sane
nɛ kɔɔ mo o nile he,
be mi nɛ imi lɛɛ i li nɔ́ ko nɔ́ ko ɔ?
I tu níhi nɛ i nui sisi a he munyu;
nyakpɛ níhi nɛ ye juɛmi sui a he.
4 O de mi ke ma bu mo tue nɛ o tu munyu,
konɛ ma ha mo sanehi nɛ o ma bi mi ɔ a heto.
5Jamɛ a be ɔ,
níhi nɛ nihi de mi
ngɛ o he kɛkɛ lɛ i le,
se amlɔ nɛ ɔ lɛɛ
i na mo paa kɛ imi nitsɛ ye hɛngmɛ.
6Nɔ́ nɛ i pee ɔ dɔ mi.
Lɔ ɔ he ɔ,
i kɛ tabo zu kɛ la zu to okadi
kaa i pia ye he niinɛ.
Nyagbe
7Benɛ Yawɛ kɛ Hiob tu munyu ta a, Yawɛ de Elifaz, Teman no ɔ ke, “Ye mi mi fu o kɛ o huɛmɛ enyɔ ɔmɛ tsuo; ejakaa nyɛ tu we ye he anɔkuale munyu kaa bɔ nɛ ye tsɔlɔ Hiob pee ɔ. 8Enɛ ɔ he je ɔ, nyɛɛ ngɔ na ku kpaago, kɛ agbosu kpaago kɛ ya ye tsɔlɔ Hiob ngɔ, nɛ nyɛ ya sã sami bɔ ha nyɛ he ngɛ lejɛ ɔ. Hiob maa fa kue ha nyɛ. Ma bu e kue fami ɔ tue, nɛ i be nyɛ tue gblae bɔ nɛ sa nyɛ kaa nyɛ je kuasia. Ee, nyɛ tu we ye he anɔkuale munyu kaa bɔ nɛ ye tsɔlɔ Hiob pee ɔ.”
9Elifaz, Teman no ɔ, Bildad, Shua no ɔ, kɛ Zofar, Naamat no ɔ ho nɛ a ya pee kaa bɔ nɛ Yawɛ de mɛ ke a pee ɔ. Nɛ Yawɛ bu Hiob kue fami ɔ tue.
10 Jehanɛ, benɛ Hiob fa kue ha Yawɛ ngɛ e huɛmɛ etɛ ɔmɛ a he se ɔ, Yawɛ wo lɛ ní ekohu. Níhi tsuo nɛ Hiob hi sa a, Yawɛ bɔ he totoe enyɔɔnyɔ kɛ ha lɛ. 11Hiob nyɛminyumuhi, e nyɛmiyihi, kɛ nihi nɛ le lɛ sa a tsuo ba slaa lɛ nɛ a kɛ lɛ ba ye ní ngɛ e we ɔ mi. A ye lɛ kɔmɔ nɛ a jɔɔ e bua ngɛ haomihi tsuo nɛ Yawɛ kɛ ba e nɔ ɔ a he. A ti nɔ tsuaa nɔ ke lɛ sika, kɛ sika tsu ga.
12Yawɛ gbaa Hiob ngɛ nyagbe be nɛ ɔ mi kulaa pe bɔ nɛ e gbaa lɛ kekle ɔ. Hiob ba na to akpe nyɔngma kɛ eywiɛ, afukpɔngɔ akpe ekpa, na blablɛ akpe kɛ teji akpe. 13Jehanɛ e kpale fɔ binyumuhi kpaago kɛ biyihi etɛ. 14E wo e biyo nɔkɔtɔma a biɛ ke Yemima. Enyɔne ɔ biɛ ji Kezia, nɛ etɛne ɔ biɛ ji Keren Hapuk. 15Ngɛ je ɔ mi tsuo ɔ, a nɛ yihi nɛ a he ngɛ fɛu kaa Hiob biyi ɔmɛ. A tsɛ ɔ ha mɛ weto ní kaa bɔ nɛ e ha a nyɛminyumu ɔmɛ ɔ.
16Ní nɛ ɔmɛ a se ɔ, Hiob kpale ye jeha lafa kɛ nyingmi eywiɛ ekohu. E na bimɛ, kɛ bibimɛ hluu kɛ ya si yi nɔ nɛ ji eywiɛ 17loko e gbo. Jamɛ a be ɔ, e bwɔ kotokoto.

english_text:
BOOK I
(Psalms 1–41)
The Way to Happiness
1God blesses those people
who refuse evil advice
and won't follow sinners
or join in sneering at God.
2Instead, they find happiness
in the Teaching of the Lord,
and they think about it
day and night.
3 They are like trees
growing beside a stream,
trees that produce
fruit in season
and always have leaves.
Those people succeed
in everything they do.
4That isn't true of those
who are evil—
they are like straw
blown by the wind.
5Sinners won't have an excuse
on the day of judgment,
and they won't have a place
with the people of God.
6The Lord protects everyone
who follows him,
but the wicked follow a road
that leads to ruin.
translation_text:
KEKLEEKLE WOMI
(La 1—41)
Bua jɔmi kpakpa
1A gbaa nɔ nɛ bui
nimli yayamihi a ga womi tue,
nɔ nɛ kɛ yayami peeli bɔɛ,
nɛ e hí he fɛu yeli a hi he;
2se mohu e bua jɔɔ Yawɛ mlaa a he,
nɛ e susuɔ he nyɔ kɛ pia.
3 E ngɛ kaa tso nɛ a du ngɛ pa tue,
nɛ woɔ yiblii ngɛ be nɛ sa mi.
E bahi gbli we gblegbleegble.
E yeɔ manye ngɛ nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ mi.
4Se yayami peeli lɛɛ pi ja nɛ a ngɛ;
mɛɛ a ngɛ kaa jakati
nɛ kɔɔhiɔ muɔɔ kɛ yaa.
5Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, a maa gbla yayami peeli a tue,
nɛ a kɛ mɛ be dali futue.
6Ejakaa Yawɛ buu dali a he,
se yayami peeli lɛɛ
a hɛ mi ma kpata.

english_text:
The Lord's Chosen King
1 Why do the nations plot,
and why do their people
make useless plans?
2The kings of this earth
have all joined together
to turn against the Lord
and his chosen king.
3They say, “Let's cut the ropes
and set ourselves free!”
4In heaven the Lord laughs
as he sits on his throne,
making fun of the nations.
5The Lord becomes furious
and threatens them.
His anger terrifies them
as he says,
6“I've put my king on Zion,
my sacred hill.”
7 I will tell the promise
that the Lord made to me:
“You are my son, because today
I have become your father.
8Ask me for the nations,
and every nation on earth
will belong to you.
9 You will smash them
with an iron rod
and shatter them
like dishes of clay.”
10Be smart, all you rulers,
and pay close attention.
11Serve and honor the Lord;
be glad and tremble.
12Show respect to his son
because if you don't,
the Lord might become furious
and suddenly destroy you.
But he blesses and protects
everyone who runs to him.
translation_text:
Matsɛ ɔ nɛ Mawu hla a
1 Mɛni ba nɛ je ma amɛ
ngɛ basabasa pee?
Mɛni he je lɛ a ngɛ soe
yaka gu kikɛ nɛ ɔ?
2Zugba a nɔ matsɛmɛ ɔmɛ pee kake.
Nɔ yeli ɔmɛ so ngɔ wo Yawɛ,
kɛ matsɛ ɔ nɛ e hla a a he.
3A ke, “Nyɛ ha wa kpɔ wa he kɛ je a dɛ mi
nɛ waa ye wa he.”
4Nɔ nɛ hii si ngɛ hiɔwe lokoo ɔ
ngɛ mɛ muɔe.
Ee, Yawɛ ngɛ a he fɛu yee.
5Jehanɛ, Yawɛ kɛ abofu
ma kple a nɔ.
E hɛ maa dɔ;
6nɛ e ma de mɛ ke, “Imi Yawɛ nitsɛ
lɛ i ngɔ ye matsɛ ɔ ngɔ to Zion,
ye yoku klɔuklɔu ɔ nɔ.”
7 Matsɛ ɔ ke,
“Nɔ́ nɛ Yawɛ de mi ɔ,
ma sɛɛ nɛ nyɛɛ nu.
Yawɛ de mi ke,
‘Ye bi ji mo;
mwɔnɛ ɔ, i fɔ mo.
8Bi mi, nɛ ma ha mo je ma amɛ tsuo;
zugba a tsuo ma ba pee o weto ní.
9 O kɛ dade tso maa gbla a tue.
O maa ywia mɛ wɔtsɔwɔtsɔ
kaa a ywiaa buɛ?’ ”
10Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, nyɛ matsɛmɛ, nyɛɛ kase ní;
nyɛ, zugba a nɔ yeli,
nyɛɛ bu ga womi tue.
11Nyɛ sɔmɔ Yawɛ kɛ gbeye yemi.
12Nyɛ he nɛ do blibliibli,
nɛ nyɛ kpla si ngɛ e hɛ mi.
Ke pi jã a, e mi mi ma fu nyɛ si kake too,
nɛ nyɛ hɛ mi ma kpata.
Nihi tsuo nɛ ba saa we
ngɛ Yawɛ ngɔ ɔ
ma na bua jɔmi.

english_text:
(Written by David when he was running from his son Absalom.)
An Early Morning Prayer
1 I have a lot of enemies, Lord.
Many fight against 2me and say,
“God won't rescue you!”
3But you are my shield,
and you give me victory
and great honor.
4I pray to you, and you answer
from your sacred hill.
5I sleep and wake up refreshed
because you, Lord,
protect me.
6Ten thousand enemies attack
from every side,
but I am not afraid.
7Come and save me, Lord God!
Break my enemies' jaws
and shatter their teeth,
8because you protect
and bless your people.
translation_text:
Mɔtu kue fami kɛ ha yemi kɛ buami
1 Yawɛ, hyɛ bɔ nɛ ye he nyɛli hiɛ ha!
Hyɛ kaa nihi babauu te si kɛ wo mi!
2Nɔ́ nɛ a ngɛ dee ji,
“Oo, Mawu be e he piɛe fɛɛ!”
3Se mo Yawɛ, o ngɛ kaa tsɛ̃i
nɛ buɔ ye he daa.
O woɔ mi mumi mi he wami,
nɛ o woɔ ye hɛ mi nyami.
4Ke i kpa ngmlaa kɛ tsɛ Yawɛ ɔ,
e heɔ nɔ ngɛ e yoku klɔuklɔu ɔ nɔ.
5I hwɔɔ si nɛ i hwɔɔ mahe,
nɛ i teɔ si ekohu,
ejakaa Yawɛ buɔ ye he.
6Ke nimli akpeakpe abɔ
ba sa ye yi kɛ kpe po,
i yi mɛ gbeye.
7Yawɛ, ye Mawu,
ba he ye yi wami koo!
Ejakaa mo lɛ o ma nyɛ
maa fia ye he nyɛli ɔmɛ tsuo ní.
Mo lɛ o ma nyɛ maa gbla a tue
nɛ a be nyɛe maa pee mi nɔ́ ko.
8Yawɛ, mo ji wa yi wami helɔ;
moo gbaa o ma a koo!

english_text:
(A psalm by David for the music leader. Use stringed instruments.)
An Evening Prayer
1You are my God and protector.
Please answer my prayer.
I was in terrible distress,
but you set me free.
Now have pity and listen
as I pray.
2How long will you people
refuse to respect me?
You love foolish things,
and you run after
what is worthless.
3The Lord has chosen
everyone who is faithful
to be his very own,
and he answers my prayers.
4 But each of you
had better tremble
and turn from your sins.
Silently search your heart
as you lie in bed.
5Offer the proper sacrifices
and trust the Lord.
6There are some who ask,
“Who will be good to us?”
Let your kindness, Lord,
shine brightly on us.
7You brought me more happiness
than a rich harvest
of grain and grapes.
8I can lie down
and sleep soundly
because you, Lord,
will keep me safe.
translation_text:
Gbɔkuɛ kue fami kɛ ha yemi kɛ buami
1Ye Mawu nɛ faa ye he,
moo bu ye kue fami ɔ tue koo!
Be ko nɛ ye yi fi ɔ,
mo lɛ o ba je mi.
Naa mi mɔbɔ koo,
nɛ o bu ye pɛɛ kpami ɔ tue.
2Nyɛ nimli adesahi,
mɛni be nyɛ ma pue ye hɛ mi si kɛ yaa si?
Nyɛ suɔ níhi nɛ a he be se nami,
nɛ lakpa munyuhi a se nyɛ dii.
Kɛ yaa si mɛni be nɛ nyɛ maa hi enɛ ɔ pee?
3Se nyɛ ná nɛ nyɛɛ le kaa
Yawɛ hla nihi nɛ peeɔ nɔ nɛ da kɛ ha e he;
nɛ ke i tsɛ lɛ ɔ, e nuɔ.
4 Ke nyɛ mi mi fu ɔ,
nyɛ ko pee yayami.
Ke nyɛ hwɔɔ si ɔ, nyɛɛ pee dii,
nɛ nyɛɛ ya nyɛ yi mi.
5Nyɛɛ sã bɔ nɛ sa ha Yawɛ;
nyɛɛ ngɔ nyɛ hɛ kɛ fɔ e nɔ.
6Nihi babauu biɔ ke,
“Mɛnɔ po maa dloo wɔ nɔ́ ko?
Yawɛ, naa wɔ mɔbɔ koo!”
7Se imi lɛɛ o ha mi bua jɔmi babauu.
Ke nimli nɛ ɔmɛ a blɛfo kɛ wai ba saminya po,
a na we bua jɔmi kaa imi.
8Ma hwɔ si nɛ ma hwɔ mahe
ngɛ tue mi jɔmi mi.
Ejakaa mo, Yawɛ pɛ
lɛ o haa nɛ ye he mi jɔɔ mi.

english_text:
(A psalm by David for the music leader. Use flutes.)
A Prayer for Help
1Listen, Lord, as I pray!
Pay attention when I groan.
2You are my King and my God.
Answer my cry for help
because I pray to you.
3Each morning you listen
to my prayer,
as I bring my requests to you
and wait for your reply.
4You are not the kind of God
who is pleased with evil.
Sinners can't stay with you.
5No one who boasts can stand
in your presence, Lord,
and you hate evil people.
6You destroy every liar,
and you despise violence
and deceit.
7Because of your great mercy,
I come to your house, Lord,
and I am filled with wonder
as I bow down to worship
at your holy temple.
8You do what is right,
and I ask you to guide me.
Make your teaching clear
because of my enemies.
9 Nothing they say is true!
They just want to destroy.
Their words are deceitful
like a hidden pit,
and their tongues are good
only for telling lies.
10Punish them, God,
and let their own plans
bring their downfall.
Get rid of them!
They keep committing crimes
and turning against you.
11Let all who run to you
for protection
always sing joyful songs.
Provide shelter for those
who truly love you
and let them rejoice.
12Our Lord, you bless those
who live right,
and you shield them
with your kindness.
translation_text:
Yawɛ, moo bu ye he
1Yawɛ, bu ye munyu ɔmɛ tue,
nɛ huu nɛ i ngɛ faeɔ, o pee he nɔ́ ko ha mi.
2Ye matsɛ kɛ ye Mawu!
I ngɛ mo tsɛe!
Bu mi tue koo!
3Yawɛ, mɔtu ɔ, o nuɔ ye gbi.
Ee, mɔtu ɔ, i faa kue kɛ haa mo,
nɛ i mlɛɔ, konɛ o he nɔ.
4Ejakaa pi Mawu nɛ náa
nɔ́ yayami he tsui ji mo;
yayami kɛ mo hí si.
5He nɔ woli be nyɛe maa ba o hɛ mi;
o sume nihi nɛ peeɔ yayami.
6Mo Yawɛ,
o kpataa lakpatsɛmɛ a hɛ mi.
Muɔ si pueli, kɛ nɔ sisili lɛɛ
o hiee mɛ kulaa.
7Se imi lɛɛ,
o mɔbɔ nami, kɛ o dloomi ɔ he je ɔ,
ma nyɛ ma ba o we klɔuklɔu ɔ;
ma ja mo ngɛ lejɛ ɔ kɛ gbeye yemi.
8Yawɛ ye he nyɛli ɔmɛ a he je ɔ,
piɛ ye he, konɛ ma pee nɔ nɛ da.
Tsɔɔ mi o blɔ ɔ saminya
nɛ ma nyɛɛ nɔ.
9 Ejakaa ye he nyɛli ɔmɛ tu we anɔkuale;
yayami hyi a tsui mi tɔ.
A tuɔ munyu dɔkɔdɔkɔ,
se lɛ tsuo kɛ gbenɔ ba a.
10Mawu, buu mɛ fɔ, nɛ o gbla a tue.
Ha nɛ a yi mi tomi yayami ɔmɛ
nɛ kpa kɛ bu mɛ nitsɛmɛ a nɔ.
Fie mɛ kɛ je o hɛ mi,
ejakaa a pee yayamihi gbegbeegbe kɛ si mo,
nɛ a tsɔ o hɛ mi atuã.
11Se nihi tsuo nɛ ba saa we ngɛ o ngɔ ɔ,
ha nɛ a nya, nɛ a la kɛ bua jɔmi daa.
Ni nɛmɛ nɛ suɔ mo ɔ, buu a he,
konɛ a na bua jɔmi ngɛ o mi.
12Yawɛ, o gbaa nihi nɛ peeɔ nɔ́ nɛ da,
nɛ o kɛ o suɔmi ɔ buu a he kaa tsɛ̃i.

english_text:
(A psalm by David for the music leader. Use stringed instruments.
)
A Prayer in Time of Trouble
1 Don't punish me, Lord,
or even correct me
when you are angry!
2Have pity on me and heal
my feeble body.
My bones tremble with fear,
3and I am in deep distress.
How long will it be?
4Turn and come to my rescue.
Show your wonderful love
and save me, Lord.
5If I die, I cannot praise you
or even remember you.
6My groaning has worn me out.
At night my bed and pillow
are soaked with tears.
7Sorrow has made my eyes dim,
and my sight has failed
because of my enemies.
8 You, Lord, heard my crying,
and those hateful people
had better leave me alone.
9You have answered my prayer
and my plea for mercy.
10My enemies will be ashamed
and terrified,
as they quickly run away
in complete disgrace.
translation_text:
Yemi kɛ buami ngɛ amanehlu mi
1 Yawɛ, koo ngɔ abofu kɛ ka ye hɛ mi;
koo ngɔ mi mi la kɛ gbla ye tue.
2Yawɛ naa mi mɔbɔ,
ejakaa ye he wami ta.
Yawɛ, tsa mi koo,
ejakaa i be he wami,
3nɛ imi nɔmlɔ ɔ tsuo i hao.
Yawɛ, mɛni be o maa mlɛ kɛ yaa si
loko o ma ba he mi?
4Yawɛ, ba he ye yi wami koo!
Naa mi mɔbɔ nɛ o kpɔ mi,
ejakaa o suɔmi ɔ be nyagbe.
5Nɔ ko kaii we mo ngɛ gbeje;
mɛnɔ lɛ ma je o yi ngɛ lejɛ ɔ?
6Kɔmɔ yemi sɔuu ha nɛ i gbɔjɔ;
daa nyɔ mi ɔ, ye sa pɔɔ kɛ vo nyu sɔuu;
daa nyɔ mi ɔ, i foɔ ya kɛ pɔɔ ye sɔne.
7Ye he nyɛli ɔmɛ haoɔ mi.
Kɔmɔ yemi sɔuu puɛ ye hɛngmɛ,
nɛ i hyɛ we nɔ́ kpakpa ko hu.
8 Nyɛ yayami peeli,
nyɛɛ je ye nɔ kɛ ya se,
ejakaa Yawɛ nu ye ya fomi ɔ.
9Yawɛ nu ye kue fami ɔ;
Yawɛ maa pee ye hiami ní ɔmɛ ha mi.
10Ha nɛ zo nɛ gbe ye he nyɛli ɔmɛ tsuo,
nɛ a hao wawɛɛ nitsɛ.
Ha nɛ a kɛ zo kpɔtɔɔ
nɛ kpale kɛ ho esɔ!

english_text:
(Written by David.
He sang this to the Lord because of Cush from the tribe of Benjamin.)
The Lord Always Does Right
1You, Lord God,
are my protector.
Rescue me and keep me safe
from all who chase me.
2Or else they will rip me apart
like lions attacking a victim,
and no one will save me.
3I am innocent, Lord God!
4I have not betrayed a friend
or had pity on an enemy
who attacks for no reason.
5If I have done any of this,
then let my enemies
chase and capture me.
Let them trample me to death
and leave me in the dirt.
6Get angry, Lord God!
Do something!
Attack my furious enemies.
See that justice is done.
7Make the nations come to you,
as you sit on your throne
above them all.
8Our Lord, judge the nations!
Judge me and show that I
am honest and innocent.
9 You know every heart and mind,
and you always do right.
Now make violent people stop,
but protect all of us
who obey you.
10You, God, are my shield,
the protector of everyone
whose heart is right.
11You see that justice is done,
and each day
you take revenge.
12Whenever your enemies refuse
to change their ways,
you sharpen your sword
and string your bow.
13Your deadly arrows are ready
with flaming tips.
14An evil person is like a woman
about to give birth
to a hateful, deceitful,
and rebellious child.
15 Such people dig a deep hole,
then fall in it themselves.
16The trouble they cause
comes back on them,
and their heads are crushed
by their own evil deeds.
17I will praise you, Lord!
You always do right.
I will sing about you,
the Lord Most High.
translation_text:
Dami sane yemi he kue fami
1Yawɛ, ye Mawu!
I ba sa we ngɛ o ngɔ.
Mo kpɔ mi kɛ je nihi tsuo
nɛ ngɛ mi yi mi wae ɔ a dɛ mi,
nɛ o he ye yi wami.
2Ke pi ja a, a maa gbla mi kɛ ya
he nɛ nɔ ko be nɛ maa je ngmlaa ha mi.
Lejɛ ɔ lɛ a ma ya tsɔtslɔɔ mi ngɛ
kaa bɔ nɛ jata peeɔ ɔ.
3-4Yawɛ, ye Mawu!
Ke i pee nɔ ko yayami,
aloo i wa ye he nyɛlɔ yi mi yaka gu,
ke i pee nɔ́ ko kaa kikɛ nɛ ɔ,
5ha nɛ ye he nyɛli ɔmɛ nɛ
a nyɛɛ ye se nɛ a nu mi.
Ha nɛ a fia mi nɔ nɛ a gbe mi,
nɛ a si mi ngɛ zugba.
6Yawɛ, ye he nyɛli ɔmɛ te si kɛ wo mi;
tee si nɛ o kɛ mɛ nɛ kpe ha mi.
O mi mi nɛ fu mɛ;
ejakaa dami sane yemi ji nɔ́ nɛ o suɔ.
7Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, ha nɛ a bua
je ma amɛ tsuo a nya kɛ bɔle mo,
nɛ o je hiɔwe kɛ ye a nɔ.
8Yawɛ, mo ji je ɔ tsuo kojolɔ.
Moo ye ye sane ha mi;
o le kaa i pee we nɔ́ ko nɛ dɛ.
9 Mawu nɛ yeɔ dami sane ji mo;
o le nimli a tsui mi, kɛ a juɛmi mi.
Ha nɛ nimli yayamihi nɛ jɔɔ yayami peemi,
konɛ nimli kpakpahi lɛɛ
o pee mɛ bɔ nɛ sa.
10Mawu ji ye he bulɔ.
Nihi nɛ peeɔ nɔ́ nɛ da a,
e heɔ a yi wami.
11Mawu ji kojolɔ nɛ yeɔ dami sane;
daa nɛ ɔ, e mi mi fu yayami peeli.
12Ke a tsakee we a tsui ɔ,
Mawu maa duɔ e klaate ɔ nya.
E pee e kɛ̃ɛ̃ ɔ klaalo momo,
13nɛ e kɛ kɛ̃ɛ̃ mi bi nɛ nya ba hɔ nya.
E dla awi yemi ní kpahi hu
ngɔ to.
14Ke yiwutsotsɛ ngɛ nɔ́ yayami susue ɔ,
e hii nɔ́ ɔ plɛe ngɛ e yi mi kpamisa
kaa bɔ nɛ bimwɔyo hii plɛe
ngɛ yohɔyo mi mi ɔ.
Nyagbe ɔ, nɔ́ nɛ jeɔ kpo ji lakpa.
15E tsuaa muɔ kɛ haa ni kpahi;
se muɔ ɔ nɛ e tsua a,
lɛ nitsɛ nɛ e maa nɔ mi.
16E musu maa tloo lɛ nitsɛ;
lɛ nitsɛ e yayami ɔ maa ye lɛ awi.
17Ma na Yawɛ si;
ejakaa e yeɔ dami sane.
Ma la kɛ je Yawɛ Hiɔwe No ɔ yi.

english_text:
(A psalm by David for the music leader.
)
The Wonderful Name of the Lord
1Our Lord and Ruler,
your name is wonderful
everywhere on earth!
You let your glory be seen
in the heavens above.
2 With praises from children
and from tiny infants,
you have built a fortress.
It makes your enemies silent,
and all who turn against you
are left speechless.
3I often think of the heavens
your hands have made,
and of the moon and stars
you put in place.
4 Then I ask, “Why do you care
about us humans?
Why are you concerned
for us weaklings?”
5 You made us a little lower
than you yourself,
and you have crowned us
with glory and honor.
6 You let us rule everything
your hands have made.
And you put all of it
under our power—
7the sheep and the cattle,
and every wild animal,
8the birds in the sky,
the fish in the sea,
and all ocean creatures.
9Our Lord and Ruler,
your name is wonderful
everywhere on earth!
translation_text:
David la
1Yawɛ, wa Nyɔmtsɛ!
Hyɛ kaa o biɛ pɛɛ ngɛ je ɔ mi tsuo,
nɛ a woɔ o hɛ mi nyami ngɛ hiɔwe lokoo!
2 O haa jokuɛwi, kɛ bimwɔwi he wami
nɛ a laa kɛ jeɔ o yi.
O he nyɛli ɔmɛ maa a nya,
nɛ a nyɛ we nɛ a peeɔ nɔ́ ko.
3Ke i susu níhi nɛ ngɛ hiɔwe a he,
nyɔhiɔ kɛ dodoehi,
ke i hyɛ ní nɛ ɔmɛ
nɛ o kɛ o nine pee ɔ,
4 i biɔ ke,
“Mɛni ji nɔmlɔ adesa, nɛ o susuɔ e he?
Mɛni ji nɔmlɔ bi, nɛ o hyɛɛ e nɔ?”
5Nɛ́ o bɔ nɔmlɔ ɔ, nɔ́ ko bɔɔ pɛ
lɛ mo, Mawu ɔ o ngɔ kɛ pe lɛ.
Se o wo e hɛ mi nyami babauu.
6 O pee lɛ níhi tsuo nɛ o bɔ ɔ
a nɔ yelɔ.
O ngɔ ní nɛ ɔmɛ tsuo ngɔ wo e dɛ mi:
7tohi, nahi, pu mi lohwehi,
8lohwe pɛlitsɛmɛ, lohi,
kɛ nibɔ níhi tsuo nɛ ngɛ wo mi.
9Yawɛ, wa Nyɔmtsɛ!
Hyɛ kaa o biɛ pɛɛ ngɛ je ɔ mi tsuo.

english_text:
(A psalm by David for the music leader. To the tune “The Death of the Son.”)
Sing Praises to the Lord
1I will praise you, Lord,
with all my heart
and tell about the wonders
you have worked.
2God Most High, I will rejoice;
I will celebrate and sing
because of you.
3When my enemies face you,
they run away and stumble
and are destroyed.
4You take your seat as judge,
and your fair decisions prove
that I was in the right.
5You warn the nations
and destroy evil people;
you wipe out their names
forever and ever.
6Our enemies are destroyed
completely for all time.
Their cities are torn down,
and they will never
be remembered again.
7You rule forever, Lord,
and you are on your throne,
ready for judgment.
8You judge the world fairly
and treat all nations
with justice.
9The poor can run to you
because you are a fortress
in times of trouble.
10Everyone who honors your name
can trust you,
because you are faithful
to all who depend on you.
11You rule from Zion, Lord,
and we sing about you
to let the nations know
everything you have done.
12You did not forget
to punish the guilty
or listen to the cries
of those in need.
13 Please have mercy, Lord!
My enemies mistreat me.
Keep me from the gates
that lead to death,
14and I will sing about you
at the gate to Zion.
I will be happy there
because you rescued me.
15 Our Lord, the nations fell
into their own pits,
and their feet were caught
in their own traps.
16You showed what you are like,
and you made certain
that justice is done,
but evil people are trapped
by their own evil deeds.
17The wicked will go down
to the world of the dead
to be with those nations
that forgot about you.
18The poor and the homeless
won't always be forgotten
and without hope.
19Do something, Lord!
Don't let the nations win.
Make them stand trial
in your court of law.
20Make the nations afraid
and let them all discover
just how weak they are.
translation_text:
Mawu sina la
1Yawɛ, ma na mo si kɛ ye tsui tsuo;
ma sɛɛ nyakpɛ níhi nɛ o pee ɔ.
2Mawu Ope, o he ɔ, ma la kɛ bua jɔmi;
ma la kɛ je o yi.
3Benɛ ye he nyɛli ɔmɛ kpale a se ɔ,
a nɔɔ si nɛ a gbo ngɛ o hɛ mi.
4Ejakaa o kojoɔ ngɛ dami kɛ anɔkuale nya;
o ye ye sane ɔ ha mi, nɛ o wo mi nguɔ.
5O ka je ma amɛ a hɛ mi.
O kpata yayami peeli a hɛ mi,
nɛ a biɛ laa pɛsɛpɛsɛ.
6Wa he nyɛli ɔmɛ a hɛ mi kpata;
a ma amɛ hu a hɛ mi kpata,
nɛ nɔ́ ko be nɛ a kɛ ma kai mɛ hu.
7Se Yawɛ lɛɛ e ngɛ daa;
e hii si ngɛ e kojomi sɛ ɔ nɔ.
8Nɛ e kɛ anɔkuale, kɛ dami sane yemi
maa kojo je ɔ, kɛ e mi nimli ɔmɛ.
9Yawɛ ji wesa he
kɛ ha nihi nɛ a waa mɛ yi mi.
Haomi be mi ɔ, e ngɔ lɛ a naa he jɔmi ngɛ.
10Yawɛ, nihi nɛ le mo ɔ,
a ngɔɔ a hɛ kɛ fɔɔ o nɔ.
Ejakaa ni nɛmɛ nɛ hla o se blɔ ɔ,
mo Yawɛ, o kua we mɛ.
11Nyɛ la kɛ je Yawɛ yi;
Yawɛ nɛ ngɛ Zion ɔ, nyɛ je e yi.
Nyɛɛ sɛɛ níhi nɛ e pee ɔ
kɛ ha je ma amɛ tsuo.
12Mawu kaiɔ nɔ́ nali,
nɛ e yeɔ a he lue.
Ke nɔ́ nali fa kue ha Mawu ɔ,
e nuɔ; e hɛ ji a nɔ.
13Yawɛ, mo nɛ o jeɔ mi
kɛ jeɔ gbenɔ dɛ mi.
Hyɛ bɔ nɛ ye he nyɛli ngɛ mi haoe ha
nɛ o na mi mɔbɔ,
14konɛ ma na bua jɔmi
nɛ ma je o yi
ngɛ Yerusalem bi ɔmɛ a hɛ mi;
nɛ ma nya kɛ tsɔɔ kaa
o he ye yi wami.
15Muɔ ɔ nɛ je ma amɛ tsua a,
mɛ nitsɛmɛ a nɔ mi.
Klama a nɛ a tsɔ kɛ laa a,
mɛ nitsɛmɛ a nane ya du lɛ.
16Yawɛ je e he kpo;
e ye dami sane,
nɛ yayami peeli a nane
ya du klama a nɛ mɛ nitsɛmɛ a tsɔ ɔ.
17Nimli yayamihi, kɛ mahi tsuo
nɛ a hɛ je Mawu nɔ ɔ,
a nyagbe ji gbenɔ.
18Ejakaa pi daa
nɛ hɛ maa je dɛgutsɛmɛ a nɔ;
ohiatsɛmɛ a hɛ kɛ nɔ fɔmi be yaka pee.
19Yawɛ, tee si;
ko ha nɛ nɔmlɔ adesa nɛ ye o nɔ!
Ha nɛ a kojo je ma amɛ ngɛ o hɛ mi.
20Yawɛ, wo je ma amɛ a he gbeye,
konɛ a le kaa nimli adesahi kɛkɛ ji mɛ.

english_text:
A Prayer for Help
1Why are you far away, Lord?
Why do you hide yourself
when I am in trouble?
2Proud and brutal people
hunt down the poor.
But let them get caught
by their own evil plans!
3The wicked brag about
their deepest desires.
Those greedy people hate
and curse you, Lord.
4The wicked are too proud
to turn to you
or even think about you.
5They are always successful,
though they can't understand
your teachings,
and they keep sneering
at their enemies.
6In their hearts they say,
“Nothing can hurt us!
We'll always be happy
and free from trouble.”
7 They curse and tell lies,
and all they talk about
is how to be cruel
or how to do wrong.
8They hide outside villages,
waiting to strike and murder
some innocent victim.
9They are hungry lions
hiding in the bushes,
hoping to catch
some helpless passerby.
They trap the poor in nets
and drag them away.
10They crouch down and wait
to grab a victim.
11They say, “God can't see!
He's got on a blindfold.”
12Do something, Lord God,
and use your powerful arm
to help those in need.
13The wicked don't respect you.
In their hearts they say,
“God won't punish us!”
14But you see the trouble
and the distress,
and you will do something.
The poor can count on you,
and so can orphans.
15Now break the power
of all merciless people.
Punish them for doing wrong
and make them stop.
16Our Lord, you will always rule,
but every godless nation
will vanish from the earth.
17You listen to the longings
of those who suffer.
You offer them hope,
and you pay attention
to their cries for help.
18You defend orphans
and everyone else in need,
so that no one on earth
can terrify others again.
translation_text:
Dami sane yemi he kue fami
1Yawɛ, mɛni hɛ mo
kɛ ya se tsitsaa kikɛ nɛ ɔ?
Mɛni he je o ya laa o he
ngɛ wa haomi be nɛ ɔ mi ɔ?
2Yayami peeli ngɛ a he nɔ woe,
nɛ a ngɛ ohiatsɛmɛ yi mi wae.
Ha nɛ ga yayamihi nɛ a to ɔ
nɛ kpa bu mɛ nitsɛmɛ a nɔ.
3Yayami peelɔ fĩaa kɛ fɔɔ
níhi nɛ e tsui suɔ a nɔ.
Nɔmlɔ nɛ hɛ kɔɔ nɔ́ nɔ ɔ,
e gbiɛɛ Yawɛ, nɛ e kuaa lɛ.
4Yayami peelɔ ɔ he nɔ womi
ha we nɛ e hlaa Mawu se blɔ.
E susumi tsuo ji “Mawu ko be.”
5Yayami peelɔ yeɔ manye ngɛ nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ mi.
E nɛ kaa Mawu tue gblami ko ngɛ ha lɛ.
E he nyɛli lɛɛ, pe e yeɔ a he fɛu.
6E deɔ ngɛ e yi mi ke,
“Nɔ́ ko nɔ́ ko be mi pee;
haomi ko be ye nɔ bae gblegbleegble.”
7 Munyuhi nɛ jeɔ e nya ji gbiɛmi kɛ sisimi,
kɛ níhi nɛ woɔ nɔ susuma he gbeye.
E he sɔɔ kɛ tuɔ yakayaka munyuhi,
kɛ munyuhi nɛ kɛ nɔ woɔ haomi mi.
8E woɔ ka ngɛ laami hehi ngɛ kɔpehi a mi,
nɛ e gbee nihi nɛ pee we nɔ́ ko yaka gu.
Daa nɛ ɔ, e ngɛ nihi
nɛ a ní ngɛ mɔbɔ dae.
9E buɔ si ngɛ e laami he ɔ
kaa jata ngɛ e muɔ mi.
E woɔ ka nɛ e nuu
nihi nɛ a ní ngɛ mɔbɔ.
Ke e nine su a nɔ
kɛkɛ e gbla mɛ kɛ ho.
10E kɛ e he wami tsuo fiaa
nihi nɛ a ní ngɛ mɔbɔ nɔ́
nɛ a nɔɔ si.
11Nɔ́ nɛ yiwutsotsɛ nɛ ɔ
deɔ ngɛ e yi mi ji,
“Oo, Mawu hɛ je nɔ;
Mawu má e hɛngmɛ;
e hyɛ we mi tete po!”
12Yawɛ Mawu,
gbla yayami peeli a tue,
nɛ o hɛ ko je nɔ́ nali a nɔ.
13Mɛni he je yayami peelɔ ma kua Mawu?
Mɛni he je lɛ e ma de ngɛ e yi mi ke,
“Oo, e tsa be mi nɔ́ ko pee” ɔ?
14Se moo lɛɛ o ngɛ nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ hyɛe.
Niinɛ, o ngɛ haomi ɔ, kɛ aywilɛho ɔ hyɛe,
nɛ o maa pee he nɔ́ ko kɛ̃.
Nɔ nɛ e fi lɛ ɔ,
o nɔ lɛ e ngɔɔ e hɛ kɛ fɔɔ.
Mo ji awusahi a he piɛlɔ.
15Moo ku yiwutsotsɛmɛ, kɛ yayami peeli
a he wami nya, nɛ o gbla a tue
kɛ yaa si yayami peemi se maa po.
16Yawɛ ji matsɛ
kɛ je neneene kɛ yaa neneene.
Je ma amɛ gbo ta e zugba a nɔ.
17Yawɛ, hiami níhi nɛ
nɔ́ nali kɛ ba fɔ o hɛ mi ɔ, o le.
Moo pee a hiami ní ɔmɛ ha mɛ,
konɛ a ná he wami he.
18Moo ye awusahi, kɛ nɔ́ nali a sane ha mɛ,
konɛ nɔmlɔ adesa kó wo a he gbeye hu.

english_text:
(A psalm by David for the music leader.)
Trusting the Lord
1The Lord is my fortress!
Don't say to me,
“Escape like a bird
to the mountains!”
2You tell me, “Watch out!
Those evil people have put
their arrows on their bows,
and they are standing
in the shadows,
aiming at good people.
3What can an honest person do
when everything crumbles?”
4The Lord is sitting
in his sacred temple
on his throne in heaven.
He knows everything we do
because he sees us all.
5The Lord tests honest people,
but despises those
who are cruel
and love violence.
6He will send fiery coals
and flaming sulfur
down on the wicked,
and they will drink nothing
but a scorching wind.
7The Lord always does right
and wants justice done.
Everyone who does right
will see his face.
translation_text:
I ngɔ ye hɛ kɛ fɔ Yawɛ nɔ
1I ba sa we ngɛ Yawɛ ngɔ.
Mɛni he je lɛ nyɛ deɔ mi ke,
“Tee kaa lohwe pɛlitsɛ
kɛ ya yo ɔmɛ a nɔ.
2Hyɛ, yayami peeli dɔ a kɛ̃ɛ̃ ɔmɛ;
a pee a kɛ̃ɛ̃ mi bi ɔmɛ klaalo
nɛ́ a ma tsɛ̃ dali ngɛ diblii mi.
3Be mi nɛ mlaa gbo, nɛ blɔ nya tomi kpakpa be hu ɔ,
mɛni dalɔ ma nyɛ maa pee?”
4Yawɛ ngɛ e we klɔuklɔu ɔ;
e matsɛ sɛ ɔ, hiɔwe lɛ e ngɛ.
E hɛngmɛ ngɛ nimli adesahi hyɛe ngɛ he tsuaa he;
e le níhi nɛ a ngɛ pee.
5Yawɛ kaa dali.
Se yayami peeli, kɛ yiwutsotsɛmɛ lɛɛ
e sume mɛ kulaa.
6Yawɛ ma ha
la nɛ ngɛ tsoe gegeege maa je hiɔwe
ba pue yayami peeli a nɔ;
nɛ kɔɔhiɔ nɛ mi dɔ la maa fia kɛ wo mɛ.
7Ejakaa Yawɛ ɔ, dalɔ ji lɛ;
e suɔ kaa a pee níhi nɛ da.
Dali maa na e hɛ mi.

english_text:
(A psalm by David for the music leader.
)
A Prayer for Help
1Please help me, Lord!
All who were faithful
and all who were loyal
have disappeared.
2Everyone tells lies,
and no one is sincere.
3Won't you chop off
all flattering tongues
that brag so loudly?
4They say to themselves,
“We are great speakers.
No one else has a chance.”
5But you, Lord, tell them,
“I will do something!
The poor are mistreated
and helpless people moan.
I'll rescue all who suffer.”
6Our Lord, you are true
to your promises,
and your word is like silver
heated seven times
in a fiery furnace.
7You will protect us
and always keep us safe
from those people.
8But all who are wicked
will keep on strutting,
while everyone praises
their shameless deeds.
translation_text:
Kue fami kɛ ha yemi kɛ buami
1Yawɛ, moo piɛ wa he,
ejakaa nɔmlɔ kpakpa be hu;
anɔkualetsɛmɛ ta zugba a nɔ.
2Nɔ tsuaa nɔ ngɛ e nyɛmi lakpa yee.
Nɔ tsuaa nɔ kɛ munyu ngɔngɔɛ
ngɛ e nyɛmi sisie.
3Yawɛ, nihi nɛ tuɔ munyu dɔkɔdɔkɔ,
kɛ ni nɛmɛ nɛ fĩaa a,
mo kpata mɛ tsuo a hɛ mi.
4A deɔ ke, “Wa ngɔɔ wa nya mi munyu
kɛ naa nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ wa ngɛ hlae.
Nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ wa suɔ kaa wa ma de ɔ,
wa ma de. Mɛnɔ ma nyɛ maa tsi wa nya?”
5Se Yawɛ ke,
“Akɛnɛ a ngɛ ohiatsɛmɛ yi mi wae,
nɛ dɛgutsɛmɛ ngɛ kɛmɛe he je ɔ,
jehanɛ lɛɛ ma te si, nɛ ma ha mɛ
he jɔmi nɛ a ngɛ hlae ɔ.”
6Yawɛ siwo ɔmɛ ɔ, anɔkuale sɔuu.
A ngɛ kaa sika hiɔ nɛ a tsu he
si kpaago ngɛ flɔɔnɔɔ mi.
7-8Nimli yayamihi ngɛ he tsuaa he,
nɛ nɔ tsuaa nɔ ngɛ nɔ́ yayami yi jee.
Yawɛ, wa kpa mo pɛɛ!
Mo je wɔ ngɛ kikɛmɛ a nimli a dɛ mi.
Nɛ o bu wa he
kɛ je yi nɔ nɛ ɔ kɛ ya neneene.

english_text:
(A psalm by David for the music leader.)
A Prayer for the Lord's Help
1How much longer, Lord,
will you forget about me?
Will it be forever?
How long will you hide?
2How long must I be confused
and miserable all day?
How long will my enemies
keep beating me down?
3Please listen, Lord God,
and answer my prayers.
Make my eyes sparkle again,
or else I will fall
into the sleep of death.
4My enemies will say,
“Now we've won!”
They will be greatly pleased
when I am defeated.
5I trust your love,
and I feel like celebrating
because you rescued me.
6You have been good to me, Lord,
and I will sing about you.
translation_text:
Kue fami kɛ ha yemi kɛ buami
1Yawɛ, kɛ yaa si mɛni be nɛ
o hɛ maa je ye nɔ?
Kɛ yaa neneene lo?
Mɛni be o maa laa mi kɛ yaa si?
2Mɛni be ma na nɔ́ kɛ yaa si?
Aywilɛho ma hyi ye tsui mi daa ligbi
kɛ yaa si mɛni be?
Ye he nyɛli ma ná ye he blɔ daa nɛ
kɛ yaa si mɛni be?
3Yawɛ, ye Mawu!
Moo hyɛ mi, nɛ o ha mi heto.
Ha mi nɔmlɔ tso he wami,
konɛ ma ko gbo.
4Ke pi ja a, ye he nyɛli ɔmɛ ma de ke,
“Wa ye e nɔ.”
A ma nya kaa a nine su ye nɔ.
5Se imi lɛɛ, o suɔmi nɛ ngɛ daa a,
lɔ ɔ nɔ lɛ i ngɔ ye hɛ kɛ fɔ.
Ma ná bua jɔmi,
ejakaa o ma he ye yi wami.
6Ma la kɛ je mo Yawɛ o yi,
ejakaa o pee ye hiami ní ɔmɛ ha mi.

english_text:
(A psalm by David for the music leader.)
No One Can Ignore the Lord
1 Only a fool would say,
“There is no God!”
People like that are worthless;
they are heartless and cruel
and never do right.
2From heaven the Lord
looks down to see
if anyone is wise enough
to search for him.
3But all of them are corrupt;
no one does right.
4Won't you evil people learn?
You refuse to pray,
and you gobble up
the Lord's people.
5But you will be frightened,
because God is on the side
of every good person.
6You may spoil the plans
of the poor,
but the Lord protects them.
7I long for someone from Zion
to come and save Israel!
Our Lord, when you bless
your people again,
Jacob's family will be glad,
and Israel will celebrate.
translation_text:
Nɔmlɔ adesa yi mi wa
(La 53)
1 Kuasiahi a susumi ji, “Mawu ko be.”
Mɛ tsuo a puɛ; ní yayamihi sɔuu lɛ a peeɔ;
nɔ ko nɔ ko be nɛ peeɔ nɔ́ nɛ da.
2Yawɛ hyɛɛ nimli adesahi
ngɛ zugba kɛ jeɔ hiɔwe.
E hyɛɛ kaa e maa na nɔ ko nɛ le nɔ́,
nɛ hlaa lɛ Mawu ɔ se blɔ lo.
3Se mɛ tsuo a laa blɔ;
mɛ tsuo pɛpɛɛpɛ a puɛ.
Nɔ ko nɔ ko be nɛ peeɔ nɔ́ nɛ da;
dɛbi, nɔ kake ngmelu po be.
4Yawɛ ngɛ bie ke,
“Yayami peeli nɛ ɔmɛ ɔ, anɛ a be juɛmi lo?
A ní tsumi kɛkɛ ji kaa a fia ye ma a ojo,
se imi, Yawɛ lɛɛ a tsɛ we ye biɛ.”
5Sawale nɛ nya wa maa nu mɛ;
ejakaa nihi nɛ peeɔ nɔ́ nɛ da a,
Mawu kɛ mɛ ngɛ.
6Ke yayami peeli ha nɛ
ohiatsɛmɛ a yi mi tomi pee basaa a,
a ma ya sa we ngɛ Yawɛ ngɔ kɛ̃.
7Mɛnɔ maa je Zion ba he Israel yi wami?
Yawɛ ma a nɛ a nuu kɛ ho ɔ,
ke lɛ, Yawɛ ɔ kpale mɛ kɛ ba ekohu ɔ,
Israel ma na bua jɔmi, nɛ Yakob ma nya.

english_text:
(A psalm by David.)
Who May Worship the Lord?
1Who may stay in God's temple
or live on the holy mountain
of the Lord?
2Only those who obey God
and do as they should.
They speak the truth
3and don't spread gossip;
they treat others fairly
and don't say cruel things.
4They hate worthless people,
but show respect for all
who worship the Lord.
And they keep their promises,
no matter what the cost.
5They lend their money
without charging interest,
and they don't take bribes
to hurt the innocent.
Those who do these things
will always stand firm.
translation_text:
Nɔ́ nɛ Mawu suɔ
1Yawɛ, mɛnɔ maa hi o bo tsu ɔ mi?
O yoku klɔuklɔu ɔ nɔ ɔ, mɛnɔ maa hi lejɛ ɔ?
2Nɔ nɛ piami ko be e he,
nɛ e peeɔ nɔ́ nɛ da.
Nɔ nɛ tuɔ anɔkuale sisiisi,
3nɛ e yi nɔ he sieku.
Nɔ nɛ tu we nɔ he munyu,
nɛ e pee we e nyɛmi yayami.
4Nɔ nɛ tuɔ munyu kɛ siɔ yayami peeli,
nɛ e woɔ nihi nɛ yeɔ Yawɛ gbeye ɔ a hɛ mi nyami.
Nɔ nɛ ke e
ka kita, nɛ e kpale we e nya se,
ke ji kaa lɔ ɔ maa pee haomi ha lɛ po.
5Nɔ nɛ ke e pa sika ha nihi ɔ,
e he we hekpa.
Nɔ nɛ he we nyɔ mi ní
nɛ e kɛ ye odase ngɔ si nihi nɛ yi fɔ.
Nɔ nɛ peeɔ ní nɛ ɔmɛ ɔ,
nɔ́ ko nɔ́ ko be e he sae.

english_text:
(A special psalm by David.)
The Best Choice
1Protect me, Lord God!
I run to you for safety,
2and I have said,
“Only you are my Lord!
Every good thing I have
is a gift from you.”
3Your people are wonderful,
and they make me happy,
4but worshipers of other gods
will have much sorrow.
I refuse to offer sacrifices
of blood to those gods
or worship in their name.
5You, Lord, are all I want!
You are my choice,
and you keep me safe.
6You make my life pleasant,
and my future is bright.
7I praise you, Lord,
for being my guide.
Even in the darkest night,
your teachings fill my mind.
8 I will always look to you,
as you stand beside me
and protect me from fear.
9With all my heart,
I will celebrate,
and I can safely rest.
10 I am your chosen one.
You won't leave me in the grave
or let my body decay.
11You have shown me
the path to life,
and you make me glad
by being near to me.
Sitting at your right side,
I will always be joyful.
translation_text:
Ngɔɔ o hɛ ngɔ fɔ Mawu nɔ
1Mawu, moo bu ye he,
ejakaa i ngɔ ye hɛ kɛ fɔ o nɔ.
2I de Yawɛ ke,
“Yawɛ, ye Nyɔmtsɛ ji mo;
o se ɔ, i pa be nɔ́ kpakpa ko hu.”
3Hyɛ bɔ nɛ Yawɛ e ni klɔuklɔuhi
nɛ ngɛ je ɔ mi ɔ a hɛ mi ngɛ nyami ha!
Mɛ ji ni nɛmɛ nɛ i naa a he bua jɔmi.
4Nihi nɛ a he sɔɔ kɛ ya nyɛɛɔ
mawu kpahi a se ɔ,
a haomi maa hiɛ babauu.
I be mɛ futue kɛ pee a tɛlimi kusumi ɔmɛ;
i be a biɛ ta woe tete.
5Yawɛ ji ye nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́;
lɛ nɛ e haa mi nɔ́ tsuaa nɔ́ nɛ hia mi.
Nɔ́ nɛ maa ba ye nɔ hwɔɔ se hu,
Yawɛ dɛ mi lɛ e ngɛ.
6O ke mi ní kpakpahi babauu;
niinɛ, i ngɛ weto ní kpakpahi.
7Ma je Yawɛ yi,
ejakaa e ha mi juɛmi.
Nyɔ mi po, ye he nile kɛ mi tuɔ munyu.
8 I susuɔ Yawɛ he daa.
Nɛ́ Yawɛ ngɛ ye kasa nya nɛ ɔ,
nɔ́ ko nɔ́ ko be mi pee.
9Enɛ ɔ he je ɔ, imi nɔmlɔ ɔ tsuo,
i na bua jɔmi, kɛ he jɔmi.
10 Ejakaa o maa bu ye he,
nɛ gbenɔ he wami be ye he blɔ nae.
Nɔ nɛ o suɔ lɛ ɔ,
o be e he ngmɛɛe nɛ e hɛ mi nɛ kpata.
11O maa tsɔɔ mi blɔ ɔ nɛ yaa wami mi ɔ.
Lejɛ ɔ, ngɛ o hɛ mi ɔ,
ma na bua jɔmi nitsɛnitsɛ,
bua jɔmi nɛ se be poe kɛ maa ya neneene.

english_text:
(A prayer by David.)
The Prayer of an Innocent Person
1I am innocent, Lord!
Won't you listen as I pray
and beg for help?
I am honest!
Please hear my prayer.
2Only you can say
that I am innocent,
because only your eyes
can see the truth.
3You know my heart,
and even during the night
you have tested me
and found me innocent.
I have made up my mind
never to tell a lie.
4I don't do like others.
I obey your teachings
and am not cruel.
5I have followed you,
without ever stumbling.
6I pray to you, God,
because you will help me.
Listen and answer my prayer!
7Show your wonderful love.
Your mighty arm protects those
who run to you for safety
from their enemies.
8Protect me as you would
your very own eyes;
hide me in the shadow
of your wings.
9Don't let my brutal enemies
attack from all sides
and kill me.
10They refuse to show mercy,
and they keep bragging.
11They have caught up with me!
My enemies are everywhere,
eagerly hoping to smear me
in the dirt.
12They are like hungry lions
hunting for food,
or like young lions
hiding in ambush.
13Do something, Lord!
Attack and defeat them.
Take your sword and save me
from those evil people.
14Use your powerful arm
and rescue me
from the hands of mere humans
whose world won't last.
You provide food
for those you love.
Their children have plenty,
and their grandchildren
will have more than enough.
15I am innocent, Lord,
and I will see your face!
When I awake, all I want
is to see you as you are.
translation_text:
David fa kue ha Mawu
1Yawɛ, moo piɛ ye he koo!
Hyɛ kaa i yeɔ anɔkuale, nɛ i sisi we nɔ.
Lɔ ɔ he ɔ, i kpa mo pɛɛ nɛ o bu
kue nɛ i ngɛ fae kɛ hɛdɔ nɛ ɔ tue.
2Mo nɛ́ o yeɔ dami sane,
moo wo mi nguɔ koo!
3Ke o hyɛ ye tsui mi,
ke o ba slaa mi nyɔ mi nɛ o ka mi ɔ,
o be yayami ko nae ngɛ ye he.
Ye munyu peeɔ anɔkuale; nɔ́ ko piɛ we he.
4I yeɔ o mlaa amɛ a nɔ,
nɛ i kɛ basabasa peeli bɔɛ.
5O blɔ ɔ nɔ lɛ i nyɛɛɔ daa;
i sane we kɛ ji nɔ hyɛ gblegbleegble.
6Mawu, i ngɛ kue fae kɛ ngɛ mo hae,
ejakaa i le kaa o maa pee ye hiami ní ɔmɛ ha mi.
Lɛɛ mo plɛ o hɛ mi kɛ kpee mi mɔ,
konɛ o nu ye munyu ɔmɛ.
7Mo je o nyakpɛ suɔmi nɛ ngɛ daa a kpo
kɛ tsɔɔ nihi nɛ ngɔɔ a hɛ kɛ fɔɔ o nɔ ɔ;
nɛ o kpɔ mɛ kɛ je ni nɛmɛ nɛ teɔ si
kɛ woɔ mɛ ɔ a dɛ mi.
8Moo baa ye yi kaa bɔ nɛ nɔ baa
lɛ nitsɛ e hɛngmɛ yi ɔ.
Ngɔɔ mi kɛ laa ngɛ o pɛli hɔ̃ ɔ sisi,
9kɛ je yiwutsotsɛmɛ nɛ ngɛ mi
yi mi wae ɔ a dɛ mi,
kɛ je ye he nyɛli nɛ bɔle mi ɔ a dɛ mi.
10Mɔbɔ nami ko be a mi;
he nɔ womi munyuhi lɛ jeɔ a nya.
11Jehanɛ lɛɛ a sa ye yi;
a ngɔ a hɛ ngɔ ká mi,
konɛ a tsɛ̃ mi kɛ fɔ si.
12A ngɛ kaa jatahi nɛ ya wo mi ká;
a ngɛ mlɛe nɛ a tsɔtslɔɔ mi.
13Yawɛ, yaa nɛ o kɛ mɛ ya kpe
nɛ o ye a nɔ.
Ngɔɔ o klaate ɔ kɛ kpɔ mi
kɛ je yiwutsotsɛmɛ a dɛi.
14Jé mi kɛ je nihi nɛ ná je nɛ ɔ mi
níhi tsuo nɛ a ngɛ hlae ɔ a dɛ mi.
Ngɔɔ haomihi nɛ o ngɔ to ha mɛ ɔ kɛ gbla a tue.
Ha nɛ a bimɛ ba na haomi ɔ bɔ nɛ sa,
nɛ eko nɛ piɛ ha a bibimɛ.
15Se imi lɛɛ ma na o hɛ mi,
ejakaa i pee we yayami ko.
Nɛ ke ye hɛ tsɛ ɔ, ma ná bua jɔmi babauu
kaa i na mo hɛ mi kɛ hɛ mi.

english_text:
(For the music leader. A psalm by David, the Lord's servant. David sang this to the Lord after the Lord had rescued him from his enemies, but especially from Saul.)
David's Song of Thanks
1I love you, Lord God,
and you make me strong.
2You are my mighty rock,
my fortress, my protector,
the rock where I am safe,
my shield, my powerful weapon,
and my place of shelter.
3I praise you, Lord!
I prayed, and you rescued me
from my enemies.
4Death had wrapped
its ropes around me,
and I was almost swallowed
by its flooding waters.
5Ropes from the world
of the dead
had coiled around me,
and death had set a trap
in my path.
6I was in terrible trouble
when I called out to you,
but from your temple
you heard me
and answered my prayer.
7The earth shook and shivered,
and the mountains trembled
down to their roots.
You were angry
8and breathed out smoke.
Scorching heat and fiery flames
spewed from your mouth.
9You opened the heavens
like curtains,
and you came down
with storm clouds
under your feet.
10You rode on the backs
of flying creatures
and swooped down
with the wind as wings.
11Darkness was your robe;
thunderclouds filled the sky,
hiding you from sight.
12Hailstones and fiery coals
lit up the sky
in front of you.
13 Lord Most High, your voice
thundered from the heavens,
as hailstones and fiery coals
poured down like rain.
14You scattered your enemies
with arrows of lightning.
15You roared at the sea,
and its deepest channels
could be seen.
You snorted,
and the earth shook
to its foundations.
16You reached down from heaven,
and you lifted me
from deep in the ocean.
17You rescued me from enemies,
who were hateful
and too powerful for me.
18On the day disaster struck,
they came and attacked,
but you defended me.
19When I was fenced in,
you freed and rescued me
because you love me.
20You are good to me, Lord,
because I do right,
and you reward me
because I am innocent.
21I do what you want
and never turn to do evil.
22I keep your laws in mind
and never look away
from your teachings.
23I obey you completely
and guard against sin.
24You have been good to me
because I do right;
you have rewarded me
for being innocent
by your standards.
25You are always loyal
to your loyal people,
and you are faithful
to the faithful.
26With all who are sincere,
you are sincere,
but you treat the unfaithful
as their deeds deserve.
27You rescue the humble,
but you put down all
who are proud.
28You, the Lord God,
keep my lamp burning
and turn darkness to light.
29You help me defeat armies
and capture cities.
30Your way is perfect, Lord,
and your word is correct.
You are a shield for those
who run to you for help.
31You alone are God!
Only you are a mighty rock.
32You give me strength
and guide me right.
33 You make my feet run as fast
as those of a deer,
and you help me stand
on the mountains.
34You teach my hands to fight
and my arms to use
a bow of bronze.
35You alone are my shield.
Your right hand supports me,
and by coming to help me,
you have made me famous.
36You clear the way for me,
and now I won't stumble.
37I kept chasing my enemies,
until I caught them
and destroyed them.
38I stuck my sword
through my enemies,
and they were crushed
under my feet.
39You helped me win victories,
and you forced my attackers
to fall victim to me.
40You made my enemies run,
and I killed them.
41They cried out for help,
but no one saved them;
they called out to you,
but there was no answer.
42I ground them to dust
blown by the wind,
and I poured them out
like mud in the streets.
43You rescued me
from stubborn people,
and you made me the leader
of foreign nations,
who are now my slaves.
44They obey and come crawling.
45They have lost all courage,
and from their fortresses,
they come trembling.
46You are the living Lord!
I will praise you.
You are a mighty rock.
I will honor you
for keeping me safe.
47You took revenge for me,
and you put nations
in my power.
48You protected me
from violent enemies
and made me much greater
than all of them.
49 I will praise you, Lord,
and I will honor you
among the nations.
50You give glorious victories
to your chosen king.
Your faithful love for David
and for his descendants
will never end.
translation_text:
David manye la
(Samuel II, 22.1-51)
1Yawɛ, i suɔ mo!
Mo ji ye yi baalɔ.
2Yawɛ ji nɔ nɛ heɔ ye yi wami;
ye tɛ sa, kɛ ye mɔ nguaa.
Lɛ ji ye Mawu, kɛ ye wesa he.
Yawɛ ngɛ kaa tsɛ̃i kɛ ha mi;
e buɔ ye he, nɛ e haa nɛ i yeɔ ye he.
3Ma tsɛ Yawɛ,
nɛ e ma je mi kɛ maa je ye he nyɛli a dɛ mi.
A je Yawɛ yi!
4Gbenɔ oslaa bɔle mi kɛ kpe;
niinɛ, nimli yayamihi babauu bɔle mi
kaa pa nɛ hia kɛ bee.
5Gbeje kpa amɛ fi mi,
nɛ gbenɔ tsɔ mi klama.
6Ngɛ ye haomi be ɔ mi ɔ,
i tsɛ Yawɛ.
I tsɛ ye Mawu,
nɛ i de lɛ ke e piɛ ye he.
E nu ye gbi ngɛ e we klɔuklɔu ɔ,
nɛ e bu ye kue fami ɔ tue.
7Kɛkɛ nɛ zugba mimiɛ,
nɛ yo ɔmɛ a sisi tomi ɔmɛ hɛ mɛ
kɛ je a blɔ hehi, nɛ a mimiɛ,
ejakaa Yawɛ mi mi fu.
8La su ku hia kɛ je e gugwɔ puɔhi a mi;
la nɛ ngɛ tsoe je e nya mi,
nɛ hã nɛ tsɛ̃ je e mi.
9E ha nɛ hiɔwe nya ba si, nɛ e kple si;
nɛ diblii kpii ngɛ e nane sisi.
10E hi kerub nɔ kɛ te;
e he sɔ kɛ nyɛɛ kɔɔhiɔ mi kɛ ba.
11E ngɔ diblii kɛ ha e he kaa bo,
nɛ bɔku kpii kɛ e mi nyu gbagbaagba ha e yi nɔ.
12Gbiɛ ngo ngu, kɛ la
je oslabai mi ngɛ e hɛ mi
kɛ gblee bɔku kpii ɔ mi kɛ be.
13Jehanɛ Yawɛ ha hiɔwe si;
Hiɔwe No ɔ wo gbi;
gbiɛ ngo ngu nɛ, nɛ oslabai gba.
14Ee, e tsɛ̃ e kɛ̃ɛ̃ mi bi ɔmɛ,
nɛ e he nyɛli ɔmɛ gbɛ fĩa.
E ha nɛ oslabai gba, nɛ a pee basaa.
15Yawɛ, benɛ o ké o he nyɛli ɔmɛ a yi,
nɛ o kɛ abofu wo gbi ɔ,
nyu dɔ ɔmɛ je kpo,
nɛ je ɔ sisi tomi ɔmɛ fɔɔ si paa.
16Yawɛ sɔ́le e nine kɛ je hiɔwe;
e nu mi, nɛ e gbla mi kɛ je nyu babauu ɔ mi.
17E kpɔ mi kɛ je ye he nyɛli ɔmɛ a dɛ mi;
e je mi kɛ je nihi tsuo nɛ nyɛɛ mi ɔ a dɛ mi.
Niinɛ, a he wa pe mi.
18A ba tua mi ngɛ ye haomi ligbi ɔ nɔ,
se Yawɛ hede ha mi.
19E ngɔ mi kɛ ba he nɛ he jɔmi ngɛ.
E he ye yi wami, ejakaa e suɔ mi.
20Yawɛ wo mi hiɔ bɔ nɛ sa,
ejakaa i peeɔ nɔ́ nɛ da.
Yawɛ gbaa mi,
ejakaa ye he tsɔ.
21I ye Yawɛ mlaa amɛ a nɔ,
nɛ i pee we yayami ko kɛ puɛ
i kɛ ye Mawu ɔ wa kpɛti.
22I ye e mlaa amɛ tsuo pɛpɛɛpɛ a nɔ;
i tɔ̃ we ekoeko.
23Yayami ko yayami ko be ye he;
i yi fɔ ngɛ nɔ́ ko mi.
24Enɛ ɔ he je ɔ, Yawɛ gbaa mi;
ejakaa ye he tsɔ, nɛ i peeɔ nɔ́ nɛ da.
25Yawɛ, nihi nɛ yeɔ anɔkuale ɔ,
o jeɔ o he si kɛ tsɔɔ mɛ kaa anɔkualetsɛ.
Nihi nɛ peeɔ nɔ́ nɛ da a,
o jeɔ o he si kɛ tsɔɔ mɛ kaa dalɔ.
26Nihi nɛ a he tsɔ ɔ,
o jeɔ o he si kɛ tsɔɔ mɛ kaa o he tsɔ.
Se yiwutsotsɛmɛ lɛɛ
o ha we mɛ hɛ mi kulaa.
27Nihi nɛ baa a he si ɔ,
o heɔ a yi wami.
Se ni nɛmɛ nɛ woɔ a he nɔ lɛɛ
o baa mɛ si.
28Ejakaa mo Yawɛ, ye Mawu ɔ,
mo lɛ o haa mi la.
Mo lɛ o fieɔ diblii kɛ jeɔ ye he.
29Mo Mawu, o he wami nya a,
ma nyɛ ma tu gbogbo kɛ ya tua ye he nyɛli,
nɛ ma ye a nɔ.
30Mawu nɛ ɔ loo!
E ní peemi níhi hi kɛ pi si.
Ke e wo si ɔ, e baa mi.
Nihi tsuo nɛ ya saa we ngɛ e ngɔ ɔ,
e buu a he.
31Se mɛnɔ ji Mawu ngɛ Yawɛ se?
Mɛnɔ ji tɛ sa? Pi wa Mawu ɔ lo?
32Lɛ ji Mawu nɛ haa mi he wami;
lɛ nɛ haa ye blɔ daa mi.
33 Lɛ nɛ haa nɛ ye nane nya sɔɔ
kaa odabɔ nane nya.
E ngɔ mi ngɔ to yo ɔmɛ a nɔ
ngɛ he jɔmi mi.
34E tsɔɔ mi ta hwumi níhi a he ní tsumi;
akɔblee kɛ̃ɛ̃ po ma nyɛ ma tsɛ̃.
35Yawɛ, o bu ye he, nɛ o he ye yi wami;
o hyɛ ye nɔ saminya, nɛ i pee nɔmlɔ.
O pɛtɛ ye he wawɛɛ,
nɛ lɔ ɔ ha nɛ i ye ye he.
36O ha we nɛ ye he nyɛli a nine nɛ su ye nɔ;
i nɔɛ si hyɛ gblegbleegble.
37I nyɛɛ ye he nyɛli ɔmɛ a se kɛ fo
kɛ ya si i nuu mɛ.
I kpale we ye se kɛ ya si i kpata a hɛ mi.
38I fia mɛ ní, nɛ a nɔɔ si ngɛ ye nane nya;
a be nyɛe maa te si hu.
39Mo lɛ o ha mi he wami nɛ i kɛ hwu ta;
mo lɛ o ha nɛ i ye ye he nyɛli ɔmɛ a nɔ.
40Mo lɛ o ha nɛ ye he nyɛli ɔmɛ tu fo.
Nihi nɛ nyɛɔ mi ɔ, mo lɛ o ha nɛ i kpata a hɛ mi.
41A kpa ngmlaa kaa nɔ ko ma ba piɛ a he lo,
se nɔ ko ji ngmlaa ha mɛ.
A tsɛ Yawɛ, se e pui a nya mi.
42I wɛɛ mɛ mɔnyɔmɔnyɔ
kaa bunyuku nɛ kɔɔhiɔ sɛ mi.
I naa a nɔ kaa blɔ nɔ mɔsɔ.
43O je mi kɛ je atuã tsɔli a dɛ mi,
nɛ o pee mi je ma amɛ a nyatsɛ.
Ma nɛ i li mɛ po ma ba sɔmɔ mi.
44Nibwɔhi ma ba kpla si ha mi;
ke a nu ye he pɛ a maa bu mi tue.
45Nibwɔ ɔmɛ a tsui maa po, nɛ a kɛ he domi
maa je a mɔ nguangua amɛ a mi kɛ ba.
46Yawɛ hɛ ngɛ! A je ye he bulɔ ɔ yi!
Mawu ɔ nɛ heɔ ye yi wami ɔ,
a wo e hɛ mi nyami.
47Mawu nɛ ɔ lɛ gbla ye he nyɛli ɔmɛ a tue;
lɛ nɛ ngɔ je ma amɛ kɛ wo ye sisi,
48nɛ e je mi kɛ je ye he nyɛli ɔmɛ a dɛ mi.
Yawɛ, mo lɛ o ha nɛ i ye ye he nyɛli ɔmɛ a nɔ,
nɛ o je mi kɛ je yiwutsotsɛmɛ a dɛ mi.
49 Enɛ ɔ he je ɔ, ma je o yi ngɛ je ma amɛ a hɛ mi;
ma la kɛ je mo, Yawɛ o yi.
50Mawu haa nɛ David yeɔ kunimi daa.
Matsɛ ɔ nɛ lɛ, Mawu ɔ pɔ nu ɔ,
e naa lɛ mɔbɔ daa;
lɛ, kɛ e bimɛ, kɛ e nina tsuo.

english_text:
(A psalm by David for the music leader.)
The Wonders of God and the Goodness of His Law
1The heavens keep telling
the wonders of God,
and the skies declare
what he has done.
2Each day informs
the following day;
each night announces
to the next.
3They don't speak a word,
and there is never
the sound of a voice.
4 Yet their message reaches
all the earth,
and it travels
around the world.
In the heavens a tent
is set up for the sun.
5It rises like a bridegroom
and gets ready like a hero
eager to run a race.
6It travels all the way
across the sky.
Nothing hides from its heat.
7 The Law of the Lord is perfect;
it gives us new life.
His teachings last forever,
and they give wisdom
to ordinary people.
8The Lord's instruction is right;
it makes our hearts glad.
His commands shine brightly,
and they give us light.
9Worshiping the Lord is sacred;
he will always be worshiped.
All his decisions
are correct and fair.
10They are worth more
than the finest gold
and are sweeter than honey
from a honeycomb.
11By your teachings, Lord,
I am warned;
by obeying them,
I am greatly rewarded.
12None of us know our faults.
Forgive me when I sin
without knowing it.
13Don't let me do wrong
on purpose, Lord,
